“You will feel so stupid when I—”

“Can we climb?” Mydei interrupts them without a care, pointing to the tree line of the forest Hephaestion found them in. He speaks slowly, taking care to pronounce every word properly.

And Phainon is immediately thrown back to their little wordless competitions, the thrill of bringing back one more animal or being the first one to light the fire. “I bet I can climb the highest,” immediately tumbles out of his mouth.

Mydei’s eyes narrow just the slightest bit in a way that signals a new bout of determination. Phainon grins. It’s on.

Hephaestion looks between them, then to to the trees. ”Pass. Lady Archidamia will already be furious that we skipped the evening practice. She will kill us if all of us end up with broken legs.”

Since Mydei is the only one she actually cares about being alive, and he’s got the ability to get revived, she might do that. But Mydei heals fast, and she doesn’t care about Phainon being hurt, so it should be fine.

“Okay,” he agrees easily.

Hephaestion stays behind to see the tree line clearly and be able to judge while each of them chooses a suitable tree to climb, starting on her call.

It all goes better than Phainon anticipated. He was initially concerned that he might have grown rusty, but he shouldn’t have worried. He forgot that Mydei never even tried climbing anything like this. He does exceptionally well, climbing to about the halfway point before calling it quits. Phainon makes it another quarter higher up than him, leaning slightly to the side and shouting about his victory.

In turn, Mydei is much quicker to get back to the ground. Phainon can see him and Hephaestion waiting at the foot of his tree, and gazing up to track his progress. To be fair, Mydei wasn’t as high up, so logically, he would get down faster no matter what. Phainon could have been down already if he wanted, but he is just taking his time.

Almost there, Phainon encounters a small problem. He thinks he may have heaved himself up more easily with a burst of adrenaline as he was climbing up or something, but now he cannot find enough branches to put his legs on. There is just a singular, very thin, and fragile-looking one to his left. Nothing else.

Without any other options, he places both legs on one branch. It’s not that far down anymore. He could probably jump down if he wanted. What’s just a few meters?

There is a crack below him. Phainon instantly regrets the thought.

Phainon reacts by instinct, clutching onto the branches above with everything he has. It doesn’t change anything. In the next moment, the wood snaps underneath his feet, pulling his weight down. It takes five more seconds as Phainon frantically searches for where to put his legs, and then he is sailing through the air.

He doesn’t scream. Maybe a little.

He barely even registers it until he hits the ground, breath leaving his lungs in a painful wheeze. Through slightly blackened vision, he sees Hephaestion and Mydei stare down at him with worried looks.

“I’m fine,” he croaks out, raising his hand to wave and finding there is still a branch clutched in it.

All is silent for a beat or two. And then, Mydei bursts out laughing. Full-on laughter, the kind that makes him hold on to his stomach from the force of it. Phainon’s vision clears, and he notices the surprised edge to Mydei’s eyes, like he wasn’t aware he could even laugh.

Falling out of the tree was worth it.

Phainon closes the door to their bedroom and turns the light on, already untying his own armguards, when Mydei appears right in front of him. He holds one hand up, something small and bright blue sitting atop it.

It’s a flower. Phainon doesn’t know what kind.

“It’s pretty,” he offers. He tilts his head down to take a closer look, noting the bright yellow dot at the center of it and an irregular line running through the middle of the petals in a slightly darker blue. “I didn’t notice you picking it up.”

“For you.” Mydei points to Phainon’s eyes with his free hand. With that revelation, yeah, it does resemble Phainon’s eyes quite a bit. It’s been a while since the last time Mydei gave him anything; Phainon nearly forgot about their little ritual from the forest.

“Oh.” He brings his hands together and cups them, and holds the little flower in them delicately when Mydei puts it there, careful of its fragility. “Thank you.”

Phainon shifts it to one hand so that he can tap Mydei’s chest twice with the other. Then he walks to the dresser on which all of their treasures are displayed and sets it down on it. He takes one of the books that Ptolemy lent them off the shelf and opens it at a random page.

“If I put it inside, it will dry nicely instead of wilting. Dying? I don’t remember if Ptolemy has covered what ‘wilt’ means yet,” he explains as he does so, carefully closing the book so that the petals are kept straight, and puts it back in its place. He hopes it doesn’t stain the pages.

Once it’s preserved and he won’t have to watch it die, he can put it next to the rest of the gifts.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Two times, the adults make an effort to begin the process of separating them.

At first, it’s a request for Mydei to resume his lessons with Ptolemy, as Phainon is urgently called in by someone else. It’s not even much of a decision for Mydei to ditch Ptolemy entirely and follow Phainon. To the Council. It leads to a conversation with a lot of disappointed stares directed at them, the adults having decided Mydei has learned enough to understand what they mean. Words of concern and attempts to explain that it’s not healthy. There should be some space between them, or it will become problematic. The Crown Prince cannot afford to have a boy attached to his side at all times.

Phainon tries to argue with them, but it’s only seen as a child throwing a fit. It’s frustrating. Mydei doesn’t care for their words. He stands tall at Phainon’s side and grows agitated only when it starts affecting Phainon.

“I don’t care. We are together,” he says firmly, one step in front of Phainon, when some guy loses his composure at Phainon’s audacity and smart comments and tries to come closer with an angry look in his eye. “Leave us alone.”

He doesn’t wait for anyone’s reaction or approval. He grabs Phainon’s wrist and drags him out, heading toward Ptolemy’s. Somehow, the too-warm heat of those fingers on Phainon’s skin makes him feel steady like never before.

The second time is more drastic. And dramatic. The lack of patience and understanding leads to Archidamia dragging Mydei away with an iron grip around his armguard, as Phainon is held in place by two soldiers in the middle of the day on one of the roads. People stare, but no one moves to help them. They probably all think the same, that someone should put a stop to whatever Mydei and Phainon are doing. Which is just existing together.

Phainon doesn’t think any of it is all that necessary, doesn’t know what harm it does to anyone else, that they are all so adamant about not letting them be. He is confused about why anyone even cares. Phainon barely feels the tears welling up in his eyes as he screams himself hoarse to let him go.

What if something happens and Phainon isn’t there? What if they’ve been waiting to get Mydei alone? They definitely have, and who knows what they would make him do.

Months of trying to get better, and Phainon is still so useless. Still can’t keep a hold on one singular person, keep him safe. Through blurred vision, he sees a familiar figure pushing through the gathered crowd, rushing in to stand in Archidamia’s path.

“Lady Archidamia, this is improper,” Ptolemy speaks harshly. He is shorter than her by a head, thin and soft. Yet he doesn’t cower under her glare, standing straight with his shoulders squared. “You will bring nothing but harm with the course of action you are taking.”

“Your involvement is as unnecessary as it is unwelcome. Stay in your lane, scholar.” She responds with clear disdain. She walks around him, daring him to intervene and bear the consequences, as Mydei tries to reach for him when he is dragged forward. “You may not be exiled like the rest of us, but Castrum Kremnos won’t welcome you back if we drop you off by her gates. Quite the opposite, you will find.”

Phainon sees Ptolemy’s hands ball into tight fists, his back trembling just so. Archidamia, having said her piece, continues on until they disappear around the corner, Mydei’s eyes flashing with gold as panic sets in.

Neither of them is strong enough. Bitterly, Phainon wishes Ptolemy were more Kremnoan instead of a simple bookworm. He knows he is shoving the anger he feels for himself at another target. It doesn’t matter.

Phainon gives one more effort to struggle against the men restraining him before he gives up, letting himself slump forward. Okay. Fine. They will let go eventually, and then he can find Mydei. The settlement isn’t that big, and Archidamia cannot have taken him outside of it. They cannot keep them apart forever either, they would have to—

Mydei walks back out, striding purposefully in their direction. His markings glow with a more vibrant color, red mist gathering around his hands. And his hands, stained with red blood.

It feels like everyone holds their breath; the guards’ grip on his arms tightening in shock and uncertainty. Until Archidamia follows after him, and people can breathe easily again. Their prince didn’t just somehow kill their leader for a matter so—in their opinion—stupid.

She stalks in Mydei’s footsteps, holding her side as red crystals slowly dissipate, and glares so fiercely that Phainon is almost fearful she might intend to seriously harm Mydei. His friend doesn’t seem to care, eyes set firmly on the men at Phainon’s sides, silently commanding them to let go before he closes the distance.

Ptolemy seems to shake it off the fastest, jumping back into action as he jogs to the boy.

“Mydei. Mydei, I’m going to put my hand on your shoulder, I am not restraining you,” he says loudly and clearly, doing just that. Mydei glances at him silently, halting. “We will make it alright, just calm down, please.” Whatever he sees in Ptolemy’s expression is enough to convince him as he stays put, returning to watching Phainon. As if, in this moment, nothing else held importance in comparison. Phainon can relate.

Mydei and Phainon fight together a lot, but it’s never serious. Bruises and slight cuts happen. Never anything that doesn’t heal within a day. Sometimes they trip over their own feet, the weapon’s weight awkward in their hands. It’s so easy to forget Mydei is still a predator raised in the vicious sea among beasts larger than buildings. He is much stronger if he lets loose and doesn’t care for proper stances and techniques. His stare is attentive and unblinking, promising violence if the guards so much as breathe wrong.

Phainon feels both of them freeze on the spot.

And Phainon knows it’s going to be fine, one way or the other. In the worst-case scenario, they will let go, and Mydei and Phainon will run away. Maybe grab Hephaestion on the way, and Ptolemy could follow too. It would be fun, the four of them in the wild. Ptolemy knows so much, he would know all berries and weeds that are poisonous and which aren’t.

Whether this ends peacefully or not, it will be fine.

Mydei is strong, and Phainon will become strong too. Soon.

“Your perception of me may be that of a foolish teenager, but I would advise you to cease this at once,” Ptolemy says calmly to Archidamia. She stopped a few paces short of reaching the two of them. He seems uncaring of the frightening glare she is directing his way. “I don’t have much of the extraordinary fighting capabilities you all strive for. But I am knowledgeable, I have researched everything I could get under my fingertips so far.

“You cannot handle a child in this way, not one you clearly wish to grow strong and capable. You all treat Mydeimos as if he were your only way to regain the glory you have lost. Kremnoans to the core, wishing to die for it.” Ptolemy says, taking his eyes off Archidamia to rake his gaze over everyone gathered. “He has Gorgo’s blood flowing through his veins, and you delude yourselves thinking the wild lion won’t bite your head off?” He scoffs, shooting a glance at Archidamia’s bleeding wound. “He won’t be tamed with the childhood he has had. The best you can hope for is that, over

time, Mydei will develop a sense of duty and belonging to this community. You cannot oppress him.”

Phainon has always liked Ptolemy, even with all the nagging and his tendency for dramatics. He is smart. He doesn’t treat them like they’re stupid just because they’re younger. And he can be fun, too. He is a friend, one of the precious three Phainon has now. But watching him stand up for Mydei so fiercely despite being one of the weakest people around, Phainon feels a surge of such intense gratitude and appreciation that it makes him want to cry all over again.

“He is indulging your ideas solely because he doesn’t care so long as his friend is happy. What do you think will happen when you take that friend away or cause him distress, you fools? He goes along with everything you say, makes excellent progress in any course you throw at him, and doesn’t say a word against anything. Yet the one time he requests you let someone he cares about accompany him on this rotten road you set him on, you deny him that one comfort? And none of you dare to stand up for him?” His voice grows frustrated, stance protective above Mydei’s body. He glares at the audience, and people shift on their feet uneasily. “This is precisely why Queen Gorgo is dead. Why all of you waste your meaningless lives away in hiding.”

Archidamia considers the teenager with a calculating gaze, her anger almost forgotten. Her stance is still rigid, but it’s like she is seeing him in a new light. No word comes out of her mouth, though. Ptolemy doesn’t care to look back at her, seemingly taking satisfaction in the way his listeners appear properly chastised.

Phainon was not ready for such a long tangent, but he isn’t complaining. It might get everyone to finally leave them be. If, from now on, no one questions them at every step, he will never complain about Ptolemy again. He takes everything back about wishing the teen was more Kremnoan.

They won’t have to run. They can stay here and have access to all the weapons, proper training, food, and a bed. Light. It’s all he can ask for.

So, it’s actually gonna be fine.

Thank Kephale.

Ptolemy clears his throat as the silence stretches on for too long, no one daring to say anything else. Then, his eyes settle on Phainon again, and his irritation bleeds right back out.

“Oh, haven’t you heard a word I just said? You shouldn’t be on duty if you are deaf,” he snarks at the guards, and Phainon feels the fingers on his right arm twitch. “Leave the boy be,” Ptolemy orders, almost on Mydei’s behalf as he still keeps one hand on his shoulder.

Mydei nods sharply, letting some crystals form and turn to dust in his right hand impatiently. Hurry up.

The gesture, combined with his expression, comes across so clearly that it’s not only Phainon correctly deciphering Mydei’s thoughts for once.

The fingers wrapped tightly around Phainon’s arms release him almost at once, and he stumbles forward, then immediately breaks into a run and barrels into Mydei. There is a winded ‘oof’ as they collide, but they keep their balance. Ptolemy’s hand might have something to do with it, shifting to Mydei’s back to support their weight at the impact, and then reaching up to ruffle Phainon’s hair.

Mydei recovers quickly, taking hold of Phainon’s arm with both hands and staring the guards down like he is trying to show people that no one is allowed to take Phainon away.

“Nice speech,” Phainon quips, grinning up at the teen. “A bit long, but I liked it.”

Ptolemy clicks his tongue, raising his head haughtily. “Keep your mouth shut,” he says, but his eyes drift off to the side nervously, fingers finding the laurels in his hair to fidget with the accessory.

“We will reevaluate how to proceed with the Young Lord,” Archidamia speaks up for the first time since Mydei broke free of her, successfully erasing any traces of giddiness Phainon felt at being allowed back at

Mydei’s side. “But watch your tongue, scholar. I would advise against speaking out of turn in the future.”

“The laws of council bid my tongue be bold,” Ptolemy bites back, getting riled up within seconds at the words.

Archidamia throws him one last stern look before she retreats without another word, deeming the altercation done and over with. It’s... a little underwhelming. Phainon expected more consequences for disobeying her so openly. Perhaps more so on Ptolemy’s behalf, since she didn’t seem to have high hopes for Phainon or Mydei.

“I think there are more pleasant forms of public entertainment than this,” Ptolemy says loudly, staring at something over their heads before he starts directing them away from the crowd.

As they walk through the streets, Phainon hears a faint tune of beautiful music carried by the wind. Mydei looks back once, head tilted and eyes curious. It’s probably his first time hearing music at all.

Ptolemy accompanies them home, staying to make them something warm to drink, and then insists they get ready to sleep despite the Parting Hour having only just begun. He sits at the foot of their bed and talks. He doesn’t try to get them involved in the conversation, even if Phainon jumps in with a question or a remark now and then, and allows them to curl up next to each other until his voice grows hoarse. And even then, he goes to make a drink for himself as well and continues.

Stories from his time in Castrum Kremnos, frustration about some authors or people not taking proper care of the books, recollections of fairy tales, and myths of old. Mydei starts dozing off just as the Curtain-Fall Hour begins. Phainon lasts another half an hour, Mydei’s hand clutching at his shirt even while unconscious as Phainon tangles their legs together. For the first time in almost a year and a half, as Phainon falls asleep, he feels the same warmth he felt when surrounded by his family.

Ptolemy is still in the house when they wake up, and he stays for the next few days as well, sleeping in the unused bedroom.

Throughout all of it, he only talks to them about what happened once.

He says it’s a subject they will have to revisit once they grow a little older, when they are more capable of regulating their emotions and have a better understanding of the consequences. Phainon doesn’t exactly get it, doesn’t really want to understand. He is confident that no matter how much time passes, he will always want to stay right by Mydei’s side.

But for once, someone says that what they are doing right now is alright. That Phainon and Mydei are fine the way they are. That they shouldn’t be unwillingly separated, and they don’t have to worry about it for now.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Hephaestion stares expectantly at them. “How is it?” She asks eagerly. Phainon feels her legs swinging up and down as her foot bumps into the table every single time. He resists the urge to kick her.

They’ve been hanging out every single day for a while now, and Phainon doesn’t know if Ptolemy has had something to do with it, or if Hephaestion heard about their disagreement with Archidamia and decided to stick even closer to them all on her own. He doesn’t mind either way. As annoying as she can be, it’s still fun.

“It’s alright,” he says, drinking. Tastes fine. Sweet, but not overly sweet. It’s a juice.

He turns his head to look at Mydei, sitting on his left, and lifts the glass to his lips. He watches as his friend takes a sip, stops. His eyes widen. Then he takes another sip and glances first at Phainon, then at Hephaestion, in surprise and excitement both. Like he cannot believe something can taste that good.

“Safe to say he loves it, though,” Phainon huffs with a smile, sliding his mostly full glass over to Mydei.

Pomegranate juice, huh.
