chapters.title: Chapter 5: and grow steady
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

“There is a line, Lord Mydeimos,” the healer says calmly. He’s got a voice that speaks of saintly patience and being used to dealing with overly stubborn people. “Don’t come barging in ahead of my patients.”

“Fix." Mydei repeats slowly as if the issue is the physician not understanding him, rather than what appears to be different priorities. It’s fine. Phainon isn’t dying. Probably. He is still bleeding, he thinks. He doesn’t really want to look down and check. “Him.”

“Perdikkas, come on,” Hephaestion whines, hovering somewhere above Phainon’s head, and apparently acquainted with the teen. “You know we aren’t letting you go back to treating someone’s sneezing fit over this.”

Chapter Notes

“Red?” Mydei questions out of nowhere.

Phainon looks up from tying his laces and follows his line of sight, finding one of the kids nursing a fresh cut on the arm. Ah. There are often yelps that signal a new injury and the bandages on limbs right after, but this might be the first time the two of them aren’t too occupied with each other to witness it occurring in real time.

“What’s red?” Hephaestion asks on Phainon’s left, sitting on the grass and fiddling with her sword out of boredom.

They took up three-way fights recently. It’s very fun, probably Phainon’s favorite exercise. Even if Hephaestion has to take some breaks to regulate her breathing or rub her chest while crouching when they go on for too long. She makes up for it with how quick she is on her feet and the fact that

she’s left-handed. It offers some novelty, being forced to defend yourself against someone who wields a weapon in a way unlike everyone else.

Those spars are perhaps second to the one-on-ones with Mydei. All their surroundings appear to fade away during those, making it feel like it’s only Phainon and Mydei left on Amphoreus, taunting one another as they try to add one more win to the tally. Nothing else can quite beat that.

“Blood,” Phainon simply explains.

“Well, duh?” She looks at them like they might be a bit stupid. Phainon rolls his eyes. Has she never seen them bleed before? Phainon is certain they got cuts here and there, but maybe she just never paid attention to them.

Mydei pins Phainon with a look, moves his eyes downward, then tilts his chin.

“Yes, it’s just us around here,” he confirms for him, sweeping his eyes around. As far as he knows, at least. “Everyone else has red blood.”

Hephaestion blinks at them owlishly, her sword stilled. “Do you… not?”

Phainon hums and reaches toward the blade, swiping his fingertip along the sharp edge purposely. He lifts it up for her to see. Her eyebrows rise as she watches the golden droplets slowly build up in the small cut.

“How? What does that mean? Why isn’t it the right color?” She asks quickly, grabbing Phainon’s wrist to pull it to herself and take a closer look. “Are you sick?”

“You don’t know about the Chrysos Heirs?” Phainon asks, tilting his head by habit.

Hephaestion shakes her head, swiping the blood away with her own fingers to inspect it.

“There’s, um. A prophecy. We are a part of it.” Phainon takes his hand back and wipes it away on his shorts, glad for their dark color that will help hide

the stain. “I don’t know the exact details myself, but I’m sure Ptolemy will explain if we ask. Mydei has never heard the details either.”

Hephaestion nods eagerly at the prospect of finding out more. It’s a good idea to question Ptolemy about it either way; he should have thought of it sooner. The girl shifts slightly, directing her gaze at Mydei. “You’re already cool and all, being the Crown Prince,” she says with a pout, pointing at him accusingly. “What do you need the prophecy for? Leave some coolness for us.”

For the first time, they might be agreeing on something to an extent. Because even if they’re both Chrysos Heirs, Phainon doesn’t have any shiny, cool powers like making crystals out of thin air. It really is unfair. But he is still glad for that prophecy binding them together.

Mydei blinks slowly, and Phainon gets the impression he doesn’t even fully understand what the word prophecy means.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Archidamia and Savvas stand above them, expressions conflicted.

“The children are taught from a very early age what value life holds,” Savvas begins, and Phainon already feels like they are in for a lecture. “Valorous death before glorious return. This is what we live by. We still have time to make you see its worth, but there is a more pressing matter.”

“We understand it’s going to be difficult for you,” Archidamia continues with an uncharacteristically gentle voice. “In war, there are always casualties. The only choice you have is to kill or be killed. The sooner you understand what an honor it is to die at the blade’s mercy, the easier it will be for you to accept it once you inflict it upon the enemy yourself.”

Phainon blinks at them. It’s not what he expected. It’s also not really an issue; he’s known for a year now that he will have to kill to get to his end goal with the moment of Aedes Elysiae’s destruction. It became a real notion about nine months ago, facing a dead body for the first time. However, if they are including him in this discussion, it means they have started viewing him as a more permanent addition to the settlement. Not just a passing friend of Mydei’s. He tries not to get overly excited at the realization.

“You will have to kill people, eventually. It will be hard to overcome, and we expect you to fail at first, but you must adapt quickly. It’s still quite some time until you will have to face this. Believe us, it gets easier af—”

“I killed before,” Mydei interrupts Savvas bluntly.

There is a stunned silence. The two give off the impression that they aren’t sure whether they should believe him. It’s a funny look on Archidamia, Phainon will admit.

“What?”

“A lot of sea monsters,” Mydei clarifies. Savvas exhales sharply as if in relief. “Men.”

Savvas chokes on either his spit or from inhaling air too fast. Phainon doesn’t think there should be any other men than the ones from the forest. He hopes there weren’t, at least. Lots of things can happen in nine years.

“Me too,” Phainon chooses that moment to butt in, watching as Savvas splutters out a cough. “Well, that second guy was more of a team effort, so I don’t know if it counts. But I’ve got one goal, and that is to kill the person responsible for my village’s catastrophe. I know I have to get used to death to achieve it; you don’t have to tell me.”

Archidamia stands completely silent, taking the words in. The two of them regard Phainon and Mydei with shock, trying to gather their thoughts. And, for the first time since they arrived, there are traces of unease in the way they look at them. Like they might be out of their depth.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

“Fix him.”

It sounds like a command. As much of a command as someone at the age of eleven can give.

Before Phainon decided that he could not take this much mortification and covered his face with one hand, he caught a very unimpressed stare from the healer Mydei dumped him in front of, right into the unoccupied bed. He saw at least three other physicians and about five patients when they stormed in. There is probably more milling around. And Phainon can just bet that everyone is watching. All of Kremnoans will be talking about it tomorrow.

Archidamia just might finally decide she’s had enough and exile him. He will be exiled from a land of exiles.

Or maybe not. Mydei would follow him immediately, and she would die of high blood pressure if that were to happen.

“There is a line, Lord Mydeimos,” the healer replies calmly. He’s got a voice that speaks of saintly patience and being used to dealing with overly stubborn people. “Don’t come barging in ahead of my patients.”

“Fix,” Mydei repeats slowly, as if the issue is the physician not understanding him, rather than what appears to be different priorities. It’s fine. Phainon isn’t dying. Probably. He is still bleeding, he thinks. He doesn’t really want to look down and check. “Him.”

“Perdikkas, come on,” Hephaestion whines, hovering somewhere above Phainon’s head, and apparently acquainted with the teen. She helped support his weight as they dragged him all the way here from the training grounds, even if her height hindered the process. Mydei could’ve definitely

carried him on his back without an issue, but she insisted. “You know we aren’t letting you go back to treating someone’s sneezing fit over this.”

Phainon sighs. This is very unnecessary; he can wait for an hour or two. It’s not like the bone is going to knit itself back together in that time span. “It’s fine, I’m—”

“Do your parents know just what exactly you are entangling yourself in, Hephaestion?” The teen asks with an edge to his otherwise overly pleasant voice. “You aren’t being subtle.”

“Subt— I can make my own choices,” she sputters out with a huff, rolling her eyes a bit too forcefully for it to be casual. “I’m ten, it’s old enough.”

The sentiment sounds familiar. Phainon cannot figure out where from, though.

Perdikkas glances at her with doubt but doesn’t comment. Mydei, though, opens his mouth as his patience seemingly wears thin.

The man who still sits awkwardly to the physician’s left beats him to it, letting out a cough that might be due to an illness or discomfort. “You can see to the boy first, Master Perdikkas. I don’t mind.”

“Nonsense,” the teen responds immediately. “Everyone here needs help, and the boy is in a stable state. He can wait just as you can. The warriors I have treated in Castrum Kremnos were forced to wait in much worse conditions. There are only three people left to treat today, all of them easy and quick cases. I cannot prioritize someone simply because the Crown Prince wishes me to.”

“I agree,” Phainon nods, half because he wants out of this mess and half because he thinks he should get on the guy’s good side. “It doesn’t even hurt much anymore.” It does, but he is getting used to it. Slowly. Some tears may have been shed when he felt the bone snap, but it’s manageable now.

“Please,” Mydei still says, voice quieter and more desperate. When Phainon looks over at him, he finds his fists clenched so tightly that his knuckles are

entirely white. He stares unwaveringly at Perdikkas with something like fear lurking underneath. “Help him. Fix him. Phainon is important. Please.”

The fragmented and short sentences make something coil tightly in the pit of Phainon’s stomach. Mydei still doesn’t speak often, but when he does, it’s clear. He always carefully considers his words before saying them out loud, arranging them one by one until they form a coherent sequence. Phainon didn’t realize his accident would affect Mydei enough to lose some of his eloquence.

Perdikkas’ eyes soften significantly, but he stays firm in his stance. “Everyone is important, Lord Mydei,” he points out gently. “I can and will stabilize his leg right now, but you will have to wait until I’m done with this for anything more, such as complex surgery.”

Mydei inhales a bit shakily and bites his lip so harshly that Phainon is surprised blood doesn’t trail down the corner of his mouth immediately. Horrified, Phainon wonders if he is about to cry. Phainon has never seen him do so, and he doesn’t intend to see it today. Not for him.

He pushes himself up into a sitting position, wincing when it jostles his leg.

“I’m alright,” he insists, taking Mydei’s hand to try and pry the fingers open. It works surprisingly easily, so he does the same with the other hand, then drops it and smiles up at him with reassurance. “Seriously. Stop worrying so much, my leg will be back to normal in no time.”

Mydei’s gaze turns incredibly doubtful at Phainon’s declaration. Which, rude.

“Master Perdikkas,” the patient speaks up quietly. “They are just children. I will happily give them my spot for today if that’s the issue.”

“No, you shou—” Perdikkas cuts himself off and at swipes his long dark hair out of his face in frustration. It’s wavy, reaching his shoulders. “Ah, perhaps you are right. This isn’t helping anyone.” He takes time to breathe in and out for about a minute before he faces them again. “I must apologize; old habits die hard.”

Phainon tilts his head silently. It didn’t sound very likely for Perdikkas to change his mind, with the way he was talking before. Blue eyes lock onto his. They are just two shades darker than Phainon’s, funnily enough.

“Am I correct in assuming you regenerate quicker than most?” He asks with sudden professionalism, like a switch flipped. “I don’t believe I’ve ever encountered a Chrysos Heir before—I only read about such things in books. I am aware that the risk of infection is almost as low as zero, however.”

“Not as quickly as Mydei, but I do heal faster than the rest, I think.” It’s been a while since he had an opportunity to compare with anyone else. He has scant few memories of spraining his ankle back in Aedes Elysiae and just walking it off by the third time.

“Say you’ve got a cut,” Perdikkas prods further with a hum. “About the length of a finger, deep enough to bleed and visibly stain your clothes. How long does it take for it to close up entirely?”

What a specific question. Phainon would have an answer if he ever paid any attention to those. But by now, he had stopped feeling the sting of shallow cuts from various blades.

“Three, five hours,” Mydei answers for him without hesitation.

“I got him with a knife the other day,” Hephaestion butts in with a nod. Phainon remembers that. He repaid it with a nice bruise to her ribs. “I didn’t stab him,” she rushes to clarify when Perdikkas sends her a sharp look. “But anyway, there was only a thin line left by the Parting Hour. I mean, look at his scars. There’s barely anything.”

Now that she mentions it—

Phainon lifts his arms and, indeed, thin white lines litter his forearms. If someone didn’t know what to look for, they wouldn’t notice the existence of past injuries. And they aren’t even that old. Huh. He never realized.

“Alright,” Perdikkas hums. His eyes are a little distant, as if he’s making mental notes of everything. “I will brew you something that will knock you

out. Give me five minutes. Trust me, you don’t want to be awake for it when I put your leg back together.” He smiles pleasantly when Phainon’s eyes widen in just a tiny bit of fear. Brew? Wait, didn’t he say surgery? What if he wakes up in the middle of it? Perdikkas spares no thought for Phainon’s internal turmoil and turns to his other patient instead. “Spyros, I should be able to treat you in about three hours. Would that be fine with you?”

“Yes, of course,” the old man nods eagerly, smiling at the teen. “I can come back tomorrow if you would rather rest, Master Perdikkas.”

“Please, don’t worry about me,” Perdikkas says as he squeezes the man’s shoulder as he gets up, heading off deeper into the infirmary.

It’s quiet, except for an occasional cough in the background. Phainon pretends that the patients resting on the beds scattered around aren’t openly staring at the three of them. He just had to get hurt when it’s so busy.

“Thank you,” Mydei breaks the silence, bowing his head at Spyros.

“Oh, it’s nothing, Young Lord. It’s merely a check-up after my surgery. Nothing will change until then,” Spyros reassures him kindly, eyes crinkling. “Master Perdikkas is under a lot of stress, and his past experiences seem to have affected him severely. I hope you can forgive his rudeness.”

“Helping people is important,” Mydei says earnestly, showing he agrees with Perdikkas’ philosophy. To a point. “But Phainon is special.”

Ignoring the way his cheeks burn, Phainon sighs. A prince cannot put his friend in front of everybody else, can he? “We will work on it.”

“But that’s understandable,” the man chuckles, eyes warm and fond. “Speaking of which, I’d better go tell my wife I will be gone until much later, so she doesn’t get worried as well. We all get anxious about the people we care about,” the man gets up from his seat with a cane’s help, smiling widely when Mydei nods in agreement, and then turns to Phainon. “I wish you a fast recovery.”

“Thank you, Mister.” Phainon waves at him in gratitude as he leaves.

Neither of them says a word after that. Hephaestion still hovers but refuses to look in the direction of Phainon’s leg, biting her thumb without realizing. Mydei is the opposite, standing at Phainon’s side with his eyes set firmly on the broken limb. Phainon chooses to stare at the ceiling. They probably paint a very lovely picture.

Perdikkas returns before the silence can turn stifling, stirring a steaming liquid in a white cup. “It has to cool down a little,” he explains at Phainon’s questioning gaze. “So, how did this happen?”

Phainon sees Hephaestion twitch from the corner of his eye. “He—”

“We aren’t talking about it,” he rushes out before much else can be said. He is fortunate enough that only Mydei and Hephaestion witnessed it. He will convince them to keep it quiet somehow if it’s the last thing he does.

Perdikkas’ brows rise in unfiltered amusement. He smirks down at Phainon, not even trying to hide it. “Oh, I think we should,” he says with a laugh. “A compound fracture isn’t easy to acquire, you know? Must have been quite an accident.”

“Can we get to the part where you, like, put that bone back inside of me?” Phainon whines, no longer caring about sounding like a child.

“I will get it out of you sooner or later,” Perdikkas says with a chuckle, but lets it go for the time being. Thank Titans. He pushes the cup into Phainon’s hands and helps him keep it steady. “Drink it, and we can get started if you’re in such a hurry.”

It’s still too hot, enough to make his mouth tingle from the temperature. More importantly, it’s the foulest thing Phainon has ever tasted. But he pushes through with it, only gagging once the cup is empty. He would rather go back to eating that bland meat from the forest for the rest of his life than have to drink anything Perdikkas offers him ever again. Next time, he is taking whatever procedure as is. Will he ever get the taste off his tongue? What did Perdikkas even put—

“Whoa,” Phainon breathes out, his mouth feeling like cotton. The dizziness hits him all at once, and he only barely hears the sound of laughter before he is out cold.

He regains consciousness slowly, mind still hazy. The lights are off, returning the room to the natural state of darkness that the vast majority of Amphoreus is bathed in. Someone snores loudly a few beds over, the sound echoing. Hephaestion is gone, but Mydei unsurprisingly stayed. It immediately puts Phainon at ease.

He sits to the right of Phainon’s bed, his torso slumped over it and one arm carefully draped over Phainon’s thighs, not to disturb the raised limb.

Golden eyes glint at Phainon in the darkness, and Phainon watches in real time as Mydei’s body relaxes instantly, eyelids slipping shut as he exhales deeply. Phainon only manages to reach far enough to tangle a blond strand of hair around his finger before sleep pulls him under again.

In the almost entire month that Phainon’s leg takes to heal entirely, they get to know Perdikkas more closely.

It’s common knowledge that most, if not all, of the residents have been exiled from Castrum Kremnos. Even Hephaestion is an exile on the offense of being her parents’ progeny, aged three when they fled the fortress. The reasons for such harsh treatment vary from person to person. Phainon has learned it’s mostly on the grounds of desertion or directly opposing the King. Or coming back alive from a battle lost, for some reason.

Perdikkas is sixteen, the same as Ptolemy. He arrived at the settlement with one other person only two years ago. He has learned everything he now knows about medicine from his parents. With Castrum Kremnos always shifting from one war to another, the injured regularly flood the infirmaries. If nothing else, it’s the easiest way to gain hands-on experience, Perdikkas once joked. He learned how to bandage any and all wounds by the age of

six. And his tasks only multiplied as time went on. Phainon cannot comprehend how someone so young can already perform a field surgery like it’s nothing difficult.

Phainon doesn’t ask whether his parents are still alive and tending to people back in the Castrum Kremnos. Instead, he and Mydei learn that the exact reason for Perdikkas’ exile was refusal to comply with the King’s orders on who should be tended to first. All for a High Priest who pitched a fit over having to wait in line to have his dislocated shoulder put back in place while people around them bled out to death. On the King’s orders, Perdikkas was dragged away from his patient and forced to treat the non-life-threatening injury, only to come back to the dead body of the person he was previously treating. A lowly soldier, not as important as the High Priest.

When being treated, they discover that Perdikkas favors remedies crafted from strange recipes collected from various cultures rather than proper medicine. It sounds odd. And wrong. But it surprisingly works.

During one of the days that Phainon sulks on the side as Mydei continues on with the training, Perdikkas comes around to check on him during the lunch break. Hephaestion is a little more out of breath than usual, and that’s when they find out about her condition. A chronic illness. Something is wrong with her heart; the name of it is so complicated that Phainon tunes it out after the second syllable, but they are working it out. It’s clear she wants to fight as much as any of her kind, and there’s nothing else as important to her.

Perdikkas, and apparently her parents, don’t share the view. They think she should lead a more peaceful life to prevent any complications. Phainon, for one, is of the mind that she should choose whatever she wants to do with her life and body. They could all be dead tomorrow. Why shouldn’t she be able to do what she loves? But even if he disagrees with her drive for combat, Perdikkas still helps her manage the symptoms as best as he can to allow her to be happy.

When the cast comes off, it turns into a game of how much he can get away with before Perdikkas loses his patience. Phainon doesn’t care; he has to

make up for the time he lost. Mydei seems torn between sitting Phainon down on his ass himself on Perdikkas’ orders or helping him avoid the healer’s attention, having missed his company on the field.

Phainon manages to eventually win him over to aid in the endeavor. At least when Perdikkas finally catches them in the act, it’s the two of them together that have to face the consequences.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

They are waved over to stop on the way to wherever it is Hephaestion is leading them to. A tall woman with a missing arm and massive scars covering the left side of her head smiles at them. Those scars make Phainon a little queasy, especially the way her lip is permanently pulled up to show some of her teeth beneath it.

“Miss Hephaestion,” the woman greets her with a smile. Her hair is braided close to her scalp and pulled up into a bun, with white streaks shooting through the dark brown. The wrinkles on her face make it look like she laughs a lot, lines around her mouth, and smaller ones crinkling her eyes. “Haven’t seen you in a while, dear.”

“Don’t call me Miss,” Hephaestion replies, a bit angrily. Phainon looks at her with confusion at the shift in tone. What’s wrong with ‘miss’? Her eyes are narrowed, and her jaw is clenched tightly, like she’s been offended. “I told you already.”

“Oh, I apologize. My memory isn’t what it used to be,” the lady laughs awkwardly, eyes locking onto Phainon and Mydei with relief, like she found a perfect subject to focus on instead. “I see you made some friends.”

“Yes.” Hephaestion lets out a long breath of resignation, but quickly changes her attitude back to normal when the conversation moves on. “You

must have seen Prince Mydei around by now; everyone knows him. And that’s Phainon. This is Areti, my dad’s friend, and an esteemed warrior.”

And that’s Phainon. He has never heard an introduction more underwhelming.

“Ah, yes. Lord Mydeimos’ companion.” Her eyes twinkle as she says it, lips stretching in a wide smile. “I hear you boys are never apart.”

Before Phainon can try to respond to it, Hephaestion rolls her eyes and huffs. “Literally. I think they even make trips to the bathroom together.”

Mydei doesn’t react to the words. Of course he doesn’t. There is barely any sense of shame in that head of his.

Phainon—

Phainon instantly flushes so strongly that there is no doubt in his mind that he looks like a tomato. The fact that his hair is white and must only highlight it further is not helping. He already knows just how bad the effect is on Ptolemy, but Phainon’s hair is even lighter. He loves his mom dearly and appreciates the one sole thing he got after her, but right now, he deeply wishes he had inherited his dad’s darker shade of hair.

“Oh, my.” Areti covers her mouth with her one hand, but Phainon sees the very unsubtle grin behind it.

“You do?!” Hephaestion reels back in shock, looking from Phainon to Mydei, getting a shrug from the latter. The only reason he doesn’t outright confirm must be Phainon’s very visible discomfort.

Truth be told, it slipped Phainon’s mind that it’s not something you typically do with other people. It’s just that it’s what they did in the forest, and in that small town right outside of it. Then, in the village they passed through. And so, their routine in the Kremnoan settlement developed in the exact same way.

They shower or take a bath together. They brush their teeth, pulling faces at one another in the mirror, laughing and smearing toothpaste around. Phainon enjoys washing Mydei’s hair and combing through it, detangling the strands. The door to the bathroom is never really closed whenever only one of them goes, all sense of privacy abandoned when they were forced into such close proximity for months.

Phainon doesn’t care that it’s not normal. He would rather have Mydei in his field of vision or within hearing range at all times than be normal.

“Titans, you two are so odd,” Hephaestion mutters, but shakes it off quickly, probably refusing to ponder the newly revealed information for long. “We’d better get going. I do not want to find out about anything else.”

The woman clears her throat, her expression delighted. “Where are you heading, sweetie?”

“To Peucesta,” Hephaestion replies with a grin, back to the excitement she was dragging them through the roads with. “I heard he is playing today? It’s the first time Mydei and Phainon are free for it, and I want to show them.”

“Everyone should hear him play at least once,” Areti nods in agreement, and only sparks Phainon’s curiosity further. Is this guy really so good? Phainon has never paid much attention to music. Sure, he likes it well enough, but he thinks there are more interesting things out there. Areti makes a shooing gesture with her hand. “Don’t let me keep you, or you might miss it; it’s almost Parting Hour already. Late happy birthday, Hephaestion!”

“Oh, thank you,” she says with a grateful smile, hugging Areti quickly before she pulls Phainon and Mydei along once more. It’s truly an experience to let Hephaestion take the lead on something. Just a big load of distractions and constant change of direction.

Eventually, they reach what seems to be their destination: a small house that doesn’t appear to be any different from the ones surrounding it, if it weren’t for all the people.

A boy, older than them and with long brown hair coming down his back in waves, sits on the stairs. He pays no mind to the small crowd gathered in front of him, long fingers deftly adjusting what looks to be a lyre. They get a little closer, Hephaestion pulling them to the front with no hesitation.

Kids watch with slightly widened eyes, and older people greet Mydei by his title as they walk by. The boy nods back like he was instructed to when they first came to the settlement. Acknowledge them, don’t pay them any more mind unless approached directly. There are rules even for interactions.

Peucesta, Phainon presumes, strums a few strings and then lowers the lyre, satisfied. He smiles briefly at everyone, gaze raking over the crowd but not lingering. If he notices the Crown Prince, he doesn’t show it. Now that Phainon has a direct view of Peucesta’s face, he can safely say that the teen is beautiful. In a... quiet way. If that makes sense. His hair is plain dark brown, eyes a little slanted and lined with some red color, and a wide golden necklace resting around his neck.

Hephaestion wears light brown in a way that makes it almost sparkling and energetic. In comparison, Peucesta’s deeper shade of brown appears sharp and elegant. Does beauty run in Kremnoan genes?

Uncaring of Phainon’s scrutiny, Peucesta raises the instrument once more and starts playing, his eyes lidded.

Immediately, Phainon feels shivers run down his spine. Goosebumps rise on his forearms, and he manages to look over at Mydei just to see him leaning forward eagerly, mouth slightly agape, and eyes wide open. Titans. What a way to experience music for the first time.

Phainon closes his own eyes and lets himself drift along the soft melody. He can’t describe it well enough. He doesn’t think Ptolemy would have been able to do it. For once, he allows his brain to go blank of any thoughts and simply listens.

Peucesta doesn’t take breaks between songs, simply shifting the tune in a different direction. He plays nonstop for what might be half an hour, or

perhaps two. Phainon almost gets bored during one of the slower moments, but he can still appreciate the beauty of the sound.

Once the performance is over, the silence lingers for maybe a minute as everyone shakes themselves out of the tranquil state the music made them fall into. Then, applause erupts. There are quietly spoken thank-yous, and shaky breathing as Peucesta smiles in gratitude to every kind word, watching people slowly get up and leave one by one in separate directions. Phainon didn’t expect someone so talented artistically to be among the Kremnoans instead of a city-state that could properly appreciate it. But, as he learned from Ptolemy, Castrum Kremnos is also known for its poetry. Maybe it shouldn’t be so surprising.

Hephaestion keeps them sitting until the last person is gone, then runs over to Peucesta and gushes over the music. Peucesta stands up as well, indulging her rambling without speaking a word himself. Mydei and Phainon follow in her footsteps, albeit much slower.

Mydei—

Mydei cannot take his eyes off the teen, truth be told. He looks at him with a star-struck expression, lips slightly parted. Phainon frowns. It was good, but was it that good? Peucesta smiles at them and nods in greeting, and Mydei nods back earnestly. Phainon returns the gesture a bit slower. Whatever. The novelty will probably wear off. It’s like pomegranates—the first reaction was a look of immense wonder, but now he barely reacts as he eats them. He does drink the pomegranate juice first thing in the morning, though. And insists on getting the fruit at every opportunity. Whatever.

Peucesta stares at Phainon for just a moment too long, and Phainon grows a little restless. It feels like the teen is reading him like a book. He is not sure what might be written in that book, but he definitely doesn’t want it to be read by someone else. Yeah.

“Can you play one more for us?” Mydei asks, successfully quieting down Hephaestion and taking Peucesta’s eyes off Phainon.

Peucesta blinks, glances at the light fixtures attached to the buildings that haven’t gone out yet. It means it’s not Curtain-Fall Hour yet.

“Just a little,” he says quietly and raises his lyre again.

Mydei smiles so brightly that Phainon forgets he was feeling slightly off.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Two very familiar voices speak incredibly loudly when Mydei and Phainon arrive. Phainon stops Mydei from entering at the last moment, gesturing to his ear. Mydei looks very unimpressed with him but complies with the request, nonetheless.

“You cannot be serious,” Hephaestion exclaims, almost yelling.

“I’m sorry,” Perdikkas says with a sigh, like he’s been repeating it for a while now.

“You are not. If you were, you would have given it to me now.”

“Hephaestion,” Perdikkas says sharply, his voice rising as well. “I already make you customized blockers from scratch. That’s as far as it can go right now. You are too young for anything else. We have to wait until you’re eleven at least, and that’s still considered way too early. It’s just barely over a year now.”

“Why?” Hephaestion asks, still angry and hurt. “I won’t change my mind, it doesn’t matter.”

“You still need to grow. Even if I gave it to you, it wouldn’t change anything yet. Look at other kids your age.”

There is a silence that rings louder than any of their voices so far. It’s a little awkward. They should probably come back later. It’s not like they had a

specific appointment or anything. He turns to Mydei and starts gesturing. His hands still at the next words.

“You are just like everyone else,” Hephaestion says quietly, words punctuated by a sniffle.

Oh.

They are very out of their depth here. Definitely shouldn’t have heard any of this.

A chair screeches loudly as it’s being pushed back, and Hephaestion marches out of the open arch that connects the corridor to the infirmary, expression stormy and fists balled up. She doesn’t even notice them as she tries to run past. Very unusual. She never wastes an opportunity to attach herself to them.

“Are you okay?” Mydei asks quietly, and they watch as she freezes mid-step.

She backtracks, her hand coming up to scratch against her bottom lip nervously, and some pink blooms across her pale skin. Her eyes are a bit red. “Yeah!” She smiles awkwardly, not even looking at either of them directly. She spins on her heel and sticks her head back through the arch. “Don’t tell them anything,” she hisses, then turns back around and literally runs out.

Phainon and Mydei look at each other after the door of the hallway slams shut behind her.

Mydei blinks. That’s weird, Phainon knows he must think.

Phainon raises his brows and shakes his head a little. Right? And she calls us odd.

Mydei huffs out a breath, turning away to head into the room. Stop it.

Perdikkas sits at his desk, head resting on his hand with his cheek squashed into it. He looks exhausted. A little hopeless.

“Are you okay?” Phainon asks. Is there some widespread thing no one bothered to tell them about? “Is she actually okay? Are we okay? What’s that about?”

“You should be okay,” Perdikkas responds with an eye roll, letting his head fall from his hand and banging it against the desk. “Patient confidentiality, can’t tell you anything.”

They walk closer, and Phainon jumps up to sit on the desk. Perdikkas’ hair appears more like dark blue than black with the lamp shining directly onto it.

“It’s not her heart, is it?” Mydei asks, leaning against the desk slightly behind Phainon.

“No, thank Titans,” Perdikkas says into the hard surface. “I sure hope she tells you before that year is up. I am tired.”

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Mydei’s birthday is… It’s a whole affair.

On his eleventh, Ptolemy spent an entire day pestering Archidamia to spare the young prince from the chaos of it, and succeeded solely because she was too busy to deal with him properly. Well, she agreed only to relieve the young prince from his duty to attend a celebration thrown in his name. But it allowed Mydei, Phainon, Hephaestion, and Ptolemy to sneak out of the settlement into the woods, where Hephaestion found them. They played some games, and Ptolemy helped them identify which berries were edible. It was peaceful. And fun.

This year was more difficult. Perdikkas came to aid in another round of a verbal battle Ptolemy had to soldier through with Archidamia. It apparently took them two days to convince her that throwing a loud and lavish feast is

anything but a good idea, even if she thought twelve was more than old enough for such things. Something about overwhelming Mydei with too much attention and tradition at once. He has never experienced having a birthday at all—as last year they most certainly focused on avoiding the feast rather than properly celebrating—not to mention so many people who would no doubt make it into a big ordeal.

Well, it still happens. Sort of. Not on a large scale, though, and Mydei again simply isn’t involved.

Phainon finds it a little mind-boggling that the Kremnoans almost seem to treat the day with the same reverence as a holiday celebrated in a Titan’s name. Is the Kremnoan royalty on par with the Titans? Maybe their lineage comes from Nikador themselves?

So, it’s important. To put it mildly.

Phainon has no idea what Perdikkas and Ptolemy must have said or promised to pull it off, but eventually, Archidamia agrees not only to leave Mydei out of it this year, but for the next two as well. The first proper celebration will be held on his fifteenth birthday when he comes of age, and his presence will be required no matter what. This allows for more than enough time to let him adjust at his own pace.

Unfortunately, it doesn’t change the fact that throughout the entire day, constant drunken and excited yells come from right outside the window, people passing by, unable to stop themselves from their loud exclamations. Sounds of good-natured fights and laughter. They are happy to have their Crown Prince living among them.

Mydei appears confused, but thankfully doesn’t wish to investigate.

So they decide to spend the entire day at Phainon and Mydei’s house. They sleep in until Ptolemy shows up to wake them up, making a fuss about the date in a mild manner. Perdikkas is soon to follow, with Hephaestion right behind him. Peucesta is the last one to arrive, and he cooks them a meal as Mydei unpacks small presents his friends brought him.

Phainon sits beside him and watches as his friend acquires more personal possessions of his own. Chuckles as he watches him refuse to part with his gifts, just as he had once done with the armguard.

They eat together, accompanied by Peucesta’s soft music once his plate is scraped clean. They talk and play around, and Mydei smiles more than on any other day, and that in turn makes Phainon grin all the time. He wishes they could have this more often than just once a year.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon doesn’t think he can even name all the weapons they test throughout the months that eventually stretch out into a few months past two years.

It’s insignificant to remember, because Phainon chooses to keep it simple and develops a preference for swords. Although he is eyeing the greatswords as well. Everyone says their bodies have yet to handle the weight sufficiently to have a go at that particular weapon, so he might have to wait a bit longer. No matter, he will grow into it soon enough. He shot up by at least ten centimeters since they arrived; it shouldn’t be long now. It’s a bit irritating that Mydei always seems to catch up to him in height eventually.

Hephaestion and Mydei generally prefer an even closer style of combat, the former with daggers as her favorite and the latter with either his bare hands or gauntlets. They have both already chosen their secondary weapons as well. Mydei happens to quite enjoy fighting with a spear, be it throwing it or dancing with it around the opponent. Hephaestion is rather proficient in archery, albeit she always complains about how boring it is to be forced to stand in one place to aim.

The three of them make something of a name for themselves, as much as it’s possible in a settlement of people who eagerly watch over every single

move Mydei makes, which puts the other two under severe scrutiny as well.

Phainon and Mydei caught up to everyone in their group within half a year. They surpassed the skill level adjusted to their age mark, and then the older group’s, in the next five months. Now, they are being pushed to their limits to see just how far their potential can reach. Even Archidamia is pleased with them, as impossible a feat as it seemed to be when they were first taken in by the Kremnoans.

Hephaestion is exactly two steps behind them in everything.

Phainon grows to quietly admire her for it, as much as he likes to gloat about being stronger. To him, it seems like even more of an achievement than what he and Mydei are doing. She is younger than them by a year and a half, and she isn’t a Chrysos Heir. Doesn’t have that genetic boost that allows them to heal more quickly, and, as Perdikkas theorizes, develop muscle memory and learn skills such as these just a little faster. Phainon has long since realized Hephaestion isn’t as fragile as she appears, but she is still undoubtedly chronically ill.

And despite everything, she relentlessly fights to be able to keep up with everything they do, if it’s the last thing she does.

There is a new exercise Archidamia and their current trainer task Phainon and Mydei with.

They are given exactly one objective: fight as long as you physically can. They, of course, take it as a challenge.

Hephaestion, in turn, is tasked by them with keeping a tally of who calls it quits on every attempt they make. No one defines how much time of the nonstop fight is required for the training to be considered completed. Perdikkas weakly protested when he first heard of it, claiming it’s extremely unhealthy. He quickly gave up when no one seemed to care.

They are young, they bounce back up from that exhaustion like it’s nothing.

Now, they can consistently push that fight into three days straight. They may have also started overdoing it a bit when they realized it excuses them from any other lessons. The trainers come and go, but neither of them pays much attention. Hephaestion goads them on now and then, sleeping under the tree and disappearing for food, but Phainon doesn’t rightly know whether she’s currently there or not.

These sessions have a funny effect like that. It’s awful at times, when stomach growls and sinks deeper into itself from hunger, and when pressure in the eyes rises, growing into a piercing headache when sleep deprivation worsens. But the focus narrows down to his opponent. To Mydei, circling him on low feet with gauntlets glinting in the lamplight. He is still more used to fighting in extreme conditions and forces Phainon to tap out more often. But it doesn’t matter when Phainon can stand alongside him through this, to strike him with a sword and watch as Mydei tries to redirect it with his metal-clad forearm.

They are just past twelve now, and Phainon never imagined he would grow this strong so quickly. He daydreamed about it happening, yeah, but in the bouts of self-deprecation and the realistic bucket of cold water spilling over his head, he figured it would take until his late teens to develop his skills to this extent on his own. It was worth it to come here, even if just for this.

Well, that’s half a lie. He also sincerely appreciates everything that has to do with Mydei. He talks. Not as much as Phainon or Hephaestion or Ptolemy, but he can talk. And he understands everything that’s being said to him. Phainon would have exchanged everything for that during their lonely travels.

Ptolemy is still tasked with educating Mydei. And Phainon by proxy. As boring as it is to have to listen to all the smallest details about history, Phainon finds it incredible how good a teacher Ptolemy actually is. He speaks about every subject with passion, shows them his sources, and tries to engage them in every discussion. Never ridicules them for asking stupid questions and doesn’t get overly frustrated when they cannot grasp

something. Although their abysmal math skills almost push him over the edge once or twice. It might be a lost cause.

Mydei’s spear makes a wide arc, and Phainon leans his head back just in time to avoid getting his nose bashed in with the blunt end. “What’s that for?” He yelps, hurriedly parrying another blow with the sword.

“You’re getting distracted,” Mydei clicks his tongue and tries to swipe his legs, but Phainon manages to sidestep the attempt. “I even telegraphed that move.”

“I’m not.” Okay, maybe a little. He barely even noticed when Mydei must have walked Phainon around the field and grabbed the previously discarded weapon. He quickly grasps at any subject to switch the conversation to before Mydei can prod. “We are at three, yeah? Unless I was so distracted that I missed something.”

Mydei scoffs, but his expression tells Phainon that he’s also wondering. “Hephaestion hasn’t called the fourth one yet.” I think, left unsaid. She will tell them after they’re done either way.

“How far do you think we’re gonna push it? Five?” He asks, grunting when Mydei tries to corner him and starts pushing back to regain some of the space. “Surely, we don’t need more than that.”

Phainon grabs the spear right between Mydei’s hands and tugs at it with his left one, making him stumble. Mydei instinctively goes with the motion, dropping the weapon and using the momentum to knock his gauntlet at a perfect angle into Phainon’s wrist, making him drop the sword.

Mydei catches it in the air and twirls it around to grasp it more securely. “I was thinking ten,” he says with furrowed brows, holding the blade defensively in front of his chest.

“Ten?” Phainon sputters out, the strike he makes at Mydei with the spear awkward but in an appropriate stance, at least.

“Not immediately,” Mydei rolls his eyes. Phainon notes the way his chest rises and falls in a deep motion. Overly controlled breathing. He is getting tired, too. He sure doesn’t show it as he tries to kick the spear out of Phainon’s hands, only to have his foot batted away by the very weapon. He rolls on the ground as he loses his balance and springs right back. “There’s that tradition in Castrum Kremnos, about fighting for ten rounds? I thought it would be nice to fight for ten days. Unless you think you can’t handle that.”

Phainon considers it, vaguely recalling Ptolemy saying something of the sort on one of the days dedicated to culture. Those tend to be fun; Phainon always compares whatever they are learning to what he used to do in Aedes Elysiae. Ptolemy and Mydei both listen attentively whenever he mentions his homeland, and it never fails to make something settle in Phainon’s chest. The fact that the knowledge of his village won’t die with him alone.

He looks at his friend, who has never set foot in the place of his birth. Wasn’t raised by people who love him and never experienced the smallest of traditions.

“We can do ten,” he shrugs, committing himself to prolonging this torture until they reach that ten-day mark one day.

They are forced to call it a draw when Mydei’s legs give out from underneath him, and Phainon can no longer hold his sword. Six hours from reaching the fourth day.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Mydei angles his head down to watch as Peucesta’s fingers make quick work of the three strands of his hair, expertly braiding them into a small braid. It suits him a lot. Peucesta is very proficient with anything that has to do with hair, they found out.

Which is just as well because the last time Perdikkas tried to give them haircuts, Phainon ended up with his sides shaved, and he wasn’t very appreciative of the look. Mydei outright refused to let anyone get close to his hair with a pair of scissors each time he witnessed a new monstrosity on Phainon’s head, whether created by Ptolemy, Hephaestion, or Perdikkas. Dametrius tried once. That was the only acceptable haircut Phainon got in this place. Mydei didn’t deem it to be good enough, though.

Peucesta is the only one who passed the difficult test consisting of making Phainon look decent. Phainon thinks Hephaestion specifically didn’t introduce him sooner just so she could periodically watch Phainon walk around with messed-up hair until it grew out again for longer.

Now, his hair is finally back to the state it had been in at Aedes Elysiae. It feels bittersweet, but it’s right.

Mydei’s is cut more or less to his shoulders. It’s more... layered than ever before. Some strands are left to rest over his forehead and frame his face, similarly to Phainon’s. It’s pretty.

“I can show you how to cut your hair,” Peucesta offers quietly, tying the braid with a golden clip.

Phainon considers it, shifting in the armchair on the right to Mydei. “We won’t ever get as good as you.”

“You don’t have to,” Peucesta shrugs, running his fingers through the back of Mydei’s hair, ruffling it up a bit. “I can still cut it any time you want.”

Phainon grins. He missed having friends. He has five of them now, ready to hang out, talk, or help out with anything. It helps bury that hatred, deep-rooted in his heart as it is. During those three months on his own out of the village, he swore to himself he would walk the path alone. No connections or distractions, he was willing to let himself be consumed by loathing, fear, and revenge.

Maybe it was a little foolish of him. He cannot imagine growing without their presence. Hephaestion’s companionship and persistence. Ptolemy’s

sharp intelligence and guidance, and all the advice he has. Perdikkas’ unshakable support, his amusement at everything they do, and his readiness to help in any situation. Peucesta’s soft and quiet presence, eager to provide distraction at any moment, even if it hasn’t been a while since they first met.

Mydei.

The one always at his side, keeping him steady and pushing him forward at every step, whether he knows it or not. The very center of Phainon’s current focus, as his revenge still remains his end goal, but not at the very front of his mind at all times.

“Thank you,” Mydei nods, the braid shifting along with the movement, the clip at its end glinting in the light.

“Of course, Young Lord,” Peucesta hums, smiling softly. Mydei doesn’t frown at the title, for once said fondly.

“You could teach us how to cook, though,” Phainon butts in, kicking his legs in the air. There have been unsuccessful attempts made at it after they grew tired of having their meals delivered every day. It feels like they are burdening people with making two meals for them specifically. “I know only the very basics, and Mydei knows nothing. We would’ve asked others, but anything that comes from Ptolemy is barely edible. And Perdikkas cooks, uh, healthily. But the taste is so horrible that it only makes me paranoid about getting seriously hurt. Don’t wanna get stuck in the infirmary and be forced to endure that torture.”

“You’re picky,” Mydei says with an eye roll.

“Picky?” Phainon repeats incredulously, his back straightening. He did not just say that. “You are the one with messed-up taste buds! You thought unseasoned meat tasted good.”

Mydei raises his chin stubbornly. “It was decent.”

Decent. The blandest food ever made that they were eating in the forest. Decent.

“The only thing that tastes worse is Ptolemy’s food. You cannot be serious.”

“Sure, I can teach you,” Peucesta quickly interrupts their squabbling with a chuckle.

As it turns out, Mydei takes to cooking as quickly as he did to fighting. The smallest amount of missteps, the same drive to perfect whatever challenge he is presented with. Phainon does… alright, but he doesn’t take as much joy from it as Mydei does. He has a feeling Mydei will continue perfecting the craft beyond the average skill level Phainon himself is aiming for.

What he does take joy from is sitting at their table and watching Mydei redo the dishes over and over once Peucesta is gone and then having the plates presented to him. Created with care and tasting just as great.

Phainon practices whenever Peucesta comes over to teach them, but otherwise Mydei takes the lead in preparing their meals. It’s simple things, and Phainon tries to help out sometimes, even. Annoy Mydei a little, more like. It’s worth it to see him freeze, eyebrows scrunching together as he tries not to react to Phainon relentlessly trying to make him slip up on a towel or trip over his foot.

It’s very amusing.

Until Mydei retaliates by messing up Phainon’s food. It’s not very fun then. It doesn’t help that Phainon’s suffering due to a too-spicy soup only brings Mydei just as much amusement.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Archidamia’s house is used to host meetings of the Council.

It’s not a regular Council, they are told. There aren’t that many members either. Ptolemy wastes an entire day’s worth of classes to explain what exactly it means. It consists of only five people, responsible for making the most important decisions, passing judgment, and handling resources. All of that boring stuff. There wasn’t anything like that in Aedes Elysiae, but apparently, all city-states have a version of it.

Beyond the five core members, others are sometimes brought in for specific matters. Five additional people who regularly attend and are held in high regard—they are almost members of it.. Ptolemy is another one, often requested to share his notes on Mydei’s progress. And Phainon’s. He is quick to firmly underline that he never shared anything personal with them, and that he never will.

Phainon doesn’t know what personal details he could even tell someone, but he appreciates it nonetheless.

Phainon should have figured there was a reason Ptolemy talked at such length about it when he dislikes the subject so much. He was probably instructed to teach them about the Council beforehand. Phainon only realizes when Archidamia greets them at the door the very next day, saying their schedule has been altered.

Phainon and Mydei don’t question her. They have learned not to, unless it goes drastically against them. There is no changing Archidamia’s mind once she sets it to something, unless you have a lot of time and strength to devote yourself to it. And she is helping them get stronger in the most efficient ways. It’s better to go along with her.

So, they walk about a step behind her. Phainon knocks his shoulder against Mydei’s, putting his weight on him. He could probably fall asleep while walking if he were given an opportunity to do so. As it is, Mydei jostles him roughly as they apparently step into Archidamia’s house.

Huh.

Phainon was aware it was the one right across theirs, probably the biggest one in the whole settlement. He never expected to see it from the inside, though. Weapons of all kinds litter every surface, and so do papers scattered on the tables and counters. Phainon glimpses them when they pass the kitchen, door left ajar.

They walk silently, Phainon and Mydei quietly taking in all the details of the de facto leader’s home. Until they reach a door leading to another room at the end of the corridor. She stops them in front of it, pushing the door open and standing slightly to the side.

“Ptolemy is an intelligent young man,” Archidamia says neutrally, letting them walk into the room ahead of her. It’s an expansive room with walls covered in papers and maps, a large table right at the center. The six people already present get up from their chairs, saluting Mydei with their right hands to their chests. His friend nods in acknowledgement like he’s been taught to, and they sit back down. “He is on the path to give you an education more advanced than what you would have obtained in ordinary schools. He will fill in any gaps in your knowledge; be it literature, history, geography, mathematics, or culture.”

Six pairs of eyes settle on Phainon over the course of her little speech. Three of them aren’t very welcoming. Phainon gets a feeling they aren’t very pleased to have him attend this. The fourth one appears mostly uncaring. Maybe a little curious. Then, there are Dametrius and Savvas, who are already rather used to his presence.

“But Ptolemy, as extraordinary an individual he is, does not possess the fighting prowess befitting the Kremnoans,” she continues, nudging them toward the two chairs at the head of the table. “He won’t teach you how to devise a strategy, or all the intricacies of true leadership. This is why you are to attend these meetings weekly from now on. We shall fill in those gaps your teacher is unable to cover.”

Mydei takes the chair at the very center, Phainon follows his lead and settles slightly to the right of him. It feels weird.

Where Phainon shuffles and fidgets restlessly, Mydei sits straight with his head held high, regarding the four staring them down with passive disinterest. Right now, he really looks like a young Crown Prince, raised with that in mind since early childhood.

The title’s importance rarely strikes Phainon as it does now.

Maybe it’s because he is with Mydei every waking moment. He has seen him fail alongside Phainon before getting back up, knees and elbows scraped raw and dripping with gold. Heard him unexpectedly giggle at some stupid joke made by Hephaestion. Watched him argue with Perdikkas about the sufficient amount of rest, like a child asking for an additional hour before their bedtime. It’s easy for him to forget. Mydei is Mydei, Phainon’s best friend.

But Mydeimos is the Crown Prince of Castrum Kremnos, with the royal blood flowing through his veins, blending with the golden color of prophecy. Phainon has heard of his mother’s breathtaking beauty in passing and doesn’t doubt it for a second when he gazes at Mydei. He heard of some of his parents’ vast achievements slipping out of people deep in their brews, and thinks of the young boy slaying sea beasts before he could learn to walk.

Queen Gorgo and King Eurypon. They had a natural ability to command their people, garnering respect with one glance, an old soldier told them once when they were waiting for their fighting instructor.

Phainon watches as one by one, the four members of the Council look away from Phainon under Prince Mydeimos’ unblinking scrutiny.

They are the same age, separated by just three months. Yet Mydei might be stepping slightly ahead of Phainon because of his birthright. But that’s alright. He won’t leave Phainon behind, and Phainon will do his best to keep up. To be able to stay right by his side until the very end.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon blindly walks across the room, too exhausted to even keep his eyes open. He could fall asleep standing up, he is sure. Who needs vision? It’s dark anyway. And blind people go around like this their whole lives. Phainon has been living in this very room for years now; he knows the layout by heart. Short years, but that doesn’t change the fact.

“Crap,” he hisses when his foot collides with something painfully.

He doesn’t even know what object it could be. There shouldn’t be anything there. Feels like a closet, though.

Mydei chuckles somewhere to his left, and Phainon adjusts his course in that direction. At this time of the evening, Mydei always sits on the chair near the bed that sometimes functions as a bedside table. Phainon blindly snaps his teeth in his direction as he walks, still refusing to open his eyes.

His shin eventually makes contact with the bed’s surface, and Phainon is just about to throw himself onto the mattress when he hears the main door open loudly. His eyes snap open, although not in much alarm. This place is filled to the brim with well-trained fighters; they aren’t in any danger.

Mydei gets up from his seat, shoving Phainon to make him fall into the bed regardless, as he moves to open the door and stick his head out to check who their visitor is. At such a late hour? It better not be Archidamia with some new messed-up training. They just got out of the fight-as-long-as-your-body-allows, Phainon isn’t moving a muscle for the next twelve hours or so.

Phainon buries himself in the blankets, ready to fall asleep. Mydei can deal with whoever it is. Though he should probably stay awake in case the situation requires him to protest before Mydei manages to agree and rope them into something ridiculous again. With a lot of effort, he cracks one eye open.

A few seconds, and Hephaestion rushes past Mydei, taking one glance at Phainon, and settling on the chair Mydei vacated. She fidgets a bit, her leg

jumping up and down as she looks right at the wall. Doesn’t say anything, which is a bit worrying.

Phainon looks at Mydei through one open eye. Deal with this.

Mydei’s head tilts. Slightly more to the side than it usually does nowadays, the gesture often watered down to a minuscule movement. He must be tired, too.

Phainon rolls his eyes, shifts to quickly look at Hephaestion, then back at Mydei. She likes you better.

Mydei’s answering stare is very unimpressed. He curls his hand into a thumbs-up but moves it up and down twice in a quick motion while looking at Phainon pointedly. You are better at this.

Okay, maybe a little, but—

“I wanted to tell you this for a while,” Hephaestion interrupts their silent conversation, speaking quickly and a little out of breath. She isn’t even making fun of them for not using their words like she always does. Instead, she brings one of her legs up and hugs it closer to her chest, still not looking either of them in the eye. “I don’t want you to think I’m weird.”

‘Can’t this wait?’ Phainon almost asks, feeling very petulant.

Mydei, definitely sensing the words coming, quickly comes over to sit on the bed at his side. “Okay,” he says in an attempt to prompt her.

“We already think you’re weird,” Phainon mumbles through a yawn, flinching out of the sleepy state when Mydei flicks him on the arm that’s pillowed underneath his head. “What? She thinks we are weird, too!”

Phainon feels his head pulsing with a dull ache from sleep deprivation. Maybe this is a ploy to get them to sleep even less. He wouldn’t be surprised. And he doesn’t care. Hephaestion can tell Mydei, and Mydei will relay it to him whenever it is that they wake up. He is going to sleep now.

“Stop it,” Mydei says, grabbing Phainon’s hair and lifting his head up from its very comfortable position it has fallen into by the strands.

“You are so cruel,” Phainon whines, head limp in Mydei’s grip.

“Imnotagirl.” It’s rushed out so quickly that words merge together. Mydei’s hand drops, and Phainon keeps his head up, blinking at Hephaestion in confusion.

It’s not a long sentence. It should be easy to figure out the meaning. But Phainon draws a blank. He really, really tries to muster up enough mental power to piece it together, but whatever he is coming up with doesn’t make sense. He glances at Mydei and finds him just as lost, albeit more alert.

“Huh?” He settles on when the silence goes on for too long, and Hephaestion starts looking like she wants to jump off the roof.

She makes a frustrated noise. “I’m not. A girl.”

Right. That clears up pretty much nothing. Phainon rubs his eyes roughly to try to force them to stay open.

“You are... not?”

“No,” Hephaestion replies quickly and sharply, not leaving any room to question it further.

He doesn’t really understand. Has Phainon missed something? Wouldn’t someone correct him, or Mydei, by now? No, everyone referred to her as such until now. Is it a recent development? A medical thing? What is she then?

“I don’t understand,” Mydei says exactly what Phainon is thinking, sounding extremely hesitant.

“I hate my body and everything else that comes with this. I know that Kremnoans don’t really... divide by gender much, and that it’s much worse in other regions, but it’s— even the few and subtle ways where it exists just make me so miserable,” she rambles, face completely red from either

embarrassment or frustration. “Don’t get me started on when they try to pull me aside with the girls and explain womanhood to me. I don’t want to hear it. I don’t want that future. It makes me want to cry. And that’s even worse, because crying is girly and I’m not, and—”

Mydei’s expression almost makes Phainon snort from the sheer bewilderment written all over it. He still doesn’t fully grasp the made-up society rules. Phainon doesn’t entirely get all of them either, truth be told, but at least he isn’t hearing of them for the first time.

He is a little confused about why crying would be girly, though. It’s childish, that he can agree on. But Hephaestion is one year younger than them. She is a child, she can cry all she wants. Phainon still sometimes cries. But only sometimes.

“So, how does this work?” Phainon cuts Hephaestion off to both save her from spiraling and Mydei from coming up with a response. What she’s saying, it shouldn’t be a problem, right? “Is there something to... make you not a girl?”

Hephaestion’s eyes lose some of the blankness as she focuses on the two of them again. “Perdikkas has been giving me some blockers to stop... the changes. He said he would give me, uh, hormones in a few months since I’m nearly eleven. So, I wanted to tell you,” she sends them a very thin smile that doesn’t reach her eyes. “I should be able to grow up like a boy alongside the rest of you. But, by Nikador’s lance, it’s so awkward telling people. Not to mention you guys.”

Alright, so she’s a boy. He’s a boy? Hephaestion is a boy.

The dull ache turns into something a bit more piercing, and Phainon tries to breathe through it. He doesn’t know if it’s really the lack of sleep or the utter confusion he is experiencing. Maybe both of them combined.

“Shouldn’t it be easier with us?” He still asks, trying not to be offended. He yawns into his arms again. “We are friends.”

“Yeah, but you are important,” Hephaestion responds, the ‘duh’ evident in the tone. “And I have to deal with you every single day, unlike the rest. It would be, uh, difficult if you didn’t take it well.”

“Who do you think we are?” Phainon mutters and stifles another yawn. Titans. His jaw will pop from all the yawning if they don’t get it over with soon.

“So, you’re a boy?” Mydei asks for confirmation, finally rounding it up. It does sound awkward.

“Yes.”

“Okay,” is Mydei’s easy and unwavering answer. Like that’s all he needed to hear.

Hephaestion stays silent for a moment, and Phainon is too exhausted to take a look at her expression. “That’s it?” She questions with hesitation.

“Is it wrong?” And here Phainon can very easily imagine Mydei’s tilted head. “Should there be something more?”

“No, it’s— Okay, yeah,” Hephaestion backtracks.

Nice. Great. So that’s all cleared up.

“Hephaestion. Do we still call you Hephaestion?” Phainon shifts his head to the side to be able to speak without the words being muffled. “Either way, we love you. We don’t care what you are or aren’t. It’s still you. I think. But can we please talk about it some more tomorrow? I swear I’m trying to think about this, but I’m literally five seconds away from passing out.”

“Yeah, uh. That works. And Hephaestion is still fine, I’m keeping the name.”

Phainon nods, not opening his eyes. She sounds relieved, though still a bit nervous.

“Do you want to stay with us for the night?” Mydei asks graciously, roughly shoving Phainon away from the edge of the bed. Now Phainon does open his eyes to glare at him weakly. “We can talk in the morning.”

“Uh. Stay with you?” Hephaestion’s eyes jump to the bed, and Phainon raises an eyebrow tiredly, turning onto his back. What’s she looking at him for?

“Yeah,” Mydei nods, moving up the bed to take his place. “We keep the spare bedroom ready because Ptolemy or Peucesta sometimes stay over.”

“Oh! Oh.” She flinches away, some pink coming back to color her cheeks. She shakes her head quickly and stands up. “It’s fine. I have to get back, anyway. Um, thank you.”

“We will talk more about this next time,” Phainon reminds, waving his hand in the air.

Mydei turns off the lamp that sits on the windowsill as Hephaestion walks out with a rushed ‘bye,’ and then finally lies down next to Phainon. The heat immediately makes him even drowsier. They stay silent as Hephaestion walks through the house, the main door creaking as she exits through it.

“I should stop thinking of Hephaestion as ‘her,’ shouldn’t I?” Phainon groans, shifting to his side so he can face Mydei. Now that he’s also in bed, he appears as exhausted as Phainon feels. Which is a lot.

Switching to calling Hephaestion by ‘he’ sounds rather easy in theory, but Phainon can already tell it won’t be so effortless. How do you suddenly switch the way you refer to someone for years? It’s not that he doesn’t want to; it’s just— can he do that?

“Maybe we should go to Perdikkas tomorrow,” Mydei says, yawning widely right in Phainon’s face.

The small fangs peek at Phainon, and he cannot stop the yawn escaping from him in response. “Day after. We stay in tomorrow.”

Mydei shakes his head slightly, eyes slipping shut. “We have two hours with Ptolemy in the evening either way.” He shuffles a little closer, arm snaking around Phainon’s waist and fingers hooking into Phainon’s sleeping shirt. “Geography.”

“Ugh.”
