chapters.title: Chapter 10: and sink into the ordinary
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"Happy birthday," Mydei whispers as Phainon stares at him with bleary eyes, sleep still clinging to his consciousness.

The light from the lamps streams through the window as it always does, but its intensity suggests they're past the Entry Hour already. They usually get up in the very first minutes of it. And yet they remain in bed, Mydei lying on his side and watching Phainon with amusement instead of forcing him out of bed within seconds of waking him up. Phainon hums, shifting to get closer and bask in the ever-present heat radiating off Mydei.

"If we can sleep in until the Action Hour ends, then it will be a happy birthday," he mumbles into the warm skin of Mydei's shoulder, the red lines almost lined up with his lips.

Chapter Notes

“Ptolemy got a girlfriend,” Hephaestion chitters with a teasing grin as his skin is being disinfected. He shifts on the chair, causing his pants to ride down a little.

Perdikkas opens his mouth to reprimand him, but instead freezes. “A girlfriend, you say?” He asks, glancing up and over Hephaestion’s head to raise an eyebrow at Ptolemy. The scholar groans loudly and pushes the book back into its spot on the shelf, slumping forward dramatically. “And stop moving.”

Phainon and Mydei watch the exchange from where they’re sitting on one of the desks, their ankles hooked together. Phainon swings their feet up and down. Hephaestion reaches down to keep the fabric in place, half of his butt on display. It’s not a big deal, they’ve seen each other half-naked before.

“I do not have a girlfriend,” Ptolemy stresses as he walks over and leans against the back of a nearby chair with his hip, arms crossed. “Nor would she ever be my girlfriend.”

Hephaestion’s leg twitches a bit when the needle goes in, though he doesn’t wince. Phainon has been told that while the injections are mostly painless, the muscle can ache somewhat afterward since the medicine is dense. Perdikkas explained it way back when they first watched him administer a shot to Hephaestion. Ptolemy also knows how to do them. Phainon wonders if he and Mydei should also request to be taught just in case. Who’s gonna do them if they’re deployed without any of their friends, and it lines up with an injection?

“Also, can we not mention this to Leonnius?” Hephaestion asks, eyes darting to the infirmary’s door as if the teen were to come in at any moment. It’s been two days, and both he and Peucesta are holed up somewhere to presumably catch up, with no hope of resurfacing anytime soon. They will have to track them down soon for some tests Archidamia will want to run, though.

“Ptolemy’s girlfriend?” Mydei asks with a confused head tilt.

“Not a girlfriend,” Ptolemy mutters.

“No,” Hephaestion rolls his eyes, twisting his head around to look at them. “Like, me not being officially a guy in the past.”

Now it’s Phainon’s turn to ask, “Why would we tell him that in the first place?”

“I don’t know,” Hephaestion shrugs as Perdikkas removes the needle and presses a piece of gauze and medical tape over the spot. “You could be telling him a story or something. Just don’t slip up. I want him to view me fully as a guy.”

But aren’t you one? Phainon wants to ask, but feels too out of his depth to do so.

“Sure,” he agrees easily instead. He isn’t certain what kind of story he would have to be telling for such a detail to come up in the first place. Mydei gives a firm nod alongside him, and Ptolemy hums affirmatively.

“Great,” Hephaestion beams at them, pulling his pants fully up, and then twists around to stare at Perdikkas, who busies himself with discarding the medical equipment. “Do you have a girlfriend?”

Oh, so that subject hasn’t been dropped yet.

Perdikkas only snorts, shaking his head. “No.”

“But you’re the same age as Ptolemy,” Hephaestion pushes on, switching to sit more comfortably now that the procedure is over. “Which means old. Don’t you want one?”

“We’re only eighteen. Well, I’m nearly nineteen,” Perdikkas simply states. “I don’t really care to have one.”

“Are you ace?” Ptolemy asks bluntly, index finger tapping along his own bicep.

“Ace?” Hephaestion repeats after him.

“No physical attraction. Or romantic. Or both.” Ptolemy explains quickly, frowning at himself. “Or was it a different term? I will admit I haven’t put much of my focus on the matter over the years.”

They had a brief conversation about sexuality not that long ago. Ptolemy sat them down along with Hephaestion and explained it’s perfectly alright to feel attracted to someone regardless of their gender. Phainon never really gave it much thought, not in the context of girls or boys. He’s still not entirely sure about his preferences just yet, though he supposes he might be leaning toward the latter. Then again, maybe it’s because his only friends are guys. Not to mention ones like Mydei, Hephaestion, and Peucesta. They are all just too pretty; it’s not a matter of being into guys or not. Anyone can see that.

“And you won’t have to since I’m not ace. Or any other variation,” Perdikkas waves him off and turns to face everyone with nothing left to do. “I just don’t have the time. Haven’t felt enough of a connection with someone to even consider a relationship either.”

“Sounds like you might be ace,” Ptolemy says in a light tone, more teasing than actually trying to prove a point.

“I’m not about to share details of all my sexual and romantic preferences nor fantasies right this very moment just to prove you wrong,” Perdikkas says flatly, rolling his eyes.

Hephaestion seems to be one second away from asking ‘why not?’, but thankfully, he doesn’t manage to in time.

Ptolemy beats him to it as he exhales loudly, like it’s the worst news he’s heard this entire week. “Already breaking my heart like that?”

Perdikkas rolls his eyes. “Don’t you have a girlfriend?”

Mydei huffs at Phainon’s side, mildly amused by the fact that the conversation rounded back to Sevasti and her not-relationship with Ptolemy yet again. And definitely finding humor in the way Ptolemy’s face turns red in frustration over the subject at an impressive speed.

“For the last time, I do not!”

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

When they arrive at the first weekly meeting since their return to the settlement, Archidamia’s eyes immediately find the blue gems resting against Mydei’s chest. He wears it in the exact same way his mother had, the large necklace hanging wide on his shoulders and nearly slipping off. Perdikkas expects both of them to grow much taller and gain more muscle

in the coming years. The necklace should sit more comfortably by then, as Mydei’s build goes past his mother’s.

Phainon cannot help but grin widely, strutting up to the table and taking his usual seat as if nothing is out of the ordinary. Mydei follows, entirely uncaring, even as Archidamia closes her eyes and breathes in deeply to center herself. She is more composed as she blinks at them again, face unreadable.

“Are those Queen Gorgo’s jewels?” A man asks in disbelief, and whispers from the attending members grow louder.

Dametrius takes a step closer, and Phainon can tell he will visit in the middle of their classes with Ptolemy one of these days to study the famed jewelry up close. Savvas looks considerably proud at the revelation of their spoils.

“Taken from the fortress along with numerous books and one incredibly competent runner who already proved himself once,” Phainon says, resting his elbows on the table’s surface. “Do you still think we aren’t ready for more demanding expeditions?”

The eyes of people he clashes with so often regard him with reluctant respect. It’s more satisfying than it should be. They don’t need to know how easy it was to extract the jewelry.

“You’ve done well. These suit you, Young Lord,” Archidamia says eventually, tone kept deliberately even but no less genuine. Mydei nods in both acknowledgement and appreciation of the compliment. And that’s the end of the subject, as Archidamia deems it fit to move onward. “I wish to see this young man you speak of within a week. If not, he can begin making his way back to Castrum Kremnos.”

“He is currently resting and adjusting to the settlement, but rest assured, we will have him ready within a few days,” Mydei says smoothly. It’s not really a lie; it’s just that they’ve seen him exactly once since they arrived. The assumption among their friends is that he’s holed up at Peucesta’s. Mydei doesn’t let anyone dwell on the matter for long, straightening up just

to address another result of their trip. “You might be aware of it by now with the rumors circulating, but Hephaestion won a tournament in Castrum Kremnos. You will find there is no reason to hold him back anymore.”

People begin whispering again, reminding each other who Hephaestion is and whether he was supposed to be there in the first place or not.

Archidamia doesn’t look one bit surprised, and Phainon suspects she has known since the beginning. She should, actually, given how she makes it a point to be aware of everything that goes on in the settlement. But, even more so, there’s an uptick to her lips that suggests she might be satisfied with this outcome. Perhaps she’s been looking for an excuse to send Hephaestion out as well. “Very well, Lord Mydeimos.”

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Archidamia isn’t overly satisfied with Leonnius upon their first meeting.

By her request, they eventually drag him over to a spot designated by her, and the six of them stand right behind him in silent support. Out of all of them, Perdikkas is the one with the least personal impression of Leonnius, save for all that the rest of them told him. They only barely got past the introductions on the first day, and then Leonnius disappeared with Peucesta. Their physician still wanted to come and see, though.

Phainon understands why, after about five minutes of waiting, when Archidamia approaches them and Leonnius pales to such an extent that Phainon is almost certain his own hair would blend in seamlessly with the current color of Leonnius’ skin. But the green hair doesn’t do the teen any favors either; the contrast only serves to make him appear sick. Or maybe it’s the way he almost trembles when she gives him a severe once-over, gaze as harsh and intense as ever.

Half a minute in, and all of them are just waiting for him to faint. Perdikkas seems resigned, as if he’s already dedicated a bed in the infirmary for Leonnius. Archidamia, meanwhile, must have already lost some of the respect because of his inability to look her in the eye alone.

And then the questions start.

Leonnius isn’t particularly versed in any form of combat, be it hand-to-hand or with a weapon of choice. Phainon’s brows rise in surprise at the fact that he’s got no favored weapon to speak of. Small kids who run around the settlement are already aiming toward something. Usually gauntlets, for whatever reason. But that’s fine; they can always change their minds to a more refined blade along the way. And even Phainon, with none of the Kremnoan blood which compels its people to almost an obsession with all sorts of combat, would feel as though he lost a limb if he didn’t have a sword at his disposal out on the battlefield. It’s as if Leonnius stopped his training at the basics. That’s something Phainon would have perhaps expected from Perdikkas, whose entire life revolved around medicine instead.

She asks more, and the words are pulled out of Leonnius so easily that one might think he is under a spell of sorts. It might be fear. He confirms that he panics easily, the fight-or-flight response permanently set to the ‘flight’ option. Not a single battle that he participated in, and consequently not a single life taken with his own hands. No particular attachment to the cause, be it slaying the King or gaining glory.

Phainon glances at the rest of his friends to gauge their reactions. Ptolemy has one hand resting against his face, his foot digging restlessly into the ground. Hephaestion looks perplexed, like he’s only just now realized how bad it all sounds, despite already being aware of most of those things.

Mydei is carefully blank, but it isn’t the expression that’s slowly being perfected not to betray any of his thoughts in diplomatic matters. It’s Mydei who isn’t exactly sure what to think of it. Phainon knows he would like to have Leonnius running for him, especially after how he handled the potentially dangerous situation of unknown people realizing his identity. Followed an order without a second of hesitation. Mydei likes the teen. But

Mydei also happens to have a pragmatic approach to things that are crucial in battle. He leans toward remaining realistic rather than optimistically supportive.

Phainon, in turn, is hopeful. He knows what it’s like to be an outsider placed under Archidamia’s scrutiny and feeling like the most inadequate person to ever exist. Leonnius is fun, and he thinks he will be nothing short of reliable when the time comes. Phainon wants to get to know him better and see if he might be the key to Peucesta’s silence. He cannot help but root for the boy who seems willing to fight against the odds constantly stacked against him.

But he can’t stop the wince from forming on his face as Archidamia nearly sneers at Leonnius, telling him he’d better pray to Janus for a blessing of speed because if he doesn’t impress her, he will be sent right back to Castrum Kremnos with a bow tied around his wrists. He wonders if she might be even harsher on Leonnius than she used to be on him. Or maybe Phainon just grew used to her.

She orders him to run four laps around the field right outside the settlement’s perimeter as quickly as he can. If she walks across the field and back before he’s done, there is no reason for him to remain in the settlement at all. Phainon thinks that’s ridiculous, and by Mydei’s frown, he can guess Leonnius will be granted entry by the Prince’s order even if he fails. Peucesta, who has stood steady and hasn’t wavered since the very first step Archidamia took in their direction, gains a sharper smile. His posture loosens further, as if he is already privy to the outcome.

Leonnius nods rapidly at her order, almost tripping over his feet in his haste to comply. He takes off without a word, and Archidamia begins her walk. It’s a decently sized field. It resembles ones they’d grow crops in back at Aedes Elysiae. Phainon always hated walking around with a sickle during the harvest, the ground seemingly never-ending.

They all watch and relax one by one as it becomes increasingly obvious that Leonnius is going to succeed. It doesn’t matter that Archidamia is walking at a deliberately unhurried pace. She is consistent with it, making it clear that the end result will be genuine.

Leonnius skids to a stop in front of them when she’s about halfway back, grinning from ear to ear, his breathing only slightly faster than usual. He jumps up and down a little as they cheer for his victory. Ptolemy is the only one who remains skeptical, watching with narrow eyes as Archidamia calmly returns to her previous spot, expression unreadable.

“Perhaps you aren’t as incompetent as you appear to be at first glance,” she comments ruthlessly. A humorless smile quirks up the corners of her lips, and Leonnius flinches, bumping into Peucesta, who stands right at his side. “Don’t think you are done just yet. You gained the right to stay, but this will determine whether you qualify for the duties that will be expected of you as a runner directly under Lord Mydeimos.”

Leonnius’ throat bobs as he forcibly swallows, Peucesta’s hand resting between his shoulder blades out of Archidamia’s sight. “If whatever you have planned has to do with running, I’ve got nothing to worry about.”

“Found some courage, after all?” The smile gains some sharpness and actual amusement this time around. “Let us hope it’s not baseless. Your objective is simple. Run.” She gestures back to the field with a wide swipe of her hand. “Out here, in any pattern you wish, be it back and forth, a circle, anything. But you cannot rest. You may only stop to relieve yourself and eat at a fast pace. Provisions will be provided three times a day, should you last long enough.”

Leonnius blinks at her for a moment, turning the words over, before he breathes in deeply as if to steady himself. “So, simply no sleep?”

Perdikkas makes a sound of protest. “I don’t think—”

Archidamia gives a single nod as if she cannot hear the physician at all. “Or standing still for longer than three minutes. You should know better than to abuse the rules as well.”

“Okay. Okay, I can do this. I will prove you wrong,” Leonnius says quietly, almost to himself. “I will prove them wrong.”

“Less talking, more running. You are starting now.” She rolls her eyes when Leonnius looks up at her, startled. “You think you will be well-rested when an order to deliver a time-sensitive message comes? Get going, child,” she barks at him.

Leonnius stumbles forward and kicks off into a run at a steady pace, no longer a sprint. It’s slower than what Phainon may have expected, but by now, he knows that if you don’t save your stamina, you will burn through it too quickly.

What’s more surprising is that he’s been assigned a task so similar to what Phainon and Mydei attempt now and then. He never thought anyone else would be subjected to something so grueling, but Archidamia is known for pushing everyone past their limits.

Still, though.

“He can do all that, but we’ve been fighting for days while starved half to death?” Phainon asks casually, trying to mask the bitterness.

He doesn’t manage well enough, as Archidamia raises an unimpressed eyebrow at him. “He can afford to take a single minute when he is running,” she says. “There is no enemy to strike him down at a single moment of distraction, unlike when you are facing countless opponents at all times.”

“So unfair,” Phainon mutters under his breath. Mydei’s lips thin just slightly, meaning he might somewhat agree even if he won’t say it. “And how come we cannot retreat for a single moment like the rest of the soldiers?”

Archidamia huffs and turns away from him, deeming her job to be done. “You are not like the rest of the soldiers,” she throws over her shoulder.

“Must she always do this?” Perdikkas agonizes, eyes following Leonnius’ figure numbly as he passes by them and waves cheerfully.

“Do you think he will last long enough to appease her?” Ptolemy asks Peucesta, also ignoring Perdikkas. Phainon pats their resident healer on the

arm consolingly. Half of their group is at a constant risk of getting seriously injured. Now, there might be one more.

Peucesta allows for a small and incredibly soft smile. “Beyond that.”

One day was everyone’s estimation by far.

They are currently on the third, with five people present as Leonnius proves his worth ten times over. Hephaestion couldn’t miss more of his training, and Ptolemy had other duties to attend to. Which leaves Phainon, Mydei, Archidamia, and a very exhausted Perdikkas. Along with Peucesta, who remained at the field at all times, sleeping on the cold ground as his friend continued on with his task.

Three days for a regular human is a bit staggering. The only reason Phainon isn’t drowning in the bitter taste of shame over his and Mydei’s slow progress is the fact that they’re at almost eight days already. Just two and a half more, and they will reach their goal. They’re going beyond mortal standards and pushing their limits to the brink. And Leonnius has access to those luxuries that they don’t, forced to engage in a very strenuous activity without any way to replenish their energy. Not to mention that they have to put force into their strikes, defend themselves, and actively think of a strategy to make the other one take a hit. So, it’s not so surprising that Leonnius can last this long.

Or at least that’s what Phainon is telling himself, shoving the irritation at his own skills perhaps not being good enough to the very back of his brain and instead clinging to the excitement he feels for the teen to succeed.

He thinks even Peucesta might be mildly impressed with how long it’s been. In direct contrast to the quiet astonishment of everyone else aware of the situation. Which might as well be the entire settlement by now. The only reason the soldiers aren’t swarming the ground surrounding the field is that Archidamia forbade them from doing so, as it might influence the outcome.

In the end, his pace slows to what resembles a determined walk, taking shaky steps one after another with a terrifying amount of perseverance. But that isn’t enough to fuel your body when it decides it has had enough of the torture you’re putting it through. Peucesta, as he decided to accompany Leonnius ever since he started flagging, catches him easily as his body drops without warning.

Archidamia watches with grudging respect. What Leonnius may have lost with his insecurity and anxiety, he made up for with sheer skill and endurance. Archidamia may be many things, but unfair isn’t one of them.

“You are permitted to participate in a battle to push back the black tide’s infestation in two weeks,” she announces to her audience of three, Peucesta and Leonnius still too far out of earshot to hear. “After your new friend goes through a thorough debriefing, which will allow him to accompany you.”

“Which will occur after a thorough rest,” Perdikkas interjects sharply and leaves to take a look at his patient.

Phainon watches as Mydei openly grins at him, and Phainon nearly vibrates with excitement. They did it. They found a suitable runner and can move forward at a pace he is satisfied with. The deadline Archidamia gave them for their new expedition will be one week before Phainon’s fourteenth birthday, even. Phainon can breathe a little more easily.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Mydei reels back a little bit, head swirling around to face Phainon with slightly widened eyes. Have I said something wrong?

Their attention is pulled away when Perdikkas puts a cap on his pen, pushing himself away from the desk with a tired sigh. He looks at Mydei. “You wanted to have your ear pierced, didn’t you?”

Immediately, Mydei slides off the empty bed he and Phainon sat on and almost runs over to their physician in his haste, having inquired about it already three days ago. Phainon and Hephaestion follow after him, curious about the whole ordeal.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

settlement. He closes his eyes, aware that his bare skin will take the brunt of the blow before he can move and disarm whoever is attacking with the other hand.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Their first battle against the black tide is certainly more difficult than fighting against fragile humans.

word among the squad of fifteen. There are many dead people, their corpses mingling with those of the enemies, discarded on the sides of the roads.

As tricky as it is with how he has to avoid being injured at any cost, at least they aren’t people. He doesn’t have to worry about cutting someone’s life short, doesn’t have to watch the frightened look in their eyes.

Phainon catches sight of Leonnius now and then, slipping in and out of his peripheral vision as he tries to be within hearing range in case something happens. He takes on the task of helping the injured find their way out of the fighting grounds and directs them back to the camp before gliding among the sharp blades yet again.

Perdikkas, having tagged along just in case and stayed behind in safety, gives them a thorough check-over when they make their way to it. He releases a relieved breath that only Titans know how long he’s been holding when he finds no injuries.

Not paying enough attention to not clench his jaw so tightly all the time when facing the creatures that plague his nightmares may have been a slight oversight on his part.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

“Happy birthday,” Mydei whispers as Phainon stares at him with bleary eyes, sleep still clinging to his consciousness.

“If we can sleep in until the Action Hour ends, then it will be a happy birthday,” he mumbles into the warm skin of Mydei’s shoulder, the red lines almost lined up with his lips. His body is very treacherous nowadays, and this would be the most inconvenient of days to be dealing with that.

Merchants do pass by the settlement now and then. Sometimes, they even get casual travelers. The settlement’s location is convenient, positioned not that far from Milios and on the way to Odestris. It’s not very common for people to travel directly from one to another, though.

Not to mention that every person who happens to stumble into the area leaves as quickly as they come when they realize the grounds are littered with intimidating militia. It raises suspicion when someone doesn’t, unless they are looking to hire them for protection.

“Do tell, what could have given you the impression that we are any different from other residents?” Mydei asks calmly, raising one eyebrow. He reins in the demanding tone he speaks in to the Council members just so, coming off as more annoyed at the intrusion than expectant of a specific and thorough answer in a very royal manner.

The stranger leans back sharply, as if startled. The uneven gray fringe falls into his eyes, the light color standing out against the black hood pulled up over his head. He laughs awkwardly, looking somewhere over their shoulder as he responds. “Why, of course, I heard rumors of the mighty army that comes to aid those in need! Two dashing individuals such as you two, in particular. Two boys moving as one against the enemies, and it’s not so difficult to guess you are the ones painted as such with the way you carry yourselves.”

Mydei narrows his eyes, not entirely convinced. The man’s grin becomes stilted, and he lets out a strained chuckle, taking a step back.

Phainon only hums agreeably, deciding it might be time to shift the focus if the direct approach isn’t working. He plasters on a friendly smile, now the one to lean forward to take attention of Mydei’s distrust. “And how are you finding the settlement so far? I hope the kids haven’t been giving you much trouble,” he adds in a much louder tone so that the little children still loitering around can hear.

They all protest one over the other, huffing in indignation. How dare Phainon accuse them of misbehaving, truly an unimaginable offense.

“Not in the slightest,” the merchant’s grin returns, albeit softer, and he reaches down to ruffle the hair of one closest to him. “They are a lively bunch. I’m glad to see they aren’t plagued by worries unsuitable to their ages.”

Phainon blinks at him in confusion, taking care to keep his smile on. What would their children be worried about? Sure, they train really hard from a ridiculously young age, but to them, it’s nothing more demanding than playtime. Almost no one ever complains until the training regimen turns into pushing the limits. But they are perfectly taken care of otherwise. Kremnoans are fiercely protective of their own.

Unless you are the queen with her newborn, forsaken by the—

“They seem to have taken a liking to you,” Phainon says brightly, interrupting his own train of thought. “Are you planning to stay for long?”

“Huh?” He looks back at Phainon, momentarily confused. “Oh, no. I’m here just in passing. A friend was worried about, uh, the passage? So she wanted me to travel through. But it all seems fine.”

Phainon looks at Mydei, finding him already staring at Phainon. To say it’s unusual would be an understatement. There is no passage for merchants this way, not unless they are looking for services more capable and cheaper than what the city guard has to offer. Protection on the road as they travel through dangerous terrain, perhaps. It doesn’t seem to be the case this time.

It’s suspicious, but not overly so. The stranger doesn’t appear dangerous, thin and scrawny as he is. Could be a spy for Castrum Kremnos, set out to search for the settlement of exiles. Looking back, it’s rather obvious that its existence must be known, if not the location. Ptolemy’s mother knew, and who’s to say someone higher up doesn’t, either. Perhaps even King Eurypon.

Phainon rubs his thumb up and down against his forehead, tilting his head to the side. Archidamia?

Mydei hums in thought, looking the merchant over critically. The young man looks between the two of them, increasingly nervous.

His friend puts his hand up, fingers spread out to indicate wait. Or later. Same thing. Phainon shrugs, not very concerned. They can stay and talk to the merchant some more to see if he will slip up, and send one of the kids to get Archidamia after a while.

But then Phainon catches sight of Ptolemy over the merchant’s shoulder, heading their way with a focused expression. Oh, well. It’s about to no longer be their problem. Phainon idly wonders if Ptolemy happened to take an interest or if he’s been sent this way by someone else.

“Master Merchant, your ornaments are most curious indeed,” Ptolemy says from behind him, leaning down to examine the pin on the side of his cloak. “This has markings of Dolos. Are you perhaps a descendant of their people?”

The stranger flinches away from him with a yelp like a startled cat. “Who, me?” He asks, the hood nearly falling from the rapid movement. He clears his throat, taking a second before he falls into the grinning and carefree persona yet again. “Oh, you flatter me, sir. You see, I allowed an old fella to barter with me for my goods; one of the things he offered was this very pin right here. Pretty thing, isn’t it? Not much to say about it, I’m afraid.”

Ptolemy hums with a pleasant smile. “On the contrary, your pendant also seems to hail from it.” He reaches up and tugs on the string that slipped out of the merchant’s cloak, and the man deftly snatches it out of Ptolemy’s

grasp, pushing it beneath the layers of clothing with a huff. Ptolemy doesn’t seem deterred, growing slightly more serious within the next breath. “I understand one’s reluctance to share their roots, especially given the reputation pinned to people of Dolos. But fret not, we do not judge around here. In fact, I’d like to request your aid in a matter I happen to currently be researching in relation to that very place.”

“Damned scholars,” the merchant mutters, looking up at the dark sky as if it’s personally responsible for this development. His gaze isn’t as friendly when it lands on Ptolemy again. “Aren’t you too observant for your own good? …What is your paper about?”

Ptolemy brightens up as if he’s already been given explicit agreement to the whole ordeal. “The Three Hundred Rogues of Dolos,” he responds eagerly, “I have meticulously recorded 196 individuals and their fate. I’m missing quite a few, as you can see. I’m wondering whether you may have heard some tales passed down by your ancestors about their lives that could give me a starting point for where to search. Even just a dozen would be helpful.”

“You’re writing about… those scoundrels?” The merchant blinks at him owlishly, taken aback. “Why?”

“I realized there are no papers created to describe their achievements, yet I kept hearing mentions of them in the places I visited over the years,” Ptolemy explains with an air of frustration, like he cannot understand why so many scholars before him would neglect to put importance on such an expansive subject. Even Phainon can recall a few instances of hearing rumors about the faction, most of them with Ptolemy around when he tagged along to his and Mydei’s expeditions. Ptolemy continues with sincerity, “Everyone’s story deserves to be told. Especially people who remain misunderstood long past their deaths, as I’m sure you can understand.”

The merchant stares at Ptolemy as if he may have grown a second head in the time it took him to say all that. Phainon feels a little out of his depth, and he is sure so does Mydei. They heard stories of three members of that faction at best. He has absolutely no clue where Ptolemy could have found

another 193 as it is. It only serves to show how smart and meticulous their friend is. To the point where it might be somewhat scary.

“Damn it,” the merchant mutters, posture slumping in defeat. “Fine.”

“Splendid!” Ptolemy clasps his hands together and then wraps one of them around his victim’s arm, dragging him away before he can change his mind. “I will be sure to compensate you for your efforts.”

“You will?” Phainon still hears the stranger ask, visibly perking up at the prospect of payment. “Why didn’t you start with that?”

“Deliverer,” Mydei calls after a moment of watching the two heading away, kids running after them and attempting to catch the newcomers’ attention for just one more minute.

Phainon shifts to face him, hands resting on his hips. “Hm?”

“Where’s that pin you had attached to your belt?” Mydei asks, pointing low.

Phainon follows his line of sight, baffled when he realizes there indeed is nothing hanging from the belt loop. “Huh?” He raises his hands to check if it isn’t hiding below them for whatever reason. Nope. Shit. “Have I lost it somewhere? No way, it was a relic!”

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 11: and learn to set them apart
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"What's Mydei's favorite color?" Ptolemy asks suddenly, fingers tapping rhythmically against some surface.

"Red," slips out of Phainon's mouth before he can even think. "Gold. Blue."

Because red is the blood on his hands and the color of his crystals. Gold is what all his accessories are, so he's clearly fond of it. And blue, the twinkling gems embedded in his necklace and the single earring, Phainon's eyes, which he once mentioned that he liked.

Chapter Notes

There is that anger rooted deep in Phainon. A place he keeps shoving more and more things into and refuses to reach back down in fear of what it might ignite. He feels so much, and among those things, there is hatred and rage. Toward insignificant things that make him feel powerless. At people who are raising them, Mydei's father, circumstances, his past, and fate. And so the list goes on.

He doesn't touch that fragile space he carved out in himself to hide those two emotions in. It only ever makes that anger and loathing blaze stronger, directed at himself for feeling such things in the first place.

But this time, he doesn't bother squandering those annoying and pointless emotions.

Because Phainon is furious.

The soldiers give him a wide berth as numerous monsters circle around his figure, not allowing him a moment of rest. Perhaps his anger is evident in

the strikes that cut the blackened limbs off as soon as they come into range. Or maybe it's the gritted teeth and, as he's been told at one point, the subtle blue glow in his eyes.

Phainon keeps his stance deliberately loose, ready to shift at the slightest provocation. His sword is caked in the goo that seeps out of the creatures spawned by the black tide. He wipes it off on his dark pants and raises it again within seconds.

Because an unconscious body lies on the ground at his feet, drowning in a puddle of gold. A dead body.

It's not the first time. It won't be the last time. Phainon hates it. Loathes it with his entire being, to the point of it physically hurting and setting his veins on fire. Mydei shouldn't view himself as expendable. Mydei shouldn't throw himself into danger with full awareness of impeding death being the consequence of it. Mydei's death shouldn't be treated like a bargaining chip, used to buy more time or exchanged for someone else's life. Mydei shouldn't die at all.

But he does. And he does so willingly, without a thought spared.

He knows it's not the fault of soldiers who Mydei rushed in to save from certain doom. A few warriors were separated from the rest of their squad and surrounded by the enemies who harness an inhuman strength. It's a death sentence. One which Mydei was glad to take for himself.

Objectively, Phainon understands that one life, which is guaranteed to resurrect, is nothing in comparison to three lives lost forever.

Somehow, it doesn't work to convince his brain that it was a good deal to strike, as much as he values their soldiers. The fact that the gaping wound in Mydei's abdomen has black lines slowly emerging from it outward and climbing up his pale skin doesn't help one bit.

Mydei will wake up. Not immediately with his full health, unlike the other times. Perhaps he will still be in good enough condition to aid them. Phainon might have to carry him to the backline where the medics wait and

treat the injured, Perdikkas among them. Maybe the black tide's power is too strong, and they will find out the extent to which Mydei's body is willing to put up a fight way too soon.

Leonnius keeps appearing in Phainon's peripheral vision, concerned and ready to run for reinforcements. Phainon steadily brushes him off each time. He can manage. He can keep Mydei safe on his own. That's his job.

He runs his sword through the glowing core of one of the creatures, letting his footwork carry him to the side to avoid a strike from another as he swiftly raises his blade again and cuts the head clean off. The body drops with a thud, head rolling further away on the ground as Phainon steps back to guard his friend's body. He's grown stronger again, he thinks, changing the grip on his sword's hilt. Not that long ago, it wouldn't have been this easy to cleave the head off of anything in one fluid movement.

They are all improving at a steady pace.

Even Hephaestion, who is participating in his first serious mission on this very day. Probably on his way back by now. A more difficult battle west of the settlement. And when Phainon and Mydei arrive in the settlement in a day or two, and when they congratulate Hephaestion on this achievement, Phainon will do his best to grin along. Yet underneath, this bitterness might still be simmering, tainting the pride felt toward his friend.

Because, yes, Mydei will be fine. He has to. Phainon knows this. Except this is the first time the black tide has infected the wound this badly. He is uncertain whether he will be able to look in his direction for the next few days without painfully clenching his jaw in an effort to suffocate an unending argument before it can even start.

They had already gone through one of such nature in the recent days, and it only proved that they're both overly stubborn, unwilling to back down. Mydei doesn't understand that dying isn't an acceptable solution to overpowering the enemy. That it's not the same as merely falling asleep and waking up. Not to even mention it's happening right in the middle of a dangerous territory. Who's to say what an enemy might do with his body if

Phainon isn't there? What if he's kidnapped? What if there is more damage done to ensure he doesn't regenerate?

And now Phainon is even more worked up.

He almost snarls as three monsters come at them together, mirroring Mydei's usual behavior, and dispatches them quickly before moving on to the next one.

It takes roughly two hours until Mydei rouses, and Phainon's whole body feels overly hot. His anger must really be showing through, as Mydei doesn't even say a word as he shakily gets to his feet. He heaves, bent in half, until he throws up a mix of gold and black.

Phainon's fury gives way to worry at the sight, just a little. It simmers down into something manageable enough to shove it tightly beneath the lock by the time he half-carries Mydei over to Perdikkas. He forgets almost entirely by the time Mydei's wound regenerates enough to allow him to sweep back in for the second wave of the enemies, somehow even faster and more alert than before.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon swallows a bite, but Mydei's delicious food feels like lead in his throat. His mouth comes out victorious in the battle against his brain, and he blurts out, "What if you don't wake up one day?"

"I am immortal, Deliverer." Mydei doesn't seem to have the same issue with his appetite, gathering more onto his fork without a worry. "I physically cannot die. That's what the word means. Should I tell Ptolemy you require more lessons on vocabulary?"

"No," Phainon says mildly, not finding much humor in the sarcastic response. He changes the strategy, hoping a wounded pride might have a

better effect than logic. "But should I request Archidamia to give you the basic training again? Since you find it so difficult to avoid death and injury, perhaps you're not skilled enough."

"I am only taking risks no one else can, so that the victory is guaranteed," Mydei argues calmly, though his eyebrow twitches.

"Maybe you wouldn't have to if you just waited for me," Phainon says, unable to hide the bitter edge to the words. He pushes his plate to the side angrily. Mydei's eyes follow the motion.

"Maybe your speed is lacking," Mydei shoots back ruthlessly. Phainon knows Mydei doesn't truly mean that. He's just being defensive. It still stings, because it's true. He is never fast enough to stop Mydei from throwing his life away. "No one is getting hurt. What's the issue?"

You are getting hurt, Phainon wants to yell at him. He wishes he could split Mydei's skull open and shove some self-preservation into his brain, make him start caring about his own body and pain. But perhaps Mydei is right, maybe all that's needed is for Phainon to improve his speed. If he were fast enough to yank Mydei back or parry the killing blow, Mydei wouldn't be getting hurt at all. Not to mention dying.

Mydei turned fourteen a week ago, and with every death, Phainon worries each of his birthdays might be his last.

"There isn't one," Phainon mutters, giving up on the argument. He gets up and goes to the bathroom, seething alone in those five minutes before he's forced to head back to Mydei's side when anxiety grows alongside the frustration, which is already combined with anger. A lovely combination. The anxiety doesn't erase the latter two, unfortunately.

Phainon and Mydei don't speak for the rest of the day, existing quietly around one another.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"Do you now understand why I was so insistent on pulling you two apart?" Archidamia asks through gritted teeth, her eyes flashing in what could be considered barely restrained rage. "Have the faintest shreds of comprehension finally reached your foolish, obstinate brains?"

Phainon breathes in slowly, hands clasped tightly behind his back, and posture rigid as he stares straight ahead. Not even at Archidamia herself. Mydei stands almost like a mirror image of him, head held high despite the dressing down they're getting. Like good little soldiers that they are.

Except they aren't.

Phainon exhales, and it comes out a little shaky. For once in so many years, he cannot even begin to argue with Archidamia against the harsh words thrown their way.

"We will accept any punishment," Mydei says in an even voice.

"Yes," Phainon echoes numbly. He feels sick to his stomach.

"Although I'd request you to be lenient on Phainon, Lady Archidamia," Mydei continues, and Phainon flinches out of the daze. "He isn't the one who abandoned his post and left soldiers for death."

"What?" Phainon hisses furiously, dropping the stance to face Mydei. His friend doesn't react, jaw clenched tightly. "You're kidding. I'm the one who got turned around and left my position first, and my squad followed. If you think you—"

"You want punishment?" Archidamia interrupts him loudly, banging her hand against the table. Phainon does flinch. Her gaze is so harsh and her expression so furious that Phainon has to close his eyes for a moment. He loathes disappointing people. "Why? So that you can feel as though you have atoned for this? The only regulation for such misstep is the ability for another person to challenge you to gladiator combat as a way of questioning your station."

Phainon swallows the lump in his throat. He wouldn't be surprised if someone took that opportunity after what happened today. He's been largely accepted by the Kremnoans, though it's no secret he remains just behind the invisible line separating him from everyone. Not everybody is content with an outsider residing at a station this high, right by Mydei's side. It's an unofficial station, but still. His drive and competency have been his saving grace so far.

"You are the leaders out on the battlefield, responsible for your soldiers. Do you know what the real punishment is?" Archidamia continues ruthlessly, and Phainon and Mydei wisely keep their mouths shut for once. "Losing their trust and faith in you, seeing them hesitate to follow your orders. Going out there and facing the families of the men and women you have led to slaughter today, as you will do."

Phainon—

Phainon has experienced that. Losing the family and becoming an orphan. He knows how devastating a situation it is. And he had a hand in pinning the same fate onto others.

It's getting hard to breathe with every minute passing, every word from Archidamia, and every thought in his brain.

"We understand. We will bear the consequences, no matter how harsh, and work to regain the trust," Mydei responds resolutely, and Phainon sees from the corner of his eye the way glance he shoots at him. "And we will resolve this issue."

"It should have been taken care of years ago. You'd better think carefully on how to proceed with this, Lord Mydeimos," Archidamia warns him, not letting up. "Lest I need to intervene. This is your chance to show us the kind of ruler you will be in the future. You are dismissed."

She turns her back on them as if she cannot stand to look at them any longer. They both still bow their heads, albeit the action stilted in Phainon's case, and then Mydei is dragging him out by the tight grip on the forearm. Their surroundings whiz around Phainon until they find themselves in a

nook between the buildings, and Mydei is leaning against the cold wall, pulling Phainon closer to himself.

"Phainon, you're fine," he mutters, reaching up to splay his fingers out on the back of Phainon's head and push it down into his neck. He's just a little bit shorter again. "Even out your breathing."

Oh. Right.

He's been breathing more and more shallowly over the course of the conversation, pointless panic spreading from his brain to the other bodily functions. He cannot stand the way it happens sometimes, how little control he's got over it.

He closes his eyes and slumps into Mydei, who bears his weight effortlessly. Phainon focuses on the rise and fall of his friend's chest against him and attempts to match the pace. Mydei stays entirely still, a steady presence. His fingers remain unmoving in Phainon's hair, offering silent support.

Phainon has based his anchoring point on Mydei for a long while. He is the first thing Phainon reaches for when he wakes up from a nightmare, and he is what guides him through an episode. It's no wonder he's become what calms him down more successfully than anything else, even now. It almost makes Phainon want to drag Mydei home and hole up in bed together, let his thoughts quiet down until they simmer away into nothingness.

Almost.

"We killed them," Phainon says quietly, rounding back to the subject at hand.

"We were stupid, and their deaths could have been prevented," Mydei agrees easily, chin bumping into Phainon as he nods. "But we didn't kill them."

"They died because of us," Phainon points out stubbornly.

If they weren't assigned under Mydei and Phainon, they would have lived.

And it had been obvious that it was only a matter of time before something of this sort happened. If it weren't Mydei today, it would have been Phainon in a week, a month, or even a year with some luck. For a while now, he has been aware that one of them would crack sooner or later, blinded by the haze of a dangerous fight and the anxiety of not having the other in sight. He always assumed it would've been him, though. It's not a secret that he handles separation worse than Mydei.

This time, Phainon got so swept up in the battle that the panic didn't even have time to set in beyond the vague realization. He isn't sure what set Mydei off to go after him like that. Not that it makes it any better.

"We will get better at this," Mydei adds, gently pushing Phainon back to stand on his own two feet without support. His eyes are set when Phainon glances up, mind made up. "We have to."

A small tendril of thought that perhaps Phainon isn't made for this takes root somewhere deep inside. Maybe he should've focused solely on getting his revenge and not meddled in the life of an unknown boy if these are the consequences. Lives have been lost, and Mydei's own duty and reputation stained. Phainon takes that thought and squanders it as quickly as it comes.

He doesn't regret his choices. He would have done the same all over again at the smallest of chances to get to know Mydei.

Instead, he only nods in agreement. They do have to do better.

Mydei's eyebrows pinch together as he gazes at him with concern. "Are you alright?"

"I'm okay," Phainon replies immediately. He shifts to look to the side, in the direction where most people are sure to be gathered this evening. "We should head over and address it, shouldn't we?"

Mydei nods, exhaling through his mouth. Just like that, his focus shifts as he pushes himself off the wall and directs them forward. They don't speak

as they walk, taking a long way around.

Phainon stands one step behind Mydei, stomach turning as his eyes rake over the gathered people. Some are injured, brought along to witness Mydei's first speech to his own people, announced an hour ago. There are no tears for the dead. The battle was won, so in their minds, the fallen have reached glory. It's already been half a day since they arrived in the settlement, and the first reaction of shock and sorrow has been tempered down by now.

Perdikkas still tends to some of the injured on the side, and Hephaestion sits by his side, biting his thumb as he stares at Phainon and Mydei. Leonnius is somewhere behind them. He had to run to the settlement to gather people who could meet them halfway and assist in carrying the wounded. Peucesta must be with him, keeping the runner from growing restless. Phainon has no doubt Archidamia is hidden away in the shadows, watching with keen eyes. Ptolemy is on the other side of Mydei, mostly as a show of support rather than anything else.

Somehow, it only stresses Phainon out more.

"Due to my negligence, many lives have been unnecessarily lost," Mydei announces, voice carrying easily and cutting through all ongoing conversation. Distantly, various diplomacy lessons resurface, and Phainon thinks it's good that he decided to get straight to the point. Remains true to his nature and shows he's transparent about the issue. "The battle may have been won, but I don't consider it as such. I am aware that on the latest missions, Phainon and I were the leading forces responsible for pushing back the more difficult enemies, ones that the regular soldiers aren't suited to fight against."

Mydei's posture remains rigid, but he manages to lower his head with remorse, eyes obstructed by his hair. Phainon follows suit, staring down at his feet. People have to know they are of the same mind.

"Even if my words are meaningless, I still wish to apologize to everyone gathered. If you're looking to challenge my authority in light of this, you are welcome to do so without facing any repercussions. I swear to give you a fair fight, and forfeit my station should you win." Whispers rise among the people, but Mydei continues on. "Please, don't feel afraid to express any of your concerns or complaints in relation to me. But in the same way, I will not tolerate any accusations and cruel remarks toward Phainon. He's not the one who caused this mess."

Phainon's head snaps up, first glancing at Mydei, who is now staring right at the crowds with sharp eyes, then at their audience. While not directly at fault this time, Phainon is still part of the problem that led to those deaths. He won't let Mydei protect him from something like this, not when they are supposed to be equals.

"Be it as it may, I would request you all to hold me accountable regardless," Phainon rushes to follow up softly, placing his hand on Mydei's shoulder to keep him from arguing. Unlike at Archidamia's, he can finish his sentences here. "I was still careless with my duty."

Mydei rolls his shoulder faintly, undetectable to anyone else that isn't Phainon with his palm pressed against that very shoulder. He isn't happy with the addition, but he won't go against Phainon's words.

"From this day onward, neither of us will participate in expeditions involving other people for the time being. It's foolish to keep us restricted to the settlement given our capability and the demand for work, so we will take up our own assignments that won't involve anyone else in a fight," Mydei announces with a firm voice, a self-appointed punishment. "I guarantee you that the next time I allow myself to fight alongside my soldiers, it will be with a clearer mind and better skills, ensuring none of them get hurt because of my own shortcomings. A leader cannot drag his people down with him, and for that I hope you will forgive me."

"The battle may have been won, but we both will carry the faces and names of people fallen on this day with us for the rest of our lives," Phainon adds sincerely. "We owe them for their loyalty and sacrifice."

It's completely quiet for almost an entire minute, and Phainon's heart drops. Is this not enough? Surely they won't be kicked out? They will deal with it, as they always do, but he doesn't want Mydei to be deprived of his culture and the people he grew to care for. It wouldn't be fair.

But then, several people begin shouting in encouragement. An immeasurable weight lifts off Phainon's shoulders. He knows there must have been other people before them, making mistakes similar to theirs and even worse. But he still worried they would be held to a much higher standard, as impossible for the people to forgive as it might be to forgive themselves.

Phainon distantly wonders if the knowledge that Mydei and Phainon are both Chrysos Heirs would have calmed him down. It doesn't matter, though, since they aren't exactly advertising the fact. From what Ptolemy told them so far, the opinions on the prophecy are divided. But this far from any of the city-states, the common people could be grasping at the straws of divinity more than anyone else.

Ptolemy lets out an aggravated sigh. "Just point us in the direction, and we will deal with it. We can discuss payment afterward."

Very slowly and even more reluctantly, the man's hand raises, and he points along the path. "By the river. We've been having a hard time getting the water supply because of this."

"Yes, yes," Ptolemy waves his hand in clear dismissal. "Whatever it is, fret not. We will be back within an hour or so." There's been a report made, and

they knew what this was about when they set out, so it's certainly nothing too difficult. The mission objectives all blur together after a while.

"Shouldn't we get paid first?" Hephaestion asks as they start walking, already preparing an arrow. They can't even hear the water current just yet, but it's good to be prepared for anything that might jump out at them.

"People are often reluctant since we're not exactly an official army. They wouldn't want to pay a group of bandits who might run away with their precious money," Ptolemy responds with a shrug. "Let the man see what you're capable of first. I will be impressed by his confidence and stupidity if he remains reluctant afterward."

"Fear is a powerful motivator," Perdikkas adds.

Phainon bumps into Mydei's shoulder as they follow a few steps behind the group; the long explanations of how things work tuned out since they're more than experienced in the procedure. It's a little cute how curious Hephaestion is about everything. More so, it's exciting that he's right there with them. Mydei kicks Phainon lightly in the leg, and he beams at his friend.

Even when they aren't partaking in the literal wars anymore, fighting on their own signifies new challenges. If the grounds are spread out, the two of them go in separate directions to learn how to handle things alone, eventually meeting in the middle. They make it into another competition, seeing who covers more distance first.

The easily provided knowledge that Mydei's position is constantly monitored by both Leonnius and Ptolemy eases some of the anxiety and gives way to the excitement of paving the way to Mydei. It's less stressful than the gnawing need to constantly ensure his friend is within sight, muted by everything else.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon stumbles over his own two feet, diving for the dirty ground to take cover. His back pressed against the barrel, he pants heavily, listening for the heavy footsteps of the person chasing him. He doesn't have many options available for hiding. And it's not like he can hide forever,

"Lord Phainon…" the man on the stool that happens to be sitting a meter away sighs heavily. He glances at him only once, in that disapproving-parent way. Phainon wrinkles his nose at the title. Is this how Mydei felt at the beginning? More and more people are starting to address Phainon this way, and it just doesn't sit right with him. "He will find you."

Phainon smiles sheepishly, tucking his legs close to ensure the barrel covers him from sight entirely. "He always does," he agrees easily.

The man only hums and resumes his work on the soon-to-be sword. "What have you done this time?"

"Hey," Phainon protests, a bit louder than he should be, given the fact that he's attempting to conceal his presence. "It was your son's idea."

"Of that, I have no doubt." Hephaestion's father sighs yet again and decides that, perhaps, he doesn't wish to know the details anymore, as he doesn't ask him to elaborate.

That might be for the better. Phainon doesn't need another lecture about childishness. They get enough of that from Archidamia, severe scowls, and harsh words that by now have no effect. She won't get truly angry with them unless they mess up again, as they did with their attachment issues. But their training progresses at a steady pace, and they're clearing their expeditions faster than expected. She has nothing to point at except the impropriety of the actions, considering their stations. Phainon keeps arguing back that he has no formal station at all, enjoying the twitch of her jaw each time.

"Is it clear?" He whispers, holding himself tight. He might have a chance to get to Peucesta before Mydei realizes where he's heading and convince the

musician to mitigate the situation. The man doesn't respond, eyes following something. Phainon opens his mouth to repeat the question, and—

Embarrassingly, Phainon does yelp as a spear lodges itself in the ground dangerously close to Phainon's thigh. His head whirls up from being startled, and he sees Mydei leaning on the weapon, glaring with that golden gaze and pupils reduced to thin slits as he stares Phainon down.

"You'd better pray to Nikador this will come off easily, HKS," Mydei warns him, eerily calm for someone who looks seconds away from murder.

"Lord Mydeimos," Hephaestion's father greets, unfazed by their antics.

And normally, Phainon would already start apologizing and promise not to do anything like this again, despite both of them knowing he will. Smile sweetly and be on his best behavior for the rest of the day, do the dishes without a word of complaint, and press in close to Mydei at any opportunity like a puppy who knows he did something wrong but wants attention. He isn't above playing it up if that's what works against Mydei.

And normally, Phainon would feel hot under that intense glare. It would make his heart kick up the pace just a little bit, and he would grin awkwardly until his brain comes up with a decent enough diversion tactic, anything to stop Mydei from directing that laser focus on Phainon for so long before the heat reaches his face.

But normally, Mydei's face isn't adorned with black ink carefully applied on his forehead and left cheek. A large symbol of the sun right beneath his hairline, and a paw print covering the entire cheek. Hephaestion insisted it's a lion's, but to Phainon it's just a cat's.

The only reason they got away with it to begin with was that Phainon and Mydei were fresh from reaching the eighth day mark in their fighting. Phainon already slept most of it off in the infirmary, but apparently Mydei was awakened by Perdikkas much sooner for whatever reason. Exhaustion, Phainon's presence, and fingers combing through the blond hair were enough to keep him asleep through the quiet giggling as Hephaestion first

created his little masterpiece, and then through Phainon recreating his own mark.

Phainon's eyes travel across Mydei's face, from the paw to the sun, and then back again. Silly doodles only highlighted by the serious expression. Phainon cannot help it as a snort escapes his lips, and then a full laugh that pushes him back with its intensity, jostling the barrel.

Red mist swirls around the spear, and Phainon only has enough time to think how deep of a shit he's just landed himself in, before he's scrambling to his feet and running in what he hopes is Peucesta's direction, still laughing. Thera waves at him cheerfully as he passes her, giggling at the whole ordeal as an older boy with ginger hair haggles with some stall owner.

Chapter End Notes
