chapters.title: Chapter 12: and heal their scars
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Leonnius only blinks at them in surprise. He's seen Mydei go all out in the fight before, but that's different. "Feral?" He repeats.

"I nearly strangled him to death when we first met," Mydei admits in a very matter-of-fact way. Phainon nearly laughs at the blunt delivery, Mydei's gaze bored as he scratches the tabletop with his index finger.

Hephaestion's leg collides with the desk's surface, a low thud echoing in the otherwise quiet room. He hisses in pain, rubbing his hand over the shin. Ptolemy makes a noise of sorts from the corridor, where he's been searching through the bookcases, and Perdikkas stops writing his twentieth medical report to raise an eyebrow at them.

"He tried to kill you?" Leonnius asks, voice high-pitched and fearful just the slightest bit. "Lord Mydei? You?"

Chapter Notes

Red lines.

That's all Phainon can focus on. He tries not to look too closely whenever they are revealed to him so freely. It's a common occurrence, which means he's got them more or less memorized by now, whether he wants to or not. And yet he still doesn't allow himself to stare, aware that tearing his eyes away once he catches a proper glimpse would be a difficult task to accomplish.

But he doesn't care right now.

The tree offers some shade as they rest beneath it, golden wheats dancing in the wind around them. With Mydei laid out beneath him, Phainon sits on

his thighs with one knee on each side. A familiar position, all things considered. Mydei's hands are folded underneath his head, and he gazes at Phainon with his lips quirked up just the slightest amount.

And there are the red lines.

One underlines his lower eyelid, the most characteristic one for all to see, relatively resembling Peucesta's makeup. The one below it is just as distinctive, a small symbol is etched high on his cheekbone. Phainon imagines pressing his lips against it in a chaste kiss whenever he allows himself to daydream. It's soft and innocent, an instinct as natural as slipping his leg between Mydei's when they are sleeping. Even if he's never let his lips anywhere near the mark before.

More red streaks down along his neck, partially obstructed by his hair, and ending just above his clavicles. Another symbol right on his sternum, a large one that Ptolemy once mused resembles flames, and Phainon cannot unsee it now. Perhaps that's where all the excess heat originates from.

And then, there are the areas that Phainon steals secret glances at when he's sure Mydei isn't paying attention to him. Ones that make him space out slightly when he does so.

They have both filled out decently over the years. It would be difficult to find any fat left lingering on either of them. Only layers of firm muscles, a result of participating more often in harsh training rather than resting as they should. Mydei's food tastes delicious, but it's also perfectly balanced, courtesy of Perdikkas. It helps with staying in shape, and it shows. Phainon glimpses it in the mirror, in the way his biceps bulge enough to be noticeable when he bends his arm at the elbow as he brushes his teeth. And now, he sees it in the toned stomach and well-defined pecs on the teen below him.

Pretty. So fitting to Mydei. Raw and incredible power, hidden beneath the captivating pale skin accented by scarlet markings.

A jagged line goes from his shoulder directly through his pecs, right above the nipples. Then, beneath the pecs. The muscles are underlined sharply by

it, making it that much difficult to look away. And yet another, running across his ribs and pointing low, disappearing into his underwear.

A red line peeks out of the waistband on both sides. Cutting through his hip and angling toward the groin. Phainon knows there is more hiding out of sight in that space that's always covered, unlike Mydei's chest. He's only properly looked maybe three times in all these years. He remembers it vividly. Embarrassing as it is.

"You like them this much?" Mydei's voice rings in Phainon's ears, a little unclear. Phainon doesn't pay it much attention, busy with drinking in every detail. "Don't you wish to touch them?"

And Phainon has done it before, still traces those red lines on his arms and legs frequently whenever they're lying on top of one another. He knows them by heart. But the lines on Mydei's chest? The ones that disappear below the waistband, or those that hug his thighs really high? They are off limits.

But now, Mydei has offered it himself, and he's splayed out so openly on their bed. He bucks his hips a little to get Phainon to hurry up, and heat spreads in Phainon's abdomen as he fights not to grind down in answer.

Phainon brushes away the bedsheets that rode up around Mydei's waist, mildly annoyed at having the view obstructed. As he does so, his thumbs settle at the tips of the red lines starting just at his hips, and he trails his fingers along them until he reaches the edge of dark blue underwear. One of Phainon's, he realizes hysterically. Mydei remains silent, though his hands reach down to press once against Phainon's palms before falling to the sides. Taking it as encouragement, he slowly digs his index fingers under the elastic material and drags it down just a little, ignoring the—

Phainon jolts, eyes snapping open to reveal the dark room. Sheets are bundled between his legs, and an overly warm arm is placed dangerously low on his stomach. He's not entirely sure where he is. He sighs and rubs his eyes tiredly. Right, no, that's stupid. He's home, in their bed, and clearly still in the middle of the night. But wasn't he doing something else…?

He blinks blankly for a long moment, head turning to see Mydei sleeping peacefully on his back. He doesn't, usually. Phainon stares some more, noting the way his friend is sprawled out, one hand above his head while the other rests against Phainon's skin, almost scorchingly hot.

He very slowly sits up, Mydei's hand sliding lower along his skin, and he violently flinches away as the dream filters back into his brain. Mydei makes a noise, and Phainon is immediately overtaken by sheer panic. He's felt somewhat uncomfortable since waking up, and now he is painfully aware why. But to make sure, because perhaps it's not as bad, he looks down between his legs.

"Ph'nn?" Mydei hums in question, and Phainon doesn't glance over his shoulder to see if he's got one eye cracked open. Instead, he watches the prominent wet spot on his boxer briefs with horror. Oh no.

"I'm okay," he croaks out unconvincingly, almost trembling. "Bathroom."

And with that, he climbs over Mydei's body, desperately hoping Mydei doesn't notice anything. As unlikely as it is in low lighting and the way his body is angled, it'd just be Phainon's luck if he did catch a glimpse. Phainon runs to the bathroom, almost slamming the door shut behind himself.

His eyes fall onto the mirror, and what greets him is his flushed reflection, hair mussed, eyes wild. His underwear feels sticky and disgusting.

"Fuck."

He wasn't supposed to like Mydei in this way. Especially not when they just began the painful process of learning how to be normal.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Something hooks onto Phainon's belt, yanking back viciously, and Phainon topples down in a heap of limbs, watching as his friend runs past him. A dull ache resonates in his bones at the impact as he quickly collects himself.

"You—!" Phainon cuts his own yell off and grits his teeth, getting back to his feet and pushing himself all that much harder to get back to his previous speed and push even further than that. He cannot lose.

Mydei has always been more fluid in his movements, avoiding any blows with ease as his footwork carries him with muscle memory alone. Phainon, fortunately, has always been just a little faster than him when it comes down to sheer speed.

It takes a minute, but he snags Mydei by his robes in the last moment, pulling the fabric off his shoulder as he attempts to twist away. Except Phainon tugs toward himself with most of his strength, and that's enough to cause Mydei to lose his balance, making him tumble to the ground in a fashion similar to Phainon's previous fall. Except that in his petty satisfaction over returning the favor, Phainon forgets to step back and gets kicked in the knee. Mydei drops to the ground, and Phainon along with him.

Mydei quickly angles himself so that he lands on his back, a position less vulnerable than if he had ended up on his stomach. He grabs Phainon's forearm in a bruising grip to prevent him from even thinking of getting back up and finishing the race. Knowing it's a lost cause, Phainon scrambles to lock Mydei into the position before he can use his agility and worm his way out of this and into the finish line.

"Now we are both second," Phainon says cheekily.

"HKS," Mydei hisses at him, but he only puts up the bare minimum of effort into bucking him off.

Phainon laughs in response, feeling a bit lightheaded, sitting on Mydei's thighs and halfheartedly maintaining a hold on his other arm. It's the most common position they land in when they're trying to restrain each other. And with each time, Phainon's despair at the proximity only grows.

Leonnius breezes past them so fast he might as well be a smudge of movement. Or maybe it's the fact that Phainon isn't paying that much attention to his surroundings anymore. Perhaps he should be, because at this very moment, he wants to put his focus anywhere but the fact that he's caging Mydei's body in beneath himself, the teen not even attempting to break free. He lies there, lips thin and unhappy at being stripped of his near victory.

It wouldn't take any effort at all to drop lower and press their lips together. Phainon's ears burn viciously at the absurd thought. It's true, though. They're halfway through fourteen, surely it's old enough to— to let things happen. And maybe Mydei wouldn't have minded as much, maybe he would have sighed into it and tugged Phainon closer. And maybe then Phainon would have been allowed to press kisses against that red line beneath his lower eyelid when he's overcome by the stupid affection for Mydei, and greet him in the morning by pressing lips to the small symbol beneath it.

Is it really so much to ask for?

But Phainon won't ever initiate this, won't let his feelings impact their relationship. What they have is good. It's amazing, more than Phainon imagined he could ever get. It's a paralyzing fear, the knowledge that Mydei might look at Phainon in bewilderment and then distance himself once he realizes what has been brewing in Phainon's head and heart.

Like right now, when the smallest crinkle appears between his brows, and his hand slips out of the grip to slowly reach up toward Phainon's face.

"Competing against these two isn't fun," Leonnius' whining carries over to them, and Phainon looks up to find him striding to them with Hephaestion and Peucesta in tow, a pout evident on his face. They're already a scant few meters away. "Hephaestion, wanna try? You're faster than them. And your priorities are more sound."

Phainon is almost offended, but it's true. Maybe he would have tried harder if he knew there was any real possibility of winning against Leonnius in a

race. As it is, even with a rather lengthy headstart, neither of them stands a chance.

“Competing against you isn’t fun either, idiot," Hephaestion snarks at him. His eyes dart down at Phainon and Mydei, but he looks away just as quickly. He crosses his arms and sighs, directing an unimpressed stare at their runner. "The outcome is always the same."

Phainon glances back down, finding Mydei's hand scratching his own neck as he stares at their companions upside down. Right. Right, they should be up already by now, shouldn't they? Phainon scrambles to his feet in a manner that he hopes doesn't look too suspicious and offers a hand to Mydei. His friend takes it, and Phainon digs his heels into the ground at the very last second to prevent himself from being yanked right back down.

"Nice try," he huffs as he pulls him up instead.

Mydei only shrugs, adjusting his robes to appear more presentable like before Phainon decided to use them as an anchor. He still leaves one shoulder off, the fabric pooling around his waist and showing off half of his chest and back. The red lines mock Phainon silently until he forces himself to snap his eyes back up.

He catches the moment Leonnius looks at Peucesta pleadingly, but gives up as soon as Peucesta raises a singular eyebrow at him. Sometimes Phainon still marvels at the power Peucesta's expressions hold.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

The enemies drop as Phainon rushes past them, cutting down each one that happens to be within reach. The battleground is rather flat, making it easy to see his friends across it. Which is how he noticed the large wall of crystals spring up from the ground far away on his right in the first place. Squinting

to see what's happening, only to realize a person cowers at the foot of the construction as Mydei fights to keep the black tide monsters at bay.

Hephaestion fights further to Phainon's left, making it difficult to get back to him in time should something go wrong when he's away. But Phainon is confident in the younger's skills. He knows how to keep up in a difficult fight, unlike some of their other friends.

Phainon will never forgive himself if something happens to Hephaestion, but he will also never forgive himself if Leonnius dies when he could have prevented it. Hephaestion would also never forgive him if Phainon prioritized him when there was no sign of life-threatening danger to his person.

So, he runs as fast as his legs can carry him, decreasing the number of opponents as he goes to make it easier on both Hephaestion and Mydei. Once he's close enough, more details can be discerned.

Leonnius kneels on the ground, his back pressed tightly against the crystal, which goes at least two meters high. He doesn't appear injured, and Phainon cannot see any blood escaping from his body, but his face is concerningly pale, and his eyes are squeezed shut. He knocks his head against the wall behind him in a not-so-gentle manner.

Mydei remains off to the side, guarding their precious runner against the onslaught of monsters. They come in waves, making it difficult to catch a break and watch his back at the same time. Which is precisely what Phainon is here for.

He skids to a stop next to Leonnius, knees digging into the dirt and sword disappearing in a flurry of white sparkles. The ability to summon it is so handy when he doesn't want to discard it and then fumble to pick it up.

"Leonnius," Phainon says loudly over the inhuman groans and sharp echoes of Mydei's gauntlets. "Leonnius, it's fine."

"I can't, I can't be here," Leonnius gasps out, curling in on himself. "I'm so sorry, I just. I cannot move. I can't. There are so many monsters, and I

thought I could be of help, but I can't. Because I'm useless, and I can't even fight like you all. This was—"

"Leonnius," Mydei barks sharply, grunting when his side gets nicked by a weapon. "Let Phainon help you."

Leonnius' mouth snaps shut with an audible click at what's virtually a command from his Prince.

"You're not a burden, and you're doing well," Phainon tells Leonnius quickly, his weapon materializing in a fraction of a second when he notices another monster trying to reach them from the side. He makes quick work of it, stepping away for half a minute to clear the other few nearby. Leonnius stays rooted in place, head angled down, and not moving a muscle as Phainon returns to him. "It's the first time your fear got the best of you since you took this role. It's impressive. Wanna know how many times we fucked up?" He asks and gently guides him to his feet. Muscle memory of pulling the injured forward kicks in, making it easier to direct him. "It's a lot. We will tell you about it over the fire later, yeah?"

"I don't deserve to be a part of this," Leonnius says shakily. He nearly trips over his own legs, and now that's concerning.

Phainon glances back, noting that Mydei's markings are glowing, and he's throwing shards at the monsters, flawlessly evading and striking them down one by one. He has started going all out and will not require much help anytime soon. In this state, he will be able to slaughter his way through this wave and keep an eye on Hephaestion within minutes.

He grinds down the stab of panic at leaving Mydei behind and instead focuses on the trust and knowledge that his friend is more than skilled enough to handle it. With that in mind, he grabs Leonnius more firmly, making sure there is no room for doubt that he's not alone in this, and slowly walks them to the makeshift camp where Ptolemy waits. The scholar takes one look at them before he takes over and murmurs to Leonnius with cold facts and soft reassurances, waving Phainon away and back into the battle.

Ptolemy, as unwilling as he is to participate, knows how to fight. He's also well-spoken enough to soothe Leonnius' worries better than Phainon or Mydei ever could. Their runner is in good hands. Phainon turns on his heel and runs back to where he last saw his best friend, adrenaline surging.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

If their clock is to be trusted, Mydei experiences a particularly violent nightmare an entire hour before the Entry Hour.

It's not pretty. It never is.

Phainon jolts awake when Mydei begins screaming himself hoarse, red mist swirling around his hands as crystals attempt to form. They materialize briefly in the air before breaking apart on their own, over and over. It's not words that slip past Mydei's lips. Simply panicked noises, mostly ones of pain, and some that might resemble wordless despair.

It takes a second for Phainon to reorient himself before he shuffles above his friend and clutches Mydei's wrists in a loose hold, attempting to wake him up. It takes longer than usual. A lot of quiet pleas, and putting the smallest of pressure against the pale skin. They learned the hard way that forcibly waking each other up or holding limbs down isn't the best idea.

Phainon feels a stinging wet line appear on his cheek where a shard manages to scratch him and break the skin, and Mydei's eyes finally snap open. They are unseeing at first, glazed over as they stare through Phainon's neck. The red mist dissipates all at once within the next few seconds, harsh panting filling the space of their room. Phainon watches as he blinks up at his face and smiles down when his gaze widens in shock and regret, hoping his expression is reassuring enough.

A drop of gold, slightly more vibrant than those eyes, lands on Mydei's cheek. Right below the red markings. Phainon lets go as Mydei's hands rise

to Phainon's face, wiping off the blood without a care for the way it stains his fingertips.

"It's fine," Phainon says quietly, one eye lidded as Mydei rubs his cheek insistently.

Mydei doesn't say anything back, the other hand dropping from the unharmed side of his face and brushing the back of his fingers against his chest in an upward motion. I'm sorry.

"It's really fine," Phainon repeats, smiling in relief that his friend is no longer stuck in a nightmare. Phainon probably looks so stupid at this hour. His hair must be a mess; he can feel it sitting weirdly against his scalp. "It's less than what I get from our spars. Will be completely gone by noon."

Mydei frowns, opening his mouth only to close it again. Ah. One of those rare days, then.

Before Phainon can get any other word out to try and drive the point across that nothing's wrong, he's yanked back down into a lying position. He's about to say something regardless, but Mydei settles in close, legs wrapped around Phainon's and one hand slipping into his, fingers tangling together.

Phainon huffs. He doesn't mind the role he plays in rescuing Mydei from the nightmares, never had and never will. He is more than happy to be of help. He's about to say as much, but then a warm nose nudges gently around the cut, hot breath on Phainon's skin, and Phainon startles. His head swivels to the side, nearly colliding with Mydei's.

Sunlight colored eyes meet the sky blue. Slit pupils against Phainon's own strange ones.

He has to force himself to swallow, painfully aware that he cannot do anything stupid here. Even if Mydei is so pretty that it physically hurts Phainon sometimes. Like right now. He doesn't even have bed hair. On any other day, Phainon would have felt annoyed over the unfairness of it.

Phainon shifts onto his side, keeping a steady grip on Mydei's hand while he moves a bit higher up in the bed until he can rest his chin over the crown of Mydei's head. He snakes his own arm over Mydei's waist and drags him closer, exhaling shakily when Mydei's nose ends up at the base of his neck, lips briefly touching his collarbone by accident before Mydei pulls back just a little bit.

And it is fine.

Phainon's stupid desires have nothing to do with this. Mydei had a nightmare, and now he needs the comfort of Phainon's presence for a little while, and so Phainon will provide without making it weird for anyone but maybe himself.

Mydei clings to Phainon, and Phainon relaxes into the hold as best as he can. The lights are still dim outside, and he knows neither of them is going to sleep again. So, they stay that way as minutes turn into hours, changing the position now and then to prevent their muscles from growing sore. It's quiet, peaceful. And Mydei's heartbeat stops pounding against Phainon's skin with the pace and strength of a scared rabbit's.

An hour and a half to the Lucid Hour, the front door opens, and footsteps echo through the house. Phainon and Mydei remain as they are, now both on their backs with one arm and leg linked together each. A sharp knock rattles against the door to their bedroom, and two of their friends walk through without waiting for an invitation. Ptolemy stops in the middle of taking in a breath to say something, one eyebrow raised. Perdikkas stares between them with a vague degree of concern.

"Are you alright?" The physician asks first.

It's a fair question. They are always up and running within the first few minutes of the Entry Hour, usually even before that. Dressed and ready to face whatever has been put on their agenda for the day. Classes, spars, meetings. Seeing their friends in between taking care of their responsibilities.

"Yeah," Phainon responds, and Mydei nods. "We're gonna have to move the separation thing, though."

"Are you sure?" Ptolemy asks, but it isn't pushy. "We can try later in the day if you think you might be up for it then."

Mydei would definitely pick himself up enough by then, ready to try and get better at this at any cost. But right now, his fingers tighten around Phainon's even as he doesn't give any other indication as to what his opinion might be. Mydei might force himself if he has to, but Phainon doesn't want him to. He took care to return and check on Phainon when the time ran too far during those first few times. He still ensures Phainon is doing well and where his limits lie each time. Now, Phainon will be the one to hold his pieces together.

"No," he replies with no hesitation. "Not today."

"Alright," Ptolemy agrees, just like that. He nods and steps closer to their bed. "Any idea on when? It isn't my intention to rush you; I simply wish to have a rough idea of the timeline."

Mydei slowly sits up, thumb idly brushing across Phainon's index finger, and then all the way down to his wrist. He shifts his grip to gently press it against Phainon's pulse point, absentminded as he considers Ptolemy's words. Phainon's frame of mind doesn't allow him to contemplate the issue as carefully. He is busy staring at Mydei, still locked into that soft bubble they encased themselves in as Mydei was coming down from a nightmare. Just existing together, as they should be.

It doesn't help that Phainon simply loves him so much. Now that he has resigned himself to it. It's a scary emotion, aching deep in his very core with its intensity. Scary, but pleasant. Exciting.

The dawn device shines eternally. The skies are dark with evernight. The stars and moons hang high above, providing scant lighting. Phainon of Aedes Elysiae loves Crown Prince Mydeimos endlessly. Perhaps in every possible sense of the word, though he doesn't let himself think of it that far just yet. But it's still simply another absolute truth of the world.

Phainon stares at Mydei's side profile, the warm glow from the lamplight streaming through the window highlighting his features. Phainon cannot believe a person this beautiful walks among the mortals.

He moves his hand, disrupting Mydei's grasp on his wrist as he tangles their fingers together and squeezes. He wants to take Mydei's palm and press it against his lips. The back, the front, the fingertips. He wants to curl around Mydei as he's sitting and rest his forehead against the heated skin of his stomach.

But he has to settle for the smallest of things, so he swallows down the painful wave of yearning and smiles up at Mydei when he quirks an eyebrow at him. This is okay. Phainon will settle for whatever he can take, grateful for anything. He doesn't want to ask for too much. He's not sure he even deserves it. He needs some more time to adjust to it, and he will be able to tamp this feeling down.

Phainon's thoughts are thankfully cut short as Mydei moves his free hand in the air, signing for, Tomorrow?

Phainon exhales slowly and inhales a bit quicker. Right. The separation.

Suddenly, he isn't as eager to proceed with it. He never would have been, if it weren't for the lives lost because of it. They have to fix it sooner or later, but with the fast pace they established, nothing will happen if they prolong it just a little bit longer. The soldiers aren't assigned to them anymore, so no one will be put in danger because of their messed-up psyches.

Phainon bites on the dry bit of skin on his bottom lip, trying to tear it off as he recalls what their schedule for tomorrow was supposed to be. "Do we move up the endurance spar, then?" He asks, remembering that's what they decided on last week.

Mydei shrugs in response, which means Phainon is the one who has to make the call.

On one hand, he feels a bit guilty about pushing this so far into the future when they technically could do the separation thing tomorrow, and then

another one after their spar. On the other hand, he really doesn't want to rush this. And when it comes down to it, even if Phainon would probably grit his teeth and push past the desperate need of contact right now, he would never want Mydei to attempt it right after going nonverbal.

"We're almost at day nine out of ten," Phainon tells Ptolemy eventually. "We're gonna need two days of rest, so we can do the separation in eleven days? Twelve?"

"It's that time again?" Perdikkas asks tiredly, as always the most unhappy about this particular sparring session. "I hope you will cease this thankless fight once you reach your goal. The effects it has on your bodies are abysmal."

"I want to be done with it as well. We had such rapid progress when we first started out, and then we got stuck," Phainon nearly whines, brushing hair out of his eyes as he moves to finally sit up as well. "It takes so long to move up by even two hours."

"What did you expect? That's normal," Perdikkas responds with distaste, on the sole principle of showing his displeasure about them staying up for ten days nonstop and focusing on a strenuous activity all the while. "It was easy at first, because you were building up on the seemingly endless potential. Now, you're pushing your limits, one tiny bit at a time." He sighs and angles his head to stare blankly at Ptolemy. "You two are already beyond the human standards, which gives me about as many gray hairs as you've been gifting to Ptolemy over the years."

Ptolemy whirls around to face Perdikkas, having to angle his head up to glare directly into the dark blue eyes. "I do not have any gray hair."

"Don't you?" Perdikkas asks with some traces of a smirk pulling at his lips, stepping closer to grab a hold of a single strand of blonde hair. He performatively squints down at it, seemingly inspecting it closely. "That's because you've got light hair. You won't realize the change is happening, but I can already spot a few."

"I do not," Ptolemy bats his hand away angrily, "Have gray hair."

Perdikkas rolls his eyes at the dramatic reaction, but it's nothing other than a fond gesture. "What am I supposed to say? Gray will stick out from that dark of a color like a sore thumb." He points to his own black hair, a shade so deep it's almost dark blue.

Ptolemy huffs before he leans forward with a dry smile, eyes glinting. "There, there. You needn't worry," he drawls. "By means of beauty all beautiful things become beautiful."

"I've already got gray hair. White hair, even," Phainon pipes up, thoroughly bored with their exchange. He's got one knee raised up, and he's resting his chin on it, one hand still loosely holding onto Mydei beneath the sheets. "Neither of you should be complaining."

The two men face him at once with narrowed eyes, and Phainon grins at them both unabashedly as Mydei snorts quietly.

"Sorry," is the first thing Mydei says in late afternoon, voice quiet and a little defeated. "It's been a while since it got this bad."

"Ptolemy should be sorry for those boring lessons he gave us instead. You're fine," Phainon repeats for what might be a tenth time. He will say it as many times as needed. "Do you want to talk about the dream?"

"It was the sea," he responds simply, watching Thera roll on the ground. It's the evading tactic that Aias' group is learning right now, Phainon recalls. "You kept drowning while the sea beasts tore into me. No matter what I did, I couldn't save you. I haven't felt that powerless in years."

Phainon winces in sympathy. Sometimes, he dreams of the cloaked figure spearing Mydei through in the middle of the settlement, or back at Aedes Elysiae. He never gets back up in those dreams. It's some of the most distressing ones, on par with those old memories replaying on a loop and witnessing his parents die all over again.

"If it helps any, my father taught me to swim when I was five," Phainon says, hoping to lighten up the subject. He almost says he would outswim Mydei, but thinks better of it. As ambitious and competitive as Phainon might be, he's not so delusional. "I would have pulled my weight even in the water."

"I know. You're the one I would always trust my back with," Mydei tells him distractedly, twitching a little when Thera falls wrong, yelping when her arm bends wrong. She gets up, shaking it off before she's back to it. Just like her brother. "Thera, come here."

She bounces over to them, eyes forever gleaming with excitement. Mydei reaches over and weaves her hair into a simple braid, securing it with his own clip. The small braid in his own hair stays in place for now, and Phainon already thinks to jostle him around enough so the strands slip loose.

"You're getting distracted because your long hair gets in your eyes," Mydei tells her, patiently pulling her hands back down when she attempts to fiddle with it. "Kremnoan soldiers are known to braid their hair for battles. Ask Aias to teach you."

"Thank you, Prince Mydei!" She chirps and runs away again, dipping into a roll that ends with her sprawled across the grass with a giggle.

"You sure it's the hair?" Phainon asks with a chuckle.

"Now she lost focus," Mydei sighs softly. He's good with children, always so gentle and patient with them.

They watch her quietly for a few more minutes, the bruises from incorrect falls slowly forming on her knees and elbows. She always gets back up, ready to repeat the action over and over again. She will be alright.

Someone runs toward them at high speed, and Phainon and Mydei's eyes follow a smudge of bright orange hair as a boy almost two years their junior barrels into Thera, picking her up and spinning her in the air with a beaming grin.

"Have you been good while I was gone? Not causing any trouble for the Prince and his companion?" He asks, forcefully nuzzling his nose into her neck until she giggles and attempts to push him away. "I saw you were training very hard."

"She takes after you," Phainon calls to him, hoping it comes across as a praise that it is. Aias is cut from the same cloth as the rest of them; his pure ambition glints as brightly as Hephaestion's.

"Mn," Aias' light blue eyes settle on the two of them, holding Thera on his hip as she attempts to squirm away. "We have to live up to our great leaders."

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"You found them in the forest?" Leonnius repeats incredulously.

"Yep," Hephaestion confirms proudly, toying with his long hair. He's got the laurel leaves in, a rare occurrence nearly a year after he acquired them. He worries about breaking them amid all the violence they engage in day-to-day. They suit him a little too well. But now that Phainon is paying attention, his hair appears to be even longer than it used to be back at the beginning, reaching halfway down his back. "They weren't quick to trust. I even fought Phainon on the spot."

"You did?" Leonnius asks, eyes wide in surprise. He tried sparring with Phainon once. Phainon gave him the courtesy of waiting an entire two minutes before sending him to the ground. He may be fast, but his reflexes aren't that polished against the truly skilled people.

"And I won!" Hephaestion gloats, swinging his legs back and forth from his seat on Ptolemy's desk, not caring one bit about Phainon's glare as per usual. Perdikkas chuckles, sitting on the actual chair at the very same desk and finishing up his work. "I still win against both of them."

Leonnius gasps, then turns to Peucesta as if he needs a confirmation to believe that, except he whirls back around to stare at Hephaestion with bafflement before his friend can give an affirmative. He's not around often enough to witness their spars, living his own life and following Peucesta more often than not unless he's needed for a mission. They still hang out, it's just that he's not that interested in their fights. "You do?!"

"We don't have serious fights as often as we should. But he does win on the grounds of never letting us pin him down. It's not as if he can strike either of us down, either," Phainon points out. "It's always a draw, if anything."

It makes for good training, as good as the prolonged spar, and their little quest to defeat Archidamia. The ten-day battle develops their endurance and reinforces just how attuned to each other they are. Archidamia forces them to learn new strategies and work around a stronger opponent—if not by strength, then experience. Hephaestion, meanwhile, serves to improve their instincts and speed.

"That's still better than anyone else in the settlement can claim," Hephaestion says with a shrug. "Except for Lady Archidamia."

"In paired spar, we should be able to take her down within a month," Mydei says confidently. "Maybe we will be able to do it individually after we're done with the ten-day fight."

Perdikkas seemingly cannot resist the deep sigh that escapes him at the mention of it. It's still an ambitious timeline, though Phainon guesses it won't be long until they hit it. Excitement runs through his veins, and Phainon jostles Mydei's calf with his foot. Mydei doesn't react, sitting slumped against the table.

"And what about the two of you?" Leonnius asks, looking between Phainon and Mydei with curiosity. "You're obviously a set. But how did you two meet? It's difficult to imagine you were ever apart."

Phainon hums, turning the words around in his head. He spent nine years without Mydei by his side, and now it's incomprehensible to him to even consider the idea of spending more than four hours away from one another.

They will stretch it out until it's at least a few days, he knows. With hope that once they reach that threshold, they might be able to push past it in dire situations, should they need to.

It's been five years since Phainon dragged Mydei out of the sea. Five years since he lost everything, and then gained everything in the shape of a person. Ptolemy would say it's not a healthy thought to have, placing so much importance on Mydei. Phainon doesn't care. It's the truth.

"What was your first impression of Mydei?" Peucesta asks quietly, curiosity clear in his gaze.

Phainon is thrown back to that day at the Sea of Souls, drenched in freezing water, as the first thought running through his mind at the sight of Mydei was that Phagousa themselves must have sculpted a creature that beautiful. So ethereal that its purpose couldn't be anything other than to lure innocents into the dangerous waters, only to devour them whole.

Breathtaking, almost slips past his lips.

"Feral," is what he forces out of his mouth. It's also undeniably correct.

Hephaestion doesn't seem overly surprised, no doubt remembering the state Mydei was in when they first arrived. And so does Ptolemy, no audible reaction from wherever he disappeared to. Mydei had attacked Archidamia and harmed her, for once. Perdikkas and Peucesta didn't witness much of Mydei's behavior from the early days, but still enough of the guarded attitude he carried with himself.

Leonnius only blinks at them in surprise. He's seen Mydei go all out in the fight before, but that's different. "Feral?" He repeats.

"I nearly strangled him to death when we first met," Mydei admits in a very matter-of-fact way. Phainon nearly laughs at the blunt delivery, Mydei's gaze bored as he scratches the tabletop with his index finger.

Hephaestion's leg collides with the desk's surface, a low thud echoing in the otherwise quiet room. He hisses in pain, rubbing his hand over the shin.

Ptolemy makes a noise of sorts from the corridor, where he's been searching through the bookcases, and Perdikkas stops writing his twentieth medical report to raise an eyebrow at them.

"He tried to kill you?" Leonnius asks, voice high-pitched and fearful just the slightest bit. "Lord Mydei? You?"

"It was just once," Phainon tells him in what he hopes is a reassuring tone. Phainon sincerely hopes this doesn't ruin Leonnius' perception of Mydei. He hums in thought and reaches out to poke at Mydei's arm. "He never harmed me outside of a spar since." Or on a rare occasion, a nightmare got the better of him. "And that one time was only because he was scared of me. But now he knows I'm not scary. And he is quite sweet to me. Isn't that right, Mydei?"

"Do you want a repeat of that day?" Mydei threatens, glaring at him without much heat. He quickly catches Phainon's hand and yanks, huffing when Phainon yelps, and pushing him back into place when he almost loses balance. Thankfully, they are sitting on the floor by the low table rather than the chairs.

"And mean," Phainon remedies with a grimace, now poking on Mydei's cheek.

He grins when Mydei turns his face and gently bites down on the finger. It's warm, is Phainon's immediate reaction. His small fangs bracket the digit, and Phainon's brain short-circuits for a brief moment. He never thought that much about those fangs, but now he wishes to take a much closer look. Trace them with his fingers, perhaps get closer and try to…

It takes several long seconds, but he manages to pull his eyes away from the act, desperately hoping his face isn't red as heat climbs up his neck. Not the smartest move as he's met with a bored expression on a too-beautiful face, coupled with the finger still inside those parted lips. The teeth grind against it with the smallest of pressure, and slitted pupils dilate a little bit before returning to their normal shape, gaze intense with its focus on Phainon.

"And pretty," Phainon mutters under his breath, barely audible.

"Of course the start of your relationship would be an attempted murder," Ptolemy remarks flatly as he enters the room and snaps him out of it, Phainon's gaze wandering to the scholar. He comes back around with three tomes clutched loosely in his hand. He swipes them over Hephaestion's head as he goes, mussing the hair up and making their friend swat at him angrily. "As if anything could ever be normal with you two."

Mydei rolls his eyes, releasing Phainon's finger just to lick his lip as he turns to reassure Leonnius that no, he won't ever attack anyone without a reason. His foot bumps into Phainon's beneath the table, Leonnius anxiously saying that if Phainon could have done something so wrong that it earned him Mydei's wrath, then the rest of them aren't safe either. Phainon watches as Mydei laughs quietly at that, but he's too busy fixating on the memory of Mydei's teeth against his finger to pay attention to his reply.

Damn it.

Phainon dreads the prospect of his unruly dreams gaining another aspect of Mydei's features to fixate on, tormenting him at night and forcing him to rush to the bathroom first thing in the morning.

The markings, his chest and stomach, his back, toned legs settling between Phainon's until they're suddenly wrapped around his hips, blond hair wrapped tightly around his fingers, or pale hands buried in his own hair.

And now, the fangs. Phainon did such a good job steering his attention away from them before Mydei decided to put up this little display.

Phainon sighs and rests his face in his palms with resignation. Surely, this will pass one day.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"—and then the string snapped," Hephaestion relays with an animated gesture, nearly bouncing in his seat. Mydei lets out a snort, the kind that slips out without meaning to, and he leans down on the table to bury his mouth in his forearms. Hephaestion's grin widens as he continues, "Leonnius got pale so quickly that it had Perdikkas concerned."

"Perdikkas gets concerned if we so much as stub a toe," Phainon replies drily. "Nearly had a heart attack when Ptolemy fell from a ladder." He watches the golden eyes crinkle with humor, a light blush high on his cheekbones from chuckling at the story.

"Okay, yeah, but," Hephaestion huffs, fingers tapping against the table in Phainon and Mydei's kitchen. "Afterward, he ran to prepare some calming brews for Peucesta because he's never seen him so angry."

Alright, that's a little funny. "He never even offered Ptolemy those," Phainon says with amusement, glancing back at Hephaestion. Ptolemy probably takes something for stress anyway. He once said he should be on a different kind of medication, but that it slows his brain too much.

Hephaestion snorts, balancing on the back legs of his chair. "Ptolemy would have told him to shove those leaves up his own ass and try boiling them there."

Another poorly muffled strangled noise from their resident prince, a continuous one this time.

And, really, neither the story nor the joke is even remotely hilarious enough to evoke such a strong reaction from Mydei. Perhaps he's simply in the mood today, or maybe he's experiencing the giggles for the first time. Phainon knows that in that case, every single word must seem to be the funniest thing ever uttered. Phainon doesn't know, doesn't really care what the reason is. It still makes both him and Hephaestion zero in on the reaction with laser focus, heart picking up the pace.

Mydei laughing so freely is a rare sight.

He deliberately snorts at things he finds amusing, chuckles here and there, and most often huffs out a breath when something is a little funny. He surprisingly smiles a lot, grins somewhat less. But a full laughter is such a sporadic occurrence that it has both Phainon and Hephaestion thoroughly captivated. Mydei's shoulders shake as he tries to keep it together as best as he can. It seems more intense than his usual laughter, too.

The two of them glance at each other at the same time, a starstruck expression on Hephaestion's face no doubt mirrored on Phainon's own. For once, instead of arguing, it feels like they're exactly on the same page.

"And, and then Peucesta grabbed him by the shirt," Hephaestion continues with all that much fervor, brown eyes glimmering. "Didn't even really yank or anything. Leonnius' knees gave out instantly, looked ready to faint."

"Did he fall or just dangle in Peucesta's grip?" Phainon asks with a laugh of his own, spurring Hephaestion on.

Again, it's not even that funny. But maybe the mental image is what has Mydei cracking up, sitting up straight and gasping for air. His hand goes up to cover up the open-mouthed grin, but it gets lost on the way, hovering uselessly in the air as Mydei continues laughing.

"Just dangled," Hephaestion confirms eagerly.

Phainon nods, letting his gaze catalogue every single detail. Mydei's lips are stretched wide, the small fangs on clear display, eyes almost slipped shut with the way they crinkle. Face flushed in warm pink, strands of hair falling messily across it. His bare stomach is visibly spasming with the effort to regain control, but his laughter wins the battle, leaving him shaky. It's such a pretty sight.

"With how short Leonnius is, and how tall Peucesta is, it's a wonder he didn't develop a fear of heights," Phainon muses. It's such a stupid joke, it barely makes sense. He knows Mydei would normally roll his eyes at it, huff if he was feeling charitable.

But Mydei's laugh cuts short, and he wheezes a few times, gasping for air. He seems startled himself at the apparent lack of sound. Phainon chuckles a little, figuring it might be time to tone it down before Mydei gets overwhelmed or something. He doubts he would, but sometimes it's hard to tell. He would rather not risk tainting an experience this innocent.

Instead, he looks to Hephaestion and finds him grinning softly, chin propped up on his palm. Their eyes meet again as Mydei slowly calms himself down with short intakes of breath. Phainon sticks his tongue out, kinda proud of both of them for achieving this feat in making Mydei laugh so much, and watches Hephaestion snort. Brown eyes still soft as they settle on Phainon.

"You're coming up with something bothersome," Mydei states, lying on his stomach as he regards Phainon calmly.

"Wondering if I can get Peucesta to dangle Leonnius in the air again," Phainon muses, feeling just a tiny bit guilty as he considers framing Leonnius for something. It's not like Peucesta wouldn't forgive him, or that Phainon wouldn't have come clean in the end.

Mydei snorts and shakes his head, taking the clip off his braid with one hand and blindly setting it on the chair. "Leave him be. He's already scared of everything."

"Was it really that funny?" Phainon asks instead of giving up on the idea. He wants to see Mydei laughing like that again, regardless of the consequences. Peucesta likes Leonnius too much to ever truly get angry at him anyway. Well, angry for more than five minutes.

"Not really," Mydei shrugs, but he's still smiling. "I'm not sure what about it set me off. But then you two kept just adding onto it, and I don't know. Last time I felt like this, Ptolemy barged into the Council meeting after oversleeping and immediately argued with Archidamia in an attempt to convince her she's in the wrong."

Phainon lets out a short laugh at the reminder of the situation. Mydei kept a hand clamped tight over his mouth as he openly watched the spectacle, shaking as Phainon laughed loudly at each hurried, ridiculous argument Ptolemy made up on the spot, entitled and wholly uncaring. Maybe that one would be easier to replicate, and he can only hope that Mydei lets himself go in the heat of the moment. One way or another, he desperately wishes to witness that breathless laughter once more.

Even if he's not sure once will be enough.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon pants harshly, the tip of his sword sinking into the abdomen of his opponent just the slightest bit, right under the rib. He stopped himself in time before it could get in too deep, but it still draws the blood out. Mydei has his spear placed firmly by the neck, sharp point pushing the chin up to avoid being pricked by it.

Phainon has the urge to laugh breathlessly. He feels delirious with victory. So much time, blood, and effort for this one moment. Just one step forward on the path of improvement, the end goal slowly materializes within reach.

Archidamia remains in her position; one leg bent where she froze in the process of getting up, the weapon loose in her grip. Neither of them speaks, waiting to see if she can find her way out of this like all the previous times. Phainon sees no opening for that to happen, but you never know. Sure enough, a loud clank echoes as her weapon hits the stone pavement, their uncoordinated fight having moved away from the training grounds due to its intensity. Phainon and Mydei still don't move a muscle, keeping their blades ready to react at a moment's notice.

"Congratulations, Young Lords," Archidamia says eventually, her approval visible from both her tone and expression. Evidently proud of them, of Phainon, and Phainon's head spins at the prospect. "I yield."

She pushes their weapons away without fear and gets to her feet, showing no signs of a sprained ankle that Phainon is sure she got throughout the fight. And that's the only more serious injury he really kept track of, traces of red both on his blade and hands.

More importantly, his heart thuds in his chest, sword disappearing in the air and leaving his hands empty. His eyes find Mydei's, the clear delight lighting them up with the crinkles from his smile, making Phainon grin widely in response. The bystanders cheer loudly, shouting with excitement and encouragement. Mentions of the Kremnoan glory. Phainon bites on his lip painfully, inhaling sharply at the staggering feeling of being included.

Wait, hold on. Young Lords, she said.

Plural?

"You—" Phainon whirls around to her with widened eyes, and Archidamia is already looking back at him with a genuine smile of her own. "I— What?"

"After everything, you're still surprised, child? You tirelessly walk this path along Lord Mydeimos, yet you're not prepared to gain the same renown?" She shakes her head with fondness.

Phainon reels at what he's seeing. Hearing.

He knows the two of them will clash with their opinions yet again this very weekend; he is aware she is brutal and holds no regard for lives lost, the pain inflicted. But this woman, the most skilled person in the entire settlement, who treated him so harshly at the beginning. She has warmth in her gaze and humor on her lips, and it's directed at Phainon. She places her hand on top of Phainon's head, not ruffling his hair because that would be too soft an action for her, but keeping a comforting pressure against the crown of his head. She has to lift her arm up to do it, standing almost at an equal height to the two of them. She doesn't seem perturbed by the fact that they will soon outgrow her.

"Your laurels are long overdue, boys," Archidamia says as Mydei finally steps closer to them both, having busied himself with giving his attention to the crowd in victory to allow Archidamia and Phainon to have their small exchange. Her eyes gain some warmth even further as she glances at Mydei, a feat once thought impossible. Phainon is certain it's reserved for this one occasion. "And it's only the beginning of your achievements. Lord Mydeimos. Lord Phainon."

Her hand falls away, and she takes a step back to give them space. Moving to address the enthusiastic people who only seem to multiply as the news of Archidamia being defeated by the two teenagers has already spread to anyone who's willing to listen.

If Phainon had a clearer mind, he would have pulled Mydei into a proper hug. But his mind is still reeling, and he remains rooted in place. So it's Mydei who leans right into his personal space that might as well be Mydei's own by now, and presses their foreheads together affectionately. Phainon feels his eyes cross as he attempts to focus on the blurry image of gold irises, but it disappears before he can find out if it's doable.

"I suspect she will allow us to leave for Aedes Elysiae in the next weeks," Mydei says quietly, barely audible through the shouts that are finally dying down. He wraps his fingers around Phainon's wrist, the cold metal of his gauntlets against the warm skin, and smiles.

Phainon laughs breathlessly and lets himself be dragged away to Perdikkas or Ptolemy, ready for the praise that's sure to come, and to pester them into planning the future trip.
