chapters.title: Chapter 13: and raise their hackles
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

A week and a half into their journey, they walk into a forest. It's no big deal, Phainon has traveled through forests throughout the last few years. Ones with deciduous trees, or coniferous, or both. Wide, small, thin, tall, short.

But in all those forests, the trees were never quite so close together to block the moonlight again. None of them had to carry the torches all throughout the trek, being careful not to ignite everything around them as they went. The leaves crunch under their steps, and Phainon is mildly nauseous.

He tells himself he feels okay.

Chapter Notes

Phainon does an excellent job of breathing in and out to the count of four. It's as calming an action as it is sleep-inducing. At night, he likes pressing his fingers against any of the pulse points on Mydei's body and counting the beats when he cannot calm down from a nightmare. This reminds him of it, somewhat. It's why he chose this as the strategy to keep himself grounded during their separation. He's been told that Mydei, meanwhile, has a tendency to trace his own red markings on the spots Phainon most frequently runs his fingers over. It shouldn't have made him smile like an idiot when he learned of it.

However, even if his calming tactic is associated with bedtime, he cannot just fall asleep. That kind of defeats the purpose of consciously making progress in this thing.

Perdikkas whisked Mydei away for a check-up as an excuse for passing the time. Phainon is not entirely sure what's there to run tests for; Mydei's body

is as flawless as can be, thanks to his curse. Blessing, as far as Phainon is concerned.

Hephaestion remained at Phainon's side this time around, the music easily carrying past the buildings as Peucesta gives a performance not too far away. They lapsed into silence about an hour ago, and neither made an effort to keep the conversation going. Phainon's head felt too stuffy to come up with a new subject, and as Hephaestion loves to go against him in every possible manner, in this matter, he follows Phainon's lead unquestionably.

It's a little touching.

Mind blank, Phainon glances at Hephaestion. The teen gazes up at the sky, eyes jumping listlessly over the same stars that shine above them every day. Normally, the two of them argue ceaselessly. From something as simple as snarking at each other and rolling their eyes to throwing insults and starting fights. Phainon has never wondered why that might be. Ptolemy once said it's because they are too similar, making Phainon physically cringe at the sheer prospect of being alike Hephaestion.

But there's no denying that they are a bit similar.

And now that he thinks about it…

Hephaestion likes Mydei better than him; it's no secret. He doesn't hate Phainon, nor does he dislike him. They are still best friends, Hephaestion second only to Mydei. But it's tense sometimes.

He squints at his own hands, recalling countless interactions between Hephaestion and Mydei. Hephaestion's happier mood, lingering glances, inserting himself as much as possible, complimenting Mydei so easily and so often.

Isn't that… sort of familiar?

Phainon feels most peaceful and content with Mydei by his side. There are times he cannot tear his eyes away from him. He makes sure to take an

interest in anything Mydei likes. And he doesn't shy away from letting people know of Mydei's incredible skills or unquestionable beauty.

"You like Mydei," slips out of his mouth before he can stop it.

He just barely resists the urge to slap a hand over his own mouth, a vague recollection of Hephaestion doing the same after calling Mydei pretty resurfacing in his brain. Alright. That, that makes sense now. He didn't even think to question it back then, but in all fairness, people often acknowledge that Mydei is growing up to be an attractive man.

"Duh," Hephaestion says, flipping his hand in the air when Phainon glances over. He shifts, grinning cheekily at Phainon. "Can't say the same about you."

"That's almost flattering, coming from a person so annoying," Phainon replies without missing a beat, smirking when Hephaestion scoffs. He readies himself to snark back, but Phainon continues his initial thought before he can. "You like him more than friends."

The words are awkward, making Phainon unsure if he's wording it correctly. But that's the best he's got, so he continues staring at Hephaestion as the sentence sinks in, and a light blush spreads across his cheekbones.

"So what if I like Mydei?" Hephaestion huffs, crossing his arms defensively and nearly glaring at Phainon. "I'm not gonna stop just because you do as well."

Phainon's brain screeches to a halt. He didn't mention his feelings for Mydei. Heat mercilessly crawls up his neck. "…Is it so obvious?"

Hephaestion's almost-glare melts away into a stare that makes it clear he thinks Phainon might be the least intelligent person in all of Amphoreus. "What, your feelings? Are you serious?"

Phainon groans, covering his face with his hands. He tries to focus on Peucesta's music in the hope that it will lessen the mortification at someone

else being aware of his affections. He undoubtedly resembles a particularly ugly tomato. He hates his complexion.

Hephaestion sighs loudly, and when Phainon dares to look at him through the gaps between his fingers, he sees him propping his chin on one palm as his elbow rests against his knee. His gaze is partly resigned, but also mildly irritated. Shouldn't Phainon feel irritated at this brat having feelings for Mydei? Why is he the only one so embarrassed?

"And what now?" Hephaestion mutters into his hand.

"It's, it's not a big deal to me," Phainon forces out, fully aware just how big a deal it is. "He's not interested. Why would he be? I won't compromise our goals and dynamic just because I happen to find him attractive. And generally… nice."

Phainon winces at his own words, swiping his foot across the steps leading up to some house that they're sitting on. He's hardly going to express the entirety of his feelings to someone when it's the first time he's even acknowledged it outside of his head. Even if, it's not like he can. How does one describe the intensity of what he feels for Mydei? There is no dictionary that could help him with that. What little he knows of Kremnoan gives him the impression it'd be the opposite of helpful.

They are fourteen, and Phainon fears what this already too-big feeling might grow into in the coming years. He cannot imagine it ever dying out, and that means it can only evolve into something larger. He wonders if Hephaestion—

Familiar voices reach them, and Phainon perks up immediately. He watches Mydei leading Perdikkas and Ptolemy toward them, walking two steps ahead. Phainon has a pathetic thought of being glad he hasn't got a tail. He remembers Snowy wagging his tail excitedly whenever he saw that one cat sunbathing on a windowsill. It looked like the appendage would have fallen off due to the intensity of the motion. Ridiculously, he now understands the dog's excitement.

He shifts to point out the new arrivals to Hephaestion, but he only finds him hunched in on himself a little bit, gnawing on the tip of his thumb as he frowns intently at the ground. Phainon's brows twitch in confusion, but before he can question the change of mood, he gets distracted by their friends.

"See, this can be done perfectly appropriately if you approach the issue steadily and peacefully," Ptolemy says loudly with a broad gesture to no one in particular, but Perdikkas still nods along. "It's crucial. Emphasizing the choice of affected parties and proceeding only when they are willing, going at their pace, reassuring them that nothing is wrong with them. What's so difficult to comprehend?"

Mydei speeds up somewhat, striding to them in a much faster pace while the other two hang back. He halts right before them, one hand lowered and stretched out toward Phainon to pull him up from the ground. Phainon looks at it for less than a second as he decides he doesn't want to leave just yet. He takes the offered hand, but instead of letting Mydei drag him up, Phainon yanks him down. Mydei allows himself to be pulled down without struggle, directing his fall so that he lands gracefully, right between Phainon and Hephaestion.

"People love taking shortcuts," Perdikkas comments after a short moment, gathering his hair back and frowning when he discovers he doesn't have a hairtie on his wrist. Ptolemy hands him one over absentmindedly. Why he's got it at all is beyond Phainon. "Thanks. They are impatient when the process takes too long. I often see it in the patients during rehabilitation. Most of them want to skip all the hard months of rebuilding their bodies and head straight into the fray. It's impossible without making matters worse."

Mydei glances Hepaestion's way only to round back to Phainon, head tilting a few degrees to the right. Phainon shakes his head, perhaps too frantically, in response. He doesn't rightly know what Hephaestion's mood may be about, but if they attempt to prod him, the prior conversation may resurface. That's the last thing Phainon wants to happen. Mydei narrows his eyes at him suspiciously, but his thinking that Phainon has done something is still preferable to him finding out.

"I will laugh in Archidamia's face about this in the distant future. See them?" Ptolemy garners their attention yet again, pointing at them with way too much self-satisfaction. "Perfectly functional."

The healer gives them a doubtful once-over. "I wouldn't go that far," he says flatly.

"Perfectly functional in comparison to what we started out with over half a year ago," Ptolemy amends, not one bit discouraged.

Perdikkas lets out a short laugh, leaning his arm on the shorter male's shoulder. "That's more like it."

Ptolemy openly grins up at him, not making a move to shrug him off. "Maybe if she didn't discourage them by using force from the get-go, we could have done this much sooner and with fewer consequences," he muses aloud.

Yeah, Archidamia's methods… Left a lot to ask for. Phainon has long since made his peace with the outright hostile approach toward his and Mydei's behavior. Archidamia has an uneven, rough scar marring her skin as a permanent reminder of her mistakes. The knowledge has served as a comfort in the first two years, a reassurance that she will not forcefully separate them again.

"You speak as if we are a special project of yours," Phainon comments, lacing it with traces of dismay. His knee knocks against Mydei's by habit before he straightens his legs out entirely. "An experiment."

Ptolemy glances at him, gauging how serious he might be. Phainon keeps his face carefully blank, and bites on the inside of his cheek when Ptolemy's expression turns conflicted, wondering if he crossed a line with his overly scientific approach. Phainon has improved in being more believable when he doesn't mean his words and in keeping his expression neutral. He halfheartedly hopes he will become better than Mydei, but it's doubtful due to his friend's natural ability to disguise deception behind a dry tone and blank face.

"He's messing with you," Mydei says flatly, not acknowledging the glare Phainon sends his way for cutting the little experiment of his own short.

Ptolemy immediately relaxes, rolling his eyes when Perdikkas snorts. "I do have notes I wish to compare with the psychology experts in the Grove of Epiphany one day," he mumbles reluctantly.

Phainon hums, thinking he's got a point. There cannot be many cases of people as closely interconnected as Phainon and Mydei are. It should be treated as an achievement to take part in bringing them into a vague scale of normalcy.

"Congratulations," Perdikkas finally addresses them with a smile, preventing the conversation from derailing further. "You lasted six hours. You're doing exceptionally well."

And it felt like the most boring six hours of Phainon's life. That's not to say he doesn't appreciate Hephaestion's company; he started out the day with Ptolemy, switched to Leonnius in an hour, and then decided to stick by Hephaestion at some point. It's just that spending an entire day actively avoiding Mydei is the furthest thing from fun he can think of.

"That's a fourth of the current goal, isn't it?" Hephaestion asks, and Phainon leans back to stare at him around Mydei's back. He is met with steady brown eyes, not a sign of his earlier stress.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon doesn't bother keeping in the snort that tears out of him at the sight of an awe-struck look on Hephaestion's face as Archidamia regards him with the full intensity she carries herself with, like a soldier. Mydei smiles, nudging Phainon when Hephaestion almost stutters out in response before catching himself. Archidamia doesn't appreciate a lack of confidence and losing composure.

They just witnessed an official acknowledgement of Hephaestion's skills and agreement for him to participate in the wars. It will take effect after they come back from their little journey to Aedes Elysiae. They leave in just under a week, and Phainon is mildly surprised Archidamia didn't wait until they returned.

"It's a reward," Mydei says quietly from his side so that he won't interrupt the conversation happening a few steps ahead of them. "Hephaestion has faltered only once in his training and kept up with steady improvement despite the illness. He learned to rebel against the instructors in more subtle ways that don't paint him as insubordinate. And she saw him return alongside us, covered in the blood of the enemies and no sight of injury, regret, or anxiety."

"She likes him," Phainon sums up simply. It's no wonder. She holds affection for Mydei, and she grew to tolerate Phainon until he somehow managed to warm her up to him. She's more distant toward Hephaestion, but she puts her faith in him nonetheless. "Why didn't she let him go earlier, though? He's been ready for a while." He thinks of the boring Council members droning on about never wasting the manpower or the opportunity to expand the valuable soldiers' expertise. "It's a waste of resources, looking at it from her angle."

Mydei shrugs. "Probably so that it wouldn't set up a precedent. There are special circumstances where we are concerned; we are Chrysos Heirs. He isn't. Can't have impatient children running into a war because they think they are good enough. Look at Aias."

Phainon wrinkles his nose. "Fair enough."

Aias is good. His abilities certainly shine brightly with the rapid improvement at every step. He's got the drive that promises a quick climb in ranks one day. But right now, he's nowhere near ready for expeditions. And there's no doubt he would have attempted forcing himself into one if he caught sight of the tiniest wriggle room for an argument. He still might, when news of this reaches him.

In the distance, Hephaestion nods rapidly. His hands are clasped tightly behind his back, and it's hilarious to watch him attempt not to stumble over his response. He will grow used to Archidamia's intensity one day. Hopefully. Although his reaction seems to stem from clear admiration rather than anxiety, as it does for most others. Phainon doesn't even attempt to comprehend that.

Mydei elbows him when Phainon laughs loudly at Hephaestion's half-aborted curtsy, which is swiftly switched for a proper salute. Archidamia takes her leave after acknowledging the gesture, and Hephaestion walks in their direction, face entirely red and eyes dazed.

Despite his first thought being to tease him, Phainon smiles proudly as they both congratulate their friend.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"When will you stop killing yourself?" Is the first thing Phainon snarls at Mydei when he notices him getting up. He is panting sharply, hair one giant mess, and gaze feral as he falls into the stance. Like he wasn't dead five minutes ago, all to put down a few Titankin quicker. Without a single soldier to save as an excuse in sight.

"When my body finally takes the hint and stays dead, Deliverer," Mydei barks at him. He takes off in the direction of the nearest enemy without so much as a glance at Phainon.

And Phainon, left standing amid the dead bodies, feels his veins boil at the careless words. When his body takes the hint and stays dead. Is he even aware of what that sounds like?

Phainon grits his teeth, catching a rapid movement at the corner of his eye. He pivots and brings his longsword up to slash cleanly through the

Titankin, glaring as the body separates into two and creates a loud thud as it falls to the ground, the dust rising. He breathes in, then out. It doesn't help.

He takes a page out of Mydei's book and throws himself into the battle, discarding any and all thoughts that fight to make themselves known on the subject of Mydei's desire to die. It's enough that his body feels like it's about to set itself ablaze. Phainon doesn't let the anger die down, lets it simmer as long as it wants to.

The assignment—the last one of theirs before they have to set out for Aedes Elysiae in three days—was not far from the settlement. Hardly more than a three-hour walk, clearing the location of the raised Titankin activity before the monsters could reach the settlement or any nearby town. Milios, even. Not a single word is said as they trek back with Leonnius nervously trailing behind them. He disappears the very moment they step through the gates to the settlement.

They exchange tense pleasantries with some of the passersby, refusing to directly interact with each other. People stare at them strangely, some with worry, while others with humor. Phainon doesn't care. He is still riding on the mixture of worry and intense anger, highlighted by the sheer helplessness. He thought this particular problem had been reevaluated by Mydei enough to take more caution, if not resolved entirely. Apparently not. It's one thing to protect someone, it's another to do it out of convenience. It's been a while since he last threw his life on the line, and even longer since the ugly stubbornness reared its head.

Phainon doesn't care. Or, he doesn't want to care.

He heard somewhere that if you pretend with enough conviction, it will become reality. Maybe it was Ptolemy; he likes his quotes. Or maybe he was ridiculing the notion. No matter, Phainon is willing to try regardless.

So, he strides through their house and gets to their bedroom on steady legs, hoping he appears sufficiently pissed off and sure of himself as he desperately holds onto those two fragments of his current emotions.

Phainon yanks the door shut, taking satisfaction in the loud bang the action produces.

The satisfaction doesn't last long.

Phainon feels raw to the core, stumbling into the bathroom to scrub himself clean of the dirt and blood. Watching his pale skin turn bright red with the force he presses his fingernails against it, he finds himself glad for these separation exercises. He can lock himself away with his fear and rage, be petty about Mydei's disregard for his own well-being as he often wished to be. Be it as it may, it's not a secret he is weak to Mydei himself. One glance filled with regret, a hand cautiously brushing against Phainon's arm, hunched over shoulders, mouth opening just to close without a sound, and Phainon is a goner.

Always the one to take the unspoken regret and accept it as the apology it is not. He is hopeless as he tirelessly closes the small distance between them and erases the charged tension penetrating the whole house. Well, not this time.

Because this time, Phainon can stand to be in a whole other room than Mydei. Doesn't have to witness the effect this might have on his best friend, leading to Phainon breaking like a dry twig. He heads to bed, ignoring the door that seems to be radiating an accusatory energy. Whatever. Phainon won't give in to his own brain trying to convince him to step out. Even if he itches to get his hand under Mydei's shirt, to ensure there's no lasting damage he might be hiding. There never is. That doesn't mean Phainon's anxiety accepts the concept.

Sitting with his back to the wall and knees raised up, elbows propped up on them, he listens to the clanking of Mydei moving around the kitchen, preparing something. Phainon's stomach rumbles embarrassingly at the thought of food alone. He scowls down at it, aware he's not eating anything today. He's not stepping out while Mydei is still in the hall. He may leave and grab something to fill up, but only once Mydei decides that's enough of stubbornness for the day and heads to the guest bedroom to catch some sleep. And after they sleep this off, they won't be so angry at each other. They will speak normally, and they will leave for Aedes Elysiae soon

enough, and they will have peace until the next time Mydei suffers too many injuries for Phainon's comfort. A flawless plan.

Except Phainon immediately feels restless. He struggles to ignore the pull to go and check on Mydei, make sure he's truly fine. He is sleepy, but it feels wrong to sleep without his friend by his side. There's a dull ache at his temples.

With a practiced motion, he lets his weapon materialize and gets to cleaning it. It's one of the largest swords he owns, not quite a greatsword yet, but slowly getting there. The blade stains their bedsheets with gore and dirt, but Phainon doesn't care. If Mydei decides to storm in despite his anger, and it pisses him off further, good. If not, Phainon will have time to change the sheets anyway.

Annoyance rising at his thoughts alone, he grabs a random cloth from one of the drawers and gets to work.

As he performs the practiced movements, he finds himself calming down with every minute passing. His mind grows blissfully blank as he breathes in and out evenly, taking care to wipe off the tiniest of specks. It's better than any meditation tactic he could have attempted. Save for maybe keeping a finger against Mydei's pulse, or watching his chest rise and fall rhythmically when he's asleep.

Floorboards creak right outside the door, loud and deliberate. Phainon's hands freeze, and he glances in that direction. Mydei can move across any space soundlessly without putting any effort into it. Phainon waits, growing slightly suspicious when there's no other sound and the door stays closed. And then, another creak.

Phainon blinks, the cloth loose in his fingers. He takes a glimpse at the clock, frowning when he notices it's already been two hours since he started up on his task, so engrossed in it that—

Oh.

It's been two hours since they last interacted in any way, with no verbal agreement to actually separate. Just their combined stubbornness. Perhaps anger and distraction are two of the best tactics to solve their problem. Which is just one of their issues, clearly.

Phainon releases a small sigh and reaches over to drag the chair slightly to the side, making sure its legs screech against the floor. He watches the door, wondering how his action is going to be taken. Mydei might interpret this as a temporary truce because of Phainon playing into the subtle request. Or perhaps he only required a confirmation that Phainon is more or less alright.

It turns out to be the latter, as there is another much quieter creak when Mydei seemingly leaves and goes to another section of the house.

Okay, then. Phainon is happy all on his own just where he is. He grabs the cloth again and resumes scrubbing the sword, from top to bottom. He ignores the fact that he can see his own reflection in the blade.

It happens two more times, the loud creaking and Phainon absentmindedly making a noise before going back to his task. He's not sure how much time passes exactly. All he knows by the time he's finished is that his fingers feel raw, like they haven't in a long time, and he has never seen a sword more spotless.

He gets up from the bed, swaying as he stretches up on his tiptoes and heads to the bathroom to take a shower, taking the bedsheets with him. He goes through his routine quickly and thoughtlessly, closing his eyes to avoid looking in the mirror as he brushes his teeth on his own. Slowly, he goes back to their room and makes the bed, adjusting the fresh sheets.

It's only then that he glances at the clock again and has a startling realization that it's been nearly eight hours. They returned in the middle of the Action Hour, and it's now nearing the end of the Curtain-Fall Hour. He curses lowly as he stares out of the window at the dim lights. He fell into some sort of blank space, and he decides on the spot that he doesn't like it. It's scary, the hours passing without so much as registering in his brain. Not even really being sure if his surroundings are real. Or he himself. Just going through a motion and having his mind float along.

They need to get up in about two hours. Well. Phainon has fought through sleep deprivation before; it's not that big of a deal. Though that's usually his body running on adrenaline alone. He sighs, wincing as his stomach aches in a familiar way, demanding sustenance now that Phainon is lucid.

He scratches his head, weighing his options. He could wait until morning. But what if they're still angry at each other then? Phainon doesn't want to lose the argument and break the silent treatment with his need to thank him for the breakfast. Mydei must already be asleep in the other room, so Phainon can just sneak into the kitchen and grab something to eat. And then he will leave the room in the very last moment, forcing Mydei to hurry up after him.

They will settle tomorrow—today—for certain, no question about it. But Phainon refuses to give in so easily.

Mind made up, he goes to the door, pressing his hand over his mouth when he yawns. Maybe he should sleep for an hour? But then he risks oversleeping, and Mydei will have to wake him up. Besides, it's not like he can fall asleep without Mydei by his side, so the dilemma is actually solved before it can become an issue.

The door slides open silently. Not for the first time, Phainon is glad for the fact that they regularly oil the hinges to keep them that way. Makes it easier to sneak around if need be. Which is not often, but still. Phainon takes a singular step into the corridor and freezes.

There's a body leaning against the wall right next to the doorframe, head slumped over so that the cheek is pressed against the shoulder. Was he any sleepier, Phainon would have tripped over Mydei's leg. His eyes jump across his friend's figure, suddenly wide awake as he attempts to identify the issue. Most importantly, his chest rises and falls in an even pattern. He is dressed in more comfortable clothes, legs bent and slightly sprawled out, like he didn't exactly intend for them to end up in that position. His face is relaxed, eyelids slipped shut, lips parted.

A plate with waffles appears to be set aside.

Phainon's gaze travels from the uneaten meal to his friend numerous times. Was that meant for him?

Phainon crouches down, swiping one hand over his own face and keeping it there when it reaches just below his nose. Mydei didn't sleep in the guest room. Mydei tried busying himself with something just like Phainon did, and checked up on him in a non-intrusive way. Mydei made food for him. Mydei fell asleep while, presumably, patiently waiting for Phainon to get over it.

And Phainon—

Deep inside, Phainon is still so angry, but.

How was he supposed not to love Mydei? How was he supposed not to… Fall in love? Anyone would, if they spent enough time with Mydei. When Mydei makes an effort to show his quiet care, even in the middle of an argument.

It's not even really a matter to ponder on, as Phainon immediately decides that he cannot just leave him like this. Maybe he can be somewhat of a bigger man this time around. He has to grow up and be bigger than Mydei either way. Titans, he's tired. Maybe they will both sleep in.

Phainon shifts closer to Mydei, carefully slipping one arm beneath the teen's knees, and keeping the other one behind Mydei's back to stabilize him. It's laughingly easy to pick him up. Phainon cannot tell if the action is so effortless due to his trained muscles or if Mydei is just that light, weighing barely anything at all. He doubts it's the latter; Mydei's body is nothing if not coiled muscles built on top of one another. Phainon should pay better attention to their physicals when Perdikkas reads off their weights.

Mydei doesn't stir as Phainon carries him over to their bed. Phainon tries not to think too hard about how he is undoubtedly the only person in the world who can manage manhandling asleep Mydei without him rousing or, in the worst case scenario, have red crystals encasing his neck within a

second. His heart still skips a beat. He feels honored to have earned that amount of unwavering trust from a once feral prince.

Rounding back to the corridor, Phainon muses quietly in the privacy of his mind. Mydei can usually push through two solid days of no sleep without the need for adrenaline. Could it be boredom that got to him? Just as he can easily last without sleep, Mydei has also been known to doze off anywhere if he feels safe enough. Phainon picks up the plate, then returns to the bed. His mind blanks a little as he watches Mydei sprawled out on the bed, one arm having grabbed Phainon's pillow already, and swung over it.

Phainon doesn't think he will ever get enough of simply watching Mydei, existing by his side. They will get over the separation thing and make sure they can at least function without each other for some period of time, but then it's not like they have to leave each other at all afterward. Right? It's just to prove they can if the circumstances call for it.

He climbs into the bed with the plate, nudging the pillow away and sitting in its place. He grabs Mydei's hand and gently places it across his lap instead. It proves to work just as well.

Phainon eats his cold breakfast that must have been intended to be served as dinner, yet the taste remains as perfect as ever. Except for the times Mydei is being petty and messes up the food on purpose. He must have thought this issue was too serious if he didn't do it. Maybe the food was supposed to be a peace offering.

It's difficult not to let his emotions dissipate entirely when Mydei shuffles closer to him, still asleep. Phainon chews on his honey-and-pomegranate waffles and attempts to glare at his unconscious friend. He sighs and chooses to glare at the ceiling instead. There is still that intense anger lurking at the pit of his stomach, immune to the sweetness of his meal.

Traces of it never fade, but Phainon taught himself to effectively ignore them over the years. He indulges in it when he's deep in the fight, only to snuff it out the very moment it's over. Right now, he digs it up and clings to the heavy and disgusting emotion. He cannot let go of this just yet. Not after what Mydei said.

Phainon zones out after he's done eating, plate set away on the chair. He stares out of the window, barely registering the lights growing stronger as Entry Hour approaches. It's only when Mydei's fingers flex against the fabric of Phaion's shorts that serve as pajamas and Phainon refocuses.

"I don't do it on purpose," Mydei says, barely above a whisper. Phainon glances down, face kept as neutral as it can be. Mydei's eyes stare directly into his, sleep shaken off in a matter of minutes in favor of confidence. Always so direct. "And I don't believe I've done anything wrong. I was carrying out my duty."

Phainon shouldn't have bothered holding onto that anger, as it ignites and blazes high, leaving him feeling uncomfortably hot at the intensity of it. It chokes him up, squeezing his throat tight. Of course Mydei wouldn't see an issue with anything that transpired. Not the dying, not the throwing himself right back into it, not the words snarled out.

"'Takes a hint and stays dead'," Phainon repeats tiredly, swallowing hard as he has to force the words out. "Do you have any idea what that sentence implies?" His voice cracks, and he clears his throat, annoyed at his body for betraying his emotions so easily. He starts thinking that he may be overreacting, but he chooses to stick with it. Whether he is right in his anger or not, he doesn't want Mydei dying unnecessarily, no matter what. He doesn't care about being selfish over this.

Mydei winces at the reminder, but he remains adamant about his stance. "I'm not suicidal, if that's what you're talking circles around. Could it even be considered that, when I'm fully aware I will never stay dead?" He shifts to lie on his stomach, holding himself up on the elbows and watching the pillow, which Phainon returned to its rightful place.

"Yes, you single-minded fool, if underneath all that you hope each of your falls will bring forth the time you do remain dead," Phainon tells him harshly, not faltering when Mydei's eyes snap up to him. "You cannot die, Mydei. By all Titans, do not tempt Thanatos more than necessary. I'm not above begging."

I will never forgive you if you truly die, goes unsaid. Phainon thinks he could forgive Mydei for anything in the world, but that's one thing that's off limits. He meets Mydei's wide gaze, and when his friend looks away first, Phainon gets an impression that his despair may be conveying his thoughts regardless.

Mydei pulls himself up to a seating position, finally grasping the gravity of the situation. Realizing Phainon isn't simply putting up a protest over his injuries. "I'm not— I don't," he cuts himself off twice, voice trailing off. He closes his eyes and takes a fortifying breath. "It's not my intention," he says on an exhale, eyes finding Phainon's again. There is the smallest amount of panic in them, mouth set in a thin line.

Not enough.

"Mydei," he calls through gritted teeth, eyes narrowing. "What do I have to do so that you will cease this self-sacrificial pursuit of death? Do I have to nearly kill myself for you to understand?" He feels desperate enough to do it. If it meant Mydei wouldn't willingly put himself at the threshold of death each time it serves his purpose, he would. "Don't test me."

"No," is the immediate and loud response, gaze growing wild. Now it's getting through to him. His hands grip the sheets tightly, face growing pale at the sheer prospect of it. "No, never. I don't—" he cuts himself off to inhale sharply, centering himself. He is more collected when he speaks next, no longer fumbling with his words. Taking control of the situation, like he usually does. "This causes you too much distress. I must apologize. I will do all that I can to take better care in the future."

It's not exactly what Phainon wants. Which is for Mydei to understand the value his life holds. But he will take what he can get for now, if it means less dying. Phainon dreads the very possibility of the generosity of Mydei's curse running out.

"Okay," Phainon acquiesces quietly with a nod. He runs one hand through his stiff hair. It dried weirdly after his shower. "Okay."

The silence remains tense, but Phainon is too exhausted to care much. He yawns and doesn't bother to cover his mouth, and feels his jaw pop. If things go well, he might nap around the Action Hour. Perhaps Mydei will feel guilty enough to cover for him, force an instructor to take a day off.

"You carried me to the bed," Mydei points out the obvious, not particularly fussed about the fact. Still mildly annoyed, but for another reason. "Why haven't you slept yourself?"

"Was too angry," Phainon says, running one hand through his hair. It dried weirdly after his shower. Angry and petty. "I knew I would immediately forgive you if I woke up next to you. But I had to make you understand, or I'm not sure how the next time would have gone."

Mydei hums, biting on his lip. Phainon doesn't have it in himself to feel satisfied with the guilt written on his face. "I can give you half an hour to sleep, but I have to get up. Are you fine by yourself or...?" He trails off, question clear without the need for clarification.

"I'm not sure," Phainon admits helplessly. It's hard to decipher the state he is in right now, what with the anger finally dying down into small embers and giving way to other feelings. Not to mention the intense bout of sleepiness. He would like to think he'd be fine. He knows he very well might not be.

Mydei glances at the clock, reconsiders. "I can stay for ten minutes. I will leave to get ready if you've fallen asleep. If not, you can try again on the armchair while I'm in the kitchen."

"Alright," Phainon agrees to the plan easily, but makes no move to follow up on it. His mind feels a little heavy, like it's running behind.

"You should at least try to rest," Mydei clicks his tongue and pulls him down to lie comfortably. Fingers slot into his hair, attempting to bring order to the mess on his head. "We have to debrief with Archidamia first thing. It's the last meeting before we leave for your village."

Phainon nods in agreement, letting out another yawn that drowns out whatever response he may have given. By the time his jaw returns to its

natural state, he no longer remembers what he wanted to say. Too long fingernails scratch along Phainon's scalp, and he might as well fall asleep on the next blink with how fast the darkness consumes him.

He is woken up by a gentle jostling forty minutes later on the dot.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"Your back will give out on you if you keep this up," Perdikkas admonishes with a frown. "Come on, get up."

"No," Ptolemy tells him from the very awkward position he folded himself into while reading. Simple and to the point.

Reminds Phainon of someone else that is currently attempting to give him a black eye as Hephaestion works tirelessly to trip either of them up. Perhaps Phainon should focus on this rather than the conversation between the other two.

"Ptolemy," Perdikkas lets out an aggravated sigh, and Phainon twists away from an attempt to hold him down to watch as their physician tiredly runs a hand down his face. "You have to move. This isn't healthy."

"We're all dying young," Ptolemy says casually, hunched over a book of sorts. Phainon has come to terms with the Kremnoan philosophy by now. Everyone around him seems very keen on reaching the Nether Realm before they get too far in life, even some random guard back in Castrum Kremnos. "The back problems won't even have enough time to develop."

"You're a scholar," Perdikkas points out drily, hands on his hips. "You will live to tell the tale."

"You might think that," Ptolemy nods in agreement, turning a page with no concern. Phainon yelps as a golden metal gauntlet comes too close for

comfort. Mydei's unimpressed gaze tells him he should focus up already, but he's too interested in the proceedings. "But I've got a feeling it won't be so. Have you seen the stress those three regularly put me through? I will be lucky to live past twenty-five."

Phainon makes a grab for Hephaestion's arm as he attempts to nick him with a dagger, but the younger teen sidesteps him quickly, laughing mockingly. Phainon exhales through his nose sharply, exchanging a look with Mydei. One day, they will catch him.

"Dying young or not, you ought to be healthy so that it's not your laziness that drives you into a shallow grave," Perdikkas continues tirelessly. He grabs Ptolemy by the arm and drags him up, the blond rising to his feet without much protest except for the grabby gesture he makes at his discarded book. "We're going to spar together."

"Ptolemy's going to fight?" Phainon asks incredulously when Ptolemy follows him, and promptly gets whacked on the head when he stares for a second too long. His tibia receives a sharp kick at the same time. He yelps, "What the f— hell?"

"Focus," Mydei and Hephaestion tell him at the same time, in the same exasperated tone, and wow, Phainon really doesn't appreciate being ganged up on. It works best when Phainon and Mydei gang up on Hephaestion, thank you very much.

He spares one last glance at the retreating figures of their two oldest friends, and then glares at his two best friends. He uses the metal-encased heel of his shoe to redirect Hephaestion's next attempt at pestering him with minor injuries. He puts more effort into bearing Mydei's weight and power packed behind the gauntlet-clad blow as he parries it with his sword.

He thinks to yell at Leonnius and Pecuesta to get them into a spar as well, but he's too occupied with yanking on Hephaestion's shirt, laughing as the teen momentarily loses balance before twisting away with a scowl.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

A week and a half into their journey, they walk into a forest. It's no big deal, Phainon has traveled through forests throughout the last few years. Ones with deciduous trees, or coniferous, or both. Wide, small, thin, tall, short. On one occasion, there was a tree so thick and old that Phainon and Mydei took a moment to admire it and commit the view to memory. The branches stretched out high into the sky, and then to the sides, tangling with other trees and providing a breathtaking canopy of leaves above their heads. The roots that snaked in and out of the ground were thicker than Phainon's waist.

But in all those forests, the trees were never quite so close together to block the moonlight again. None of them had to carry the torches all throughout the trek, being careful not to ignite everything around them as they went. The leaves crunch under their steps, and Phainon is mildly nauseous.

He tells himself he feels okay.

There are seven of them, a team so experienced and capable that Phainon would feel confident hunting the Titans down with them alone. Perdikkas is the best medic the settlement has to offer, and Ptolemy might be one of the smartest people to walk Amphoreus. Peucesta has a keen mind and fighting skills he rarely brings out, while Leonnius can run back for reinforcements at an astonishingly fast pace. Hephaestion fights the best out of all underage warriors, save for Phainon and Mydei themselves.

They are his friends, his family. Three of them dutifully carry torches to light the way, and at least one person is always talking.

Five out of these seven are as relaxed as ever, maintaining the calm atmosphere as they travel through the trees. Even if Ptolemy periodically glances over with a searching gaze, attempting to spot any cracks that may be forming on the surface if Phainon or Mydei aren't careful enough to mask them. He is the only one with detailed knowledge of what precisely happened after they left the Sea of Souls. Something about keeping the

record of their King's life story. He is the one person they didn't mind divulging the memories of their first few months together in their entirety. The rest are more or less aware, but Phainon and Mydei both moved the subject along before any questions could be asked.

Mostly for Phainon's sake. He doesn't enjoy talking about the past.

And even now, Mydei isn't exactly tense either. He walks by Phainon's side, footsteps so quiet they are nearly inaudible. A learned habit, taken to as quickly as breathing, even when he was taught to walk way too late in life. Mydei's whole existence is a deadly force; it only figures he would be as silent as any predator. It's normal. What isn't, is the way he only hums in response to the group's extensive jabs, not allowing himself to be dragged into the conversation as he usually would by now. Phainon watches on, and he catches him absentmindedly raising his hand to gesture something at whoever asked the question, only to drop it just as quickly at the realization that Phainon is the only one who can understand.

He doesn't even try to say aloud what he wanted to respond with.

Phainon does try.

But the words are stuck in his mouth, refusing to cooperate and leave the safety of his brain.

Leonnius takes over the conversation when there's no reply for a few minutes too long, stepping right over the dromas-shaped hole the two of them usually fill in with their bickering. He retells a story from his childhood, running away with a cheerful laugh when Peucesta attempts to grab him to avoid the embarrassment of Leonnius revealing his past mishaps. Hephaestion slows his pace to hang back until he's walking with them instead of at the front. Much to Phainon's surprise, he goes to his side rather than Mydei's, leaving him in the middle.

Hephaestion doesn't acknowledge the change, waving his torch in the air, an entirely bored expression on his face. It lights his face in the warm yellow glow, underlining the sharp features. Pretty as ever, not a single blemish or

unflattering angle in sight. He, too, could have any person in the settlement if he sets his mind to it, Phainon is sure.

Anyone but Mydei, if he's got anything to say about it. But it doesn't stop his mind from forming the thought that, perhaps, once they are all adults, Mydei might choose Hephaestion. It wouldn't be that much of a stretch. Phainon would understand the need to have a less complicated romantic relationship. Who would want to get involved with someone you're already so tangled with as the two of them are? It's a recipe for disaster.

Phainon. Phainon would.

But, ultimately, he will always put Mydei's happiness first. Which doesn't mean he won't try his hardest to come out on top.

He looks to the other side, finding Mydei already watching him. His friend nods once, then tilts his head to the side. You alright?

Phainon nods with a small sigh. He deliberately sways as he walks, bumping into Mydei to hear him huff and watch the warmth in his eyes as his lips quirk up just slightly. Yeah, he is fine. They both just need to adjust as they travel through the area, convince their brains there's no need to go haywire. They will be talking soon enough.

It's quite some time before they decide to call it a day, and Phainon even manages a few stilted sentences out by the time they stop to wash up in a river. If nothing else, it serves as an excellent means to shed the last traces of apprehension in Phainon. He snaps out of it almost immediately when he takes a look at Mydei's lips pressed into a thin line, brows furrowed in frustration. Right. Running water.

"We should take turns washing up," he says, and their friends are too surprised or perhaps relieved to see him suddenly speaking like nothing is wrong to either agree or disagree. "I will go with Mydei. Then Leonnius and Peucesta, and then the rest of you. Yeah?" He doesn't wait for a response and instead grabs a torch before herding Mydei forward. "Great."

Mydei still doesn't say a word, but that might be more out of convenience rather than anxiety. Phainon has no issue with that, whistling a tune Peucesta enjoys to play as they disappear between the trees and reach the river itself. Phainon stays as close to Mydei as he can, smiling a little when he helps to wash his hair without fully submerging his head. He is glad for the deepbone exhaustion catching up to him and preventing him from letting his eyes stray too far and his brain from creating certain scenarios that will never come to pass. He would have died of mortification if his body decided to have a reaction now, of all times.

When they return, the fire is already set, and Hephaestion argues about something or other with Ptolemy. Leonnius laughs as he runs past Phainon and Mydei, Peucesta's hand clutched in his own, and dragging him forth. Mydei sits down to make good use of their provisions, heating up the preprepared food for everyone to enjoy. He takes his time with it, and Phainon makes himself useful by setting up their sleeping space.

As they settle for the night in another hour or so, and Phainon wraps himself around Mydei to ensure they are touching in every possible way, he knows the night won't be peaceful.

He hasn't dreamed of axes in years.

His aversion to them remains strong, and he used up every excuse in the book to get out of chopping the wood in the settlement. On one notable occasion, he split the log into pieces with a sword when he couldn't escape the chore. Whoever had forced him into it was so appalled that they never tried to assign wood chopping to him again.

He forcibly smothered the memory of the incident to the back of his mind, buried in a drawer never to be willingly pulled open. It's not the worst thing that could have happened to two children out in the wild. Not when he and Mydei had come out of it alive, healthy, and unscarred. Some of the things they do and the habits that have become their second nature might be a direct consequence of it, as Ptolemy said one day. But that's fine, it really is.

What he truly hates is the reminder of letting himself slip in a dangerous environment and risking his friend's life. Because what if Mydei didn't have

his unnatural regeneration? Phainon supposes they would have both long since resting in the Nether Realm. Still together.

So, when Ptolemy offers the first shift to watch over their surroundings, Phainon resigns himself to his fate of a restless night, yet falls asleep surprisingly quickly. Maybe it's the stress catching up to him, pulling him under as soon as Mydei's arm settles over his waist, Phainon's chin resting against his head.

And, startlingly, he dreams of an axe.

It's not as vivid as some of his other dreams are, just a sequence of quiet actions. Almost blurry at the edges. There are no black eyes tracking their every move. Phainon and Mydei aren't ten years old anymore. They aren't so skinny or small, and Mydei's hair doesn't reach to his hips. They are teenagers, still lean and growing slightly taller by the month, with solid muscle mass already formed and still increasing.

Phainon feels the weight of the tool in his hand as his fingers curl around it, the uneven wooden surface of the handle as he walks into the campsite, the fire dying out. He glances down, notes the blood still wet on the blade.

Slowly, he raises his eyes to look at Mydei more closely.

Crimson smudges run across his body, overlapping with the markings. His hands are the worst, utterly drenched up to the elbow. He is relaxed, stance loose. Phainon glances higher at his face, finds golden eyes staring impassively at the trees behind him. Red stains his lips and one cheek, glinting in the fading firelight.

And Phainon notices the five dead bodies strewn around the place, their features painfully familiar. Massacred, with unseeing eyes and twisted limbs. He reaches up to brush away something wet from his own lip. His thumb comes away in the same exact shade of red, slowly dripping down his hand despite the fact that it shouldn't.

Phainon inhales sharply as he wakes up, eyes springing open to the fire, much brighter than the one he has just seen. Careful with the arm holding

him and legs tangled with his, Phainon raises himself up on the elbows. Four bodies on the ground, sleeping soundly with no traces of liquid red in sight. Leonnius snores to the right, Peucesta's hand pushed into his face in subconscious protest at the sound. Hephaestion remains off to the side as well, the first time he chose to sleep away from Phainon and Mydei since they took up traveling together.

And Ptolemy sits directly across Phainon, back to the tree.

'You okay?' He mouths clearly, taking care not to wake up anyone else.

Phainon sighs, tiredly sweeping his hair away from his eyes. He nods, and gets one back in acknowledgement. Phainon is momentarily distracted by the fire's intensity. It's so bright, and the smoke rises high into the trees. Should they have a fire going at all? It's not so cold, not like it was back in the forest by the Sea of Souls.

Phainon almost signs for 'Tired?' on habit alone. But he only sighs instead, wincing at the headache that's silently growing behind his eyelids. He tries to grab a handle on it and points a finger at their sleeping friends, then at Ptolemy in what he hopes is a questioning manner. Ptolemy shakes his head, then points to Mydei with his chin and stares at Phainon expectantly.

Phainon sighs again and tiredly waves his friend off. This is nothing to be worried about. Phainon literally proved it time and time over that he can fight very well, no matter the circumstances, body running on pure adrenaline and no sleep at all. Ptolemy, meanwhile, really should get some rest. But he's as stubborn as any of them, even more so when he sets his mind to it. And neither of them wants to wake everyone up from their scant few hours of rest.

With that in mind, Phainon forces himself to lie back down. The ridiculously warm arm is still thrown across him, the limb now having fallen slightly lower and resting against his abdomen. Phainon attempts to shift a little bit without waking Mydei up. He is not very successful with it, the golden eyes blinking at him sleepily within a second. Some tension leaves Phainon's body at the sight, and he breathes out in relief. Mydei's

gaze could never be as uncaring as the one in his dream, and Phainon feels guilty for his imagination daring to imply so.

Mydei takes one look at him and simply drags him toward himself with his hand, easily turning Phainon to lie on his side until his head is nestled in the crook of Mydei's neck. The new position effectively blocks the view of everything, be it their sleeping and vulnerable companions or the bright fire.

The blankets are tightened around him, fingers lazily carding through his hair. It feels safe and familiar. Phainon pretends they are back home in their own bed, safely hidden away from the rest of the world.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"Are you sure you want to proceed?" Perdikkas asks with an overly concerned gaze two days later, digging in the bag to produce a remedy for Hephaestion's irregular heartbeat.

So, Ptolemy must have told him of the nightmare. Of course. Because it's not like he and Mydei frequently have all sorts of nightmares, a trip to a destroyed homeland or not.

"Yes," Phainon responds firmly. He smiles thinly and takes care not to look over at Ptolemy with murderous intent. Just a little strangling would do him some good. "I have to see it for myself, check for anything that may have remained."

"Sometimes the past is best left abandoned," Peucesta tells him quietly, sharp eyes settled on him as he idly runs his index finger down the string of a lyre. Leonnius' eyes eagerly track the movement, nearly vibrating with energy at the prospect of Peucesta playing them a song sometime soon. "Forcefully digging into the painful memories may bring you more misery than any good."

His friends are aware of what became of his village. More or less. Once again, Ptolemy and Mydei are the only ones Phainon relayed the whole story to. The details of watching the large sword sink through Cyrene's small body, the crying for his parents as they died in front of his eyes, and the hazy memories of wandering the lands until he stumbled on Mydei. The rest, they know enough to warrant concern over his well-being when Aedes Elysiae is concerned. More than they know of the time between the Sea of Souls and the settlement.

And those are wise words that Peucesta chose, and maybe Phainon would have nodded along if it was said in relation to anyone and anything else, but —

"I have to see if it's truly all gone." Because some tiniest, smallest part of Phainon's soul has hid away since his childhood days and dared to hope that perhaps the village had been rebuilt in his absence. Logically, he realizes it's impossible. But there is nothing rational in that sliver of hope, left to be crushed and abandoned as he's bound to eventually see the results for himself. "I have to search for any clues about the person responsible for it."

"What if you truly find nothing of value in there?" Ptolemy picks up, undeterred even when Phainon scowls at him. "All this turmoil might be for nothing, and that's the most likely outcome. We are still not too far out; we can return to the settlement fairly quickly."

Phainon shakes his head tiredly, feeling like a broken record. "I have to go," he repeats, undeterred. "Look, you can all turn back if you want. I won't hold it against you."

"Like hell we are," Hephaestion snorts, grabbing whatever pills Perdikkas found and swallowing them dry with a wince. "If you think we aren't following you and Mydei to the ends of Amphoreus, maybe you're not well enough to continue."

Phainon glares, ignoring the warmth he feels at the sentiment, and opens his mouth to argue against the scathing remark, but Leonnius is faster.

"We are just worried," he nods, sending him a smile before he turns back to watching Peucesta's fingers. "But even if the results bring no merit or if the situation turns drastically against us, we will remain by your side."

Hephaestion shifts lazily, throwing a cheeky grin at Phainon and Mydei both. "We are the royal retinue, are we not?" He asks, clearly proud of the title, as unofficial as it still is. "It would bring us shame if we left our charges unattended."

Phainon and Mydei exchange a thoroughly unimpressed look at being called Hephaestion's charges. If anything, they are the ones who still keep an eye out to ensure he doesn't get overwhelmed against the more powerful opponents.

"But I would like you to remember there is no shame in turning back," Perdikkas rounds back to his original point. "Whether it is now, or one day before we reach Aedes Elysiae. Or even as we step right into it."

"The proud heart feels not terror nor turns to run and it is his own courage that kills him," Ptolemy quotes with a sage nod, Perdikkas' lips quirking up as he glances at him. "It's a formidable quality. And your stubbornness is almost impressive at times. But don't let those qualities chain you to heartbreak."

"I appreciate the concern," Phainon tells them sincerely. He does, truly. What he doesn't appreciate is the frustration born from being questioned on his decision so much when he's already made a choice, though. "But I'm afraid I still wish to continue, and none of your arguments could change my mind."

"If Phainon says he can keep going, then he can keep going," Mydei speaks up right after him in a voice that says he won't hear any further comments about this. The tone reminds Phainon of Archidamia just a little bit. He winces at the thought, discarding it immediately. What a dreadful comparison.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 14: and reassemble their entrails
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Warm fingers delicately grab his chin and direct his face back in his own direction. When Phainon lets his eyes fall back on his best friend, he notes the slight tension in his brows. Eyes that carefully take in the ugly and distressed image Phainon must make.

"I'm tired," Phainon whispers hoarsely.

Mydei's fingers travel up across Phainon's cheek and brush over his forehead. Swiping back his bangs, uncaring about the way hair sticks to skin, drenched in cold sweat as it is. Phainon closes his eyes against the sensation, fighting not to lean in.

"I know," Mydei replies quietly.

Chapter Notes

!!!!! you miiiiight want to refresh your memory of this one scene in canon material, the link is here. obv not that necessary but the first scene references it very closely

They step cautiously.

Phainon's hand tightens on the hilt of his sword with each new detail that comes into view.

The wheat fields have long since turned to dust. The blackened ground stretches out into the horizon, moonlight casting an eerie glow over it. The dirt road, or more of a path, is overgrown with grass so muted it might as

well be gray. The once glimmering and clear water is now murky, barely reflecting anything on its surface. It's like something drained every vibrant color Phainon's homeland used to possess. He bragged about its beauty to his friends over the last few months in a desperate attempt to remain optimistic about the trip. Nausea hits him as he stares at the fallen trees, ruined beyond any ability to regrow.

The Dawn Device is nothing more than a shadowed dot of light in the distance, barely distinguishable behind the thick curtain of dark clouds. Even Kephale refuses to gaze at this corner of Amphoreus anymore.

Phainon halts when they reach the spot where the scarecrow he and Cyrene put up together had been. An empty patch of dirt remains. His friends stop with him, following Phainon's lead. He knows that Leonnius shifts uneasily from the sound of feet moving on the ground restlessly. It ceases when Peucesta must put his hand on him. Phainon doesn't want to know what face Hephaestion is making, and he's glad that Ptolemy remains silent, from where he's walking further away with Perdikkas. The two of them are supposed to hang back at all times to avoid any potential danger.

Phainon averts his eyes from the deteriorating woodwork, the skeletons of houses left behind by the flames of a fire that Phainon still doesn't know the origin of. He glances at Mydei, watching the pensive expression as he takes in all the details on his own. Slowly, he turns his head to meet Phainon's gaze, already aware of him looking.

Mydei tilts his head, eyes darting to the side and then back to Phainon. Want to leave?

There is no judgment in that unspoken question. Phainon knows Mydei would never judge him for anything, except maybe the alleged occasional stupidity. He still feels hot shame curl around his guts at the sheer prospect of leaving this place without exploring further after dragging everyone all this way. Potentially missing clues because he's, what, frightened of his past?

He shakes his head once and takes a step forward again.
