Out of reach, just as it was years ago. Nothing changed.

"Are we strong enough to defeat that person if they chose to attack us in this very moment?" He asks, spurred on by the nightmare. They've improved, well past the human standards. But is it enough? Will it ever be enough? "What if they do? What if they just slaughter us?"

"Then we fight them. And if we are still too weak, we die fighting," Mydei replies after no more than a few seconds of loaded silence. The simplicity of his response almost makes Phainon snort. "There is no use in pondering on such a possibility. Right now, I don't believe we are important enough to garner such attention from them. We shall become the strongest in Amphoreus and take down this person when we are ready."

He says it with such conviction. For a goal that isn't his own.

Mydei is incredibly intelligent, portraying an image of a person larger than life since the very moment Phainon met him. A small malnourished kid, feral yet still caring for a crying boy. Snarling and throwing himself into any danger. There is no thought of defeat in his mind, never has been.

But this time, Phainon cannot fully believe in those words. There was no reason for his village's destruction either. Anything could happen; they could die at any moment. Even Mydei, as much as he swears up and down that there is no place for him in the Nether Realm.

"Sorry," Phainon breathes out, shaking his head. He regrets that action when Mydei's hand slips off. "I'm not— I don't know. Not much feels possible right now. Maybe I'm just messed up."

"You're not," Mydei responds quickly, fiercely, tone rising but not enough to wake anyone. He inhales, fingers flexing in one hand where it's resting against his own knee. "Is there anything that could help?"

Not really. Phainon wants to scoff. There's nothing that can fix him. But…

"Can you come here?" He asks, scratching the back of his head sheepishly at the stupid idea that escapes his mouth before it can even take root in his brain.

"I'm already here," Mydei says, turning his hand in a circular motion.

And yeah, he is, but that's not. That's not close. Not like when they're back home, not like Phainon wishes to be. He misses sleeping side by side,

unable to take comfort in Mydei being pressed close to him now that his friend always takes the watch for almost the entire night.

"No, like I did. After, you know, the last fight. Please?" His voice gets thinner as he continues with the request, more unsure of himself than anything else. Maybe it's not a good idea. Just depicts him as weak, unable to overcome things on his own. "Nevermind, it's okay," Phainon chuckles awkwardly, waving his own hand in dismissal. "It must be embarrassing, I'll just—"

Words die in his throat as Mydei shuffles closer, unceremoniously swinging his leg over Phainon's thighs and raising an eyebrow down at him, staying half raised. Phainon blinks up at him dumbly, all thoughts momentarily erased from his mind. Alright. He may not have considered this request thoroughly enough. He curses himself further when Mydei places one hand on his shoulder and then sits down, legs bracketing Phainon's hips. Suddenly, Phainon is thankful for the nightmare and the fact that the leftover traces of it keep him from ruining the moment with a different kind of awkwardness.

As it is, he snakes his hands around Mydei's waist, relaxes into the proximity of the person most important to him. It's good. Phainon yearns for their own bed, where this was more common. They still lack personal space even outside of their house, but it's not really like this.

Mydei rests his forearms over Phainon's shoulders, one hand keeping a tight grip on his nape as it did not so long ago. Phainon inhales, then exhales. Yeah. This is what he wanted. He almost considers letting himself fall backward and taking Mydei with him, attempting to get some more sleep now that he feels more at ease. It's not like Mydei cannot look out for danger while on top of Phainon.

And it's then that soft, warm lips press against Phainon's sweaty forehead, making him blank for the second time in a very short time span.

"Happy birthday, Phainon." The words are whispered into his skin, barely audible among the crackling flames. A shiver runs down Phainon's spine.

The small peck must have been unintentional, only done due to the effort of speaking aloud.

More importantly, Phainon realizes he is now indeed fifteen. He forgot the date was supposed to fall on their way back to the settlement. He winces at the reminder, not in the mood to celebrate at all. He would've rather everyone forgotten about it.

There wasn't any place for it in his mind with everything else going on. This whole year passed by in such a rush. Mistakes too big to forget or forgive, attempts to fix them, forcing their way through one battle after another. A busy year. In three more months, Mydei will be of age. Phainon recalls Ptolemy's musings on Archidamia's distant plans, a potential campaign far away from the settlement. It sounds exciting. It could provide them a direction to move toward, a new experience outside of the routine expeditions.

Phainon squeezes his arms together, feeling the hard muscles of Mydei's waist brush against his skin. They both grew so much since they first met, too scrawny and always hurting.

"Where's my gift?" Phainon jokes halfheartedly, finally finding some of the humor.

He forcefully abandons the subject of the cloaked figure in his mind, spontaneously deciding to lock it out entirely for the foreseeable future. They are going to accomplish their current goals, and only then will Phainon go back to his plans of revenge. He won't get stronger if he gets scared like this from nightmares alone, and Mydei always gives him strength. They will get better. They have to.

"I can go scavenge for a trinket, for old time's sake," Mydei offers quietly, giving Phainon something for his brain to latch onto. "If you wish me to."

Phainon makes a considering noise, tacking on a very thoughtful expression, and Mydei huffs fondly. His fingers tug a little on Phainon's hair as he pulls back just slightly. His gaze is amused as he stares at Phainon, the usually sharp features rendered soft by the warm hues of

flames. The corners of his lips tick up, and he leans down again to press them against the tip of Phainon's nose. They've seen Peucesta peck Leonnius the same way multiple times, and perhaps that's where this behavior comes from. Just watching and copying. Phainon rationalizes to himself, because otherwise he might combust.

His hands still squeeze impossibly tight over Mydei's waist, making him shift to dislodge the grip somewhat. Phainon's face is definitely bright red. And where Leonnius usually grins and returns the gesture by pressing a kiss to Peucesta's cheek, Phainon goes cross-eyed, trying to stare at the very spot Mydei's lips just left.

Hephaestion engages Phainon in an incredibly pointless yet heated argument the next morning, going from a faltering remark about something or the other at first and spiraling into a burning insult before Phainon can truly get annoyed about being handled like something fragile. At least it doesn't last for long at all. The two of them just bring that out in each other, no matter the circumstances, it seems like.

What it also accomplishes is for the rest of the group to lose the tension in the way each of them holds themselves, expression relaxing and cracking smiles as Phainon throws literal dirt at Hephaestion's face and then sputters when Hephaestion produces a thin dry branch and repeatedly whacks him on the arm. And here he worried they would awkwardly attempt to cheer him up and insist on celebrating his birthday.

Just as the thought settles, Mydei resurfaces from between the trees on his left. Phainon blinks at him dumbly, then glances at Hephaestion with narrowed eyes. Their friend grins sharply. Oh.

Phainon did notice when Mydei had stepped away from them, but didn't wonder about it or how long it might take him to get back even once. Clearly an orchestrated event.

Before Phainon can get properly annoyed at it, Mydei attaches himself to his side again, an overly warm press of his body making him settle

immediately. A small smooth stone is pressed into his fingers, thumb trailing across his wrist as Mydei's hand retreats into his own lap.

Occasional shuffling interrupts the otherwise continuous silence, and Phainon can easily imagine all the well-wishes his friends must be thinking. Refraining from speaking them aloud as they usually would.

A quick glance down tells him it's a river stone, a callback to their old days if he's ever seen one. It's as warm as Mydei's skin, and the colors intersect with thin lines on the lower half of it. It's light blue.

Phainon laughs quietly at the small gift, but he still pockets the small treasure.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"That campaign of yours," Mydei prompts Archidamia apropos of nothing as soon as they sit down. He entirely disregards the report they're usually required to give after their expeditions, and Phainon finds himself breathing a little easier. He's not entirely certain how well he would handle retelling the entire battle to the people gathered.

A few of them shift in their seats, thrown off by the unusual progression. They've been trained too well, Phainon and Mydei. Any deviation from the standard course is all the more stark contrast to the usual procedure.

A lady finds her voice first. The one who, despite everything, remains remotely kind to them both. Unlike most of her companions when Phainon is concerned. "Respectfully, Lord Mydeimos. You've just returned, and we would wish to request a—"

"Ptolemy made notes. There are no casualties or injuries on our side. We have eradicated some of the black tide monsters." Mydei rattles off briskly.

Without waiting for an answer, he addresses Archidamia again. "Aidonia, wasn't it?"

Archidamia raises an eyebrow, but doesn't acknowledge the clear dismissal. Perhaps it's their right to keep it private, what with how the expedition wasn't ordered by the Council. "Aenionus, as a matter of fact. But through Aidonia, yes."

They talked about it for the remainder of the way back. Mostly Mydei, Phainon, and Ptolemy. Mydei's birthday is less than two months away. The expeditions in the area won't suddenly rise in their difficulty, and it seems inefficient to travel for months on the off chance the experience turns out to be valuable enough to be worth the time. Missed lessons, training, and Mydei potentially losing his people's favor by being forced away from them for so long.

With Archidamia's burning ambitions, presumably left to ponder on until Mydei is old enough to claim the throne, it seems foolish not to make use of them. Ptolemy is the one who suggested it, most familiar with Archidamia's plans, as she isn't prone to discuss unofficial matters in these meetings with the two of them. Phainon is the one who pushed for this, though, realizing it's the perfect opportunity to set his revenge to the backdrop and focus on the current goals.

Mydei looked between them, heard them out with slightly narrowed eyes as he took all the details in, and then agreed without making a fuss after asking a few questions of his own.

The settlement's people are Kremnoans. Hailing from a moving fortress to aid in wars and conquer the lands. It's not in their nature to remain at one spot for so long, as functional as they've made it be. Castrum Kremnos may be out of reach, but that in no way means they cannot get wherever they need to be on their own. It's a good idea, really. Appeals to the desperate need to regain their former glory, as it's a sliver of what their old lives revolved around.

Phainon looks right into the eyes of one of the generals, watching as he frowns and attempts to guess where this might be leading. Phainon smiles.

"How about we leave the settlement behind," Mydei says, voice steady and confident, "and instead move forward as an army detachment?"

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon buries the tip of his longsword in the ground and allows himself to lean on it. He looks around the battlegrounds, takes stock of the dead bodies littering it.

Their opponents are retreating, and he knows that behind him, soldiers are being dispatched by Ptolemy to round them up. Perhaps not as experienced and talented a general as the ones in the Council are, but he's been steadily improving his skills as a tactician. Ptolemy may never be strong enough to fight at the frontline, but he can certainly call orders in Mydei's name. Or, perhaps, he will lead a cavalry of his own one day. Nothing is impossible with Ptolemy.

Phainon sighs, kicking lightly at his blade. He hears a familiar laugh in the distance, lets his eyes follow in the direction of the sound, and feels relief wash over him as he spots a teen with bright ginger hair pushing Hephaestion with the dull end of his spear. Still restless enough to search for a fight. Hephaestion, splattered with blood and his hair half-undone, rounds on him when he's distracted and delivers a swift kick to the back of his knee, sending him sprawling to the ground.

Phainon snorts, smiling as Aias springs back to his feet to strike at Hephaestion, taking the action as an invitation for a spar. Hephaestion evades lazily, and Phainon cannot see his expression from that distance but is certain there must be a smug expression painted across his features.

Deciding they've got it covered, Phainon lets his sword dissipate in a flare of sparkles and sets off to find Mydei again. The battle took a while, the soldiers rotating in and out to get some rest. The two of them aren't ever allowed the same luxury, and the last traces of adrenaline are slowly

vacating his body. He's beginning to itch with the need to see his best friend, though he's sure he could still push it back for the time being. Fortunately, there's no reason to.

His pace increases and heartbeat kicks up when he finally spots him, kneeling on the ground with his back turned away. Not moving to celebrate with the rest of their soldiers, let them congratulate him and Phainon for a victory in a war well led. His mind races, holding onto the fact that if Mydei is kneeling, not calling for help, then it cannot be anything too bad. It's countered by the fact that Mydei barely ever calls for help unless forced into it.

Some of the tension releases its hold on him when he notices Mydei's hands are moving across the ground in front of him, busy with a task of sorts. There are almost no traces of gold on his skin or clothes, just the usual crimson splatters.

"You alright?" Phainon still asks cautiously as he steps closer. He halts right behind his friend, looking over Mydei's shoulder. Puzzled.

Mydei grunts in what's supposed to be an affirmative. He doesn't stop digging, gauntlets stained with the brown of wet dirt rather than red like the rest of him.

"Are you sure?" Phainon asks skeptically, eyes raking over the corpses strewn around. He doubts that seven of the Kremnoan soldiers happened to die right in this spot. There is just one dead body of an enemy, a few paces to the side, discarded carelessly.

Mydei doesn't stop, doesn't even look up. "If you aren't offering to help, Deliverer, go bother Hephaestion."

Phainon rolls his eyes at the testy response. "Aias is currently occupied with just that," he says drily and crouches next to Mydei. That's a large hole he dug out. A sword won't be of much help in this endeavor. Phainon already mourns the state his hands will be in by the end of this. "Why are we burying the bodies?"

Mydei's hands halt, and he rests against the heels of his boots. The earthly scent of wet dirt and metallic tinge of blood mix together in the air, creating a weird combination. It's a familiar one, albeit never quite this intense.

"Wherever we go, carnage of bodies follows. Some of them are our own soldiers more often than not. Usually not as many of them, as they are skilled warriors, but those are still their bodies rotting as animals feed on them," Mydei explains quietly.

Phainon lets his eyes wander over the pieces of golden armor that have become a permanent fixture in his life, cracked and streaked with gore. They were taught to abandon the fallen, as the grounds of a victorious battle bathed in the enemies' blood are sure to bring them to the Nether Realm under Nikador's watch. With the chaos of a fight still sparking in the air and their handlers always ushering them back on the road immediately after, Phainon doesn't think they've given much thought to it either.

Until now, apparently.

"So, we are breaking the Kremnoan custom?" Phainon asks lightly, ignoring Mydei's gaze on him as he nudges a pile of dirt to the side with his shoe.

"They deserve better than death under our watch," Mydei replies, resuming his thankless task.

Phainon nods once in agreement, even if Mydei isn't looking at him anymore. "This may be the first time we're fighting with soldiers assigned to us since then, but we did everything perfectly. It's not our fault."

"And yet they still sacrificed themselves to ensure our glory." Mydei gestures to their deceased comrades.

Death is the currency Kremnoans deal in more skillfully than the shrewdest of merchants who hoard their Balance Coins. And Mydei has paid the price more times than it's physically possible to count. Phainon strongly doubts a person with more intimate experience with death exists on Amphoreus. Even those Aidonian fanatics never died over and over and over again

themselves. It's fitting, somehow. That he would care more for a common soldier's demise than his own.

"So they ought to be honored," Phainon finishes with a thin smile.

Far it be from Phainon to disagree with the notion of giving proper burials to their soldiers. It should have been in practice to begin with. Perhaps this can be one of the first changes Mydei vowed to bring back in the Kremnoan library. A more sound regard of death. There are not many people stationed above them who can do much more than scowl at lost time for trying to bury the deceased today. Ptolemy might whine about it once the boredom gets to him, but that's bearable.

He steps back a few paces, immediately finding the familiar figure in the far distance. Perfect. It'll go faster with some help.

Phainon presses two fingers into his mouth and blows air through them, giving two sharp and loud whistles. One has always been a signal for the soldiers to gather. Recently, Phainon and Mydei added another one to function as a call across the battlefield between their inner circle. He watches Hephaestion's frame turn toward him, features nowhere near possible to decipher as they're almost completely on the other side of the grounds. Phainon raises his hand and beckons him, hoping Aias will follow despite not exactly belonging in their closest group. Phainon and Mydei watch over Thera every now and then, and the younger teen seems to have taken a liking to Hephaestion as well. He is close enough.

Sooner or later, they all gather. Save for Peucesta, who stayed behind on this expedition, and Perdikkas, who is presumably busy tending to the wounded. They stride through the battlefield as the last of their soldiers retreat, and the bodies dwindle down to the last dozen or so. Their hands are caked in mud so thoroughly that Phainon idly wonders whether there might be some permanent stains left behind by this well-meaning act.

"Want me to run back and ask if someone has a shovel?" Leonnius asks out of nowhere, returning from the run he took to check if they truly recovered all the bodies. "Should've thought about it sooner."

Ptolemy startles enough to stumble forward, nearly falling into the shallow pit filled with bodies. Mydei's arm shoots up to push him back to the safety, leaving a dark smudge of dirt on the white tunic.

"You think someone brought a shovel to war?" Ptolemy asks incredulously, mud streaks all across him. Even his hair didn't escape unmarked.

"Anything can be a weapon," Aias pipes up unhelpfully.

Hephaestion snorts, kicking him in the back when he bends down to bring out another pile of dirt. He nearly faceplants into it.

He yelps, "What the f—"

"Don't curse," Hephaestion tuts, dirty hands resting on his hips and a smug grin on his face. "You're even younger than me."

"By a month!"

"You're both too young," Ptolemy grumbles, using the conversation as an excuse to straighten out and rest. Phainon and Mydei wisely keep their mouth shut, but Ptolemy's flat gaze still falls on them. "I won't pretend that I wouldn't prefer all of you to wait longer before you descend into this improper behavior fully, but there isn't much to be expected when you are raised among the soldiers."

"Every once in a while won't hurt anyone," Phainon says brightly, beaming when Mydei snorts and Ptolemy shakes his head in resignation.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.title: Chapter 15: and celebrate their growth
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Beautiful is one word to describe him, but it still feels absurdly inadequate.

"Are you ready?" Mydei asks, voice a bit rough.

Phainon nods, doubling down on a grin and not trusting himself to actually speak. His voice might actually crack if he does.

He follows after Mydei, only to catches sight of the antique pin he bought a year ago. Phainon offered it to Mydei, but it got put in some drawer without much hope of actually wearing it. It's too ornate and delicate. And now Mydei dug it out from Titans know where, and put it carefully into his hair on this very special day.

Phainon strangles the hysterical laugh that threatens to escape, pressing the heels of his hands into his eyes instead with so much force that it's a little painful. It's going to be a long day.

Chapter Notes

One, two, three, four.

Over, and over, and over again. Phainon counts, and recounts. Sometimes he goes from one to four a few times, and then switches to going from four to one. Keeps his breathing deep and steady. Tries to make a noise in his throat as he inhales and exhales, focuses solely on that and nothing else around him.

He can smell metal. He can taste metal. He can see red and gold mixed on the ground by his feet. And he can hear Leonnius heaving through shuddering sobs into Peucesta's chest off to the side.

One, two, three, four.

Four, three, two, one.

Easy.

He hums to himself louder, drowns out all the noise inside and outside of his head slightly more successfully. Locks his eyes on the rock by his heel. He doesn't have any other choice but to force himself into staying as calm as the situation can allow for, not really. But he will do that, he will keep a tight grip on the panic attack that waits for a second of distraction to sneak up on him. He can't let it. And if he pushes it back far enough, it may stay there until the urge to fall apart is gone forever.

He doesn't glance to his right, where he thinks Hephaestion may have already bitten through the skin of his thumb. Perdikkas will take care of it once he's done. Because he will be done soon; he's an incredibly skilled medic, even beyond his beloved brews that he wants to shove into everything. Not much the flowers, leaves, and roots can do in this situation, though. Phainon would rather drink the most stomach-churning of brews instead of having to sit through this.

"It's working," Perdikkas says faintly, voice full of relief and stress alike. There is a dull thud as he must fall to the ground behind them.

Phainon almost whips his head around to check for himself, the visceral need to be aware of what state Mydei is in at all times making itself known. Especially right now. But Ptolemy's hand shoots out at an even faster speed, settling on top of Phainon's head and firmly shoving it back down to rest between his raised knees. Phainon doesn't protest. Instead, he lowers one of his legs and finally glances to the side, watching violent shivers wrack through Hephaestion's body. Eyes widened and unseeing, directed at the bloodstained dirt.

"Do you need help?" Ptolemy asks with concern, the most collected one out of them all. It's reassuring. He never truly panics during a crisis. Phainon will know when the world is ending, because that's the only instance when Ptolemy will crumble. Perhaps not even then.

"No, it's—" Perdikkas stumbles over his reply, close enough that his shaky inhale can be heard. "I did everything I could. He is stable. There is— He's got a pulse."

"Perdikkas," Ptolemy calls, tone softening further. "I knew our Prince was safe the moment you let go of him, and I am beyond relieved about the matter. But are you quite alright?"

"Me?" Perdikkas asks, and Ptolemy is distracted enough that Phainon is able to shift and glance over his shoulder. Sees Perdikkas' frighteningly pale complexion and haunted eyes, ink-like hair plastered to his face. There is gold smeared across his cheek and covering his trembling fingers. "I wasn't hurt."

Mydei lies next to him, head obscured by Perdikkas' frame, but Phainon can make out his chest moving up and down in a shallow movement. He keeps his eyes there and tries to match the pace with his own lungs. It's not enough. He has to move, go over, and see the healing wound, feel the blood circulating under his fingertips. He shifts, turning his body toward the two of them.

"Phainon," Ptolemy says in a warning, the hand still resting on his head tightens its hold just a bit instead of slipping off.

And, really, what's the warning for? Phainon has seen worse. He's done worse. Mydei lives, and breathes, and whatever state he may or may not be in, Phainon does not care. He almost scoffs. "I lost track of how many times I stood above his corpse," he declares flatly, carefully brushing Ptolemy's hand off. No matter how gruesome the injury, Phainon always remained. He doesn't intend to break the habit. "I watched his skull knit itself back together, brain matter stuck between his hair. You didn't want me near because I would get in the way, fine. But if you don't let me get back to him right now, I might stab you."

He wouldn't; that's more of Hephaestion's thing. But Phainon wouldn't have any qualms about forcibly moving him back a few paces and getting through regardless. If Phainon is really determined, there's nothing Ptolemy can do to stop him.

Ptolemy rolls his eyes at the empty threat of bodily harm but says nothing. That's as good a permission as he's going to get.

Phainon gets up and walks closer immediately. He promptly sits down at his friend's side with a wince, his own injury making itself known. Remarkably, Mydei looks fine. Peaceful. If not for the thick line of stitches running around his neck, the wound a little skewed. Phainon forcibly swallows. It was one thing to hear of it. It's another to look at the clear mark left by it.

Mydei was beheaded.

Phainon never witnessed him sustain an injury this severe. To him, there's never a guarantee Mydei will come back despite all the evidence pointing to the contrary. With Phainon's rotten luck, he always waits for the other shoe to drop. To finally fail Mydei with Phainon's incompetence so thoroughly that he won't be able to get up. Perhaps it's the fact that he didn't see the head separated from the body that allowed him to remain in blissful denial about the severity of it.

Leonnius, who found him, was not so lucky. The quiet crying and hiccups of their runner are still audible in the background.

"Perdikkas, come here," Ptolemy directs, drawing Phainon's attention away from Mydei's body. He rests his fingers against Mydei's wrist, right on the pulse point, and looks over. Sees Ptolemy deflate when Perdikkas remains rooted to the spot on Mydei's other side. "Phainon will call you if Mydei so much as twitches. Now, could you come here? Hephaestion is awfully pale; he might faint."

Hephaestion is still in a state of shock. But there's not much they can do for him except wait at his side until it passes. It's more of an excuse, Perdikkas must know it. But, finally, he rises to his feet.

Phainon watches him stagger, so unlike the incredibly determined and focused man he is when working to save someone's life. He falls forward, right into Ptolemy's chest. One arm catches him around the waist, steadying him. It's an amusing image with their height difference, except the circumstances don't allow for much humor. Ptolemy makes sure Perdikkas

is leaning on him without a risk of falling over, and then raises his hands. He gathers the healer's hair back, tying it neatly with a hair tie that he still carries on his own wrist. They don't talk.

Absentmindedly, Phainon counts the slow beats of Mydei's heart. He gets to a hundred and then starts over from the beginning.

Eventually, Perdikkas slides away from Ptolemy, sitting on the ground himself as Ptolemy gazes at him with his lip bitten raw, fingers worrying against the hem of his shirt. Hephaestion has since angled himself to face them, face regaining some color, eyes clearer as he surveys their surroundings. Still too keyed up to check on Mydei.

And that reminds Phainon that the seven of them have been like this for only Janus knows how long. Phainon barked at the soldiers to leave the area immediately when he got to the scene, and as the one with the highest ranking among them, they had no choice but to follow the order. The gossip must be spreading, and unrest may be growing. There is only one general along with them, and she may lose her patience soon.

Phainon taps on Mydei's skin, warmer to the touch by the minute. Someone has to go inform everyone of Mydei's recovery. Perdikkas has to stay and make sure Mydei is fine. Hephaestion and Leonnius are too shaken to do much else than sit and wait. If Ptolemy leaves, the rest of them may crumble. And not even Titans themselves could make Phainon step further than a meter away from Mydei right now.

"Peucesta," he calls, voice cracking embarrassingly on the name. The musician raises his head and glances at him with steady eyes. Hands cradling Leonnius' head close to his chest. He is humming a soothing tune. "Let our soldiers know Mydei will be up soon. Please."

"Two," Hephaestion corrects with a thin smile. "My parents will be annoyed that I'm still out. I'll leave you to it."

"I'll just tell them you were with me," Mydei protests, mouth set in a stubborn pout. "It's fine."

Hephaestion shakes his head, already taking some steps backward. "I'm tired as well." He raises his fingers into a lazy salute, then performs a mockery of a curtsy for good measure. It's the second time Phainon has seen it today, and his head starts spinning as he thinks about it. "Happy birthday, Lord Mydei."

Mydei frowns, the expression more pronounced than he usually allows it to be. He acknowledges the gesture, and then they are left in silence as Hephaestion leaves them alone. He quietly walks away, and Phainon thinks he might be taking left instead of right as he should be, but who's to say.

Phainon sighs. "We should get at least an hour of sleep before facing Perdikkas, shouldn't we?"

"Might as well rest in the infirmary," Mydei nods.

He gets up first and then offers a hand to Phainon. They both stumble when Mydei yanks him up, giggling as they walk to Perdikkas' almost-permanent place of residence. And if they don't even notice as they walk past the infirmary, and they have to turn back after a good ten minutes, no one needs to know.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon's stomach unfortunately falls victim to an assault of a very vicious slap delivered by Mydei. Phainon probably would have slept through the

noise, but it's no surprise his friend was startled enough to lightly lash out. Lightly lash out, he thinks at himself in a mocking little voice while grunting through the pain. He will be lightly bruised, maybe.

It's way too early in the morning. If it's still the morning at all. It's certainly seven hours too early for him to wake up. Or so. Even if it's been seven hours already, he feels like he could still use seven more. Or fourteen. With his luck, it's been barely an hour. He's about to shift onto his other side and trap Mydei's arms beneath his own to avoid any stray limbs flying in his general direction, but then he hears it again. Roused from sleep as he is, the noise is clearer.

Because an awful, disgusting sound echoes in the room, followed by the groaning of at least two people, one of them being Phainon. With great effort, he forces one of his eyes open, immediately wincing as the light causes a piercing ache to bloom at his temples. Alright. He blinks through it, feeling his own stomach flip around as the noise continues, and finally manages to glance over at the source.

Ptolemy is half sprawled out on the floor, heaving over a bucket. And shoving two fingers deep into his mouth, gagging on them. His blond hair is plastered to his forehead, and spit trails down his chin. He coughs roughly, forcefully jabs his fingers inside again, and then the actual contents of his stomach spill out.

"Ew," Phainon mumbles, burying his head into the pillow as his own stomach makes a short revolt of its own.

"Shut the hell up," Ptolemy rasps in an awfully scratchy voice. Hearing it makes Phainon's own throat hurt.

"Do it in the bathroom," Leonnius whines from somewhere, as miserable as Phainon feels.

"I'll pass out if I try walking," Ptolemy replies in the same angry tone as before.

And then resumes his task of torturing them by forcing himself to vomit. Thankfully, it doesn't last longer than five minutes before Ptolemy shoves the bucket away with a loud clang, and the silence settles once more.

Phainon falls in and out of the dozing state for some time, grateful for any additional sleep he can get. Mydei shuffles closer to him, placing his arm over Phainon's eyes when he starts squirming too much.

"Rise and shine," Perdikkas calls into the room some time later, knocking sharply on some surface, and now three people groan in reaction. "Oh, be quiet. Drink these and get out, I'll be dealing with several cases of alcohol poisoning and harmless but annoying hangovers today."

Phainon opens his eyes as two small objects hit the infirmary bed next to his leg. He grabs them and watches as Leonnius eagerly downs the same vial two beds over.

"You were taking too long," Ptolemy complains as he squints up at Perdikkas. He looks like the most disgruntled person in the entire world, sitting cross-legged with his back to the wall, arms folded together.

Perdikkas uncorks the vial himself and tilts it into Ptolemy's lips, shaking his head. "Shouldn't have drunk so much."

"Well, it shouldn't be so fun, then," Ptolemy says, entirely unapologetic as he winces through the taste of whatever brew Perdikkas brought them. "I already took care of most of it. Your bucket was handy."

Perdikkas only shakes his head in response, already moving his attention to them. "Phainon, Mydei," Perdikkas calls, shaking the empty vial. "Drink the medicine if you want to get rid of the hangover."

Mydei raises himself on his elbows, looking at them blandly. "What hangover?"

"Thought as much," Perdikkas says, but it's almost drowned out by Ptolemy and Leonnius, who both grumble about the unfairness of it. Even Peucesta sends a very flat stare in his direction.

Phainon opens the brew and decides not to mention he's only got a light headache to deal with. Well, might as well rid himself of that quickly.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: and find what makes them fragile
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"I cannot imagine what must have transpired to warrant such secrecy," she says calmly, glancing at Hephaestion and Ptolemy again, before settling back on Phainon. "But, as I'm being continuously reminded, you are the ones who had been chosen for Lord Mydeimos' royal retinue, ultimately tasked with taking care of him under any circumstances." Her tone is as resigned as she would ever let it show, which is not much, but she also lets out an exhale, slow and tired, weary.

"You should have been more careful with who you were handpicking for the duty if you wanted to have full control," Ptolemy tells her with the seriousness uncharacteristic of how he usually handles Archidamia.

The corners of her lips tick up in a smile that's too small to reach her eyes. "If your loyalty to him outweighs your loyalty to me, then I would say I picked the perfect candidates."

Chapter Notes

Phainon raises an open palm to his chest, then flicks it away in a shooing motion. I want to leave.

He's pretty sure Mydei can read that in the stare Phainon directs at him, but Phainon is both exhausted and bored. He needs something to do. Unless the people gathered provide some adrenaline to pump through his veins, Phainon might stop trying to remain upright and slam his head against the table.

"Tretos is just as viable an option as Loukas," a man argues, and Phainon nearly rolls his eyes.

So insufferably stubborn, the lot of them. And entitled. They may be intelligent and skilled enough to warrant seats at the Council, but clearly, their main objective shifts to posturing and ensuring they have the last say once no one is actively engaged in a fight.

Mydei looks thoroughly unimpressed, but he bends his index and middle fingers once. Twenty. Minutes, presumably. Phainon wishes he meant seconds instead.

Someone makes an indignant noise. "Are you hearing yourself? That sentimentality would give us away instantly. Loukas is an unquestionably superior choice. Ladon would be preferable, even."

"Ladon is too risky for a starting point," a collected woman adds smoothly. "Not with the unfavorable location and the soldiers who sneak behind the enemy lines to spread disarray."

Phainon blinks sluggishly, keeping his lips pressed tight to avoid the yawn from slipping out. He wishes he had Mydei's endurance when it comes to running on little sleep, but he doesn't. Not if there's no danger to be wary of. A week of getting up too early and dealing with the annoying proceedings that are required to ensure the smooth beginning of their campaign, on top of still keeping up with the rigorous training… He can admit it's a little bit much for him.

Just once, he would like to go to sleep at a reasonable hour. Not sit here like he's one of the decorative pieces on the wall, and listen to them squabble over nothing.

"For it to have the same gain as a successful battle against Ladon, we would have to breach the prison that Loukas prides itself on," Savvas points out. "That course of action is questionable at best."

Faster, he signs when he's sure another yawn won't threaten to make an appearance. Please.

Mydei frowns at Phainon's insistence, traces of concern surfacing in his gaze as he tilts his head. Phainon is sure that his incessant whining

throughout the day and very obvious eye bags speak for him as to why he wishes to hurry this along. What Mydei wants to know is if there's anything more that could warrant urgency. It's sweet of him to worry.

Phainon smiles tiredly and shakes his head. He swipes one hand over his eyes. Just sleep.

"Lord Phainon," a man calls, and Phainon bites back the urge to groan. Nikasios is his name, Phainon vaguely recalls. "Are we boring you?"

Yes, he thinks. Fortunately, the question wasn't directed at Mydei, or the answer wouldn't have stayed as a thought alone.

Phainon exhales, meeting the man's eyes. "You are all going to settle on Ladon," he says, cutting right to the point.

Someone scoffs, but now everyone's eyes are on him. Most of them are filled with curiosity. The two of them haven't bothered voicing their opinions since this started. This is Archidamia's campaign. As much as Phainon and Mydei are hopefully both the core elements of the future Kremnoan rule, they don't hold many stakes in this extended expedition. They are weapons to be pointed at the enemy. Besides, when the Council gets like this, they don't wish to hear reason.

Stupid politics and the endless tug-of-war to evaluate who sides with whom.

Mydei rolls his eyes, hand making a dull clank against the table as he lets it drop. "Ladonians are violent and slowly forcing neighboring towns under their rule. Their army is large enough for the word to spread about our victory should we defeat it, making it relatively easy to establish ourselves," he sums up easily, pushing things along for Phainon. If Mydei says it, they have no choice but to acknowledge it. "The city-state's desire for conquest means we won't be taken as bandits or raiders once the word of it carries. We won't know the terrain until we arrive, as we hope to ambush their army when they march, but it's nothing we cannot work with. Loukas, while we can catch them off guard at the time of peace, has no enemies to speak of and would give us an unfavorable reputation."

Phainon nods, pointing at Mydei. He leans back in his seat and roughly rubs his eyes to stop them from stinging. He has no doubt they would be entirely red if he looked into the mirror, a hauntingly familiar side effect of sleep deprivation.

"But you're all aware of that, aren't you? You pointed out each of those facts throughout this evening," he picks back up tiredly.

He glances at Nikasios, stares until the man looks away. He's the one who brought up the issue of the Kremnoan Detachment separating itself from the typical Kremnoan conquest in order to stave off any suspicion of their origins. Phainon barely feels any satisfaction at having proved to the man that he was listening. He brushes one hand through his hair, glances over everyone again.

"What you have yet to mention is Campa, though," Phainon continues. "Their feud with the Ladonians dates back centuries and is unlikely to ever be extinguished. If we lay siege to Ladon, we are guaranteed to be hailed as heroes and treated well by the Campanians. Campa Mountains aren't that far of a detour and could help us get back on our feet after the battle against Ladon."

People mutter quietly between themselves, and Phainon yawns instead of scoffing.

They are fifteen, for Kephale's sake. They aren't children anymore. They participated in the wars, they sat through so many of these meetings, so many lessons. It's enough to recognize patterns and advantages, be it geographical or historical. They have been relentlessly trained for this. If the Elders think Phainon and Mydei are still two kids who know nothing of the battlefield, it's going to be a rude wake-up call once Mydei takes charge of the leadership, and they find out he's got no need for their petty quarrels.

"Which indicates you are all stalling. I'm not certain why you're content to tolerate these meetings running well beyond the scheduled time lately," Mydei directs at Archidamia, tone firm and successful in conveying he hasn't got a need for excuses. Phainon huffs and cannot stop the small smile from forming as he glances at Mydei. "You should know that I will not

allow this much longer. It's a waste of time that could be spent on more productive matters."

Like resting, in Phainon's humble opinion.

"Some of the people gathered do not contribute in a way they ought to. You are indeed correct," Archidamia inclines her head, but her eyes don't lose the sharp glint. So many overly proud individuals gathered, and no one dares to even huff at the accusation as they usually would. Phainon glares at them for their cowardice. "The purpose of letting these move past the allotted time slot is for you to learn how to navigate the entitled. To see through them, and take note of the conversations held beneath the surface."

"You are aware I have no patience for the theatrics," Mydei argues back, unrelenting. "I'm not interested in granting my attention to people who won't converse with me head-on."

"Your sincerity will gain you the favor of your subjects, Young Lord, but you are also aware that the political scene won't treat you so kindly." Her smile is a wry thing, bordering on condescending, and Phainon feels his annoyance spike.

"And for that I have Phainon," Mydei responds without missing a beat. Phainon presses his leg against Mydei's under the table. It's staggering how quickly the anger simmers down with the warmth spilling into his gut. "I may have a better head for strategy when we are devising battle formations, but he is the one who can handle people effortlessly. And anything we might miss, Ptolemy will undoubtedly catch. As my official advisor, there isn't any reason for him to be absent from the official meetings, isn't that correct?"

Archidamia's gaze sharpens, turning disapproving. "It's not advisable to be so dependent on—"

"Have I misspoken, Lady Archidamia?" Mydei asks, perfectly calm yet still in a clear warning. Archidamia closes her mouth, expression unreadable. "I don't see the harm in letting capable people take charge when it's needed."

Archidamia presses her lips together briefly, thinking about her next words. "Whether it's in a year or a decade, you may find some of your friends to be gone," she explains slowly, holding eye contact even as Mydei's eyes narrow. Most people would look away and bow their heads. "Such is the nature of our lives. All rulers have advisors and diplomats, but I would urge you to take an active role in those areas as well."

Mydei remains silent, carefully considering her comment. Privately, Phainon thinks what she said is uncalled for. There's enough suffering in their lives already, and no one wants to hear about their dearest friends potentially dying. It's a real possibility. But three out of five of them don't regularly take to the battlegrounds. Leonnius can outrun anything as long as he sets his mind to it. And Hepahestion—

Well, that's the one inevitable death they do have to come to terms with.

Besides, Phainon is never going anywhere. He will stay glued to Mydei's side through all the battles, all the meetings, converse with the dishonest assholes, and debate them until they're left with no options but to accept whatever conditions Mydei lays out. He will support Mydei for years, decades, however long it takes.

On any other day, Phainon would've argued with Archidamia about it. He would scoff and indirectly insult the rest of the Council as they would no doubt get drawn into the discussion. But today, he is too drained to put effort into it. Mydei knows of Phainon's stance, and that's all that matters.

After a few minutes pass in silence—no one is willing to speak up after that exchange—Mydei is the first one to look away. It's telling, Phainon observes tiredly. Not a good quality for the Kremnoan Prince to be so attached and, as Archidamia put it, dependent. He couldn't care less.

"I believe we are done here," Mydei says to the room at large and gets up before anyone can protest.

Phainon scrambles to his feet, nearly tripping on nothing in his exhaustion, before Mydei grabs him by the arm and keeps upright. Phainon lets out a long exhale, closes his eyes as Mydei leads him forward. Doesn't hear the

door closing behind them, barely pays attention to their surroundings as they move toward home.

He could fall asleep like this, placing one foot after the other with Mydei's warm hand ensuring he goes in the right direction.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"She's doing well," Phainon comments, watching the archery practice of the younger group. It's kind of endearing, some of them frowning with that childish focus and determination, while others get distracted by absolutely everything.

"Thera certainly has the potential," Mydei agrees. "Hephaestion is no doubt overjoyed. I'm not certain about Aias' enthusiasm over his sister's improvement; it's the one weapon he's been having difficulty mastering."

A kid screeches, running past them after having retrieved all the arrows from the targets, waving the sharp objects in the air. Hephaestion makes an aborted motion to stop the child, but realizes it's hopeless to insist on safety when it's an overeager Kremnoan kid.

"As much of a mastery of all weapons as he can hope for at that age. And as a mortal," Phainon remarks quietly, continuing the subject. Not that he's one to talk. Phainon didn't really take to archery. He is proficient enough, but always more than happy to default to his weapon of choice since he earned his right to do so. "You must be his role model, having truly achieved that level of expertise in every field."

Not many people can claim to be so skilled at such a young age. It's a little unfair. The fact that Mydei could flawlessly fight with any weapon in the world, but he still chooses his fists more often than not.

"He will get there," Mydei says easily, eyes following Thera's movements as she draws an arrow under Hephaestion's watchful eye. He smiles when the nearby target is hit with a dull thud. "Though you are right, I'm sure Hephaestion is delighted to have become one of the most skilled people in the one area Aias cannot seem to grasp."

"Have you seen the way he threw the arrow last time?" Leonnius chides in, stretching his hands high up above his head. There are some small yellowish bruises littering his neck. Bug bites? Or friction burns? It doesn't look too bad. "Instead of shooting it."

Maybe it's hickeys. Phainon grimaces.

His eyes travel further up, into the branches and leaves of the tree Leonnius is leaning against. It's a large one, their usual spot if they're hanging out outside. The fruit seems ripe enough to climb up and grab a few for each of them. Now that he's thinking about it, they do have an hour or so to kill. Might as well.

Phainon grunts as he gets to his feet, dusting off his pants.

"I had to hold back Hephaestion from making good on his threats of bodily harm," Mydei says fondly.

Phainon snorts at the reminder. He had to whisk the bow away from their friend's grasp to stop him from showing Aias first-hand how the act of shooting is supposed to be performed. It looked too much like his target might be Aias' ginger head.

"Regardless, I think he will be proud of Thera," Phainon says and walks around the tree, waving Mydei off when he glances up in question.

"No doubt about that," Leonnius replies with a hum. "You reckon Hephaestion will throw a fit if I suggest Aias to teach Thera that move?"

"Are you that bored?" Phainon asks, placing his foot on the lower branch and testing its sturdiness. He scowls when it threatens to break under his weight already. That fruit might be a lost cause. "Peucesta won't save you

from Hephaestion if you do that. Aias will rat you out as the one who came up with it."

"Well, I got used to all the traveling," Leonnius grumbles. "And now we're just waiting until everyone is ready to abandon the settlement."

"You could always help with the preparations," Mydei suggests.

"All I need are my shoes," Leonnius replies quickly. "And whatever Peucesta decides is needed, which is not much anyway. I think I'd rather rest before we're suddenly thrown into a fight every second day than overexert myself, thank you."

Phainon huffs and kicks at the tree's trunk. He really wanted that fruit, thought he might grab an extra one for Ptolemy and bribe him out of that test. For today, at least. He looks up, about to decide whether it's worth it to try and scurry his way up without relying on the branches anyway.

A sound, and all of Phainon's muscles tense at once.

A familiar sound, always present around them in the wars. Not so much as when they are fighting against the Titankin, their weapons are too powerful to have so little impact. But in the fights with ordinary men, it's close to impossible to escape it.

Usually accompanied by a grunt or scream or gurgling blood if the neck is injured.

There are none of those right now, but Phainon still whirls around the tree to check the source. Sees Mydei crouched over Leonnius' body, who stares at him with wild eyes. Immediately, Phainon knows something is wrong.

In the fervor of a battle, Mydei once barely blinked as a greatsword severed his forearm. He pitched his spear up with his other hand, and sent it flying toward another target, not even glancing to check if it hit—and, of course, it connected with the enemy's head—before sending a wave of crystals at the person who attacked him, closing in on them until he could snap their neck.

Countless times, Phainon watched him look on with a bland expression as Perdikkas put stitches on every surface of his body over the years with no anesthesia, not a single muscle in his body twitching. A clenched jaw or a huff of air is the only reaction he ever gives, and it's usually in frustration at allowing someone to get close enough to hurt him rather than the pain itself.

He always pulls arrows out of his body one by one. Be it to utilize them further in the fight or noticing them only when the last of the fresh corpses hit the ground. A sound of an arrow, whirling through the air, and the sound of it piercing flesh, digging in. Mydei must be well acquainted with it.

And now, a thin stick protrudes from his back, barely visible at the angle Phainon is looking at him. But it's his frighteningly pale skin that catches Phainon's attention, all blood drained from it. He is panting through a clenched jaw, trembling in place as if it's taking significant effort to remain upright. He looks like he may throw up.

Mydei has never reacted in such a way to an injury.

Phainon is at his side within a fraction of a second, hovering as he's unsure what to do in an unfamiliar situation. What if he makes it worse, whatever it is? "What's wrong?"

"Burns," Mydei grits out. He winces at the pain. That alone has Phainon's heart racing with fear.

His knees give out, and Phainon catches him easily, holding him close. He's burning up, scalding to the touch. When Phainon glances at the wound, ichor drips through his shirt in a steady trickle. It takes a moment to realize that it's not his hands shaking that he's seeing, but rather Mydei trembling. Fuck. This isn't the usual reaction to an injury at all.

Dread fills him. What if Mydei ran out of luck? What if this is the last one, the limit finally making itself known?

No.

It's not that. Can't be that. It's just one arrow, and it couldn't have hit anything vital. Phainon will fight Thanatos by himself if he has to, for revoking the gift that is Mydei's immortality without so much as a warning.

They will fix this.

Perdikkas is still at the infirmary, and he will know what to do. Phainon holds himself back at the last moment, remaining rooted in the spot as he remembers the circumstances.

Mydei is injured, to an extent he's possibly never been hurt before.. It wouldn't do well for people to know, and the kids— Titans, there are the kids nearby. And the one who must have shot the arrow. He glances over his shoulder and notes Hephaestion quickly approaching them, a concerned frown marring his face.

"Leonnius," Phainon calls in a tone that has Leonnius at attention immediately. Even if he still appears shaken. "Take the children to Peucesta. Let him know what happened, and have him somehow convince the kids that nothing of the sort transpired. Go get Ptolemy after."

Leonnius nods stiffly and takes a second to scramble to his feet before he's off, running to the kids and presumably distracting them with stilted laughter and nervous eagerness to move away.

"Okay," Phainon mutters to himself, shifting his grip to let Mydei lean on him instead of keeping him up in what must be an uncomfortable hold. "Okay, okay."

"What is it?" Hephaestion asks immediately upon his arrival. He gently places one hand on Mydei's shoulder, only to jerk back at the unexpectedly high temperature. More out of shock than anything else, Phainon suspects. Kremnoans and their heat resistance.

"Something is wrong with the arrow," Phainon offers, unsure what the actual issue is himself. They should go to Perdikkas, but perhaps it's not such a good idea. People will see, and they will panic once they realize

Mydei isn't walking it off as he usually would. This cannot get out, can it? "We have to get him away from here. Then, then get Perdikkas to come."

Hephaestion nods once, as alert as he is during a battle, and he takes Mydei's arm to swing it around his own shoulders, making it easier to carry him. Or just drag. His eyes are molten steel when they meet Phainon's, calm and prepared to help even though the boy they both love is in a rather dire state. Maybe it's nothing. Maybe he's dying. Maybe—

"Where to?" Hephaestion asks, successfully snapping him out of his thoughts.

"Our house," Phainon responds on pure instinct, and, yeah. That's not a bad idea.

Hephaestion nods again, and they half-guide, half-carry Mydei forward. It's not far, thank Kephale. What's more, the hour isn't a particularly busy one; most people are occupied with wrapping up their affairs or settling in for dinner rather than stumbling across the roads.

Phainon could stay with Mydei and let Hephaestion go get Perdikkas. It's exactly what he would like to do, in fact. Keep his eyes on Mydei, make sure his condition doesn't worsen. But is there even anything he can do to help if he stays? He has no medical training, no knowledge of what to do except for keeping the arrow as still as possible to avoid any further damage. Hephaestion knows that much as well.

If Phainon is left alone with a Mydei who might be on the verge of death and given no task to busy himself with, agonizingly helpless in watching, there is a chance he might have a panic attack. And that doesn't help anyone, only takes the focus off what's important, which is Mydei's health.

So it's not really a choice at all to let Hephaetion through the door, gently slipping Mydie's arm off his shoulders and bolt after exactly four words spoken to their friend. This way, he does something. Runs as fast as he can, keeping his mind steady on the one objective, which is to get Perdikkas. He can do that. He can get help, and then he can sit by and watch as Mydei is being tended to rather than stuck feeling useless.

The front door makes a loud bang against the wall as Phainon pushes through in a time that even Leonnius would be impressed with. His footsteps thunder against the floorboards, and he fights to keep his panicked breathing in check as he makes it to the archway to the actual infirmary.

"Perdikkas," Phainon calls as soon as he is through, finding him further in the back, treating what looks to be a sprain.

Perdikkas shakes his head, glancing at his patient with exasperation before addressing Phainon. "I'm not letting any of you skip the—" His eyes shift to him as he starts walking over, and his hands halt. He straightens up, eyes narrowing in focus. "What happened?"

"It—" Phainon cuts himself off forcefully, coming to a stop in front of him. He cannot say it's Mydei. The word will get out before they step one foot outside. "You have to come right now."

And, for a beat, Perdikkas hesitates. Phainon knows Perdikkas loves them, takes care of all of them as best as he can, and he would do a lot for them. But in this moment, Phainon cannot help the stab of panic tinged with anger at the visible reluctance to leave.

He doesn't know, Phainon reminds himself. He may think it's not that serious.

Phainon blinks at him, tilting his head.

That's a first. In all the years since the conversation with Archidamia and since seeing the portrait in Castrum Kremnos, Mydei never spoke of seeing his mother in his dreams. Of course, he could just not tell Phainon if he did. But with a subject of this significance, Phainon thinks he would have at the very least mentioned it.

"I don't recall the specifics," Mydei elaborates when he sees Phainon's reaction. "She was telling me something, over and over. In Castrum Kremnos."

Phainon hums. Their time in the fortress was rather hectic, all things considered. Phainon dreamed of it enough times himself. It's usually more

about overthrowing the current King, or running through the winding corridors, hiding behind the columns or statues as something chases him, or exploring the grand library.

Mydei's mother, though. It sounds like a much more precious dream.

"Tell me more."

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon has been rummaging in the same drawer for about ten minutes now. And that's the second drawer already. This one stores mainly some of their trinkets, so he's idly pushing them around, thumbing at the edges of shiny rocks and eyeing the dry shed snake skin. Mydei gifted it to him solely out of sheer pettiness after one of their arguments, he is sure. Well, Phainon still kept it, so the joke is on him.

He wonders how much longer he will have to busy himself with acting like he cannot hear anything being said a few steps behind him. When Hephaestion came in an hour to Curtain-Fall Hour, Phainon only had to take one look at the red-rimmed eyes and dried tears on his cheeks to know he shouldn't participate in the conversation.

Kremnoans and showing weakness don't go hand-in-hand, even to friends. So he immediately turned his back to Hephaestion and Mydei, and what followed was an incredibly sad apology that made something twist inside of him. The accident wasn't Hephaestion's fault. And Phainon had to bite his cheek to stop himself from saying it aloud. Mydei thankfully said as much himself, perhaps without much finesse, but his fierce and blunt conviction did an even better job at reassuring Hephaestion than pretty words ever would.

If Phainon were a better man, he would have left and joined Peucesta and Leonnius in the kitchen. But this is his room, and he hasn't left Mydei's side

for longer than to quickly use the bathroom since it all started, so Hephaestion has to deal with it. Phainon never claimed to be selfless, even if Mydei would've definitely called him just that.

They are speaking in hushed tones now, and Phainon truly tries not to eavesdrop on them. He's thinking extra loud and recalling the story behind each and every trinket in the stupid drawer. Antlers of some unidentified animal that they forgot to ask Ptolemy about, found on one of the walks they sneaked out of the settlement for, soon after they first arrived. Mydei still couldn't speak back then, communicating through half-developed signs, expressions, and body language. Phainon was feeling a bit down, and Mydei dug the antlers up from underneath a tree, presenting them to Phainon with an expectant golden gaze.

Oh, and there's the weirdly shaped pine cone that—

Hephaestion laughs wetly, protesting at something or other. Mydei says something encouraging, followed by a comment about hierarchy, and now Phainon is confused about what their conversation could have possibly gotten derailed to.

"Stop pretending you're not listening, Phainon," Hephaestion says suddenly, and Phainon closes the drawer with an eyeroll. So much for trying to be decent. "You're supposed to hear this as well."

Phainon turns around and raises an eyebrow at him. He feels the corners of his lips involuntarily pull up at the sight of Hephaestion, brimming with determination. There's no sight of guilt and regret, now exchanged for confidence, eyes bright. Mydei sits on the bed with his back against the wall, clearly amused.

"The role of King's Aegis is taken, got it?" Hephaestion announces, chin raised. Clearly, he expects Phainon to start an argument. "Find your own position."

The King's Aegis. The title is currently held by the man named Krateros.

The one closest to the King, save for the consort.

Instinctively—and predictably—Phainon wants to fight him on it. He is Mydei's protector and companion, always will be. Devotion runs through his veins as surely as his blood, mixed with the ichor. And as a Chrysos Heir, there won't be much left that is stronger than him at one point in the future.

But he thinks of Hephaestion, willing to go against the woman he admires as much as Mydei, the leader figure he's been following for longer than he's known either of them. She is his role model, Phainon is certain. And he would still fight her and hurt her for Mydei. In a scenario that doesn't even fall under life-or-death.

He imagines a future where Phainon is truly Mydei's equal, where they still travel everywhere together. And Hephaestion grows into himself, his bright ambition turned deadly and precise. Following in their steps day in and out, adding one more layer of protection. To the easy companionship, when the rest of their group may be too busy with their lives to follow them everywhere.

Phainon doesn't need a fancy title to fulfill his role at Mydei's side.

He smiles. "It's yours."
