chapters.title: Chapter 17: and bide our time
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"Sounds good enough to me," Phainon grunts as he rises to his feet.

He ends up running his hand up and down his shorts for good measure, deeming them dirty enough for a wash anyway. He bumps his shoulder against Mydei's, leaning too much of his weight on him, and finds himself supported without so much as a blink.

Phainon grins up at the large creature, wiggling his fingers at her in a greeting when her eyes fall on him. "Nice to meet you, Kokopo."

Chapter Notes

Phainon grumbles unintelligibly into his palm. Displaying his displeasure in a semi-open manner is a risky endeavor, given that he's already expressed his opinion multiple times. It's the perfect moment for Mydei to mess up his food if Phainon evokes all of his ire at once.

"I'm cooking a traditional meal from your homeland for you." Exasperation rings clear in Mydei's voice, yet he doesn't turn around from the stove. "When will you cease your complaining?"

Phainon tries his very best to keep himself in check. Don't anger Mydei when he is in charge of food. That's an actual and formal rule that Phainon follows, one Hephaestion falls victim to on a much rarer occasion than he does. Phainon's success rate of holding back when Mydei is concerned isn't high at all, regardless of the circumstances.

"When will you rest?" He asks, louder and more disgruntled than he intends to. "You got up at the Entry Hour and haven't sat down since."

Phainon is getting tired just watching him. Peucesta's quiet tune cuts off in favor of a huffed-out laugh. Phainon glares at him halfheartedly.

"You don't want me exerting myself? Fine. But I will break your leg and force you into bed rest if you even try to keep me there for one more day, HKS." Mydei waves his spatula at Phainon like one would a weapon as he proclaims his threat, momentarily distracted from the food. Phainon wants to yank that spatula out of his hand and hit him in the head with it. But a fight would have followed, and Mydei hasn't recovered enough to allow for that. In the end, Mydei turns back to the pan when Phainon doesn't react. "I had to get up for a conversation with Archidamia two days ago. There is no sense in remaining bedridden when I feel fine."

"While cooking when the two of us watch over you should be fine," Peucesta begins in a calm tone, trying to reach for reason as always, "I don't think it's a good idea to overexert yourself when Ptolemy fought to convince everyone you require a whole week of classes to catch up on before we start moving the settlement so that you could rest."

Mydei doesn't respond to that immediately, letting the sound of sizzling vegetables fill the room. Phainon sighs a little, watching his tense back and unable to help. "I'm hardly going to injure my spine if I decide to go for a run," he grumbles in the same reluctant tone Phainon would use.

No one responds to that.

Peucesta resumes the humming, tapping his foot against the table in a beat. Phainon doesn't speak of his worries, knowing Mydei cannot be restrained until he is deemed fully healed, even if that would have been ideal. And Mydei doesn't argue to resume his training, nor will he try to sneak out of the aforementioned run. A compromise where they don't force each other into bouts of pettiness.

So Phainon quietly watches his back, chin resting against his palm. He searches for any sign of stiff gestures, faltering, or a twitch of pain. What he notes instead is the steadily disappearing tension as he cooks. He guesses the activity must serve as a meditation technique to Mydei, just as cleaning his weapons does to Phainon.

He still tracks every minute movement as Mydei finishes up and brings all three plates to the table. "Thank you," he says quietly, a bit sullen, when his own is placed in front of him. He feels guilty over his lack of enthusiasm and gratitude. This is the food from his homeland, and who knows when will be the next time they've got enough supplies, space, and time to indulge in something like this? But—

"You are still mad about our plan to ensure I don't have any other weaknesses," Mydei states rather than asks, falling into the chair on Phainon's left. His foot nudges against Phainon's and stays there, body angled toward him.

Phainon rolls his eyes and reaches down to drag both of Mydei's feet into his lap. The more affectionate touches and actions have been slowly abandoned by Mydei whenever they have company. Phainon doesn't appreciate that development. Even if Mydei decides he is too princely for such lowly displays, Phainon will continue dragging him into them until he is firmly pushed away. Going by Mydei's warm gaze, it's not happening anytime soon. Hopefully never, frankly.

"I am deliberately not thinking about that," Phainon responds eventually. He brings one of his hands up, taking hold of a fork. "First, we are going to choose our dromas tomorrow. Let's focus on that."

Mydei hums in agreement. Peucesta praises the food. The conversation carries on, and Phainon eats with his right hand while tracing the red lines on Mydei's calf with his left. He knows his fingers are directly on the mark without having to look.

Almost no time passes at all until the food is gone from their plates, and the only reason Mydei doesn't get up from his seat to do the dishes is that Phainon is still holding onto his legs. A flat stare is directed his way, but Phainon only grins in response. He will take care of the dishes later. He won't even complain about it, just this once.

The front door opens with the slightest creak. Intentionally preserved to alert them to any potential intruders, unlike the pristine hinges on all their other doors. Intruders, meaning five people in particular. They are the only

ones in the settlement who would dare to enter without permission or invitation.

One such individual quickly strides through the house with a bright smile, heading in Peucesta's direction with a mere glance spared at the two of them. A loud kiss is planted on Peucesta's forehead, eliciting something between a giggle and a chuckle from him. And then Leonnius is falling into Peucesta's lap, pouting at the empty plates as he nudges one nearest to him with a finger.

"There is nothing left?" He asks, looking back to the kitchen counter with longing. Only dirty pans and empty pots stare back at him.

"You weren't supposed to be back just yet," Peucesta says with a soft smile and crinkling eyes, hands slipping around Leonnius' waist to pull him closer. "Running correspondence tends to take an entire day."

"Yeah, well," Leonnius moves in his lap, meeting Peucesta's eyes. Peucesta turns impossibly softer, and Leonnius' grin is so blindingly bright that it could rival the Dawn Device. "No Kremnoan is faster than me, right? I missed you, so I rushed my chores."

Peucesta sighs, but it's fond. Shakes his head as if he cannot believe him. But who else would cut the time of a regular runner performing the same tasks in half and not even appear out of breath, other than Leonnius? Peucesta kisses him on the nose, then bows his head further down to press their lips together. Leonnius chuckles into his mouth, happy in such a carefree way that Phainon feels a pang of envy. He is glad that they found love in each other. That they can be so comfortable and confident to express it so openly. He still wishes he could have the same.

"I can make you something," Mydei offers quietly. Leonnius turns to send him a grateful smile. There is an obvious difference in the affectionate nature of it.

"There are leftovers in the fridge," Phainon says quickly, pretending he doesn't notice Mydei shifting to stare at him. "I'll heat them up for you. I was just getting up to do the dishes anyway."

He gently removes Mydei's feet from his lap, letting them fall to the floor, and gets up. He will put the food on the stove, and then return and get all the plates at once. He moves before anyone can protest, stopping for no longer than a few seconds behind Mydei's chair to wrap his arm around his shoulders, press his nose against the blond strands in his own form of affection. Mydei lifts his head curiously, and Phainon's nose brushes against his forehead for a moment. He straightens up and meets the keen golden gaze upside-down. His favorite shade of gold.

He grins at him, hoping it's less obvious than Leonnius' expression not too long ago.

Phainon may not be allowed to express the true extent of his feelings for Mydei. But he can still get away with enough to make it bearable.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"I'm sorry we couldn't be of more help with the preparations," Phainon apologizes sheepishly as they follow Savvas into an open area near the settlement.

"Nonsense, Lord Phainon," Savvas waves him off, eyes crinkling as he looks at them over his shoulder. "You two have other responsibilities. Let us worry about these things while you focus on bringing us to glory."

Phainon's smile dims somewhat, but he forces it to spread into a cheerful grin before the man can notice. The glory. He is slowly growing sick of the word. Not a good thing, considering he is likely to spend the rest of his life among Kremnoans. Until his revenge, at least. And hopefully afterward.

It's impossible to miss the enormous creatures resting nearby when they slowly approach. Phainon had seen them before, of course. Briefly ridden one as a child, thinking the dromas was large enough to touch the sky if one were to climb up on its head. Then he saw them in the distance as they

moved from one location to another on expeditions, among traveling merchants walking to their own destinations. Once or twice in a city-state, though they rarely ventured out to those corners of Milios.

Dametrius gives them a nod when they step up to him, busy with scribbling on a clipboard. "Lord Mydeimos, Lord Phainon. These are the three best dromas we could acquire. Please choose the one that is most appealing to you."

Phainon and Mydei step closer to the dromas, craning their necks up to see two of them munching on the tree branches while the third rests on the ground. Honestly, they look the exact same. Phainon isn't sure how they are supposed to—

"This one," Mydei decides astonishingly quickly.

"That was fast," Phainon comments, squinting at the one he's pointing at and trying to discern why this one in particular might be special. It doesn't appear to be any more muscular or bigger than the others. "Any reason for it? I suppose its scales are slightly more blue than the other two…"

Mydei tilts his head to the side as if he never even noticed the difference in the scale color.

Dametrius strolls over, clipboard held loosely in his hand. He raises his brows at them, and Mydei again silently points at his apparently chosen dromas.

"Oh. Wonderful choice, Lord Mydeimos." Dametrius nods, gaze sliding up and down the animal. "She is quite a fierce individual, compared to the docile nature of the other dromas. A little difficult to tame, we've been told. But if there is anyone who could accomplish it, I believe it would be you two." A beat of silence as he stares at the dromas in contemplation. "And Lady Archidamia, perhaps."

"Does she have enough patience for that?" Phainon asks dubiously.

"The dromas or Lady Archidamia?" Dametrius asks drily, smiling to himself. "I would like to think she does. Alas, we won't be finding out," Dametrius says, then shifts his focus back to the more important matter. "Why don't you try giving her some of the yellowsoil? It should leave a good first impression on her. She may not accept it just yet, but do try not to hold it against her."

Phainon takes a block from the basket. It's lighter than it looks, having the appearance of a large brick and the weight of half of one. He makes a noise to get her attention, waving the yellowsoil in the air as he makes eye contact and keeps it. He hopes to attract her attention enough for her to understand he intends to feed her.

He doesn't really know how to handle animals. It's been a while since he had Snowy. And there are vast differences between a simple dog and a dromas.

Phainon can admit he gets a little excited when she lowers her neck and brings her snout closer, sniffing at the offering. He nearly beams with pride, having tamed the large and supposedly mean beast.

But then, she opens her maw, an incredibly large set of blunt teeth staring back at Phainon before it closes with a dull clank right where Phainon's hand had been a second ago. Thank Titans for quick reflexes.

Phainon chuckles nervously, nearly dropping the yellowsoil to the ground. "Is it too late to switch?" He asks faintly.

Before he can shake off the shock and be more insistent on picking another dromas, Mydei goes up on his tiptoes and touches her nose, swiping his hand over it comfortingly. She watches carefully but doesn't snap. Mydei catches Phainon's wrist in a loose grip with his other hand, guiding it closer to her mouth. Phainon stiffens, but he doesn't have time to come up with a protest as she rumbles loudly, a giant tongue slipping out to grab the soil from Phainon's hand and covering it in saliva in the process. He grimaces at the disgusting sensation, though he cannot quite smother the smile.

Dametrius blinks at them, then up at the very content expression on the dromas' face. As much of an expression as dromas is capable of.

"How did you know to do that, Lord Mydeimos?" He asks, bewildered. "Is Pto— Is Lord Ptolemy in possession of materials specializing in dromas handling that I haven't had a chance to read?"

"Not that I recall," Phainon responds as Mydei is too busy petting the giant scales with a small smile on his face. "He would have forced it onto us in preparation for today. Maybe she is more gentle than you thought."

Another dromas takes interest in the newcomers, eyeing the yellowsoil resting in the bucket by Phainon's feet. He is busy contemplating whether it'd be worth it to wipe the slobber off his hand on Mydei's clothes. He can already imagine the pissed-off expression, maybe even a hissed-out HKS.

And then, there will be too much salt in his dinner, or something accidentally gets burned. And then, Mydei will be too annoyed to allow Phainon near any plates and will do it all by himself. So, perhaps next time.

The dromas walks closer, angles its head toward Phiainon. He only has enough time to consider reaching out and trying to pet it to check if it reacts any better, before the entire ground shakes. Mydei's dromas repeatedly stomps her feet, kicking up the dirt and making the three of them scramble to keep their balance. Phainon watches as the other dromas backs off with a thoroughly confused look. Mydei's dromas nearly fumes.

The ruckus ceases in another moment, and after an assault so noisy, everything suddenly seems too quiet. Phainon stares at the spilled yellowsoil, then up at Dametrius and his skewed glasses. Mydei, entirely unbothered, reaches out to pet their dromas again. She huffs once, and Phainon thinks she might be proud of herself.

Well.

"Who do the other two go to?" Phainon asks, dazed.

"One of them will be Lady Archidamia's, and the cargo will be split across her group, including myself," he responds, fixing his glasses and glancing down at the clipboard. "I am still uncertain whether the other one will be assigned to the armory or infirmary. The one you picked belongs to you two, but it will be shared with your royal retinue. We would like to keep it as one dromas per group, or even two groups, if possible."

Yeah, this dromas isn't going anywhere.

Dametrius crosses something off on his clipboard, nodding to himself. "I have faith in Ptolemy that he imparted the knowledge of common dromas allergies to you, as well as their grooming habits."

"We had a test on it," Mydei remarks, having stepped closer to them now that he is apparently done appreciating their brand new dromas.

"Excellent," Dametrius says, and clips his pen to his notes. He looks over his shoulder to where Savvas is rummaging in some boxes. "I will leave you two to it, then. It could be beneficial to strengthen your bond with her before we set out. Good luck, Lord Mydeimos and Lord Phainon."

With a hum of acknowledgement from Mydei, Dametrius strides off, leaving them alone with the two apprehensive dromas and a very fierce one. Phainon crouches down and finally wipes his hand on the grass, wincing. It's nearly dry now either way. Disgusting.

"We should name her," he says absentmindedly. He won't call it dromas in his mind forever. "How about Scaly? Because, you know, she's got scales."

"You named your dog Snowy, you are not naming another animal," Mydei replies in a flat tone. "Maybe Kokopo?"

"What's wrong with Snowy?" Phainon glances up at him with a frown. It was a perfectly adequate name on account of his pure white fur. So what if Phainon has never seen snow himself. "…Kokopo? What's the meaning of 'Kokopo'?"

Mydei stops admiring their dromas and stares down at the ground in consideration. "…Labor? Trouble?" He says eventually, though it doesn't sound like a definitive answer. Phainon nearly laughs when Mydei shrugs with a small scowl. "I think I heard it somewhere."

"Sounds good enough to me," Phainon grunts as he rises to his feet.

He ends up running his hand up and down his shorts for good measure, deeming them dirty enough for a wash anyway. He bumps his shoulder against Mydei's, leaning too much of his weight on him, and finds himself supported without so much as a blink.

Phainon grins up at the large creature, wiggling his fingers at her in a greeting when her eyes fall on him. "Nice to meet you, Kokopo."

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"Have you ever thought about dying?" Phainon blurts out just as Hephaestion's dagger misses his throat by centimeters.

Hephaestion staggers to a stop. A less graceful than usual but just as effortless motion.

He eyes Phainon, expression flat. "What do you think, Deliverer?" He recovers quickly from the shock of the question, firing back with his own. "I may not be fainting or coughing my lungs out every other minute anymore, but it's only a temporary moment of peace. It's not a secret that this illness will ensure I am the first one to die out of all of us. Of course I thought about dying."

Phainon resists the urge to try to kick him in the knee for the unnecessary sarcasm. It might be warranted given that, as a general rule, Phainon tries not to think about Hephaestion's fragile mortality. If he pretends he is

getting better and the symptoms won't ever worsen, then surely it will become reality.

Though that's not the direction he intended for this to go.

Ah. Maybe he should drop the subject. But then again, Mydei is away on another check-up with Perdikkas. Ptolemy might be the person most suitable to bring this to, but he doesn't want to burden him even more. Not with the stress of Mydei's injury added on top of the stress of being so involved with the logistics of transitioning the settlement into an army detachment. And Phainon…

He stares at Hephaestion's hair, today tied in a high ponytail with two braids woven into it from his temples. It reminds him of Mydei's last birthday. "But have you thought about, you know." Words stick to his throat. Hephaestion makes a questioning noise, and Phainon still doesn't look him in the eye. "Doing it."

He is met with silence. He waits for a beat, then another.

"I don't know," he continues quickly, feeling the heat of embarrassment lick up his neck toward his face. He should have kept his mouth shut. "Like, I wouldn't ever do it, not really. Obviously. It's just a question. A stupid one, I know. You do love to tell me I'm stupid."

"But you thought about it," Hephaestion says, voice strange.

Phainon lets his sword disappear and watches the sparkles fly through the air in front of him. "I thought about it," he admits with a sigh. "I mean, I wished I had died after I ran from Aedes Elysiae all those years ago. I wished for that a lot. And then we went back to the village, and then I really thought about it. And during those three days when Mydei nearly died and wouldn't wake up, I entertained the idea again. I'm not sure how long I would have made it without him just… here."

He finally forces himself to look up and meets Hephaestion's wide eyes. Mostly shock. No repulsion or mocking. That's somehow reassuring, as deep down Phainon feared the Kremnoan values may lead to a not-so-

favorable reaction. Even if, logically, he knows Hephaestion would never intentionally disregard a subject this heavy when it concerns Phainon. And Mydei, actually.

"And Mydei as well, he—" Phainon continues just to cut himself off, wondering how to word the sentence. He breathes in deeply, then exhales in a rush. "His perception of death isn't very realistic. It may serve as an appealing quality to Kremnoans. Personally, I find it unsettling to watch him willingly run into a sword. Even if it assures us of a victory with fewer casualties."

Hephaestion's mouth opens just to close again. More silence. Phainon's lips thin, and he considers abandoning the subject. Distracting him with something else, hoping he might forget the issue had ever been brought up. But Hephaestion sheathes his dagger, then tucks a strand of hair that slipped out of his ponytail behind one ear. Briefly bites on his thumb before he curses and drops his arm.

"You two are so messed up, you know that?" Is the reaction he settles on, and Phainon feels his heart drop. He physically recoils, taking a step back. "What am I supposed to do with this, Phainon?"

"Sorry, I—"

"And why are you telling me only now? It's been months since Aedes Elysiae!" Hephaeston cuts him off, one arm wrapping around his own waist, clutching at the fabric above his hip. "I never considered killing myself, but you know what makes me utterly relieved when I think about my inevitable premature death?" He pauses, breathing pattern uneven, and Phainon winces at the wording. "Unlike you, I don't have to think or worry about what would happen if you two met your end before me. Because it won't happen. Do not ever make me worry about that."

Phainon nods automatically. He should've kept his mouth shut. It's no one's problem but his own, and he shouldn't have burdened his friend with this.

"Shit. See, I don't—  I'm not good at this." Hephaestion bites on his thumb again, scowling at the ground in frustration. "I, I don't know how to handle

these subjects."

Titans. It's just like Phainon to make a mistake like this. "I shouldn't have brought this up. Maybe I got hit on the head one too many times," Phainon says ruefully, trying to bring back some levity with a smile that feels too shaky. "I'm sorry, this—"

"Oh, shut up. Stop apologizing, you idiot," Hephaestion glares at him. It softens into resignation tinted with concern way too quickly. "Peucesta, Perdikkas, and Ptolemy would have been able to help you much more effectively. With advice, or some book, or— or medicine, I don't know," he says, almost on one breath, and he seems a little lost after he is done. "And what can I even do, pick a fight about it with you? What's helpful about that? Why me, Phainon?"

Because Ptolemy might be the steady pillar to lean on, the backbone of their mismatched group. And Peucesta could stare them into compliance and make them talk about things until something in their brains shifts. Perdikkas would sit them down while laying out all the brews and listing their desired effects.

But Hephaestion is the first person they met, the one who led them into this life. They climbed trees with him when they shouldn't, they skipped lessons and trainings to play hide and seek from the adults. They learned alongside him, fought off the enemies alongside him. Phainon exchanges insults and heated arguments with him while Mydei gives bland non-committal answers whenever they ask for an opinion, just to rile them up more. He is the best archer the settlement has to offer, and he is one of the very few people who can avoid a strike from either of them.

He is a part of Phainon and Mydei's life, more so than anyone else.

"You are our best friend," Phainon shrugs helplessly. "I don't need help. I'm not going to do it. Mydei doesn't want help; he already gets angry enough at me when I mention those things." The experience of finding out he isn't as immortal as one might think should do the job of making him less prone to jumping into risky situations with no regard for his life. Phainon isn't quite naive enough to hold onto that hope too tightly. "But it's been knocking

around my brain a lot lately, and I thought it might, uh, be a little easier? Letting someone know."

Hephaestion visibly deflates, expression strangely vulnerable for a person who hasn't experienced potential suicide ideation and isn't currently revealing said experience. But Phainon gets it somewhat. He would have felt just as lost if the situation were reversed. If Hephaestion came to him, struggling to come to terms with the unavoidable end of his life due to his illness, what could Phainon do? Pick a fight, as Hephaestion said, since that's what their relationship revolves around? Smile and spin a diplomatic response, redirect the conversation?

Hephaestion is his and Mydei's best friend, even if their relationship might overshadow him a little bit. Phainon feels guilty about it when he lets his mind wander. Like they're keeping Hephaestion out. But it doesn't change the fact.

Phainon would do a lot for Hephaestion, and he deserves honesty at the very least. A piece of vulnerability that Phainon fights to keep unseen from most other people.

"I cannot afford to even think of wanting to die," Hephaestion offers him in turn, biting on his lip and staring at him with uncertainty flickering through his eyes. "I'm already racing against the clock. But sometimes, I feel like I shouldn't have been born. My body works against me at every step; I have to fight it so that I can exist in the way I want. I'm not always this determined to prove I can handle it."

Phainon bites his lip. It's been a while since he last witnessed a full setback in terms of Hephaestion's illness. He knows of the exercises he's doing to have a firmer grasp on his heartbeat regulation. And sure, there are better or worse days. However, it's been months since he had a coughing fit so severe, let alone lost consciousness.

Just his hand, regularly pressed to the left of his sternum. Subtle enough that Phainon has a hard time telling whether it's a simple habit or his heart that continues to bother him.

He hums, rocking back on his heels. "Ptolemy would have sprung some quote about time on us, wouldn't he?"

Hephaestion cracks a smile. "Maybe the strength of oneself," he snorts. "Or whatever else."

Phainon looks up at the dark sky, the lamps failing to obstruct the view of the stars. Can he really not recall a single quote? Ptolemy does it all the time; it cannot be too hard. And Phainon has even read a book recently, bullying Mydei into taking it easy. Not that it was very difficult once a history book was pressed into his hands.

"Time is the…" he starts, only to frown when the next word eludes him. "Time is the smartest of all things, for it… does something," he finishes lamely.

But Hephaestion lets out a genuine laugh, one loud enough that someone passing by throws a bewildered glance at them. Phainon waves at the person cheerfully.

"Yeah, yeah," he says eventually when Hephaestion only continues giggling, rolling his eyes. "I don't see you springing any quotes on us anytime soon. Do you want to resume this fight, or should I claim victory?"

Phainon ducks with a low curse when a dagger immediately sails through the air without so much as a word. He scowls at Hephaestion, but cannot keep it up for long when Hephaestion is still chuckling, spinning the other dagger across his knuckles.

With empty hands, he lets his muscles lead him through the familiar strikes and lets his sword materialize at the very last moment, white sparkles shining between them as Hephaestion yelps and jumps back.

"You are messed up," Hephaestion repeats, now in a calmer tone.

"Thanks," Phainon says drily. "Should I leave you here to limp to Perdikkas on your own, then?"

"Shut up, Deliverer." Hephaestion smacks the side of his head with the hand he's thrown over Phainon's shoulder. Phainon strongly considers just throwing him over his shoulder and carrying him the rest of the way. With his busted ankle, it might even be doable. "We're all messed up, I think."

Phainon cannot argue with that, not with how he knows all the intimate ways the Kremnoans are brought up and can compare it to his own childhood. They are messed up, no doubt about it. But it's a different kind.

"I shouldn't be messed up," he says instead. He's had a peaceful childhood, two loving parents, and a bunch of friends. A warm village and carefree days. Things happened, and now those precious things are gone forever, replaced by bloody revenge to be enacted. But he's also a Chrysos Heir. He is supposed to stand at Mydei's side as an equal. "I should be stronger than this."

"What you shouldn't be is this stupid," Hephaestion snarks at him, and Phainon doesn't bother resisting the urge to yank on his ponytail, smirking when Hephaestion's head snaps back to ease the pain but making sure he keeps his weight off the injured leg as he stumbles. And then hisses when Hephaestion viciously tugs on his earlobe in retaliation. "You can rely on us a bit more, you know?" Hephaestion continues softly after a moment of dismayed silence. "We will always love you."

A sentence so quiet and gentle that Phainon needs a moment to register it, his grip on Hephaestion tightening momentarily. Such a contrast to his friend's tendency for grating arguments and snappish insults. No less truthful.

Phainon's throat feels dry when he tries to come up with a response, mind uncharacteristically blank. When a minute passes, and he still hasn't said anything, he glances at Hephaestion, now only five centimeters shorter than him. He's catching up. He looks back, raises an amused eyebrow, accompanied by a wry smile. But no sadness or annoyance at a lack of response.

Phainon inclines his head in acknowledgement, forcibly swallowing. He will have to grab a drink at the infirmary.

"You think Perdikkas will let you skip the line?" Phainon asks eventually when the familiar building comes into view.

Hephaestion groans, throwing his head back. "The day he lets me skip the line is the day my heart gives out on me, so he's got no other choice."

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

After a conversation that may have been derailed into an argument before fading into reluctant acceptance, it was decided that the infirmary is not the best place to conduct an experiment regarding Mydei's potential weaknesses. It's just their luck that two patients are currently confined to their beds in there. Being the head healer, Perdikkas has a small private office that they sometimes hang out at, but it's still too close to people who remain at the infirmary at all times.

At that point, they might as well do it in their house. In the guest room, Phainon has had enough of watching an injured and bleeding Mydei in their bedroom. Their friends are confined to the kitchen, waiting for the outcome so that they don't get in the way.

Mydei unceremoniously strips off all his clothes, Perdikkas disinfects his scalpel, and Phainon watches the white sheet spread out on the ground in front of him. He chose to already take his seat, prepare mentally for staring as Mydei gets cut into. They all wanted Phainon to stay out of the room for this, but he didn't budge. With his nerves frayed to this extent, it would've ended in a rather destructive fight with Hephaestion at best.

"For the record, I don't like this," he says loudly. Perdikkas raises an eyebrow at him. But before anyone can respond, he reluctantly continues, "But I understand why it's necessary."

"Good," Mydei says, lying down on his stomach. He rests on his elbows, looking at Phainon with his head tilted and hair slipping onto his face. Pretty as ever, even as he's about to be covered in his own blood, head to toe. Phainon will diligently wipe it away for him. "We would have gone through with it even if you didn't."

"Asshole," Phainon mutters and shoves him on his shoulder. Mydei's other arm aids in preventing his face from smashing into the ground, even though it gets dangerously close to it. He even throws a smirk at Phainon, entirely unbothered about what's to come.

"For clarity's sake," Perdikkas clears his throat, taking his seat on the opposite side of Mydei. "Based on your recent experience, you should be able to immediately tell something is wrong as soon as I make a deep enough cut."

"Yes."

Define deep enough cut, Phainon wants to snark at him, but he holds back. It depends on the tissue, he knows. He already asked.

"Since it's the kind of pain that goes beyond your usual threshold and might impact you enough to have consequences even if the area isn't lethal itself, we will go over your entire body," Perdikkas confirms in a steady voice. "If you feel it, you're to stop me at once."

"If he won't, then I will," Phainon chides in, waving a cloth at Mydei. Everything is about to become stained in a gold not so dissimilar to his eye color. "It's easy to tell."

"Don't overestimate yourself in thinking you can spot when I'm in pain if I'm actively suppressing it," Mydei tells him, expression unconvinced.

Phainon is sure his face mirrors the exact expression. "Don't delude yourself with thinking I won't notice the smallest shift."

"Let's start," Perdikkas talks over them, already exasperated.

And then he makes the first cut.

It wouldn't be a surprise if so much gold couldn't be entirely removed from the floorboards. A basin filled with water sits at Phainon's left, now also completely overtaken by the color of ichor. The rags will have to be thrown out.

Mydei's fingers are tangled with his own, keeping the hold secure even as his breathing turns quiet and even. Phainon is intimately acquainted with the breathing pattern he adopts when truly asleep. For some time now, it's no longer as easy to fool him into assuming his friend is asleep when the opposite is true. Phainon rubs his thumb over the back of Mydei's palm, trying to swipe around the last cut that remains on his stomach with his other hand. It continues to bleed sluggishly, but it's not deep enough to warrant stitches.

The gold only smears on the pale skin, muting the vibrant red of the markings. Phainon sighs, dumps the rug into the basin. So much for being helpful. At least it's over.

"No other weak spots to be found," Perdikkas says into the heavy silence that settled once Mydei's blood loss-induced rambling slowed, trailing off into an absent look in his eyes and eventually dozing when no new cut came after a few minutes. "That's good news."

"What are the chances there's something deeper inside that you weren't able to check?" Phainon asks.

"Incredibly low, but you never know," Perdikkas responds. He hums and sets his tools down onto the towel set out in front of him. "Most of his organs, if not all, had been injured or rendered beyond repair over the course of his life. Yet they never failed to regain their full functionality without a hiccup. If I had to give you a single area I am not confident with, it would be his brain." He reaches out and hovers one hand over the back of Mydei's head. "A sword cleaved through here, stuck approximately six

centimeters deep." He points just above Mydei's right ear. "An arrow shot in this spot, embedded halfway into his head."

"Watch out for the head and the single spot in his spine," Phainon summarizes, staring at Mydei's stomach, where the tenth thoracic vertebra sits on the opposite side. A week ago, he didn't exactly remember the names of the spinal segments. For the rest of his life, he will be able to point to that specific spot without a thought spared. "Got it."

Perdikkas sends him a tired smile, wincing when he gets to his feet. "We should help him clean up and then settle him in bed. His healing factor still drains him too much after that scare." And the slow and constant abuse of it during this procedure didn't help one bit.

"I will take care of it," Phainon waves him off, already slipping his forearms below Mydei's knees and behind his back. "You go let the others know so they can stop worrying already."

Perdikkas huffs, reaching out to ruffle Phainon's hair when he straightens up. "So determined to do everything on your own. How about letting us help, so that we don't feel so useless?" He asks. Partly sad, mostly resigned. "I can get you some food."

Phainon grimaces the moment his brain connects food and Perdikkas. He's had enough of it to last a lifetime, even if he still believes it's better than Ptolemy's. At least it's edible.

Perdikkas laughs at his expression, hand slipping off. "Alright, Peucesta will make some food for you. Deal?"

Phainon nods and moves toward the door. Perdikkas sidesteps him, opening the door before letting him through. "Can you ask him to make waffles?" He asks quietly, mumbling thanks when the door to their room is opened for him as well. "We should still have some pomegranates."

"Of course. Feel free to fetch any of us if you change your mind or decide you might want some company," Perdikkas tells him, gently closing the door as he leaves him to it.

Phainon hums to himself as he sets off to their bathroom, Mydei's weight as light as ever. He hopes it's because Phainon has developed more muscles, along with Mydei getting heavier, rather than him still being underweight. He certainly doesn't look like it, at least.

Phainon rouses him enough to make him sit down on the toilet, and he cannot help the small smile when he watches Mydei yawn, canines peeking out. He rubs one of his eyes, the other blinking down at Phainon sluggishly. Cute.

He goes through the motions as he takes off Mydei's shorts along with his underwear as the bathtub fills with water. He's become an expert in keeping his eyes averted. For once, it doesn't take much effort, even if deliberately thin golden lines still litter his body.

Phainon helps him into the bathtub, mindful so that Mydei is seated comfortably and can continue sleeping as Phainon takes his own clothes off. He follows in, ready to methodically rinse him off the remaining blood and keep his eyes carefully averted.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Their house is one giant mess. Phainon carefully maneuvers around the objects, big and small, dug out of closets, shelves, and piles. He makes various sounds of consideration and indecisiveness as he attempts to sort them somehow.

"You cannot take all of them," Mydei's voice tells him from the doorframe, and Phainon, in his annoyance, snaps his teeth at him in response. Shut up. Mydei only raises an amused brow. "You should have listened to me when I told you to slow down with your purchases."

"Yeah, yeah," Phainon flicks his hand in the air. "Do you think Ptolemy isn't currently occupied with disassembling his entire library and sneaking books

into all sorts of compartments? We will all be carrying his textbooks, and we won't even be aware of it." Surely Phainon can sneak some of his relics into the bags belonging to his friends as well.

"Even he won't be able to bring with him the entirety of his collection," Mydei feels the need to remind him, which, yeah. Ptolemy's library is packed from shelf to shelf, some tomes thicker than Phainon's forearm.

"Well, what am I supposed to do with all this, then?" Phainon despairs, gesturing wildly at every surface in his sight. He would dramatically sprawl across the floor, but there is barely any space to stand, much less sit or lie down.

"Sell to Milios?" Mydei suggests.

It pulls a snort from Phainon, followed by an eyeroll. "And so what, I just return everything that I bought back to them?"

"Don't be stupid," Mydei clicks his tongue, gaze traveling over artifacts and knick-knacks closest to him. "You've got plenty of items we collected through the travels to villages and towns. We even visited two other city-states. I believe Ptolemy mentioned that some of those must have gone up in value over time as well. Don't you think we could use some more money after we depleted our reserves for this journey?"

Phainon doesn't just think acquiring more money would be useful; he knows it would. But it's difficult to choose which relics hold the most monetary value, and which ones he would rather keep out of sentimentality. Obviously, all the small treasures the two of them gifted to each other are taking priority in his packing. But what about the rest?

"I suppose you're right," Phainon mutters, scratching the base of his skull as he looks mournfully at his belongings. "How am I even supposed to sort through these, though?"

Mydei lets out a non-committal hum. Phainon didn't exactly expect him to be helpful with this, just like Mydei doesn't expect his help in packing the cooking equipment. He wouldn't even let Phainon make an argument in that

area. Mydei crouches to pick up a vase, the first ever relic Phainon purchased in Milios. He remembers the smug feeling when Ptolemy validated the authenticity of it after the guards questioned his taste. Mydei then walks up to Phainon, carefully stepping on his tiptoes around various goods and knick-knacks.

"One day, you will be able to store all the relics you desire to keep with no regard for money or space required for them," he promises, lips quirked up at the corners. He presses the vase into Phainon's arms, making sure it's held securely before he lets go. "I'm going to Hephaestion's. At least clear a path to our bed, bathroom, and kitchen before I'm back."

He turns around and makes his way back, and Phainon's hands are occupied with the stupidly fragile vase to grab him and keep him in place. "Wait, you are leaving me just like that?" He asks instead, incredulous. Mydei encouraged him to buy all these things, stood by and glared at shopkeepers as Phainon bartered to get the price down, or even bought some for him. Clearly, he is just as responsible.

"I cannot decide for you which relics are worth keeping, Deliverer," Mydei says and waves at him over his shoulder, not turning to look back. Phainon can hear the self-satisfied smile in his tone. "I'll be back in an hour."

And then the front doors creak, Mydei gone. Phainon refrains from kicking the small box to his left, but just so. They both know there is no way he'll accomplish all of this in an hour.

chapters.title: Chapter 18: and bid farewell
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei unceremoniously slips Ptolemy off his shoulder right in front of Perdikkas. He doesn't appear fazed by Ptolemy's shriek at being dropped to the ground with no prior warning.

"What happened?" Perdikkas asks, immediately crouching to untie the blue fabric wrapped around the bleeding wound and inspect its severity. It's nothing serious. Might need stitches, but it's about time Ptolemy acquired a scar or two.

"It's your fault," Ptolemy complains, or more accurately whines. "Forcing me to spar with you, making me confident with all the practice I've been getting. You should take responsibility for that disaster you wrought on me."

Chapter Notes

Phainon recalls hearing the exact number of people residing in the settlement being mentioned during the Council meetings. A lot of times, in fact. The amount changes frequently, taking into account the inevitable deaths, regular births, and stragglers that appear every now and then to join them.

It's Dametrius' responsibility to keep track of their population, and Phainon has no desire to put effort into mentally updating the number every other meeting. But what he does know is that the number is high enough to fill a small town at the very least.

It's not a settlement anymore, though. They abandoned the location, left it for someone new to find and populate again. To make use of the established structures and systems created with incredible Kremnoan engineering. Those are good grounds for a proper town to be established one day.

Now, Phainon and the Kremnoans surrounding him form a detachment army. A large enough one that they have to travel in groups.

The ones at the very front, leading and mapping their path toward Ladon, consist of Archidamia, Savvas, Dametrius, and a few of the most trusted soldiers. Second in line until they reach Aenionus is Mydei and his royal retinue. They can see the others just ahead of them, close enough to follow but far enough to have privacy in their conversations.

Archidamia and Mydei's groups are definitely the smallest in the detachment. Third is a considerable number of common soldiers who are capable well enough of handling combat, Hephaestion's parents, Aias, and Thera among them. And so on.

Phainon busies himself thinking of the state of his life years ago. When he left Aedes Elysiae and walked forward with no clear destination ahead of him. The suffocating solitude of it. The fortune of meeting Mydei. Traveling through the forest together, and then the towns and villages. Taking care of themselves as best as they could.

It's difficult not to compare what his life was like for that half-year or so to what it's shaping up to be now.

Leonnius laughs as he randomly runs off, and Peucesta never stops humming. Ptolemy climbs onto Kokopo somewhere along the way, and it takes about fifteen minutes until Hephaestion starts shouting at him to get down, Perdikkas joining in soon after. Mydei smiles at Phainon's side, watching their friends bicker.

It's a familiar scene, one they'd taken part in countless times as they embarked on a new expedition. But now, traveling will become an even more permanent constant in their lives for the foreseeable future. Years, possibly.

And Phainon finds himself enjoying the prospect. He loved the settlement, their warm home, and familiarity. But he is also glad to move on, to have a goal to focus on. Other than the goal seared onto his brain, one he refuses to revisit just yet.

Besides, he likes traveling.

When it's all over, when their campaign is completed, and Phainon has slain his enemy, and Mydei has established himself as a strong King, then Phainon might attempt to drag him on a simple adventure like this. Convince him to travel for a few months and discover new places together. Peacefully, with sparring as their only option to release the restless energy that settles in their bones when too much time passes without a fight.

"Get down and walk, it will be good for your back," Perdikkas yells up to Ptolemy.

Phainon glances over to see Ptolemy literally turning his nose up. "It will be even better for my legs if I just lie down here for an hour or two. You don't even need me down there!"

"There is no reason to put even more strain on Kokopo," Perdikkas argues. "She shouldn't be overworked."

Kokopo huffs irritably as if she finds the idea of her running out of strength ridiculous.

"I will give you a massage once we settle for the night if you get down right now," Perdikkas offers with a small sigh, arms crossed and grinning as if he knows he's already won.

Mydei snorts in reaction, but Ptolemy is already climbing down with a speed that could rival Leonnius.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"Ptolemy," Hephaestion calls incredulously, easily intercepting the blade meant for their scholar. "What the fuck?"

In doing so, he lightly bumps into Ptolemy, causing him to stumble forward. Ptolemy yelps, catching himself in the last moment before he can fall face-first into the dirt. And instead, comes face-to-face with another enemy. Hephaestion stays a step behind, handling three other assailants. Phainon watches from his own spot in the fight, only paying half of his attention to his opponents to make sure Ptolemy isn't overwhelmed.

"What does it look like?" Ptolemy snipes back, glaring at the armed stranger in front of him. When the man moves, Ptolemy quickly jabs his dagger right above the knee. Then watches as he drops to the ground, and doesn't hesitate to drive that very same dagger into the neck. "I'm leaving."

Phainon wouldn't even call this a battle. A small skirmish at most, detected by one of the runners who came back with an offer of cheap coin from the villagers if they were to rid them of the terrorizing pests demanding money as protection for nothing. Seeing as their group was getting keyed up with restless energy of constant walking but no real outlet, Mydei sent Leonnius to inform Archidamia, and they took a detour to handle it.

They should catch up to the rest within a few hours, really. There are somewhat more enemies than anticipated, but their skill remains mediocre in comparison. Peucesta and Perdikkas wait a significant distance from the fight for safety while Leonnius watches from the outskirts. Phainon, Mydei, and Hephaestion are making quick work of it.

Ptolemy insisted on tagging along. To stretch his legs. Allegedly.

And now he is abandoning his post, scurrying away as he has clearly had enough of the adrenaline for the day. To give him some credit, he killed about seven people before calling it quits. But these are Ladonians from a squad dispatched to expand their territory, and their forces keep on coming. Blades dipped in poison, unrelenting in their pursuit. At least they are ensuring there will be fewer reinforcements once it's time to battle against Ladon itself.

Phainon looks away for a moment, trying to gauge how many more people will swarm them in the next few minutes. He glances back, and suddenly,

three men are circling Ptolemy. Phainon will remind him of this the next time Ptolemy teases them about being magnets for trouble.

He could probably take care of himself, given time. Phainon is still there within seconds, three bodies dropping down within a minute.

"You wanted to fight alongside us," Phainon points out as he gestures with his sword to the corpses strewn about, even if there aren't that many. For once, he is in the position to be the one unimpressed with Ptolemy's actions. "And now you're running? Desertion is punishable by death in Kremnos, Ptolemy."

Phainon cannot keep the humor from his voice as he says it, very aware of the irony. More than half of their people are deserters. The rest are exiles.

“The man does better who runs from disaster than he who is caught by it,” Ptolemy still has the time to quote at him, throwing him a wide and insolent grin as he runs forward, back to the meeting point. "Your empty threats won't work on me!"

When he wants to be, Ptolemy is quite fast. His stamina never lasts long, but the short bursts of energy are enough to carry him a decent distance. Which is why Phainon can only wince as he watches an enemy run toward Ptolemy, who nearly trips over in his haste to change the course. It's alright, it's just one soldier. Ptolemy is perfectly capable of defending himself against one person when no other factors are at play.

Except that before he manages to cut their throat or stab them through the skull as he prefers to do—quick and to the point, unlike all his tirades—the enemy's blade makes a cut across his thigh.

Phainon sighs, watching as Ptolemy unsurprisingly comes out victorious. Wide gray eyes stare at Phainon from across the field.

Time to wrap it up.

Mydei unceremoniously slips Ptolemy off his shoulder right in front of Perdikkas. He doesn't appear fazed by Ptolemy's shriek at being dropped to the ground with no prior warning.

"What happened?" Perdikkas asks, immediately crouching to untie the blue fabric wrapped around the bleeding wound and inspect its severity.

It's nothing serious. Might need stitches, but it's about time Ptolemy acquired a scar or two. Can someone even call themselves a Kremnoan if they have no scars to speak of? Phainon has yet to meet a person with spotless skin. Someone who isn't Mydei, who would bear more scars than anyone else if that weren't impossible for him.

"It's your fault," Ptolemy complains, or more accurately whines. "Forcing me to spar with you, making me confident with all the practice I've been getting. You should take responsibility for that disaster you wrought on me."

He is whining for the sake of whining. Everyone gathered knows he's already possessed the skill, as reluctant to use it as he had been.

"I'm afraid I'm the only one who can take responsibility," Perdikkas mumbles. He swipes his finger right around the cut, and it comes away sticky with a fluid different than the familiar crimson blood. "It's poisoned," he announces.

He doesn't sound overly concerned, but five pairs of eyes still snap to Ptolemy. He doesn't appear poisoned. Skin the regular shade, eyes clear instead of watery, red, or unseeing, capable of keeping an upright position, no sign of excessive sweating.

No, Ptolemy simply stares blandly at Perdikkas for a long moment. "I'm going to die," he deduces.

Mydei's one hand keeps a deathgrip on his own shirt, having refused to take hold of Phainon's own hand. Phainon didn't insist; he doesn't heal as quickly as Mydei. He would throw up if he had to get his bones set because of it, and someone other than Perdikkas was in charge.

Nose buried in the pink strands of hair—the blond not quite there, even after they took care to wash the blood out—Phainon rubs gentle circles across Mydei's back and thinks they should stop doing this in such drastic situations. Is this the third time one of them shatters to pieces in another's lap? Fourth?

A drop of liquid against his neck startles him out of his thoughts. Is it starting to rain? Phainon doesn't want to walk past everyone on the way to their tent. He doesn't care about them seeing him out of sorts, not right now. But he definitely doesn't want them to see Mydei like this. They probably wouldn't care since they are still in awe of his violent revenge. But some rules are already ingrained in Phainon's brain, the multiple cautionary lectures of how a prince cannot ever show his grief. Weakness as a whole, as it always boils down to.

Phainon glances up at the dark sky, but no clouds greet him. Only stars twinkling in pale light where they peek from behind the tree canopies. Another droplet slides down his skin. And Mydei coughs wetly, ending in a horrible, broken sound.

Terrified, Phainon freezes entirely.

Mydei is crying.

For over half a decade that they've known each other, Phainon has never seen him cry. Not a single tear escaped his eyes, even when faced with his own death or impossible situations. Even when Phainon jolted awake to screams torn from Mydei's throat in the middle of a gruesome nightmare, it was never to tears staining his face.

"Mydei," Phainon says with despair, voice cracking. Mydei shudders again, head angled low so that his face isn't visible, and Phainon's chest is cleaved in half. "Fuck, Mydei. You can cry, alright? No one will know, and, and it's normal. It's—" fine, he doesn't say. It's not.

Mydei's head knocks into Phainon's chest as he sniffs loudly, and Phainon wraps his hands firmly around him, pressing him even closer. He's burning, and Phainon can make out the tiniest swirls of red in the air. He never wanted Mydei to experience this.

"I'm here," Phainon says instead. "Mydei, I'm here. And I'm not going anywhere. We will deal with it together, and we will—" his voice catches, and he has to sniff to keep his voice clear, has to push through his own tears. "We will mourn him together. Not alone, together. You always say that, right? So we can cry together, too."

Mydei's hand finally unclasps, and it snakes just beneath Phainon's arms, clutching to the back of his shirt. The stump of his other hand presses in the same direction. He pushes his head slightly up, hiding it in the crook of Phainon's neck, hair tickling his face. Phainon hears his shirt tear behind him, feels the warmth of Mydei's fingers brushing against his skin and the cold air slipping through. Phainon would let him tear any of his shirts if it gave him a piece of mind. He would let him break his bones and face the unknown medic if it settled his grief.

Phainon is, unfortunately, painfully aware it will never be that easy.

Mydei heaves for a long moment. "He said not to mourn," he whispers, breath hitching.

Phainon winces. Yeah. Perdikkas did say that, and Phainon holds his tongue from expressing how foolish a request that was, even if he loves Perdikkas dearly. How do you not mourn your family?

"Just for today, then," Phainon says desperately. Just a little bit, to give Mydei some time to let it out. "Let's mourn, and tomorrow we will pick up the pieces. Yeah?"

The rest of their friends won't move on immediately, nor should they. But Perdikkas' dying wish for Mydei was not to mourn, and Phainon isn't the only one who would do everything in his power to honor their dead friend. So, Phainon will try to help him through it the best he can.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

This is the first time someone so close to Mydei has died, but also the first death in their group as a whole.

Perdikkas' death is still fresh, the dirt they dug up to place him into a shallow grave still wet. Ptolemy placed some of Perdikkas' belongings beside his corpse, then sobbed himself hoarse atop the evened out ground. Blood is still caked under his fingernails.

Leonnius openly sniffles into Peucesta's shoulder. Hephaestion stares into the fire blankly. He looks numb.

Stop it, or you will hurt your eyesight, Perdikkas would have said with exasperation by now. Phainon chokes those words down before they can even begin forming.

Ptolemy looks the worst out of them all, more out of it than even Mydei. Because Mydei created an outlet for himself, he brought vengeance on an army of hundreds that anyone else could only dream of carrying out. He is one leg and arm short for it, staring at the bandages that are tied differently than usual, by foreign hands of a medic with a quiet focus rather than sharp reprimands.

Ptolemy, meanwhile, trembles silently. His head is cradled between his knees, hands covering the back of his hair and gripping so tightly that the knuckles have turned white. Phainon has never seen him without the laurels woven into the blond strands, yet now they sit abandoned on the ground. Discarded like a meaningless decoration. Like Mydei, a spot on his hair remains discolored where Perdikkas accidentally smeared his blood.

They were the oldest of their group, closest in age. They spent countless hours together, quiet company as each wrote down different sets of notes. Perdikkas often stayed over at Ptolemy's, searching for medical books in the ever-growing collection. They talked animatedly about subjects Phainon could never find interest in. For Perdikkas, Ptolemy picked up training and walked into the battles.

Phainon feels the need to say something, anything. Offer support and be the pillar they all can lean against, as Ptolemy has always been. He knows they will get through this, honor Perdikkas' death, and move on, as that's what he would have wanted. It's as certain as the stars hanging high above them. But he feels useless, sitting there quietly.

His throat is choked up, and there's a buildup in his nose, eyes stinging.

Mydei shudders where he lies beside him, still wide awake and turned away from everyone in their group. Phainon glances down, notes the eyes squeezed painfully shut, and one arm wrapped around himself protectively. He swallows and exhales roughly. He prays to any and all Titans that nothing of this sort will happen again, even if he knows better than to believe in their care for the mortals.

Phainon swallows the lump in his throat and lies down with Mydei. No one pays them any attention, not that he expected them to. Mydei stiffens briefly

before allowing himself to relax, and Phainon treats it as permission to press himself close enough that neither of them would be able to move without shifting the other as well. He covers Mydei's spine with his own body, wraps one arm around his middle. Mydei's messy hair tickles his nose, so Phainon presses it against the too-warm shoulder.

He knows it's not enough. He tries not to think about it. He would offer Mydei everything he has if he knew it would help.

The only sounds accompanying them are the crackling flames and occasional sniffling.
