chapters.title: Chapter 19: and bind them tightly
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"Phainon," Mydei speaks into the darkness of their room once they settle in for the night. Ready for sleep to claim them, as elusive as it's been lately. "You aren't allowed to die."

Phainon expected to hear that sooner rather than later. He shifts onto his side so that he can face Mydei, their legs still tangled. "Is that the Crown Prince's decree?"

"Yes," Mydei responds immediately.

"Alright," Phainon says easily, smiling. "As long as you live as well."

Chapter Notes

After what feels like an hour or maybe more of lying on his back with eyes closed but no sleep to claim him, Phainon gives up on the notion of rest. Restlessness itches beneath his skin, calling for him to get up and do something, anything.

It's the middle of the night, and everyone is supposed to be sleeping. Supposed to. Because Phainon clearly can't. And when he sits up in defeat, careful not to jostle Mydei around, he notices another person hunched over near the fire. He blinks a few times until it clicks which one of their friends it might be.

Ptolemy.

He is staring directly into the flames, and Phainon briefly worries about his eyesight. He is toying with the hair tie, delicately snapping it against his fingers. His expression is closed off, blank in an unfamiliar way. Ptolemy usually never shies away from being expressive.

Maybe Phainon should lie back down. Pretend to sleep until his body catches on and pulls him under.

Grey eyes snap to him, and Phainon keeps still.

Ptolemy regards him with an intense focus he usually reserves for ancient texts written in languages he only has a rudimentary understanding of. Phainon remembers the day they first arrived at the settlement. When Ptolemy found out about his and Mydei's crude rendition of sign language, that gaze held more levity and excitement. There are no traces of either right now.

"You should tell him, Phainon." Ptolemy's voice is nothing more than a hoarse whisper. It would crack if he were speaking at full volume. "Figure it out together. Don't waste time."

Phainon frowns, not fully understanding. "Tell him what?"

There is a lot to figure out. There is a lot of time being wasted. He's got no clue which of those things Ptolemy might be referring to.

"That you love him," is the simple answer he gets, and Phainon stops breathing. "That you want more."

Phainon swallows as words tumble out of Ptolemy. There is desperation in there, one Phainon never would have guessed Ptolemy carried. The two sentences echo in his brain, and he bites on the inside of his cheek. There is no use denying who the him in question might be; Phainon has only ever felt this way about one person. He doesn't think it would do well for him to play stupid right now, not when Ptolemy is out of sorts.

Which is more than understandable. Perdikkas died two days ago. Peucesta has only spoken in halted words since. Hephaestion's eyes are permanently swollen and red around the edges. Mydei watches every shadow for an opportunity to let loose again, and red mist swirls in the air when he forgets himself.

With his go-to option of denial out of the equation, Phainon settles on responding with why he cannot do just that.

"Isn't this just… Doesn't everyone always say that love at this age doesn't last? It's all hormones, both you and Perdikkas said once. And circumstances. And feelings we don't understand. Or something." He runs one hand through his hair, glancing at Mydei's sleeping form. He thinks he would have fallen in love with this boy under any circumstances. These are feelings he unfortunately understands quite well. "I don't want to risk everything on something so unsure."

He doesn't think he would survive it if Mydei distanced himself from Phainon purely because of some stupid feelings.

"Unsure?" Ptolemy lets out a hollow laugh, the hair tie falling from his fingers. "Phainon, seriously?"

Mydei twitches, lips thinning and fingers clenching on nothing. Without thinking, Phainon presses his hand into them, giving him something to hold onto even while he is unaware. He shuffles a little closer, keeps his thigh pressed to Mydei's revealed stomach. And Mydei settles just like that, tension disappearing from his face.

And something inside Phainon swells with affection at being trusted so openly, having been given the ability to soothe Mydei into slumber even when there is foreign noise around him. Half a decade ago, Mydei would've been up and scanning his surroundings within a second. And then that something inside Phainon breaks a little, remembering the conversation at hand.

"Your eyes follow Mydei. Always." Ptolemy's voice carries to him easily, back in an appropriately low volume. "He is the first thing you lock onto when you return after you are away from each other, like a magnet. Separation anxiety or not, you two give the impression you would have been attached at the hip regardless. If he wasn't cursed to return to life in nearly every instance without any help, I have half a mind that you would have ventured out to drag him back yourself." Ptolemy glances down at Mydei, whose fingers have tangled with Phainon's of their own accord. "Or

maybe ventured out after him and stayed there, to remain by his side again. That isn't hormones."

"He would have hated me if I forfeited my life like that," Phaion huffs softly. With his free hand, he detaches the clip from Mydei's braid, forgotten in the wake of an exhausting and stressful day. They are stepping into the heart of Ladon tomorrow, forced to wait until Mydei fully recovers.

"Not as much as you would have hated living without him."

Phainon gazes up and meets Ptolemy's eyes over the fire for a moment. The moths fly wildly around the flames, disoriented by the light. Phainon is not used to Ptolemy keeping still like this. He's always rattling off some new information with a grin or an exasperated eye roll. He fidgets with things, or bounces his leg, taps his fingers against something. He jumps from one subject to the next before anyone can catch on to his thought process.

"There isn't much to think about, not really." Ptolemy sighs, looking so exhausted he may as well have aged a decade. He picks up the hair tie from where it fell to the ground. "Just tell him."

Phainon shakes his head before he can even give it any thought. But as Ptolemy said, there's not much to think about in relation to the matter. "What's to say he would even love me in the same way?"

Ptolemy blinks at him, and some brief traces of that exasperation and disbelief finally crack through. "You are the only reason he is even soundly asleep in this moment, you know this. I have yet to meet a person with a stronger sense of self-restraint than him, and yet he used to lose his mind at the sheer prospect of you being hurt. Doesn't initiate touch often, but he's been all over you since the very beginning," Ptolemy counts out, and Phainon almost tells him to shut up already when he feels his face burn. None of these mean anything; it's just the way the two of them are. "I have explained to him the meaning of HKS a while back. And even then, he never stopped calling you just that."

They never did get around to more complex Kremnoan lessons. Phainon has the basics of it down, he is pretty sure. He could probably communicate

well enough if he had to by using simple phrases. Mydei often stays up at night, frowning down at the pages of old books written in what was meant to be his mother tongue. They can listen just fine, but neither of them can write more than a few words despite the years passing. The nuances are lost on them.

Phainon assumed there was nothing much else to the insult than the initial explanation. But the way Ptolemy says it, it seems important. It cannot be that different, can it?

"What exactly does HKS stand for?" Phainon asks quietly.

"In the traditional Kremnoan, its original meaning can be translated to hyena, scoundrel, bastard, or fool," Ptolemy repeats what Phainon has thought the word meant all this time. Carefully, almost reverently, he slips the hair tie around his wrist again. "In more modern times, and when spoken to your closest, it is usually interpreted as beloved."

Phainon's brain screeches to a halt.

Beloved.

He tracks back to all the little instances Mydei casually threw the word at him. Never anyone else. And, apparently, aware of the double meaning.

"It's the one person from whom you will bear any pain or grief they might serve you," Ptolemy explains, fingers grasping tightly on blond hair. "Perhaps they betray you, or break a promise, or simply behave in a way that's so infuriating despite the great efforts you went to to make them stop.

"And yet you continue to love them through everything." He lets out a shuddering exhale, hair disheveled when he lets go to trace the hair tie with his fingers instead. "The origin of the more recent definition stems from two generals of opposing armies who had fallen in love amid the raging war, despite trying to kill each other to secure peace or victory for their own lands. An acknowledgement of strength, admiration, and a love born in the short few-day truce established to handle the dead and injured. One of them was Kremnoan."

His gaze clears somewhat. Maybe it's a relief for him to lapse into relaying the historical context. Phainon almost grasps onto the question of what happened to the two lovers and asks for more. Given his knowledge of many Kremnoans legends and stories of old, he is not sure if hearing the ending aloud will do either of them any good.

Desperately, he searches for something else to say.

"Perdikkas called you HKS once before," is what tumbles out of Phainon's mouth once the memory resurfaces, brain still looping around the word.

Ptolemy inhales sharply, coughing when he seems to choke on empty air. "Wha— When?"

"The baths. Milios. We were… I just remember Leonnius being a dick. And then Perdikkas was walking past us after you annoyed him, I think," he says, a little hysterical. "I thought he was just angry with you. Mydei is usually one moment from snapping when he calls me that."

Ptolemy stares at him in astonishment for one short moment. Phainon watches as his lips press into a thin line first, expression gradually shattering. He clutches one hand against his mouth, eyes going blank before they squeeze shut. He looks like he is in pain. Phainon hesitates, feels an impulse to wake up someone else who might know what to do.

Before he can make up his mind, a strangled noise makes it past Ptolemy's throat and stops him in his tracks. Ptolemy's shoulders shake minutely, and he hunches in on himself, pressing one hand into his face with so much force that Phainon worries he might hurt himself. His head is angled low, and his hair obstructs the view, but the sound of sniffling is unmistakable. He is crying.

"Ptolemy," Phainon croaks out, louder than he probably should. He nearly gets up, ready to help in any way he can.

Ptolemy only shakes his head, so fast that it might actually be painful. "Don't," he chokes out, and it ends on a sob.

Phainon feels tears well up at the corners of his eyes. He swallows and tastes salt.

Ptolemy never panics. He is dramatic, and he will run from danger rather than face it. But he will stand tall at their backs, he will argue with the members of the Council like they are beneath him, he will research every written word for a solution, and he will keep them steady as he remains unwavering.

Only when the world ends will Ptolemy crumble. Phainon thinks of being in his shoes and having to face the rest of his life without Mydei, and knows that it would feel like nothing short of the end of the world to him.

He looks back down at Mydei, takes care so that he doesn't squeeze his fingers too hard. He wants to lie back down, press close, and pacify his mind with the fact that they are still together. Always together. Cover the spot on Mydei's spine with his own body to ensure no harm comes to it. But Ptolemy is still crying, and he doesn't want help or attention on him, and if Phainon moves too much, Mydei will wake up.

So he stays put and sniffles on his own. Phainon's heart aches for his friend, the one he would call a brother without hesitation when asked. He owes so many things to Ptolemy, the first person who truly took care of them among the Kremnoans. Phainon settles on watching the moths flying wildly around the fire, distorted by the bright light.

"Phainon," Ptolemy eventually calls, voice hoarse and cracking. Phainon winces, but glances over nonetheless. Ptolemy's eyes are red and puffy, and he's cradling the wrist with the hair tie close to his chest. He looks small, and that's not a word Phainon would ever associate with him despite his lithe figure. "There is no pain so great as the memory of joy in present grief. If you don't tell him and something happens, you will never forgive yourself. Believe me."

"I…" Phainon trails off, swallowing hard. Can he really promise to do that? "I will try to resolve this."

The sadness in Ptolemy's gaze mixes with pity, and Phainon doesn't want to think about his own situation. Not ever, but especially not in the context of Perdikkas and Ptolemy's missed opportunity. He doesn't think Ptolemy will get any sleep tonight. Phainon isn't sure he got more than an hour since everything happened.

He glances one last time at the fire burning near them, and catches sight of one moth just as it flies too close. Its wings catch a spark of flame. He tracks the movement, watches as it beats its wings frantically, even more disoriented than by the light itself. Until eventually, it gets swallowed by the fire in its entirety.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Three days after the war's conclusion, half of their detachment army marches through the streets of Ladon. People stare and whisper, cower and hide in their houses. Their soldiers are clad in golden armor and blood-red fabrics, and Phainon is sure those two colors will haunt the citizens for the rest of their lives.

Mydei leads the way, eyes listless and set straight ahead. Not a single mark of the encounter with the Ladonian militia remains on his body. Phainon saw the last few Ladonian soldiers retreating. He knows they caught sight of Mydei on the verge of death. The rumors must have spread like wildfire by now, Mydei's very presence like a mythical being that stepped out of the ancient texts.

The leaders meet them at the plaza. A large open space paved with stone and adorned with statues. Large storefronts circle around, people peeking from the windows openly. Those with more bravery have wandered closer, though their faces are as pale as a sheet. Phainon feels something crawling through his skin.

The King and Queen of Ladon stand with four guards kept close at their backs. The royal couple tries to portray a unified front, resolute and unyielding. Their facade drops with every step the detachment marches closer, and by the time Mydei stands in front of them, their postures have turned subdued and their eyes grown fearful.

Phainon glances at the soldiers behind them. He notes the too-tight grip on swords, stances tense, and, in their stress, incorrect. It would take less than a minute to disarm them.

The King visibly steels himself and finally regards Mydei.

"What do they call you, young man?" He asks, and Phainon is impressed that his voice doesn't waver. "Where do you hail from?"

"My name is Mydeimos," is all Mydei offers.

No one reacts to the name, but this far from the Kremnoan influence, it would be more of a shock if they did. As far as they know, the Crown Prince's fate as an infant wasn't heavily announced outside of Castrum Kremnos' walls.

Ptolemy argued for revealing Mydei's name if asked for it in the last Council meeting this morning, exhausted and heartbroken, but his mind no less sharp. Their detachment bears no flags or sigils, armors only lightly modified to retain the Kremnoan effectiveness despite the altered appearance.

People talk, and what they don't understand, they justify as divine. Ptolemy could be wrong. All it would take to ruin the illusion is one person who recognizes any soldier by name or face. But until then, it should work to craft a certain image of their detachments.

When Mydei doesn't elaborate or acknowledge the second question, the Queen asks next, "Have you come to usurp our city-state?"

"No," Mydei responds earnestly, even if it sounds hollow. "We decided to put an end to your quest for forceful territory expansion. You should

relinquish the land you have taken from the defenseless."

They aren't quite that noble. They didn't pick this war for the sake of those people. Archidamia is the one responsible for this campaign, and the goal remains the same as what the Kremnoans in Castrum Kremnos have been abiding by. Search for an ongoing struggle or ignite it yourself.

Anything in the name of bringing victory in a battle.

They could have moved on without addressing this at all after laying siege to their forces. Mydei remained firm in his decision to put pressure on the Ladonians. As pointless as the rest of the people attending the meeting undoubtedly found that notion, no one dared to argue.

Unlike right now.

The man sputters in incredulity. "We fought for them." He must have taken pride in what they've done.

Phainon cannot say with confidence that, were Castrum Kremnos not confined to the moving fortress, the Kremnoans wouldn't have done the very same thing except more effectively.

Kremnos takes no hostages and has no need for the expansive lands to be ruled under its name. And yet, the Mountain Dwellers were subjugated during one of the conquest campaigns. They aren't that much better than the Ladonians who terrorize nearby villages and towns. Some would argue that Kremnoans are worse.

Mydei tightens his jaw, his gaze hardening. The man flinches back.

"We, we cannot give all of them back," the man continues with bravery fueled by foolishness. "How are we supposed to—"

"This is not a negotiation," Mydei interrupts him with a steely voice.

He tilts his head, pinning the King with the intensity of his gaze. It's scary when combined with the utterly blank expression. Resembling a predator

like it rarely does anymore. Phainon barely suppresses a shiver, realizing he somehow missed that expression. It's not often Mydei goes into such a state.

"We won't massacre your people unless they engage us in a fight," Mydei continues, "But we can set fire to your walls and ensure you don't have the means to rebuild. You will find yourself too occupied with fixing this instead of terrorizing others. Would you prefer that?"

The man's mouth opens and closes, face growing red. The Queen places her hand on his elbow, and he stiffens before visibly deflating.

"If you leave our city-state right away and never set foot in it again, we will content ourselves with its original size and halt any further expansion," the woman offers. Her gaze remains steady even as her voice trembles ever so much. "The villages and smaller towns will regain their autonomy within the next few months."

Mydei gives a sharp nod, satisfied with the answer. He doesn't seem to care that Archidamia planned to restock some of their supplies here, and she doesn't speak up on the matter either.

"You have half a year. If you go back on your word," Mydei still says, "We will return and take your heads with us."

The pair looks nauseous at the threat, and the guards' hands tighten on their weapons. Mydei disregards them completely as he turns his back to them, deeming them harmless, and gives a command to retreat.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

It's quiet in a way Phainon isn't used to when surrounded by his friends.

Ptolemy already appears thinner, cheeks hollow, and deep purple bruises underlining his eyes that never stray far from the pages of journals.

Peucesta strums on his lyre, speaks maybe five full sentences total since Perdikkas' death, and only in Leonnius' presence. Leonnius runs between the groups tirelessly, willingly carrying correspondence even when he's not required to, stopping only to hydrate.

Hephaestion and Mydei both stride with their gazes similarly blank. But where Hephaestion walks forward carelessly as if repeating the motions by habit alone, Mydei's body coils tightly with tension, each step determined.

Unlike in any other situation when their entire group jumps on the occasion to reassure each other and provide support, this time they are too fragile to do much else than carry on. Which leaves Phainon with nothing to distract himself with, giving his thoughts free rein.

It's only two subjects that could come to his mind in this moment, really.

And Phainon would rather chew glass than let himself crumble under the weight of guilt over his friend's death. He should have reacted faster, he should have checked their surroundings, he shouldn't have distracted Mydei, and maybe he would have caught sight of danger in time. Or maybe it's just his curse that leads to people he cares about dying.

Phainon forcibly shuts those thoughts down, inhaling sharply and thinking about anything else louder the moment they slip through.

It leaves him pondering on the conversation he had with Ptolemy instead. As agonizing a subject as it is, it remains preferable to the other one. He replays Ptolemy's words over and over in his mind, tries to find courage despite the self-consciousness rearing its head.

So, Phainon loves Mydei.

Mydei could love Phainon back. Romantically. Potentially. Days have passed, and they will reach Campa soon, yet he still struggles to shed the last bits of uncertainty.

He spent so long telling himself all these touches and trust couldn't have meant more than the most platonic of attachments. With the way Mydei

grew up, it makes sense. Phainon, the first person Mydei experienced care and love from, was the one he would latch onto with no real understanding of societal rules and concepts.

But—

Phainon isn't Kremnoan. He doesn't share the core values of Kremnoans. He may be a Chrysos Heir, but even his power doesn't measure up to what his peers are seemingly capable of. He lost his own village and couldn't save anyone. He failed to protect Mydei numerous times. And even now, the deaths of precious people follow him.

Whether Mydei means it or if he simply doesn't care to put importance on the word, is Phainon the right person to be on the receiving end of it?

They are already intertwined enough. What if they go further, and Phainon brings him nothing but misery? Months ago, Phainon came to terms with the fact that Hephaestion might be more suitable for Mydei. Or that both of them would have to settle on watching Mydei fall in love with someone else. Maybe they would have learned how to get along better then.

But what happens now that Mydei miraculously reciprocating his feelings has become a real possibility?

And even if he doesn't, Phainon would… like to tell him, one day. Not yet. Not until he is sure it won't affect them negatively should Ptolemy be wrong. He ignores the exasperated voice at the back of his head telling him Ptolemy is never wrong.

And where does that leave Hephaestion?

All the groups the detachment is divided into gravitate closer together for the night, mingling and enjoying each other's company while they rest. Sharing drinks, carrying out chores, sparring.

Mydei leaves to join the people assigned the cooking duty for the day, busying himself with what has become his hobby in recent years. Ptolemy stays with his nose buried in Perdikkas' belongings. Leonnius and Peucesta disappeared somewhere the moment they all pitched their tents.

It creates a perfect opportunity for him to have a conversation with Hephaestion and not worry about anyone overhearing.

He walks around for a bit, grinning back at everyone and dodging attempts to make conversation. Usually, all he has to deal with is hero-worship from kids and open admiration from soldiers. But sometimes, people get the idea that they can get in Mydei's good graces through him, what with Phainon being deemed as more approachable. He doesn't have time for any of that today, not when he's on a time limit. Mydei could finish any moment, and he will search for both Phainon and Hephaestion with plates of food in his hands.

Phainon eventually finds him near a small fire, purposefully lit up away from everyone. Hephaestion sits on the ground, focused entirely on toweling his wet hair. He must have just finished washing up in the nearby river. Phainon wonders if he has found a private enough spot. He also absentmindedly contemplates how they are going to take care of things like wet hair once they reach Aidonia, where the weather isn't so warm.

Before his mind wanders off too far and he loses his resolve to get this conversation over with, Phainon heads over.

"Hephaestion," he calls once he is close enough, then stops. Both walking and talking.

Now what?

Hephaestion doesn't stop toweling his hair, careful with it so that it doesn't get tangled. He only throws Phainon a questioning look. Phainon breathes in deeply as if he's about to speak, and then doesn't. He scratches the back of his head.

Hephaestion rolls his eyes. "Spit it out."

"I'm in love with Mydei," he rushes out the obvious. He has to stop blurting things out when talking to Hephaestion. "And so are you. That's— How do we navigate this?"

Because one of them will get hurt, and there is no way around it. Phainon would rather it be him, if he's being honest. He would bear all the heartache and sorrow for his friends if he could. He would pay the price in a heartbeat.

If Hephaestion truly wishes to pursue it, Phainon might back down with a smile and let him. He will be okay with loving Mydei from the sidelines as he's done so far. What could be better than watching two of his best friends be happy together?

Hephaestion simply looks at him as Phainon goes through the internal pep talk, something weary and resigned settling over his expression. "Phainon," he starts tiredly, slowly, as if they've had this conversation before. They very clearly hadn't. "You are considered to be the Prince Consort by our people, did you know that?"

"I—" Phainon loses momentum, thrown off by the single sentence. Prince Consort. People. "The what."

Hephaestion raises both his eyebrows and stares at him in such an unimpressed manner that it reminds Phainon of Mydei for a moment. "Lady Archidamia should have ensured you know better than to ignore the gossip," he states, but his amusement falls flat.

Phainon scowls at him. Ptolemy and Peucesta both know all the rumors, and they frequently relay them to both Mydei and Phainon. It's become their unofficial duty, and part of the reason he and Mydei insist there is no need for them to personally get involved. Somehow, two of their friends neglected to mention to Phainon that bit of information. He scowls further at the thought that Archidamia may have had a point once upon a time.

He would have known if he had taken the time to engage in the gossip, yes. He is sure one of the drunks would have let that slip, even if the rest of the settlement might have kept their mouths shut.

"You look dumb," Hephaestion says, slipping the towel around his shoulders.

"You are dumb," Phainon shoots back by reflex. "What do you mean by Prince Consort?" His voice cracks embarrassingly on the two words. Phainon clears his throat and pretends it didn't happen.

"Exactly what you think it means," Hephaestion snaps. Just as quickly, he deflates and only rubs his forehead. "We are the royal retinue. Leonnius is the runner. Ptolemy is the scholar and advisor. Perdikkas is— was the appointed medic, even if he refused to abandon his duties as the head healer. Peucesta may be the musician, but he is also the counsel. Phainon's mouth opens and closes a few times hopelessly, no doubt making him appear as an idiot that Hephaestion thinks him to be.

He did know all that. He thought it a hundred times, and he called on their friends' functions in arguments against the Council. And he never exactly figured out what his place in all of it might be. He cannot be Mydei's equal in the eyes of the law. So he would settle somewhere between an advisor and a fighter, an undefined role. Perhaps.

"Mydei is our charge," Hephaestion continues with a click of tongue, looking past Phainon in the general direction of where Mydei must be. Hopefully, he is still occupied with feeding his own people. "And so are you."

Phainon exhales roughly. He takes the last two steps and drops to the ground beside Hephaestion. It's obvious in hindsight. He thinks it may have even been stated aloud before. It wasn't important enough for his brain to catch on, he supposes.

Prince Consort.

He looks at his feet, scratching his neck nervously.

Is Phainon suitable for the role? The Prince's lover. And, in the future, the King's lover. Phainon is just a poor kid from a village that fell to ruin. He isn't Kremnoan. At his very core, he doesn't share their values. And he has a goal to reach above all else, which means he won't prioritize the good of Kremnoans. If he is being honest with himself, sometimes he isn't sure whether he will come back alive from his quest for revenge.

He may be Mydei's equal. But he may not be worth the official title that could come with it were they to get together. Does he even deserve Mydei's love at all, if he cannot commit himself to the Kremnoan rules?

Hephaestion, though. Hephaestion already—

"When I said I wouldn't back down just because you also love Mydei," Hephaestion cuts through his thoughts, as if aware where his mind is going, "back when we were thirteen, I meant it. I cannot stop loving him simply because you two are made for each other or whatever. But," he sighs heavily and rubs his thumb against his bottom lip, scratching it with his nail, "I made my peace with it. Phainon bites on his lip and tries to hold his tongue.

No, he didn't think this was the only possible outcome. Quite the opposite.

But he did know it would be difficult to figure out how to fit another person into Mydei's life without Phainon obstructing his potential relationship with them. Maybe they would have grown out of these childish behaviors eventually, leaving a sliver of space open for someone to fill it. He thinks Hephaestion is kind enough that he would tolerate their oddities until the very end, even.

"Phainon, stop," Hephaestion interrupts him, a little choked up. "I know you would. Because I will be happy for you as well. But can you not make this more painful for me? I will not change my mind on this even if you try to convince me otherwise."

Phainon winces. "Yeah. Sorry."

Hephaestion closes his eyes briefly, then gives in to the urge and bites on his thumb. They sit like that, silence holding a certain weight to it. The flames crackle. In the distance, people cheer at something. Phainon still reels from the conversation.

Prince Consort.

Something giddy rises at the pit of his stomach, and Phainon smothers it viciously. He still isn't entirely convinced it's a good idea.

Hephaestion exhales, long and slow. "Are you going to tell him?"

Phainon bites his lip, makes a noise of consideration. Tries to buy himself some time. Is he going to tell Mydei? Ptolemy urged him to do so.

Perdikkas died, and Phainon doesn't want to live through an unfulfilled love. Risk losing the opportunity to at least reveal the exact depth of his devotion to Mydei.

Perdikkas died, and Phainon doesn't want to pressure Mydei into anything on top of that. Although knowing Mydei, he sorted every negative thought and emotion into tightly shut boxes, then threw them into a space of his mind that Phainon suspects to be shaped like the Sea of Souls. Haunting and containing all the worst memories.

Phainon has his own space like that, does his best to block the frightening nightmares he lived through. It's a fire that burns through everything, threatens to take him under, along with the worst of his memories, and to keep him alight for the rest of eternity with no respite. Like his village, which remains nothing but a blackened husk and graveyard of deformed corpses.

Perdikkas died, and he will remain in their memory for as long as they live. A healer, caretaker, friend. Family that they found despite everything they had gone through. But the two of them will recover faster than the rest, used to the pain. Mydei might have more experience with the physical sort, but he won't let it stop him.

A thought crosses Phainon's mind that perhaps he should wait until the campaign is over. Once Mydei takes the throne, then Phainon can make his feelings known. An established ruler will have different worries, ones that wouldn't be affected by their relationship souring because Phainon cannot keep his mouth shut. And if it does impact Mydei's rule, they will be at the moment of their lives where Phainon can leave and carry out his revenge. Hopefully, he could return afterward and be reinstated at Mydei's side, their relationship back to its original fragile balance.

It would be perfect, actually.

But the campaign will take them years. Then the struggle to fight their way through Castrum Kremnos.

He isn't so sure Ptolemy and Hephaestion would be happy if he took that long.

"I don't— I'm not sure," he eventually responds, wincing. "I don't know when the right time would be?"

It comes out more like a question near the end, but he isn't certain what he is supposed to say. Maybe he is a coward. But it's the one thing he refuses to mess up with impulsivity.

Lost in his mind and miserable thoughts, he doesn't catch Hephaestion's too-fast movement until it's too late, and Phainon is tumbling to the ground with the force of a punch to his shoulder. He yelps, pushing himself back up to a seating position immediately and glaring.

Hepahestion glares at him, arms crossed. "Get over yourself," he tells him, frustration ringing clear. "Knowing Mydei, he will beat you to it at this rate. If he does and you reject him out of your misplaced guilt, I will shoot an arrow into each of your feet."

Hephaestion's eyes nearly flash as he says it, and Phainon has no doubt he would at least attempt to carry out the threat.

He chuckles nervously. "What, you wouldn't be aiming for my head?"

"No."

Hephaestion doesn't elaborate, and Phainon doesn't risk his luck in digging his own grave.

They remain quiet after that, coming to a silent agreement that they will wait until Mydei finds them himself with their plates. If it takes him too long, the chance of him growing annoyed and stopping by the cooking station to subtly transform their food into something disgusting rises. But it's a risk they are apparently willing to take. Phainon is sure he will still be reeling from what he's learned, so he might not even notice.

"I'm sick anyway," Hephaestion mutters under his breath as he busies himself with brushing his hair.

It takes a moment to register among Phainon's muddled thoughts. But when it does, Phainon blinks at him, unsure what that's supposed to mean. "And?"

Hephaestion doesn't look at him, staring resolutely at the ground and nearly yanking on his hair. "What do I even have to offer him? My premature death because I'm stubborn?"

"That doesn't mean you don't deserve to enjoy your life," Phainon argues back, strangely fierce about it. "You can still experience love."

And you've been better lately, he wants to say, but doesn't due to the fear of jinxing it. It's stupid, but he won't take any chances.

"He wouldn't care either," Phainon continues, because he knows Mydei better than he knows himself. "He would have loved you until the end. He — I'm sorry," he cuts himself off, knowing it cannot be helping. He scratches the back of his head and tugs on his own hair as well. "You still love him, and I'm just making it worse."

"I don't want your pity," Hephaestion scoffs, but his head is held high. "It's been so long that these feelings are just a part of me, alright? And the last thing I want is for you two to forsake your happiness because of me."

Phainon doesn't respond because he is certain he will remain happy as long as he has Mydei by his side, regardless of the nature of their relationship. But that's not what Hephaestion wants to hear.

The silence that stretches between them is no longer so heavy, a wordless mutual agreement that they've talked about this subject long enough. They stay that way until Mydei eventually appears in their field of vision, three plates carefully balanced in his hands and a pinched expression that might not be obvious to the naked eye.

"What do you think it's gonna be this time?" Phainon asks, resting his chin on the palm of his hand and smiling into it as he watches Mydei approach them. "Overcooked or over-salted?"

Hephaestion snorts, his toes nudging Phainon's thigh. "My bet is on burnt."

"Ptolemy," Hephaestion calls quietly.

All of them watch as Ptolemy doesn't react, brows furrowed at whatever he is writing.

"Ptolemy." It's louder now, more insistent.

Ptolemy glances up, but his hand doesn't stop moving across the paper. Hephaestion's arm tightens where it's wrapped around his own knee.

"I… need an injection."

They take their time traveling to Campa, and by the time they arrive, they are greeted with cheers and awestruck looks. Delight at the warriors who brought demise to their enemies. It's such a sharp contrast to the way Ladonians—understandably—regarded them.

They are asked for the name of their lands, and Mydei only responds with an off-handed, "Just an army detachment."

He's been slowly losing some of the tension, the haunted look disappearing from his eyes as Phainon slowly began yammering his ear off about this or that. Bumping into him as they walked enough times for Mydei to glare at him with irritation and attempt to trip Phainon up in turn.

But his presence is still commanding, the same way it had been in Ladon. His guard is raised so high up that no outsider even thinks of tempting fate by insisting on more information than Mydei is willing to give.

They fight deep into the Curtain-Fall hour, until Hephaestion is exhausted enough that pinning him down doesn't even count as a win. Kremnoans know how to hold their liquor, though,

so he imagines Campanians must assume Mydei is simply a well-respected leader. Thank Phaugousa.

It's just Ptolemy and Hephaestion occupying the space now.

and Mydei met his untimely demise, Phainon would be making that very same trip not long after.

His only other motivation in life is his revenge, and in the event of Mydei's permanent death, he isn't sure he would remember that for long enough to carry on. Ptolemy hasn't given any indication of planning to join Perdikkas despite the state he is in

It's an unremarkable day.

Mydei raises his eyes, meeting Phainon's. First looking right into the left, then switching to the right. Gold, prettier than their blood. Black pupil no longer a thin needle, now more of a wide oval. He inhales slowly, and then, "I love you."

A strangled noise escapes from Phainon's throat without his permission.

They've said it before. Maybe. Phainon thinks they have. It was obvious even if they didn't. But this sounds different, more serious, and Phainon's brain scrambles to keep up and get it right.

"I love you, too," Phainon rushes out, hand twitching to wrap around Mydei's forearm. To hold him close and make him understand. Those three words he's thought and felt every single day for months, years. They don't feel like enough, yet he hopes they convey everything. Except. Except. "But you— do you? Love, in what way?"

There are all kinds of love, but the one he has for Mydei doesn't compare to anything else. He would understand, though. If it were a regular kind of love. If Mydei just decided to say it aloud for the sake of it.

But Mydei doesn't get nervous.

And he rarely hesitates in his actions. Though he doesn't hesitate now either, not really.

"Does it matter?" He mutters, eyes lidded.

Before Phainon can retaliate that yes, it very much so matters, Mydei is leaning forward at a very slow pace. Slow enough that Phainon has all the time in the world to move away. Phainon is too stunned to react, keeping himself entirely still, so all that happens is his breath hitching. Phainon's eyes naturally navigate lower, finding the slightly curved lips as they get nearer. Mydei carefully navigates closer, nose brushing against Phainon's clumsily until barely-there pressure is placed on Phainon's mouth.

Phainon's heart might break through his ribcage.

Heat burns up his neck and cheeks, but all Phainon can focus on is the softness against his lips, the warm air as Mydei exhales through his nose. Unable to stop himself, Phainon pushes closer. Feels Mydei's lips twitch. Wants more.

It lasts maybe ten seconds, and Mydei pulls back.

Phainon refrains from chasing after him, resisting the urge to press his lips against every spot on his face. Place small pecks all over, show every bit of affection he held in for so long.

But he blinks, and he notices Mydei's eyes. The gold is only a thin rim around the black pupils, rounder than they usually are when he's particularly happy. Like a cat, and completely focused on him. Phainon feels such a surge of affection that it almost leaves him winded.

"I love you," Phainon stresses, voice nearly cracking. He loves him. He loves him so much that he wants to carve his heart out and offer it to him. He bites on his tongue to keep those thoughts in.

Mydei's gaze jumps down as if he thinks of kissing Phainon again, but he only smiles in response. He leans back, supporting his weight with one hand on the bed. Phainon's injury is long since forgotten, not that he cared in the first place. He has enough presence of mind to tap his sword and make it disappear among the white sparkles. Glances down to make sure his thigh isn't bleeding anymore and shifts to face Mydei.

"Does that answer your question?" Mydei asks, soft and amused. "I love you in all the ways."

It's everything Phainon ever wanted to hear and more. It might be a dream. Except the cut on his thigh stings with a dull ache, and his lips still tingle with the phantom sensation. He doesn't think even his dreams would have conjured up a situation so painfully ideal.

Still, though. There is a reason he hasn't said anything for this long, and he will die happy with the knowledge that Mydei returned his maybe not-so-silly feelings. So, Phainon swallows the lump in his throat.

"And you're sure?" He asks, a bit stilted and uncertain. He waves his hand between the two of them. "That this is what you want. That it's fine for us to —" he stops for a moment, tries to find a correct word. Is this enough to assume? "To be like this?"

"Like what?" Mydei tilts his head, eyes pinning Phainon in place. "Together like we have always been? I don't imagine much will change between us now that we've acknowledged it."

"Not much, but some stuff will change, right?" Phainon asks just to make sure. Like more direct kisses, and perhaps even more than that. And being open about his feelings.

"Anything you want," Mydei responds readily with one of his wide smiles, the rarer and more precious ones. "You just have to ask, Phainon."

And that's something Phainon never even dared to hope for.

He crawls further onto the bed, settling into the space near the wall and pulling Mydei down to fully lie down beside him. Mydei allows for it, landing with a soft oof. His face is angled toward Phainon's, not losing the smile or the brightness in his eyes.

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

Mydei's expression is too blank to be natural. He mastered it, but the thing is that Phainon can read him like a book. And sometimes it's just painfully obvious when something is missing from his usual expression. Like plain amusement that he is trying to cover up right now.

"Stop it," Phainon protests quietly, tugging on the three strands of hair held carefully between his fingers. "It's not a big deal. It's not even anything advanced. Just one braid. The simplest one, too."

Mydei's gaze meets his, and Phainon is very aware of their audience of four.

Chapter Notes

Phainon taps on Mydei's arm to stop him, then crouches to retie the laces of his sandal. They look nice and are comfortable enough for slow days, but he might prefer the boots he wears during combat over them. At least he doesn't have to stop every so often to adjust them.

"So," Phainon begins in a very casual manner. Like he's about to strike a chat about the weather and not the subject that hasn't left his mind since that one significant moment. "How long have you loved me for?"

Hephaestion will never let him live it down if he finds out Mydei actually beat him to the punch with the confession, now that Phainon thinks about it. He might inquire about this sooner or later, once he realizes they are together. And Mydei, blunt as he is, will likely reply with no hesitation. Ah, well. The embarrassment should be easy to swallow when Phainon can turn around and kiss Mydei to distract himself at any moment.

Phainon's hands work methodically to adjust the strings as he glances up at Mydei. His lips are quirked up as he gazes back down at Phainon, shifts slightly to the side so that he can lean against the building.

"Don't you know you are the one who taught me the meaning of love?" He asks like it's an obvious fact of life. Phainon's hands freeze. Mydei's smile is soft as he regards him. "I think I loved you since I watched you faint with the effort to get us as far away from danger as you could. I remember watching over you and thinking I would kill anything that might come within range before you woke up."

Phainon's lips part in bewilderment. Those were some of the worst moments of his life. Barring the invasion of his village by the black tide creatures and Mydei being struck in the back by an arrow, the trek through the pitch-black forest with a single-minded focus on escaping was the scariest thing he's ever experienced. His memories of it are blurry past the moment the men caught them in their makeshift camp and then their time by the river.

He must have been a pathetic mess, barely able to defend himself and messing up on every step. But Mydei saw it, a child himself yet much more capable even at that age, and something about it pulled at his heart.

"I fell in love with you," Mydei continues, oblivious to Phainon's thoughts, "Simply by having you by my side. It was always there. I am rather sure it would have happened under any circumstances, whether we grew up together or not. It's difficult not to develop these feelings for you, Phainon. You are an easy man to love."

The intensity of his gaze, combined with the weight of his words, makes Phainon flush all over. He curses in his mind, tamping down the urge to cover his undoubtedly red face with something.

He doesn't entirely agree with Mydei's view of him, but—

Something inside of him squirms happily, revels in the attention.

Mydei huffs, amused by his expression or perhaps the flush. "How long have you known?"

Phainon glares at him halfheartedly, then decides that looking at Mydei is too distracting to ponder the question. He squints at some spot to the right of Mydei's head, parsing through his memories. At the very least, it serves to distract him from the embarrassment. He's always loved Mydei, he thinks. It's difficult to pinpoint when exactly he fell for him, the childish crush and idealized love. When did he realize he was in love, though? Wasn't it—

Ah.

"Um." Phainon's lips form a thin line, and he feels the damned hot flush spike up again.

His realization—it was because of a dream, wasn't it? He thinks it was. He doesn't remember the exact details of it anymore, but he recalls the panic he felt as he sprang up from the bed and frantically made his way to the bathroom to clean up. And the revelation of just how into Mydei he is had suddenly brought to attention the romantic nature of his feelings as well. He is confident they'd always been there, though. He simply never realized.

Phainon coughs, hands hanging limply by his sandal. "Yeah, also always. Of course I've known the whole time."

Mydei blinks at him slowly. He doesn't have to voice it aloud for Phainon to know he isn't fooled by it.

"Do you need help with tying that?" Mydei points at the shoe. "We will be here until tomorrow at the pace you are going."

"Shut up," he grumbles and finally rises to his feet. He walks the remaining few steps to Mydei and grasps him by the wrist to get them back on course. "Were you aware that I've been given the title of Prince Consort for a while now?" Phainon asks faintly, changing the subject.

Mydei briefly raises his eyebrows at the blatant attempt of distraction, but graciously decides to humor Phainon instead of pressing the matter. "Archidamia would have thrown a fit if I weren't aware of such an important matter that all of my people seem to be in a united standing about," he remarks.

He twines his fingers with Phainon's as he says it, meaning they are actively holding hands while they are walking. They've been dragging each other to places for years, and they hold hands while resting all the time. But now they are wandering the streets of Campa, and it's in the context of being together. Phainon glances skyward and curses whichever Titan bestowed him with a complexion this pale and prone to blushing.

He blames that for the way it takes him an entire minute to halt them again, yanking Mydei to his side when he continues walking with no care for Phainon's new plight.

"Hold on," Phainon hisses, his grasp on Mydei's hand tightening. "You knew?"

Mydei matches the strength of his grip easily, then tilts his head. "Yes?"

Phainon sputters incredulously. "And you never said anything?"

Was he really the only one unaware? Phainon refuses to believe he is that oblivious.

Mydei shrugs, pulling on Phainon's hand until he concedes and lets himself be steered forward. "It's not your fault you didn't know," Mydei reassures him, ignoring the accusatory question. "Everyone was exceptionally tight-lipped about this. Thera let it slip when I left our four-way spar to hydrate."

"And you never said anything?" Phainon repeats, though more calmly.

"She started panicking right afterward because she wasn't supposed to say anything," Mydei sighs. Then, reluctantly, "I had to pinky promise her that I wouldn't say anything. It wasn't difficult to catch whispers and tail-ends of conversations afterward."

"Pinky promise," Phainon echoes. His frustration ebbs away entirely, giving way to lighthearted hilarity.

"Could you stop with the repeating?" Mydei complains irritably. "Yes, I pinky promised. And I wasn't about to disappoint a child."

Phainon imagines Mydei, covered in cuts and bruises, as Thera excitedly chatters at him from her spot where she watches their spars. Drinking water and choking on it as she reveals the very important bit of gossip that's been intentionally kept from them. Trying his best to pacify her before any of them realizes what she is distressed about.

He can easily picture Mydei's determined expression and visible relief when he makes that pinky promise with a girl who doesn't reach his shoulders. It's adorable. Of course Mydei would take his promise so seriously that he wouldn't even tell Phainon about it until he breached the subject himself. Always so earnest.

"I love you," Phainon laughs, stumbling after him.

Mydei abruptly drags him into an establishment he didn't catch the name of, the door closing behind them with a chime of a bell. The lady at the counter takes one look at them before smiling, her eyes crinkling.

"Ah, esteemed guests from afar and young lovers to boot," she waves at them cheerfully. "Welcome in. Are you looking for anything specific? A souvenir?"

Phainon grins proudly, swinging their hands in the air. She is the first one to say it aloud, and it makes it a little more real for Phainon. It's not a fever dream conjured in the safety of his head.

Mydei shakes his head in reply to her questions, then regards Phainon. He gestures with his free hand to the shelves lining the walls, and Phainon's eyes widen at the unfamiliar objects as they follow the motion.

"Pick one at a reasonable price," Mydei tells him, then lets go of him to step away and lean against the counter to wait.

Phainon hums happily and approaches the relic closest to him. As he examines it from every angle, his mind wanders away instead. They should visit a smithy in search of some unique adjustments Mydei might like to his weapons.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

They have to drag Leonnius to the makeshift training ground by force. And rope Peucesta into it as well.

The three of them had decided it might be time to broaden their friend's skill. He is a gifted runner, but he also has the potential to do more with it. If only Leonnius wasn't avoiding them like a plague ever since they arrived in Campa, trying his best to place Peucesta between them at all times.

Peucesta always lets him, smiling apologetically.

They tried to ignore it for a little while, because—

Because their dear friend died not too long ago. Sometimes they turn around to address Perdikkas, only to see no one there. Everyone is still on edge. Why would Leonnius be any different?

They do manage to drag him into training, though, and that's progress. They don't even expect that much to begin with, but it's clear something is wrong. Failure isn't met with sheepish smiles or playful groaning, but instead, Leonnius withdraws and edges away.

And after numerous unsuccessful attempts to teach him the art of stealth, each of Leonnius' actions stilted and hesitant in a way he rarely is, Hephaestion snaps with a remark. Leonnius doesn't respond, eyes averted and shoulders hunched in. It's hard to ignore that it must be more than just grief over a friend that's eating at him.

"Leonnius," Mydei calls after an awkward silence lingers. "Are you afraid of me?"

"No," is the immediate response. Too quick. Leonnius winces, still not looking in their direction. "Maybe a little. It was kind of scary on that day, but I felt relieved to witness you avenge him. It's not that, Lord Mydei."

Leonnius sends them a shaky smile, directed at Mydei in particular. Mydei settles somewhat, though not entirely convinced. Phainon nudges him, keeps an arm pressed against his instead of pulling away afterward. It was a reasonable guess as to what might be eating at Leonnius, Phainon thinks. He is still fearful in the face of combat.

"Is it because of my whole thing?" Hephaestion asks, almost anxious. Phainon glances at him, then down at his hand, where he is digging the nail of his middle finger into his thumb. "I know there aren't many people like this among us. But it's also not unheard of, and I know I pass well."

Leonnius stares at him with wide eyes. "What?"

"Oh, come on. I dealt with stupid questions and assumptions before. People being uncomfortable when I told them and all." Hephaestion rolls his eyes, glaring at no one in particular. "But you already met me like this, so. If you treat me any differently from how you used to, I will cut your dick off. Peucesta won't mind too much, I'm sure. He can fuck you for a change."

Oh, that—

Well, that didn't even cross Phainon's mind.

Leonnius sputters, a light blush rising across his features. "I will have you know we take turns," he protests in embarrassment. Then grimaces like he regrets revealing that information. He shakes it off quickly, deciding to move on before anyone can latch onto it. "And I don't… mind? I mean, I've never really dealt with anything like this, but you are still you. Right?"

Hephaestion nods once, a clear and decisive movement. Content with the answer, though he remains a bit on edge. To Phainon, Hephaestion's gender

isn't something he thinks about at all. Hephaestion simply is. Is it really something people pay that much attention to, much less the negative sort?

"Who was uncomfortable?" Mydei asks with a frown, eyes set on Hephaestion.

"I hope you would have told us if someone was out of line," Phainon follows up with a similar expression. Maybe he is unintentionally ignorant about the whole issue, but he wouldn't stand for it if Hephaestion felt uneasy among some others.

"Shut up, both of you," Hephaestion reacts, and shoves Phainon's shoulder hard enough that it makes Mydei sway due to how close they are standing. "I can handle myself."

Phainon shoots him a disgruntled look regardless. "We don't doubt that," he says. Though never outright tested, it's quite certain that Hephaeation is already stronger than at least half of the Council members. He could take on any average person in the detachment.

"Then let me handle my own mess," Hephaestion replies, unconcerned and determined.

Phainon and Mydei glance at each other. They will keep an ear out, though no one would dare to ever say a word in their presence, he is sure. People respect them because they are aware of their strength. And Kremnoans of all people know best how to pick their battles. But it doesn't mean they cannot help make their friend's life just a little easier if they have an opportunity to do so.

Phainon shifts his gaze to Leonnius, pinning him in place with it. They should get this over with already; they will go in circles if they get distracted by everything. It's been known to happen before.

"What is it, then?" Phainon asks, as tired as the rest of them. Might as well ask directly at this point. And pester him until he gives in if that doesn't work.

Leonnius flinches at that, eyes skirting around as if he is preparing to bolt just to escape this conversation. This time, Peucesta moves out of the way and rests one hand on Leonnius' shoulder in encouragement. He still hesitates, gaze jumping between the three of them before it settles on the ground.

"I wanted to leave you," Leonnius admits quickly. Out of all things, that one wouldn't have possibly passed Phainon's mind. '"After Perdikkas died. When we were walking to Campa, I tried convincing Peucesta to leave a few times. But he doesn't want to, and I don't want to leave him more than that, so I stayed."

"But do you still wish to leave?" Mydei asks carefully. Not angry, more so attentive.

Leonnius takes a moment. "No," he decides in the end. "But Ptolemy's reaction, and— What if something happens to Peucesta? How am I supposed to— I cannot go through that. I don't want to die, I don't want any of you to die either, and I don't want him to die."

They stare at him in silence, digesting the words.

Leonnius shrugs with one shoulder helplessly. "That's the thing about Kremnoans, and part of the reason I never let anyone drag me out of the fortress. We die often and quickly."

Phainon can relate to the fear of someone's death. How many times has he wondered what would become of him were Mydei to meet his demise? He wouldn't be able to move on. Not immediately, possibly not ever. So, he doesn't fault Ptolemy for drinking himself into a loss of consciousness. In the same way, he cannot now find it in himself to be offended by Leonnius' desire to leave them.

"I'm not sure I would have actually gone through with it, though," Leonnius backtracks as if sensing Phainon's thoughts.

"You don't have to justify yourself," Mydei tells him easily. "I don't desire to force anyone into duty."

"No, see," Leonnius shakes his head, taking a step to the side to stand next to Peucesta rather than halfway behind him. "It's not that. You changed my life in a way I never imagined possible. For you, Mydei, I would give my life in a heartbeat if it came down to it."

Hephaeston makes a face. "But you just said—"

"I know!" Leonnius throws his hands up to the air. "It's weird. I'm prepared to die, I know I am, but Ladon scared me. And I— I thought we were invincible," he says weakly, eyes darting to the side. "You are the strongest of fighters, and our support ensures you stay that way. And yet, Perdikkas died. And Ptolemy fell to pieces while we try to go on like Perdikkas would have wanted us to. It doesn't paint the most optimistic of a future, does it?"

He smiles ruefully, scratching his head and disturbing the green hair in a way that they stick to the side a little. Peucesta notes it with a small uptick to his lips, but doesn't move to fix it.

"I'm a coward," Leonnius continues with a resigned sigh. His gaze isn't heavy with shame as it once would be, though. "Running will always be my first instinct, I can't help it."

"I promised I would make Castrum Kremnos into a place you wouldn't be afraid to remain at," Mydei responds easily. Earnest in a way a prince shouldn't be when making such claims. "I don't have the means to do it just yet, but I assure you that one day you won't have to worry about the potential deaths anymore. I will ensure there won't be anything for you to feel the need to run from."

"Yeah," Phainon nods in support. "It won't be like this forever, and we will protect you until then."

"And Peucesta and I will both make sure I won't give in and run away until that happens," Leonnius says, a small but beaming smile on his face. He chuckles a little, growing embarrassed. "I avoided you because I was ashamed of this. I apologize for that."

"You should have said something sooner," Hephaestion scolds him now that the situation has been resolved. Phainon holds back a wince, having heard that before.

But Leonnius only scoffs, unconcerned with Hephaestion's irritation. "Yeah? You should have said something about being," he waves his hand pointedly over his body. "So that I wouldn't say stupid shit."

Hephaestion pretends he cannot hear him, and Peucesta pats Leonnius on the head, finally smoothing out his hair.

"Well," Phainon starts, leaning on Mydei and smiling widely. "If you still feel bad about it, why don't you make up for it with training?"

Leonnius freezes, mouth still open as if he were about to make another retort. Mydei doesn't say anything because he wouldn't use anyone's guilt against them, but Hephaestion doesn't have such qualms and nods eagerly in agreement to Phainon's suggestion.

They run him through exercises until Leonnius successfully steals a fruit from a stall—which they then return to its rightful place—without the owner noticing. Two times, he fails so spectacularly that they have to explain to the poor Campanians what they are doing.

Phainon is most relieved to find out that he has, fortunately, improved in sweet-talking people.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon twitches as he wakes, a little disoriented.

He cannot recall what he was dreaming of, but something tingles pleasantly across his body. An urge to press closer into the heat in front of him, chase

more of that feeling. Content. Pleasurable. His hips twitch of their own accord.

Very quickly, he realizes there is a thigh wedged between his legs. Not an unusual position for them to sleep in; their legs always get tangled. But it's different when he crashes into consciousness with pressure put on his already hard dick in just the right way.

He inhales sharply, then quietly curses on an exhale, "Fuck."

His hands fight to grasp at something, but Mydei doesn't wear a shirt to sleep, and the covers slipped low. He ends up grabbing Mydei's arm instead, feels the soft skin, its warmth, then the hard muscle beneath it. He almost makes another noise.

This will not end very well. This will not end well at all.

He shifts, and it nudges Mydei's leg higher up. Phainon nearly falls off the bed, bites his lip viciously when his dick jerks in an increasingly despaired sort of interest. They never talked about this. Well, they had one or two conversations about sex with Ptolemy and Perdikkas both. But it doesn't count. It was clinical knowledge, a step-by-step guide to intercourse. It wasn't this.

No one disclosed a guide on… on getting off like this. Against each other.

And Phainon and Mydei never talked about this between themselves. They haven't even properly kissed yet, just small, innocent pecks. Lips pressed together for a moment too long, but never prodding further than that.

He almost talks himself into cutting short this one-sided chase of a high, makes a resolution to get up and take care of himself in the bathroom as he always does. And then have a very awkward but hopefully informative conversation with Mydei. Because to do this without the other one participating fills him with so much anxiety, he might die. And the prospect of waking Mydei up because he is horny fills him with an equal amount of humiliation.

But then Phainon glances up from the spot on the covers his eyes fixated on while he despaired over the circumstances, and is met with two eyes fixated on him. Pupils blown wide and lips parted slightly. Phainon jolts in surprise, inadvertently squeezing his thighs shut together and further trapping Mydei's leg.

"Fuck," he repeats with more feeling, as the hand he apparently still has on Mydei's arm tightens its grip without his permission. He forcibly relaxes his legs, stars moving away. His face feels on fire. "Sorry, I— I didn't mean to."

Mydei's ankle locks around Phainon's shin without a word, keeping him in place with the other leg. Phainon startles and then freezes when he realizes what else he can feel. Because having Mydei's thigh between his means that Phainon's own rests against his crotch. Phainon didn't realize, because he was too busy talking himself into a spiral.

Mydei grinds down, obvious hardness pressing against Phainon's skin through the thin fabric of his underwear. Phainon keens at the touch, in too much shock to try and repress it. Alright, yeah. They are doing this. No conversation required. Phainon cannot find it in himself to oppose it, not with Mydei so close to him and precum leaking into his underwear.

"It's gonna be quick, you know," Phainon tells him when he no longer feels like he might choke on air.

"I don't care," Mydei responds, more collected than he has any right to be. He pulls away, detangling their legs with the expertise of having to do it daily, and kicks the covers to the floor so that he can climb up to straddle Phainon's thighs instead. All before Phainon can process a single thought. "It's supposed to feel good, not last long."

From the scant few books he got his hands on regarding this subject, Phainon isn't sure that's the idea. He also doesn't care one bit at the moment. His hands lie awkwardly at his sides, eyes glued to Mydei's underwear where it strains against a visible bulge. He swallows, wonders what the protocol for this might be. Does he grind up? Sit up to meet Mydei halfway?

The girl remains frozen, fear clear on her face, until Phainon gestures with his head sharply, and she finally takes off in a run. The man's frantic attempts at shouting are muffled by Phainon's hands. When he sees the girl round the corner, well out of sight, he snaps his neck with almost no effort at all.

Phainon doesn't enjoy killing. But sometimes, it might be necessary.

It doesn't take long until a sharp whistle comes from up north, and Phainon figures Mydei must have started on the second part of the plan. Phainon turns toward the south and gathers his hands up to his lips, forming his fingers in the familiar shape. He whistles as loud as he can in hopes that it might reach Hephaestion as well.

As he joins Mydei and fights through a horde of enemies, Phainon sees the Bulsans cackle as their companions are slaughtered. They are deranged, and it shows even in their fighting style; they throw themselves at the opponent with single-minded desperation. All sensibility lost. Phainon thinks it might be a fate worse than even the black tide. Haunting Amphoreus and bringing destruction to it, spreading the depravity. All while still whole and alive, no infection to control their bodies.

A Bulsan charges at him and shouts something about regaining the glory forcibly taken from them. Phainon nearly staggers in shock before he shakes it off and separates the person's head from their body.

It's almost like looking into a mirror, except the reflection is warped in the worst ways possible. Bulsans might be what the exiled Kremnoans could have spiraled toward if they lacked the self-discipline and determination.

Phainon banishes the thought when he spots Hephaestion running in their direction, a dozen people following after him with their weapons raised.

They stay for a few more hours after they kill the last ones standing, ensuring there aren't any other people from Bulsa to terrorize the locals or anyone ever again. In the last hour, the citizens rounded up the stragglers who began hiding, ready to be taken care of.

The total number of Bulsans was much higher than Phainon expected it to be. It's fortunate how disorganized they were, or their group might've been out of their depth.

The remaining Bulsans don't beg to be spared. They stare into their eyes with burning hatred as they call them the worst scum of Amphoreus. Compare them to the vile Kremnoans who took everything from them, and Phainon winces as he slits the throat of another one to stop the babbling. The irony isn't lost on him.

The residents of the town regard them with hesitation and fear. It's alright, that's what they are used to in reaction to their services. Rarely are they hired by military forces that treat them with camaraderie rather than fear. Civilians might willfully pay them for carnage, yet they never seem prepared for the sight of it.

"It's not much," the man who approached them in the camp tells them as they prepare to leave, eyes stuck to the ground. "But please accept this as payment."

He hands out two hefty pouches. People openly stare, but no one protests.

"Keep your coin," Mydei tells him, wiping the drying blood off his gauntlets with a cloth provided by another stranger. He offers the man one glance before he resumes his task. "People of Bulsa shouldn't have ever left the sky alive. Think of this as amending what transpired in the past."

The man clutches the pouches to his chest. He bows, still not looking at any of them directly. "Thank you. We will never forget your generosity."

Mydei nods, switching to his other gauntlet. And that's that.

Phainon looks over the faces of other people gathered and thinks generosity might be the last thing running through their heads. Again, they are all used to it. Sometimes he wishes things were a little different.

"Leonnius," Phainon calls quietly, forcibly discarding the chain of thought.

Leonnius steps closer, then hums in question.

"Try to grab some of the weapons by the corpses if you can," he instructs, staring at the bodies left by their feet. Their blades are etched with the markings of Skyfolk, not to mention from a tribe that was supposedly eradicated so long ago. "If we get the smiths to restore them, we can sell them as relics to collectors in the next city-state."

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

It takes them only two days to return to the detachment. It's at the sacrifice of some sleep, but it doesn't have many consequences when they revel in the victory well-won. Ptolemy even brings up Perdikkas once, and though he stutters over his words, he doesn't appear as if he wishes for nothing more than for death to claim him.

Perdikkas would have patched up the cut on Phainon's arm better than the make-shift scrap of material, but it's okay. They will carry his memory with them until the end of their lives, and retell their stories to him once they reunite in the Nether Realm. In fact, they should keep track and then relay to him the details of all their injuries that he couldn't take care of.

Phainon will, that's for certain. And he will tell him of Mydei's deaths, all of them, and watch with satisfaction as Mydei gets lectured for his recklessness one more time. Yes. Perdikkas' death doesn't mean they won't see him ever again.

They sleep huddled in threes during those two nights, their tents and usual amount of blankets abandoned in favor of traveling light. Before Phainon passes out, he sees Ptolemy pressed with his back to Peucesta's, Leonnius' hands and legs practically attached to his boyfriend's body from the front.

On their side of the fire, Mydei remains in the middle as he usually does. His warmth is certainly enough to make up for the lack of supplies. Mydei's back is nearly glued to Phainon's chest, though the leg that snaked in between Phainon's might be Hephaestion's. With the close proximity, Phainon is fairly certain his hand is resting over Hephaestion's side, Mydei's elbow keeping his arm pressed to his own.

It's a bit difficult to keep track of all the limbs.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Kremnoans cheer when they enter the premises of the camp and walk through the entirety of the detachment to reach the very front. Archidamia listens to their reports, backed by two of the Council officials. She doesn't say much except giving simple acknowledgement, but Phainon can read the proud gleam in her eyes.

They leave to wash up, then eat the food shoved in their faces by the eager Kremnoans. Hephaestion's parents even make an effort to sit with them for a bit, not hiding the fact that they are impressed with their son. Hephaestion only rolls his eyes at the singular remark that he should pace himself better, but otherwise basks in the praise.

Thera sits by their legs and listens eagerly as they retell the story, which might be embellished with some fancy details about the way they got rid of the Bulsans. She is nine now, though she never shied away from the brutality of the Kremnoan lifestyle. Aias whines at the missed opportunity to come along, and Hephaestion drapes himself around his shoulders to pacify him with a promise of a spar.

It's as they are settling in for the night that Leonnius comes to fetch them, saying a group of people is approaching the detachment head-on and they are needed. They throw on their clothes and keep their weapons ready as they walk to Archidamia.

They reach her just in time when people surface from between the trees with their hands up. Phainon and Mydei flank Archidamia on either side, standing tall at the same height as her. She has her weapon sheathed, but Phainon's sword is held loosely in his hand, and Mydei angles his arms, gauntlets glinting in the moonlight.

"Lord Krateros," Archidamia announces, voice measured. She doesn't appear tense, but the lack of reaction is just as good as a command. Remain on guard.

Phainon's mind whirls. He's heard the name before. Not as often as the revered way the people speak of Queen Gorgo, but here and there in mentions of her past. The current King's Aegis.

If he is here, then Eurypon must know their location as well. Has he sent his strongest soldier to defeat them, drag Mydei to the fortress kicking and screaming? Phainon changes the grip on his sword, silently counting the warriors standing a few paces back. At least twenty. He quickly glances to the right and sees red mist clinging to Mydei's hands in a clear warning.

In this situation, it's reasonable to let Archidamia take point. She is the one most familiar with Krateros and how to handle him. Phainon, a mirror of Mydei with his intense scrutiny of the intruders, feels almost like a guard dog waiting for a sign to attack.

Krateros stops about a meter in front of them, stance loose and no weapon in sight. It doesn't put any of them at ease; nearly all Kremnoans can do plenty of damage without a blade in their hands. And who knows what tricks this man might bring with him?

"Lady Archidamia," Krateros inclines his head in greeting. His eyes quickly jump to Phainon and disregard him in the same beat, moving to Mydei. "Lord Mydeimos."

Chapter End Notes
