chapters.title: Chapter 21: and hold on to them
chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

"Phainon of Aedes Elysiae," he introduces himself firmly before Krateros can question why Leonnius lacks the strength to face him head-on. Instead, he watches with a thin smile as Krateros' brows scrunch up in displeasure.

"I wouldn't have expected an outsider among you," Krateros says, just a touch shy of reprimanding. "Aedes Elysiae? I have never heard of such lands."

Chapter Notes

When the situation doesn't escalate into an altercation, their small group, which could count as the detachment's representatives, stands frozen and watches the situation unfold.

Krateros is down on one knee, right hand settled firmly over his chest in a salute, his face angled low in respect. Or at least what's supposed to be respect; Phainon still isn't convinced this isn't a ruse. He is in full armor, one as elaborate and decorated as Archidamia's. Dark brown hair falling into his eyes in a cut even messier than Mydei's, and a short beard in the same color. Phainon can make out a scar on his cheek, still in a fresh pink hue.

"I apologize for having failed you," Krateros says, his voice remorseful. Phainon doesn't know the man well enough—or at all—to tell if it's genuine. "My duty is to guide and protect you, Lord Mydeimos. And for over sixteen years, I have not fulfilled it. If you allow for it, I will dedicate my life to rectifying that."

Silence follows, but Krateros doesn't falter. Phainon glares at the soldiers who keep a careful distance behind Krateros, and they suddenly remember

where they are. They salute Mydei, but make no move to explain their own motives. Clearly defected under Krateros' leadership, then.

"What of my father?" Mydei asks first and foremost, rather than acknowledging Krateros' pledge. "You are the King's Aegis."

"Following my victory at the Kremnos Festival, a more important role had been bestowed upon me before your birth, Lord Mydeimos," Krateros elaborates easily. Phainon has a very vague recollection of Archidamia mentioning something about this. Not much, though. She never liked talking about Krateros beyond the bare minimum. "One of a mentor and protector, chosen by your mother."

Mydei tilts his head in puzzlement. "Don't you think that calls your loyalty into question? You spent many years by my father's side. One might think your resolve to remain in that spot would outweigh my mother's decision."

Krateros' expression tightens, but his eyes resolutely stare ahead at the dull grass. "It is by the directive of King Eurypon himself that my loyalty to you shall supersede my loyalty to him. Just as well, Queen Gorgo was my most cherished companion," he says, a little hollow. "Please understand that I am trying to amend my wrongs."

Phainon knows something about having the one person who is the most important thing in the whole world. He really does, though he is sure it was different between Krateros and Queen Gorgo. And so, he has to bite his tongue so that he doesn't allow for a scathing remark about leaving your loved one alone to face a mad ruler to slip past. He might not have a full picture. And it's not his place either.

Mydei, meanwhile, looks to Archidamia for a hint on how to proceed. She is the one with the most knowledge of the man. Her face is unreadable, but just as she doesn't express explicit approval, she doesn't seem to be against it either.

His eyes settle on Phainon next. His head tilts again, this time in a specific question rather than bemusement at the situation. Phainon stares back at him for a second, considering. They could always use more soldiers,

especially of Krateros' competence. It would give them an advantage, and if not now, then definitely in the eventual battle against Eurypon. Phainon being childishly upset over the fate of Mydei and his mother doesn't matter.

More advantages point to letting Krateros and his soldiers join them rather than sending them back. Or killing them. Allowing them to remain doesn't mean they are to be trusted immediately. They will be placed under constant watch for the time being, no doubt about it.

Phainon sighs, realizing tomorrow they will spend an entire day saddled in a meeting. Listening to the dull, repetitive questioning to catch potential inconsistencies among the soldiers. And get as much valuable information as possible about the current infrastructure of Castrum Kremnos. So much for moving forward. Maybe if they hadn't caught up with the detachment so quickly, Archidamia would have dealt with this on her own instead.

Mydei raises an eyebrow, and Phainon mournfully abandons the delightful thought of forsaking Krateros solely to avoid being stuck with the Council for an entire day. He nods once instead, though he quickly signs for careful as well.

"You may stand," Mydei tells Krateros after a lengthy pause. The man swiftly pulls himself to his feet, letting his hand drop from the salute. He doesn't appear perturbed by how long it took to make a decision. "Should we find your intent to be genuine, your presence might bring us great advantages. You are free to remain within the premises of the detachment, but only if your group agrees to be separated and supervised. You will be questioned at the soonest opportunity tomorrow."

"Yes. Yes, of course." Krateros nods, clearly satisfied. "Thank you, Lord Mydeimos."

"There is nothing to thank me for," Mydei says mildly.

Krateros' lips twitch into some semblance of a smile. He still stands at full attention, posture rigid. As if he is incapable of relaxing, much less slouching. He takes a minute to let his eyes wander over Mydei's figure.

They stop briefly on the jewelry, expression growing slack in shock before it schools into its obviously trained neutrality.

"You have grown into a fine young man." Krateros clears his throat, then lets his gaze slide over the rest of the people gathered before it rounds back to Mydei. "I recognize Lady Archidamia, Lord Savvas, Lady Tyche, and Lord Kallias. But may I inquire about the others surrounding you, Lord Mydeimos?"

It's obvious what he is doing. An innocuous question to gauge the current hierarchy he will have to adjust to.

"My royal retinue," Mydei responds easily, nothing to hide. "Two of them are missing. There was no sense in disturbing their rest since we had just returned from an expedition. You might recognize Ptolemy by name, though."

"The young scholar, yes," Krateros lets out a thoughtful hum, evidently trying to recall anything he's ever heard or seen of Ptolemy.

He will have an opportunity to refresh his memory soon enough when Ptolemy annoys him into exhaustion during the interrogation. Phainon almost looks forward to it.

"My name is Hephaestion," Hephaestion chimes in, not doing a good enough job of masking his amazement. "It's an honor to meet you, Lord Krateros."

"I look forward to testing your capabilities," Krateros says, and Hephaestion nearly shakes with excitement.

"I'm Leonnius," their skittish messenger offers up, halfway hidden behind Mydei. He is the only one of them who has seen Krateros in Castrum Kremnos. Phainon doesn't imagine he's enjoying a reminder of the time before they snatched him away from the fortress.

"Phainon of Aedes Elysiae," he introduces himself firmly before Krateros can question why Leonnius lacks the strength to face him head-on. Instead,

he watches with a thin smile as Krateros' brows scrunch up in displeasure.

"I wouldn't have expected an outsider among you," Krateros says, just a touch shy of reprimanding. "Aedes Elysiae? I have never heard of such lands."

He doesn't follow up on it, but his tone makes it clear he is far from approving of this. He looks Phainon up and down, and Phainon meets his eyes evenly despite the anger rising and heating up his blood. Phainon has spent years never leaving Mydei's side; he will not be cowed by a man who shows up a decade and a half too late.

Krateros seems to realize he has no standing in this matter—his high position is meaningless until he is cleared, and even then not guaranteed to hold up—and abandons the subject. It's good for everyone involved that he doesn't press further.

Not much is to be said after that, and Krateros watches with curiosity as Mydei and Archidamia both dismiss everyone, leaving the logistics of appointing guards to every soldier to the latter.

Phainon promptly drags Mydei away to their tent to settle for the few hours of sleep, silently grateful that his companion doesn't seem eager to talk about the potential additions to the detachment. They will deal with that tomorrow.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

As Phainon anticipated, it's a long day.

The soldiers are interrogated first. Their reports are much the same. People who fought under Krateros long enough to view him as their leader, more so than Eurypon, or those who suffered under the King's rule and wished to leave.

Ptolemy takes a special sort of glee in talking circles around Krateros, bringing out the most insufferable traits of his personality when he regards him. Krateros listens and responds while entirely unimpressed, evidently considering him nothing more than a brat. It's still worth it to witness the few times he loses his patience.

Things shift a little when Krateros' account is begrudgingly deemed genuine. Not about to be included in the most important of talks or secrets, but enough to reinstate him among the people as important.

Toward the evening, they clue him in on their next destination. Giving a rough recount of the settlement and Mydei's life so far. A very brief recount, but one nonetheless.

Then, Krateros takes point of his own accord. He gives insights and draws up a new distribution of their forces without being asked. Poses questions, probing for opinions from everyone gathered. Next, he reveals every minute detail and weakness hiding within Castrum Kremnos, all the ways to exploit them in the future. Possibilities of what changes might be implemented after his desertion.

He is skilled and experienced. There is no denying that. Years spent as the King's shadow would do that to anyone.

Archidamia reluctantly abides, though she sits with crossed arms and clenched jaw. Mydei listens with sharp focus. Ptolemy grumbles under his breath, and Hephaestion doesn't stop grinning, nearly vibrating in his seat.

Phainon settles on observing, being the only person in the large tent who isn't asked a single question. Barely looked at, as if he's nothing more than a decoration. Only tolerated because the Prince wishes him to remain. It almost feels like when they first stepped into the settlement all over again.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

"I've been meaning to ask," Leonnius starts, stretching his legs as a warm-up. "Which coreflames are you getting?"

Oh. They haven't thought about that, have they? They are Chrysos Heirs, but it doesn't relate to their current lives much. All that matters is that Mydei is the Crown Prince. And Phainon is—

Apparently, Phainon is the Prince Consort.

The thought alone is enough to make his face heat up, even though he's had time to get used to it. Prince Consort. Officially now, no longer something people gossip about but don't seem to deem it significant to mention to him.

Much more importantly, he is Mydei's equal. That's the only title he cares about.

One day, the most notable thing about them will be the fact that they are Chrysos Heirs, though. Their role in the prophecy and bringing in the new dawn. They will have to slay a Titan and recover a coreflame for themselves.

"Do we even have a choice?" Phainon asks. He is idly braiding and then untangling the strands at the back of Mydei's head, propped up against Phainon's shins as he is.

Ptolemy looks up from his notes with a thoughtful expression. "I'm not exactly sure," he responds. "The process isn't widely discussed among the people who aren't involved, much to my displeasure. For all we know, there might be a part of the prophecy related to it that we aren't privy to."

"Okay, sure," Hephaestion says in dismissal, not very interested in the actual methodology. "But you're getting a coreflame one way or another, what with that golden blood of yours. Which ones do you think you will end up with?"

Phainon hums, weaving the three small braids into a singular larger one.

"I don't know," he says, not bothering to think too hard about it. "Maybe I will get Oronyx? Our village was under Their domain. Not sure if I would be any good with the prayers, though."

He isn't very concerned, though. He will worry when they reach Okhema and the idea of gaining a coreflame becomes a real possibility.

But what about Mydei?

Phainon's first thought when he considers the options is Mnestia. Right behind it is a more fitting option in the shape of Thanatos. He still nearly slams his forehead into Mydei in sheer embarrassment at even having the passing thought of Mnestia.

It's just—

He's loved Mydei for nearly as long as they've known each other, and has been in love with him for at least half of that. Some of the protectiveness, devotion, and affection mixed together into an emotion he didn't quite comprehend the meaning of for some time.

But more importantly, Mydei himself. His obvious love for Phainon, but also for their friends. For his people and their livelihoods. He enjoys Kremnoan poetry and books with more focus on romance than Phainon would ever prefer. Love and beauty, both of which he possesses plenty of.

But if Phainon is being realistic, Thanatos is a more fitting choice. Mydei's connection to the Sea of Souls and a decade spent in its waters, more familiar with its depths than any other human. The way he effortlessly defies death, coming from it unscathed. Taking the lives of many, with speed and ease that the most experienced soldiers cannot match.

Phainon almost says that one aloud. Except he knows the coreflame of Thanatos rests in the hands of some girl, the Maiden of War. They wondered once whether she might be a good fighter with a moniker like that. A title that wouldn't be out of place in Castrum Kremnos.

He carefully pulls the braid apart, then gets to detangling the three small ones.

There is only one available option that suits Mydei best, isn't there?

He thinks back to the blood-soaked grounds as the consequence of Perdikkas' death. The competitiveness he sparks in Phainon and Hephaestion both. The way Mydei embodies the Titan of Strife in a way that no one on Amphoreus could ever dream of achieving when engaged in a fierce battle. Phainon doesn't know the Chrysos Heris, but he doubts any of them could ever begin to resemble their own Titan so closely.

All in all, the path Mydei is destined for is obvious.

"I don't want one," Mydei speaks into the silence, snapping everyone out of their thoughts.

Their friends blink at them in surprise. Phainon stares at the crown of Mydei's head, the braids gone, leaving wavy blond strands in their wake.

Ptolemy is frowning. "The Strife—"

"I'm not taking it," Mydei says in a harsher tone. It's the one he barks orders in, a clear warning not to question him. "I don't like the way— I will slay Nikador, of course. But I am not interested in Their coreflame."

Oh. He really doesn't want it.

It might be the expectations, or the harm and impact Strife has had on his people. It's obvious he doesn't fully agree with their values either, at least to Phainon. It has been since the day in Castrum Kremnos when he agreed to the plea made by the librarian. But the reason doesn't matter much. Because Phainon will gladly take on Mydei's burden. If stepping on the path of destiny brings Mydei distress, Phainon will alter fate itself if he has to. Whatever it is about the coreflame of Strife that he doesn't like, Phainon will shoulder it for him.

"I don't think you are killing Nikador," Phainon says casually, resuming his futile task again on a different section of hair. Braid, then unbraid. Mydei angles his head up to glance at him, mostly with annoyance but partly in question, halting Phainon's hands. "I will be the one to kill Them first because I am stronger than you, and then I will take their coreflame for myself."

Golden gaze searches Phainon's face for a moment, and he makes sure to let his determination show. He means it. Then, Mydei's lips quirk up just the tiniest amount, and Phainon knows he's succeeded. Mydei lets his head drop down with a short 'hpmh,' and Phainon regains the space to play with his hair.

"Dream on, Deliverer," Mydei scoffs. "Only I can bring an end to Nikador's insanity and ensure Their demise."

"You're right, I am the Deliverer," Phainon repeats after him, purposefully tugging on a strand to hear him click his tongue in a warning. "So I will make sure to deliver Them to eternal rest and retrieve the coreflame from Their carcass."

Mydei pinches him on the thigh, no doubt about to retaliate.

"You could always slay the Titan together," Peucesta offers mildly.

"No," they vehemently deny at the same time.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Two of Phainon's training swords are broken, and he hadn't prepared the third one for this fight. Red powder paints grass across the premises that they set out for this, courtesy of Mydei's constructs being continuously shattered. Krateros, after a grueling six hours, is cornered.

Phainon has finally wrestled the spear from him, pointing Krateros' own weapon at his throat. With much less expertise, but it's no less deadly in his hands. Mydei has a spear of his own, angled to graze where Krateros' armor offers an open space.

Last time they sparred with Archidamia, it took about three hours to pin her down. On their own, it's about four hours each, since their individual skill levels are rather similar. Phainon is unsure how long it would take to defeat Krateros without each other's support.

It's a reminder that as powerful as they both are, there are still people who can offer them a challenge. Archidamia and Hephaestion are great examples of that. They both keep them in check in different areas and make them scramble for a victory. Though as they got better, even the way Hephaestion excels in evasion isn't quite enough to hold them back.

Krateros brings in new strategies that are enough to trip both of them up. Phainon cannot confidently say that they wouldn't be forced to yield on the first few attempts of a one-on-one fight, and that alone is remarkable.

Krateros stands tall in the face of his defeat. Gracious, even somewhat impressed with their feat. It's a stark reminder of the Kremnoan might and where the standard of the best of the best lies, aside from Mydei.

The onlookers talk loudly among themselves, eager to catch a glimpse of a warrior they might have once looked up to while still serving in Castrum Kremnos. Now, that figure of respect walks among them, more approachable than ever before. They are all a bunch of exiles and deserters, after all. The lines of the high-standing positions, while still greatly respected, are a little bit more blurred than they would be in a formal setting.

Phainon is begrudgingly acknowledged for his skills, though Krateros' eyes remain on Mydei. Thoughtful in a way Phainon doesn't appreciate.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon swings his sword through the air, beads of sweat gathering at his temples. He raises the hem of his shirt and wipes them off again. His clothes are already soaked through, but he pays it no mind. He will continue taking his frustrations out later by the river, washing them with more force than necessary. Better that than saying something wrong.

It's obvious Mydei regards Krateros with a lot of respect. He has skill. He has knowledge. He is one of the last connections to his mother beyond Archidamia. And even then, he is a personal connection. A childhood friend, the one who knew Queen Gorgo through and through before she gained her title.

Phainon doesn't blame Mydei for growing attached quickly. Perdikkas' death is still fresh, leaving a hollow gap in their group that will never be filled again. And this thing between them that shifted just a little bit, Phainon is scared of losing it by doing something wrong. Reverting to their usual dynamic, which is nothing that much different except the lack of soft kisses placed against each other's lips or rutting into one another's bodies with desperation when need calls, wouldn't be a disaster on its own. He can deal with losing the ability to freely express his feelings.

Perdikkas isn't there to scold him about wasting what someone took time and effort to create, even if it's alcohol. The silence doesn't ring so heavy anymore, though.

chapters.html:
Chapter Summary

An awkward laugh spills from Phainon's throat, fingers twitching against Mydei's cheek. He looks away, up at the small waterfall that cascades into the body of water a few meters away.

"Already flushed," Mydei remarks with obvious satisfaction, "And you haven't even touched the water just yet."

Phainon stubbornly doesn't look back down at him. "It's the steam," he reasons. Like it's not a flimsy excuse.

Chapter Notes

"Why do you care so much about Krateros?" Phainon asks, the first thing he's said to Mydei this morning other than incoherent mumbling right after waking up. They sit by their tent, cold morning air effectively erasing the last traces of sleep. "It's— it's okay. Really. I just, I don't understand."

Mydei carefully takes another sip of his pomegranate juice, buying himself a few more seconds. Phainon doesn't mind. He could wait an entire day.

"He might be right," Mydei says eventually, voice quiet. "I shouldn't be weak in the ways he can spot so easily. And he—" Mydei stops, gestures with his hand. "He talks about mother's childhood. We've heard all the stories of her reign, but never what occurred before it. And if she trusted him with so many aspects of her life, then there must be something about him."

Phainon nods along, downing the last bits of his coffee. He doesn't care for it much, but on certain mornings it's required for him to get going at all.

Perdikkas was almost addicted to the stuff, even if he liked to pretend otherwise. Ptolemy doesn't drink it all, claiming it puts him to sleep instead.

"And he is strong," Phainon adds reluctantly.

"And he is strong," Mydei agrees. "I appreciate his input. His knowledge of Castrum Kremnos proves to be invaluable. He seems devoted to helping me out. And he… As I said, he offers a lot of insight into my mother's life."

Seems is not good enough for Phainon. But it's important to Mydei, and it might be the only chance to catch a glimpse of his mother's past he'll ever get. Phainon will grit his teeth and tolerate the man if he has to.

"Alright," he sighs and puts his cup to the side.

If Phainon's relationship with Archidamia could grow into something that borders between tolerable and respectful, it shouldn't be much of a struggle to achieve the same with Krateros.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Even a large group of people trained to fight from an early age can be caught off guard. Phainon would like to curse out whoever is mapping out their path, but it's not like he has any knowledge to offer of his own either. They should definitely discuss sticking Ptolemy more permanently into the Council so that this can be avoided in the future, though. Phainon is sure he would have realized they are too close to danger early enough to redirect their course.

Black tide is spreading, the monsters' power growing. Their sizes have changed as well, many of them so large that it feels almost impossible that they could have originated from mutated human corpses.

He hears Hephaestion yell, in a warning rather than pain, and naturally gravitates toward him. He can afford to glance away as he yanks his sword back out of a blackened corpse and sees Hephaestion rapidly firing off a flurry of arrows. They strike right into the glowing orbs that serve as the creatures' core. The monsters fall as if their strings were cut.

In the circle of dead bodies stands Aias, covered in the gunk head to toe, dual blades clutched in his hands. His chest is moving rapidly, ginger hair plastered over his face. He is gazing across what became the battlefield, torn tents and overturned furniture.

"Aias, slow down!" Hephaestion screams, arrow drawn as if he is contemplating shooting Aias in the foot to slow him down. "You will kill yourself!"

"Shut up!" Aias whirls around to yell back. Phainon is closer to him than Hephaestion is, and can easily see the crazed look in his eyes. "I don't care, I have to find Thera!"

Oh.

Phainon looks around, noting the distinct lack of the feisty child. When caught in a fight, she always sticks to Aias' side, happily training her skill under her brother's watchful eye.

Aias takes off, and Phainon sets out after him.

He knows it's pointless to try and stop him, so he only lends some aid and ensures Aias' blind spots don't get exploited in his inattention. Aias will regain his senses only when his sister is found.

Phainon scans the ground, noting the burst of red crystals in the distance. He looks further and finds who he was searching for. He whistles twice, loud and sharp. For good measure, he shouts, "Leonnius!"

Their runner quickly makes his way, checking on Mydei as he goes. He reaches them without much effort required, then glances in question between Phainon and Aias' figure a few meters ahead.

"Could you try locating Thera?" Phainon asks, relieved when Leonnius' eyes set in determination.

"Of course," he agrees easily, visibly steeling himself for the task before running off again.

Phainon watches anxiously as he falters in front of a large group of monsters obstructing his path. Fortunately, he seems to gather himself quickly and weaves in between them with ease. Phainon hopes he finds Thera easily, that both of them return whole and safe.

Participating in an ongoing battle never fails to prove how difficult it is to keep track of time. It could be five minutes, it could be an hour. Phainon wouldn't know; corpses falling to his feet are the only measure available to him. He is certain that to Aias it must feel nothing short of an eternity before they spot Leonnius approaching at a quick pace.

Half of his face is drenched in dark red, the other half smeared with it, as if he tried to wipe it off. But he pays it no mind, expression steadfast as he nears them. Thera is draped over his back, face buried into his shoulder. She is on the taller side for her age, but the growth spurts have left her thin, with perhaps slightly more than twenty centimeters between her and their messenger. Leonnius, shorter than most Kremnoans Phainon's met so far, resolutely uses both of his hands to support her weight.

Aias drops his weapons as soon as he spots them, then nearly runs into them in his haste to get to Thera. Phainon jogs after him, looks around to see Hephaestion shoot a few arrows before spotting them, then starts slowly making his way over as well, shooting off more as he goes.

"Are you injured?" Aias asks, grabbing her with ease. He sounds calm despite the way his hands tremble just so when he pulls her closer to himself. In her big brother's arms, Thera looks almost like the same child who told Phainon and Mydei of her parents' death all those years ago. "Thera, have you been harmed?"

Thera shakes her head, her long auburn hair swaying with the motion. Aias shifts her so that she can settle on his hip, her height no longer so pertinent when her brother is much taller. He runs his hand over her back in relief, possibly to check for himself whether Thera didn't acquire a new injury without realizing due to adrenaline, smearing the remnants of black tide monsters on her clothes without realizing.

Hephaestion brushes past them and nearly shoves Leonnius onto the ground to make him sit. He rummages in his small bag for water, squinting down at the wound. He finds it eventually, then pours it over Leonnius' face to better assess the damage. Phainon walks over with a wince, knowing from experience how it must feel.

Leonnius only lets out a startled yelp in reaction, not saying a word otherwise. He seems to be in shock.

"I'm so sorry," Thera says shakily. "I, I didn't mean to—" She bursts into tears, clutching onto Aias.

"You're alright," Aias shushes her, placing his chin on the crown of her head. He closes his eyes, rocking up and down on his feet. "I'm never again letting you out of my sight, though," he mutters with a deep sigh. Slowly, his eyes open and focus on Leonnius with guilt and worry. "Is he okay?"

"He will need stitches," Hephaestion says, delicately angling Leonnius' face up. "He's got two cuts across his face, but it doesn't look very concerning. The right eye is swollen, though. I cannot tell the damage done to it."

"Maybe I won't look so weak anymore," Leonnius comments faintly. The blood is more of a pink hue staining his face now that it's been partly washed off. But the wound keeps on bleeding sluggishly, and as it repaints his skin with a scarlet streak, it makes his already pale face comparable to a sheet of paper.

"Phainon, take Thera from Aias," Hephaestion requests. Phainon looks at him in puzzlement, but Hephaestion's eyes are firmly on Aias. Then, he adds like an afterthought, "Please."

Aias freezes, somewhere between confusion and apprehension. Phainon shrugs, deciding he doesn't really wish to meddle. He walks up to them and reaches for Thera. She lets go reluctantly, immediately wrapping her hands around Phainon's neck when she is handed off. Phainon steps back to Leonnius, who only smiles up shakily at Thera when her lip wobbles at the sight of his face.

Phainon glances back at the other two just in time to glimpse Hephaestion's fist connecting with Aias' jaw. Thera jerks in his arms, and he tightens his hold on her. Yeah, no. He is not getting involved in that unless Hephaestion pulls a dagger on Aias.

"Perdikkas died not even a year ago," Hephaestion says fiercely, his clenched fist trembling at his side. "If you make me bury another friend because you are being stupid and irrational, I will find you in the nether realm and make you wish you never died."

Aias straightens up from the stance he fell into to bear the force of Hephaestion's strike. He rubs the spot as it begins to redden, wincing in pain. He isn't glaring, though. Doesn't seem angry in the slightest. He appears appreciative, even.

"Yes, sir." Aias salutes halfheartedly. He keeps his tone light as he continues, "I am genuinely sorry that Leonnius got hurt. However, I would have asked this of him again if it meant finding Thera faster and preventing her from being in harm's way."

"It was Leonnius' choice to go find her," Hephaestion says angrily. He steps closer to grab Aias by the collar, effectively erasing the few centimeters of height difference between them as well. "And while I am concerned over his injury, he is better suited for searching. I knew he wouldn't fail."

He lets go, pushing Aias away in the same movement. Aias stumbles to regain his balance, blinking widely in bemusement.

"I'm talking about you, you utter moron." With that, Hephaestion turns on his heel and walks up to Leonnius, helping him to his feet. He steers him to

the backlines where the medics already set up makeshift stations to aid the injured.

Aias stares after him in bewilderment. "Huh?" Phainon can easily imagine the question marks floating back and forth in his brain. It's a little funny.

"Hephaestion is so cool," Thera whispers to Phainon. Somehow she seems calmer now.

Well. That's one way to put it.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

The poor medic's shoulders are tense as he works, tying a secure knot. He almost flinches away in his haste to declare his work done. He does good enough of a job, though. Refrains from running out of the tent and instead double-checks his work for a minute longer.

Phainon wouldn't have blamed him if he did run. Five pairs of eyes track his every minute movement, each of them sitting closer than they probably should. Perdikkas wouldn't have tolerated this behavior. He would have had them all vacate his space within five minutes at most.

But this medic isn't Perdikkas. No one ever will be, and they cannot help but place all the new healers they stumble through under severe scrutiny because of it. Especially when this happens.

Leonnius is propped up on the cot, more than half of his face obstructed by the bandages. The singular eye visible in between the bloodstained cloth is opened wide and bouncing from surface to surface. Peucesta sits right on the edge despite the healer's protests, hand clasped tightly around Leonnius'.

"He is lucky," the medic says, swallowing nervously as he pulls away. "The cut digs deeper right under his bottom eyelid, meaning it skipped over the

eye entirely. Just a small gash over the brow ridge. That one won't even leave a mark."

He gets up, rummaging in his pack until he produces two sets of pills. He looks between Peucesta, Ptolemy, and Mydei, no doubt wondering which one of them he should address. Ultimately, he places them on a nearby table and keeps his gaze firmly on Leonnius.

"These are antibiotics and painkillers. I will come back tomorrow to redress the wounds and check for any signs of infection." He squints at the bandages one more time, assessing. "There shouldn't be any, though. Oh, but I'm afraid nothing can be done about the prominent scarring that might be left down his cheek and over the nose. We will remove the stitching in a few days."

"Thank you," Mydei says with a nod.

The healer visibly relaxes, saluting once before taking his leave.

No one says a word after that, all of them staring at Leonnius. It's a lot of bandages covering his face. It's nearly a miracle his eye wasn't harmed. But he still got a rather severe head injury. Were he less lucky, it could have—

"No one will think that I'm a coward anymore," Leonnius says happily, teetering on the edge of delirious.

"I will personally punch them if they do," Hephaestion offers lightheartedly, getting a bright appreciative grin from their dear messenger.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Mydei lies on the ground without a single worry, one leg dipped into the water from the knee down. Phainon watches the display warily, more than a little concerned about the way the water continuously produces a large

cloud of steam. It's not even a cold day for the phenomenon to be justifiable. The weather is hot, and Ptolemy would definitely have something to say about their current environment if he weren't busy with obsessively scribbling in his notes.

Thermal springs. That's all he offered when they made rounds around the area.

Phainon somewhat regrets not asking more details beforehand. On the lands, yes, but also how high the possibility of him getting cooked alive in these things is. He would rather leave without his skin covered in blisters.

"Scared of the water?" Mydei mutters sleepily, eyes half lidded as they stare up into the cloudless sky.

His skin is bathed in the silvery lights of the stars and moons alike. He still isn't as pale as Phainon, but in this lighting he comes close enough. The red of his markings almost glows, inviting wandering eyes to roam across the lines that stretch all over.

Mydei, shameless in his nudity as he always is, doesn't have a towel covering him. Phainon swallows as he lets his gaze fall lower from the safe area of his chest and toned stomach. Just for a second.

Mydei's dick rests angled to the side on his thigh, no longer an unfamiliar sight. Phainon almost wants to reach out and run his hand over it, grip it tightly the way he now knows Mydei enjoys. Use some of that water to slick the way, then slide up and down until it hardens.

His own cock twitches in interest in tandem with his imagination.

It's a sign to take his mind out of the gutter, and Phainon snaps his eyes back up to Mydei's face. He is still gazing at the stars, not paying any attention to Phainon. Probably searching for any constellations that he might still recognize. Now that he thinks about it, if they butcher the names and placement enough, Ptolemy might snap into action for a little longer. Phainon will have to talk to Hephaestion about this.

Mydei blinks slowly, chest rising at a measured pace. Relaxed. His expression is smoothed out entirely, and his hair messy from an entire day of traveling, spread out more than usual with his singular braid untangled.

Phainon could admire him for hours and not get bored of it. It's ridiculous how a single person can look so flawless. Were he not the Crown Prince of Castrum Kremnos, Phainon could easily imagine one of those beauty-worshiping regions falling all over themselves to acquire Mydei.

Maybe he is biased. Except even before he developed these feelings, before he and Mydei became attached beyond belief, he already held this opinion. Surrounded by the freezing waters and stared down by someone so stunning they seemed like a creature of the sea.

Phainon crouches down, and Mydei's eyes lazily meet his.

"Do you have any idea how beautiful you are?" Phainon asks, then reaches out to run his thumb beneath the left eyelid. In the spot where a red line rests on the opposite side.

Mydei exhales, face turning somewhat to nuzzle into Phainon's hand. "Flattery won't get you anywhere."

Ptolemy is the living proof that flattery will get you far, if Phainon remembers his tryst in Castrum Kremnos correctly. It's not really what Phainon is after, though. Not right now, anyway.

"I'm serious," he tells him, pinching the skin on his cheek lightly. "It's almost unfair."

Mydei hums, turning his head to bite lightly at the base of Phainon's thumb. "Perhaps you've forgotten the image that greets you in the mirror, then."

"Are you calling me pretty, Crown Prince Mydeimos?" Phainon drawls with a teasing smile. "Such an important figure has deemed me attractive—isn't that the highest form of flattery?"

"Isn't your attractiveness an obvious fact of life," Mydei shoots back with a small smirk, "Prince Consort Khaslana?"

Phainon's body stills entirely, breath stuttering in his lungs. Hearing his full name called in such a context is a staggering experience. No one uses Khaslana often, or at all. Ptolemy might have snapped at him once or twice with it. Hephaestion called it exactly once before grimacing and never speaking it again.

Mydei might have tested it out once as well, just to acknowledge it, right after they left the fortress. Phainon doesn't care. Prefers it this way, even. It's not like he casually calls Mydei by his full name either.

Prince Consort Khaslana.

His perception of the world tilts slightly, just like when he heard that title for the first time. He thinks it sounds good. Too good, actually.

An awkward laugh spills from Phainon's throat, fingers twitching against Mydei's cheek. He looks away, up at the small waterfall that cascades into the body of water a few meters away.

"Already flushed," Mydei remarks with obvious satisfaction, "And you haven't even touched the water just yet."

Phainon stubbornly doesn't look back down at him. "It's the steam," he reasons. Like it's not a flimsy excuse.

"Are you saying I don't put enough effort into making you blush so prettily?" Mydei asks casually, but his eyes glint when Phainon caves in and glances his way.

Alarm bells ring at the back of Phainon's head a moment too late.

Mydei's hand reaches up to tug at the towel Phainon had wrapped around his waist, and it falls to the ground. In the position he is in, it doesn't reveal much, but Phainon still twitches. He has to fight the instinct to cover himself up. Even if it's just the two of them, and the possibility of anyone

showing up this late into the night is close to none. Besides, Mydei has already seen all Phainon has to offer.

Phainon still cannot help but keep himself motionless. His smile freezes in place as he can physically feel the temperature of his skin rising. In the area of his face in particular.

He watches, barely processing, as Mydei props himself up on the elbow closer to Phainon. Then he angles himself to wrap the other arm over Phainon's shoulders, hooking it around his neck. Phainon has whole two seconds to get out of the loose hold before it tightens. Instead, he stays in place, eyes dropping lower when Mydei's face appears right in front of him.

He is promptly dragged over Mydei's body and shoved into the water, Mydei toppling in soon after, letting himself fall with the motion.

It's hot, almost scalding on Phainon's arguably sensitive skin. It's just this side of warmer than what they managed to force out of the Milos baths. It's not pleasant. But as soon as they find balance in the water and resurface to breathe, warm lips find Phainon's, and that's the only too-hot sensation that matters.

Their legs tangle, one of Phainon's hands finding the surface of stone behind Mydei and reaching up to rest against the edge, helping keep them both afloat. Mydei pulls Phainon against him, his back flat against the stone where Phainon's hand just trailed over. One of his legs shifts until he can snake it behind Phainon's thighs.

Phainon is glad for the way he can read him so easily. He prepares himself for what's to come, and only exhales shakily when Mydei forces their groins close. Phainon's free hand settles on Mydei's hip, squeezing the flesh when their cocks brush together teasingly one more time.

"I will last longer than you. We are four to five in your favor so far."

Mydei angles his head closer, smiling into Phainon's cheek. "Everything is a competition with you," he sighs. It's affectionate.

"You love it," Phainon grins cheekily, and Mydei pulls away a little to give him an apathetic stare.

Phainon grinds against Mydei just to feel his hips twitch and see him bite on his lip to maintain his composure the best he can.

"I do."

Phainon rummages through the pile of clean clothes he took with him. He nearly resigns himself to the fate of walking back with no underwear beneath his shorts. But then he spots the pair, colors standing out vibrantly against the rest of the fabrics. He makes a triumphant noise and slips it on.

He plans to dress slowly, give Mydei time to relax until his hair is dry. When they were younger, Phainon never would have thought that Mydei would enjoy being submerged in water quite this much. It might be partly due to how often Phainon ushered him into bathtubs over the years. The other reason must be the difference in temperature. Phainon recalls with painful clarity the freezing state of the waters in the Sea of Souls. And Mydei's skin that had taken on a blue hue by the time Phainon got him out of it.

"Phainon," Mydei says, voice colored with disapproval for some reason.

Phainon halts with his shirt stuck around his forearms. He glances over his shoulder in question, head tilted. Has he done something?

Mydei's elbows are placed on the edge to keep himself steady, half of his face covered by one hand. His eye is visible through the fingers. "Where did you get that…" Mydei's gaze jumps down to Phainon's crotch, followed up by an obvious grimace. "…Thing."

Phainon blinks at him in confusion, then glances down as well. He looks back to Mydei, still just as confused. "My underwear?" He confirms.

Mydei nods, covering his eyes entirely.

"The last city we passed through. You were busy with Peucesta so I kind of wandered around on my own," Phainon says. The cut is a bit different, the openings for his legs more diagonal than the standard briefs he usually wears. He didn't care about that when he bought it, though. "Why?"

"You might be the only person on Amphoreus who would purchase something with this color scheme."

"What's wrong with the colors?" Phainon demands. Purple and yellow complete each other nicely.

"Did they not have more muted versions?" Mydei asks, very clearly not actually answering Phainon's question.

Phainin pouts, snapping out of it to finally pull his shirt on all the way through. "But I wouldn't like the colors so much, then."

Mydei remains silent for a brief moment, as if digesting the words. Phainon still has no clue what's wrong with his underwear. He reaches for his pants, stopping for a second.

"I suppose even the most disastrous of garments would appear passable when you are the one wearing them," Mydei graciously allows eventually. Phainon looks over again, unsurprised to find Mydei staring directly at his ass. Possibly ignoring the colors in favor of something else entirely.

Phainon rolls his eyes. "Is it the garments or the shapes beneath them?"

Mydei doesn't respond to the question, though he does get out of the water. Phainon watches him towel off, the appreciation of his companion's physique overriding the mild annoyance.

"No underwear of your own?" Phainon comments with some amusement that only rises when Mydei waves him off shamelessly.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Mydei laughs, and Phainon physically feels his heart skip a beat.

Leonnius is too absorbed in his task to care, not that anyone but Phainon and Hephaestion ever pay that much attention to Mydei's everything. Leonnius blows into the odd instrument Peucesta pushed into his hands—an odd combination of two flutes made into one. It's called an aulos, apparently—trying to add to the melody his boyfriend plays without any instructions to follow.

It's the one instrument Leonnius would be hard-pressed to damage short of snapping it in two, so Peucesta allowed him to handle it. Mostly for amusement rather than anything else, though Phainon is sure there is at least one tune he must have taught him.

Ptolemy keeps throwing wry looks at them whenever a new screech is produced, shaking his head in exasperation. Leonnius begins making those high-pitched noises at regular intervals, and Peucesta works it into a less-than-perfect but still somewhat fitting tune. Or at least that's what Phainon thinks with his very limited musical knowledge. Until Leonnius gets bored of it and lets Peucesta play his song, only interrupting when he thinks it's most inconvenient.

Mydei laughs softly once more when Peucesta's brows furrow in frustration, Leonnius' chest puffed up in satisfaction at successfully annoying him.

"Lord Mydeimos," a voice calls behind them.

Phainon tenses and Leonnius drops his aulos. Ptolemy doesn't acknowledge the new presence, and Peucesta continues to play with no regard for it. Hephaestion would've possibly fallen over himself to greet Krateros.

"May I request your presence?"

It cannot be urgent, or someone else would have fetched him. Them. Because in all official matters, Phainon is called alongside Mydei.

Mydei looks over at Krateros, then exhales a bit longer than usual. Phainon knows it's because he already decided to go despite the fact he's been enjoying himself. Sure enough, he gets up and stretches on his tiptoes, ready to follow.

"Mydei, we—" Phainon forcibly cuts himself off. They what? Were having fun? So childish. But Phainon started saying something already, got everyone's attention, so he might as well proceed with something. "Can you stay?"

It's a simple question. It rings in Phainon's ears.

Phainon shouldn't be selfish; he's already taken so much. There isn't any space for his pathetic desperation among the Kremnoans. Phainon needs to do better, not risk everything because he wants more on top of what he has.

What Phainon should want is for Mydei to be able to nurture his relationship with Krateros, considering how important it is to him.

What Phainon actually wants is to not be alienated from Mydei every other day, separated for no good reason, excuses of why Phainon should be kept away whispered into Mydei's ear.

Phainon knows Mydei wouldn't let anyone else's opinions affect his judgment, probably doesn't entertain them at all, but the fact it's happening in the first place still stings.

Phainon should keep quiet and let him go.

Except Mydei said, twice now, that if Phainon wants something, he should just say a word. If there is one thing Phainon always does his best to adhere to, it's Mydei's wishes.

Please, he signs while Mydei's eyes are still on him before he can stop himself. Shame immediately fills him at behaving so obnoxiously needy.

Mydei watches him, blinking slowly, but says no word. After a moment, he looks back at Krateros.

Phainon drops the hand he used for a sign, fingers clasping the grass blades. Peucesta's music has lost some of its volume, transformed into a gentler melody without Phainon noticing. He latches onto it to distract himself from what's going on in his head.

"Sorry," he says, a little strangled. "I shouldn't have… yeah."

"I will stay," Mydei says immediately, a little exasperated. He takes a step closer and physically drags a corner of Phainon's lips up.

"Simply because some boy requested it?" Krateros asks in disbelief. He places his hands on his hips, an image of obvious disapproval. "Some more discipline would serve you well, Lord Mydeimos. You cannot comply with just about anyone's wishes, or people will get ideas that you should comply with what anyone says. And you," Krateros redirects all his attention to Phainon, somehow even more dismayed. "His name is Mydeimos. You should speak to him with respect."

Phainon is so taken aback by that load of nonsense that he struggles to come up with a response. Mydei, more disciplined? Phainon, disrespectful toward Mydei?

Mydei is the one to recover first, shooting back in a steely tone, "Phainon has never been some boy; he is—"

"I don't see you taking issue with the rest of us referring to Mydei as such either," Ptolemy muses and effectively cuts Mydei off. He points with his pen, gray eyes narrowed. "At least try not to be hypocritical about this, Lord Krateros."

"You shouldn't be doing that either," Krateros tells him, unwavering despite being called out. He refocuses on Mydei, lips thinning. "You aren't a child anymore. Act like it and prioritize your responsibilities over leisure."

The annoyance Phainon feels rises into the territory of genuine anger at that. The audacity—

"Excuse me, do you have an appointment on our schedule?" Phainon finally asks, leaning around Mydei's legs to address Krateros fully but not bothering to actually stand up. "I don't think we would have been sitting here if you did have one. It's not Mydei's responsibility to comply with your whims, Lord Krateros."

Besides, Mydei was ready to follow. It's his time of rest, as little of it as they get, and he didn't mind forsaking it because Krateros asked.

Krateros looks positively like he would love nothing more than to murder Phainon. A more difficult opponent or not, it's rather obvious who would have come out victorious in that duel. Maybe he should taunt him some more, goad him into pulling a weapon on Phainon and showing Mydei he isn't someone whose example should be followed.

He spots Archidamia approaching from behind the man just in time, and wisely decides to keep his mouth shut.

"You are correct, Lord Krateros. They are fully grown now," Archidamia says as she comes to his side. Krateros doesn't react beyond throwing her a glance from the corner of his eye. "They can do as they please so long as their duties aren't neglected."

"And you approve of this?" He rounds on her, agitated. "It's improper at best, unacceptable of a worthy ruler at worst."

"And do tell, what exactly is so unacceptable?"

It must require a gallant effort for Krateros to refrain from letting his gaze jump to Phainon. "I believe you are well aware."

"You've witnessed the immense power this boy holds, yet you still condemn him so much," Archidamia rubs the bridge of her nose in a rare display of frustration. "It fills me with shame to see a Kremnoan such as yourself lack respect in the face of such potential. Could it be that the King's madness has taken root in the depths of your body as well?"

Phainon cannot stop the smile from quirking his lips up. Of course he's known that Archidamia holds him in high regard for years now. It somehow never fails to squeeze something deep inside of him in that giddy way when he hears it aloud, though.

He lets himself lean against Mydei's leg, head pressed to his hip. Mydei's fingers tangle in the white strands for a moment. Krateros misses the gesture, all his barely suppressed anger now set on Archidamia.

"Need I remind you that even by Queen Gorgo's side, you spent most of your time carrying out wars instead of residing by her side at the court?" He asks haughtily. "You have no knowledge of what it takes to uphold the image. You should reconsider your station, Lady Archidamia."

"Your position doesn't outrank me anymore," she retorts calmly, not letting him get under her skin. Like a leader she's truly been for so many years, before slowly letting Mydei rise in power. "It would serve you well to remember your previous prestige means only as much as you can contribute to us."

Krateros' jaw clenches, lips pulling back somewhat. Phainon stifles a snort, wrapping his hand around Mydei's ankle. If it takes much longer, he will just tug him back down to the ground.

A minute later, she adds, "Have you heard what became of the Ladonian militia?"

Krateros seems thrown off by the question, brows furrowing. "Only rumors that bore little credibility. The sole reasonable information I could obtain was related to its eradication, but nothing more concrete."

Archidamia's smile is all sharp teeth. "It was a consequence of Lord Mydeimos losing one of his dear friends. A rather thorough act of revenge, wouldn't you say?"

Mydei's fingers twitch where they are still tangled in Phainon's hair, and in turn he grips his ankle with more strength, thumb swiping back and forth across the bone protruding at its side.

"The bond between these two boys goes even deeper than that; they are inseparable. You may not realize, but if Lord Phainon decided to leave the settlement all those years ago, Lord Mydeimos wouldn't have stayed either." Her eyes swipe over them, and she continues with a defeated sort of acceptance. "Even now, there is no guarantee he would remain with us should his companion depart."

Phainon wouldn't do that to Mydei, because he loves his friends dearly and he's come to genuinely care for the Kremnoans, as obsessed with obtaining glory as they sometimes are. Mydei has a duty to uphold, as everyone loves to remind him. And Phanion knows it's important to him on a personal level. He wouldn't ever place him in the position of having to make a choice whether to follow Phainon or stay behind.

Regardless of Phainon's intentions, Mydei's silence is very telling.

"Don't attempt to pull them apart," Archidamia says simply. She places one hand over her side, palm flat to it. "I have scars to show for it, my ignorance forever marked on my skin."

Krateros opens his mouth, perhaps ready to retort that he wouldn't have allowed the situation to escalate to that point. Archidamia has none of it, cutting in before any words can escape past his lips.

"I think it's time the two of us had a more detailed conversation regarding what followed my Queen's death and your failure to uphold your duty," she says, impressively neutral in her delivery. Phainon just barely avoids grinning widely at the furious red spreading over Krateros' face in anger, but Ptolemy has no such qualms, laughing openly. Archidamia ignores them, simply gesturing over her shoulder. "Make your way to my tent, would you? Unless you would rather remain oblivious or gather outdated gossip yourself."

"You could use some humility," Krateros comments as he walks past her, leaving without another look at any of them.

Ptolemy parrots him under his breath, rolling his eyes afterward in such a manner that it has Archidamia clicking her tongue at him.

"I believe you have an hour before you are expected," Archidamia reminds them when Ptolemy doesn't react to the subtle reprimand, aware of their schedule as ever. "Enjoy it."

And just like that, she also leaves.

Phainon is not sure what to think about the whole ordeal. Should he be glad Archidamia is intervening? Will Krateros finally back down, as unlikely as it seems? Or will he become worse, developing even more misgivings toward Phainon based on past events? Phainon isn't even sure what he could have done to warrant a reaction of that sort, but he doesn't doubt Krateros' ability to turn the situation around.

The pink scar on Leonnius' nose scrunches up with all the effort he puts into blowing into the aulos, producing a loud, low-pitched noise as he covers nearly all holes with his fingers. He grins proudly right after, successful in his attempt to release the tension at the cost of their eardrums.

"Ptolemy, would you like to try your hand at playing?" Peucesta asks mildly with a wince at the sound.

Ptolemy raises his head slowly from what he's been reading over, blinking slowly in such disbelief that it pulls a laugh out of Phainon.

"Hard pass."

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

Phainon and Mydei sit out the skirmish the detachment engages in. It's been decided it would be over much too soon were they to get involved. Phainon supposes Kremnoans might want to fight on their own sometimes.

"Aias is carrying all of Hephaestion's arrows back to him," Phainon comments, internally debating whether he should steal Ptolemy's book from

the nearby backpack to entertain himself with.

"Seems pointless," Mydei replies, stretching his arms to the sides and then up. "We have people that make sure archers have enough arrows at all times."

Phainon hums in agreement. That's what Hephaestion's function was as an aide when he first started coming along on the official expeditions, before he was allowed to fight himself. For Aias to collect them and bring them back is utterly senseless.

"He threw an arrow at someone again," Phainon laughs and points with his finger at the teen in question. "Hephaestion might shoot the next one at him like the last time."

"I've utilized a discarded arrow to slit someone's throat before," Mydei points out. "You make do with whatever you have at hand on the battlefield."

"Yes," Phainon says dryly. "I think you are part of the problem with Aias' mishandling of arrows. He admires you."

Mydei picks up a pebble and flicks it at Phainon, hitting him straight in the jaw. Naturally, it evolves into a battle of its own.

Two hours later or so, Phainon has various small bruises littering his body, and Hephaestion plops down onto the ground next to them. His quiver is slipped into his lap already, and Aias trails after him, Thera attached to his side once more.

Hephaestion takes one of the arrows out and begins carefully wiping all the gunk off it, then sets it on the ground next to him and repeats the process with the next one. Phainon tilts his head at it. It's truly incredibly rare for them to pick the arrows back up from the corpses. They are usually damaged, so it's not worth wasting the time. Kremnoans are crafty enough that restocking on them is hardly ever an issue.

"Anything special about these?" Phainon asks curiously. Mydei leans over from his side to take a look as well, resting one arm over Phainon's shoulder.

Hephaestion's hands stutter on the movements before returning to the practiced ease he treats the arrows with. "They were a gift from Perdikkas."

It's stiflingly quiet for a moment.

Phainon didn't know about that. And if Phainon didn't know, Mydei couldn't have known either.

In the distance, people gather in their usual groups, preparing for an hour of rest before they return to the journey ahead. Aias whistles to himself quietly, spinning Thera around. Hephaestion focuses on cleaning, not paying attention to anything around him.

Phainon pushes against Mydei to get him to lie down and then throws his limbs over him, feeling a huff of air as much as hearing it.

Perhaps not so pointless.

˖✧ 𖤓 ✧˖

It takes every bit of willpower that Phainon possesses not to grimace. Or send a prayer to Kephale to strike the man who just took a seat in an empty chair with no invitation. Mydei wouldn't like that; he has to remind himself.

"Welcome," Ptolemy greets simply, the only buffer Phainon can hope for.

"Lord Ptolemy," Krateros inclines his head. He regards Phainon with much less warmth, the words leaving his throat almost reluctant, "Lord Phainon."

As uncomfortable as Phainon felt when people first attached a title to his name, it now brings him great satisfaction to see Krateros grit his teeth

through it. Phainon takes it a step further, only nodding in simple acknowledgment the exact same way Mydei does.

Ptolemy's face does a funny thing at the display before he smooths his expression out.

"I have given thought to my conversation with Lady Archidamia," he says, leaning with both elbows on his knees. "I got an impression she hasn't given me all the information, only familiarizing me with some key past events that occurred."

"And what may those be, Lord Krateros?" Ptolemy asks, tone pleasant but smile thin and forced.

"It all relates to this unhealthy attachment Lord Mydeimos holds."

Toward Phainon, he doesn't finish.

Ptolemy hums and nods sagely, scratching his chin for good measure. "And I suppose you have turned a blind eye to the specific nature of said attachment?"

"Its nature," Krateros repeats slowly, glancing at Phainon warily. Phainon waves at him cheerfully, still not speaking a word.

"Have you really not noticed?" Ptolemy asks, perplexed. It even sounds genuine now. "I find it difficult to imagine an observant man such as yourself could miss a clue this obvious. All of the detachment has known about this before Mydei and Phainon realized themselves."

Phainon winces. Not his brightest moment; not realizing just how mutual his feelings for Mydei are.

Krateros' jaw clenches and releases, then he rubs one hand over the side of his head. "I have heard certain… Conversations about Lord Mydeimos' preferences," he says faintly. "But the notion seemed so ridiculous that I took it for nothing more than a joke."

Phainon feels mildly offended. "Maybe if you weren't that occupied with separating us and took a moment to let us be with each other as we usually are, you would have gathered as much yourself."

He isn't sure whether all of the detachment is aware they caught up to what everyone could see between them for however long. Neither of them cares for keeping it a secret or revealing the development. As Ptolemy said, it might be difficult to discern whether anything changes from an outsider's perspective. Krateros might not know they got together, and he could have disregarded the talk of their feelings for one another as something meaningless. It's not so far-fetched.

Krateros opens his mouth to no doubt take issue with Phainon's disrespectful tone and words, but Phainon beats him to it. Might as well show him the undeniable proof before he goes spouting nonsense again.

"Hey, Mydei!" He yells, as loud as he can. Mydei turns around, tilts his head instead of shouting back. "Come here for a second!"

Mydei glances at Krateros as he approaches, but doesn't pay him any mind. Phainon spreads his legs and raises his hands expectantly, smiling up at him. Mydei stares for a moment, then rolls his eyes. He does come closer, though, stepping right in between Phainon's knees. One of his hands goes to rest on Phainon's shoulder, and once their eyes meet, he doesn't look away.

Phainon grins and reaches up to gently tug him down by Queen Gorgo's necklace. Their lips meet in a chaste kiss, Mydei breaking off after no more than a few seconds.

"Did you just call me all this way for nothing but a kiss?" He asks.

"Yep," Phainon says, popping the 'p' at the end of it.

"Insufferable," Mydei mutters, but still presses another peck to Phainon's forehead before he steps away.

Phainon watches him leave with an unreasonable amount of satisfaction and adoration. When Mydei is well outside of earshot, he turns back to the other

two. Ptolemy is red in the face from the effort to hold the laughter in. Krateros appears pale as a sheet. If Phainon didn't know any better, he would worry the man might be about to pass out.

Phainon grins widely, entirely shameless about the whole display. "I am the Prince Consort, don't you know?"

Ptolemy nearly falls over with the force of his laughter.

Chapter End Notes
